# OgreBot for EverQuest II - API reference: ALL OF IT IN ONE FILE

Plain text for AI assistants, generated from the same tables as the API reference pages (https://kannkor.github.io/ISXOgre/EQ2/bot/developer/api/).
This file is the whole API reference; the same text in smaller pieces is listed in the index.
How to read an entry, and every file like this one: https://kannkor.github.io/ISXOgre/EQ2/bot/llms-api.txt

== OgreBotAPI ==

${OgreBotAPI.Abilities}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: The Abilities sub-object: the in-memory ability catalog loaded from this character's ability export, the ability reads built on it, and the cast and cancel verbs. Opening OgreBot loads the catalog; without OgreBot open, load it with its :Load before reading abilities from it.
  returns: object: the Abilities sub-object; it always exists, and as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Abilities.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Abilities (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Abilities}

${OgreBotAPI.Access}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: The Access sub-object: this session's access level (SetLevel) and UnauthPCsNearMe, which reports another player nearby who is not one of your own characters.
  returns: object: the Access sub-object; it always exists, and as text it reads Access[level/highest], this session's level and the account's highest level.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Access (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Access}

${OgreBotAPI.Actors}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: Opens the Actors sub-object: counting and finding actors near you (by name, by type, NPCs within a range, mob ID, is-a-player), and clicking, hailing or applying a verb to an actor, now or queued. It always resolves and takes no arguments; the work is in its own members and methods.
  returns: OgreBotAPI.Actors object: never NULL; as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Actors.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Actors (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Actors}

${OgreBotAPI.Assist}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: The Assist sub-object: who this character takes its kill target from. Its members (TargetID, InControl, IsAssisting) read that choice, and :Anchor sets it.
  returns: object: the Assist sub-object; it always exists, and as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Assist.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Assist (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Assist}

${OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: The AutoHunt sub-object: the AutoHunt driver's state (Mode, Active, AllowMovement, SafetyTripped, PullTargetID, LastAction, FreezeReason) and its setters (:SetMode, :SetScanRadius, :SetCheckHP, :SetCheckMana).
  returns: object: the AutoHunt sub-object; it always exists, and as text it reads OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt}

${OgreBotAPI.AutoTarget}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: The AutoTarget sub-object: the auto-target list and its settings - enable, scan radius and height, add or remove actors, presets and saved lists. As text it reports how many entries the current working list holds.
  returns: object: the AutoTarget sub-object; it always exists, and as text it reads AutoTarget[N entries], N being the number of entries in the current working list.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.AutoTarget (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.AutoTarget}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:AutoTarget

${OgreBotAPI.Bot}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: The Bot sub-object: the running bot's own lifecycle - pause, resume, reload, end, camp to desktop, exit the client, run OgreBot commands and scripts. It is the running bot, not the saved profile options.
  returns: object: the Bot sub-object; it always exists, and as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Bot.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Bot (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Bot}

${OgreBotAPI.CampSpot}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: The CampSpot sub-object: the camp spot this character holds to - set, nudge, clear and enable it, relative spots, spots behind or in front of an actor, and formations. Its members read the active slot, the effective spot and whether you are at it.
  returns: object: the CampSpot sub-object; it always exists, and as text it reads OgreBotAPI.CampSpot.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.CampSpot (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.CampSpot}

${OgreBotAPI.CastStack}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: The CastStack sub-object: the cast stack - load or import it, turn entries and tags on or off, hold and clear tag embargos and allows, and inspect it. Bot:Pause and Bot:Resume pause and run it.
  returns: object: the CastStack sub-object; it always exists, and as text it reads OgreBotAPI.CastStack.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.CastStack (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.CastStack}

${OgreBotAPI.Client}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: The Client sub-object: things done to the EQ2 client rather than the character - reset the camera, set the camera pitch, and move the mouse. It holds methods only.
  returns: object: the Client sub-object; it always exists, and as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Client.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Client (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Client}

${OgreBotAPI.Combat}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: The Combat sub-object: whether you are fighting and what the bot may do while you are - InCombat, the no-offensive and no-defensive switches, the threat ignore list and the countdown.
  returns: object: the Combat sub-object; it always exists, and as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Combat.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Combat (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Combat}

${OgreBotAPI.Comms}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: The Comms sub-object: messaging between your characters - events, messages, broadcasts, tells, group queries and IRC. As text it is a one-line summary of its send and receive counters, prefixed "Comms ".
  returns: object: the Comms sub-object; it always exists, and as text it reads "Comms " followed by the one-line counter summary (the same text as ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Stats}).
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Comms (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Comms}

${OgreBotAPI.Consumables}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: The Consumables sub-object: things you eat, drink, click, mount or summon - replenish food, drink and stat potions, mount up and down, summon a familiar, rekindle the heartstone, and the mount, mercenary and familiar training checks. It holds methods only.
  returns: object: the Consumables sub-object; it always exists, and as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Consumables.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Consumables (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Consumables}

${OgreBotAPI.Craft}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: Opens the Craft sub-object: the crafting calls of ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft} with a for-who in front, so each runs only on the characters it names (add a recipe, start, writs, scribe, tinkering). It has methods only and takes no arguments.
  returns: OgreBotAPI.Craft object: never NULL; as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Craft.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Craft (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Craft}

${OgreBotAPI.Cures}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: The Cures sub-object: cures, curses and dispels - the group curse counts, uncurable and detrimental reads, cure requests, item cures, cancelling a detrimental and replenishing cure potions.
  returns: object: the Cures sub-object; it always exists, and as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Cures.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Cures (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Cures}

${OgreBotAPI.Debug}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: The Debug sub-object: the version, the debug output switches, debug echoes and the variable and stat spews.
  returns: object: the Debug sub-object; it always exists, and as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Debug.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Debug (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Debug}

${OgreBotAPI.Encounter}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: Opens the Encounter sub-object: one method, List, which lists the available encounter setups on the characters a for-who names. The encounter engine itself is ${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter}, a different object.
  returns: OgreBotAPI.Encounter object: never NULL; as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Encounter.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Encounter (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Encounter}

${OgreBotAPI.Events}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: The Events sub-object: add and remove rows of the Chat, Spawn and Despawn event tabs, the same rows the panel edits. It holds methods only.
  returns: object: the Events sub-object; it always exists, and as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Events.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Events (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Events}

${OgreBotAPI.ForWho}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: Opens the ForWho sub-object: ask whether a for-who expression selects this character or a named group member, and manage for-who aliases (add, remove, change, rename, list). It always resolves and takes no arguments.
  returns: OgreBotAPI.ForWho object: never NULL; as text it reads OgreBotAPI.ForWho.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.ForWho (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.ForWho}

${OgreBotAPI.HOs}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: Opens the HOs sub-object: heroic opportunity reads (is the starter or wheel up, which wheel, who can start or advance it, time left) and the verbs that start, advance or cancel one and set which icons may be used. It always resolves and takes no arguments.
  returns: OgreBotAPI.HOs object: never NULL; as text it reads OgreBotAPI.HOs.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.HOs (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.HOs}

${OgreBotAPI.IM}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: The IM sub-object: the Inventory Manager session - IsOpen, IsRunning, Status and one method per `ogre im` word. As text it is the session's status line, not the object's name.
  returns: object: the IM sub-object; it always exists, and as text it reads the status line - "closed", or "open" (or "closed (running headless)") followed by ", idle" or ", running <mode>", plus "; will close when finished (-end)" when that is pending.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.IM (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.IM}

${OgreBotAPI.Inventory}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: Opens the Inventory sub-object: item counts, free bag slots, equipment slot names, adornments, and the verbs that use, examine, equip, unpack, consume or destroy items plus the item rotation embargo list. It always resolves and takes no arguments.
  returns: OgreBotAPI.Inventory object: never NULL; as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Inventory.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Inventory (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Inventory}

${OgreBotAPI.Loot}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: Opens the Loot sub-object: loading the loot rule files, deciding what to do with each item in a loot window, loot-all, auto-loot mode and the loot options. It always resolves and takes no arguments.
  returns: OgreBotAPI.Loot object: never NULL; as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Loot.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Loot (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Loot}

${OgreBotAPI.Looting}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: TRUE while looting is going on: a loot window is open, or OgreBot did loot work (opened a corpse, chest or shiny, or worked a loot window) in the last 3 seconds. It simply runs out 3 seconds after the last loot activity, so a script waiting for looting to finish can poll it.
  returns: bool: TRUE when a loot window is open or the last loot activity was under 3 seconds ago; FALSE otherwise (including when nothing has been looted yet).
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Looting}
  oldbot: Obj_OgreIH.LastLootWindowAppeared, Obj_OgreIH:EQ2_onLootWindowAppeared, Object_Instance_Inherit.LastLootWindowAppeared

${OgreBotAPI.Merchant}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: Opens the Merchant sub-object: buying from, selling to and repairing at an NPC merchant (not the broker and not the depot). It has methods only and takes no arguments.
  returns: OgreBotAPI.Merchant object: never NULL; as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Merchant.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Merchant (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Merchant}

${OgreBotAPI.Movement}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: Opens the Movement sub-object: distance, heading and facing reads, points around an actor, and the walking verbs - move to a loc, navigate, follow, joust, face, fly, jump, crouch, evac and movement blocks. It always resolves and takes no arguments.
  returns: OgreBotAPI.Movement object: never NULL; as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Movement.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Movement (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Movement}

${OgreBotAPI.NPCUnkillableBug}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: TRUE when your current target looks stuck in the unkillable state: an NPC or NamedNPC that cannot turn, is feign-dead, is not aggro and is rooted. FALSE when you have no target or are not in the world.
  returns: bool: TRUE when your target is an NPC or NamedNPC with CanTurn FALSE, IsFD TRUE, IsAggro FALSE and IsRooted TRUE; FALSE otherwise, with no target, or out of the world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.NPCUnkillableBug}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.NPCUnkillableBug

${OgreBotAPI.Options}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: Opens the Options sub-object: read an OgreBot option value, set options, load a profile, revert, and warn before saving. As text it shows the loaded profile name, or "no profile" when none is loaded.
  returns: OgreBotAPI.Options object: never NULL; as text it reads Options[<profile name>], or Options[no profile].
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Options (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Options}

${OgreBotAPI.Overseer}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: Opens the Overseer sub-object: four Overseer verbs (add agents, check quests, auto-add quests, buy missions). The Overseer engine itself is run from ${ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer}, a different object.
  returns: OgreBotAPI.Overseer object: never NULL; as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Overseer.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Overseer (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Overseer}

${OgreBotAPI.Paths}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: Opens the Paths sub-object: saved walks through the zone you are in, each a list of points of interest or locations. It always resolves and takes no arguments.
  returns: OgreBotAPI.Paths object: never NULL; as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Paths.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Paths (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Paths}

${OgreBotAPI.Pet}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: Opens the Pet sub-object: four pet commands - attack, back off, assist and get lost. It has methods only and takes no arguments.
  returns: OgreBotAPI.Pet object: never NULL; as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Pet.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Pet (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Pet}

  kind: member of OgreBotAPI

  returns: OgreBotAPI.Position object: never NULL; as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Position.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Position (its members and methods are listed under it)

${OgreBotAPI.Quest}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: Opens the Quest sub-object: whether you or an actor has a quest, and the quest and mission verbs - share, accept, delete, show info and mission timers. It always resolves and takes no arguments.
  returns: OgreBotAPI.Quest object: never NULL; as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Quest.

${OgreBotAPI.Roster}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: Opens the Roster sub-object: group and raid reads (sizes, counts and members picked by class, archetype or role, leader, in zone) and the group verbs - flag, mark, invite, disband, make leader, mentor, kick. It always resolves and takes no arguments.
  returns: OgreBotAPI.Roster object: never NULL; as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Roster.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Roster (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster}

${OgreBotAPI.Session}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: Opens the Session sub-object: whether this client is at character select, the character name, revive and res verbs, harvesting a node, collecting a shiny, and logging a character in. As text it shows your character name, which is empty while you are not in the world.
  returns: OgreBotAPI.Session object: never NULL; as text it reads Session[<your character name>], or Session[] out of the world.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Session (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Session}

  what: The TempAdorns sub-object: the temporary-adornment profiles - IsOpen, Profiles, the window (:Open, :Close, :UI), :Apply and :List.
  returns: object: the TempAdorns sub-object; it always exists, and as text it reads OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns}

${OgreBotAPI.Travel}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: Opens the Travel sub-object: ordinary travel - bells, druid rings, spires, the guild hall, zone doors and the travel mesh. It always resolves and takes no arguments.
  returns: OgreBotAPI.Travel object: never NULL; as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Travel.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Travel (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Travel}

${OgreBotAPI.Util}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: The Util sub-object: helpers LavishScript does not have - number and text conversions, rounding, range checks, colour-code and zone-number stripping, time formatting, MD5, file-exists, plus on-screen timers and delayed actions.
  returns: object: the Util sub-object; it always exists, and as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Util.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Util (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util}

${OgreBotAPI.ValidKillTarget}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: TRUE when the bot's current NPC kill target still exists. The kill target is refreshed once per pulse in the world: your target if it is a living NPC or NamedNPC, otherwise your target's target if that is one.
  returns: bool: TRUE when there is an NPC kill target and its actor still exists; FALSE when there is none (${ISXOgreEQ2.NPCTargetID} reads 0) or the actor is gone.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.ValidKillTarget}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.ValidKillTarget

${OgreBotAPI.Vars}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI
  what: Opens the Vars sub-object: two named-value stores - a plain one for your scripts (Get, Set, Clear) and the bot's own internal one (GetInternal, SetInternal, ClearInternal). It always resolves and takes no arguments.
  returns: OgreBotAPI.Vars object: never NULL; as text it reads OgreBotAPI.Vars.
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Vars (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Vars}

${OgreBotAPI.Zone}

OgreBotAPI:ArcannaseEffigyOfRebirth[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI
  what: Double-clicks the nearest Arcanna'se Effigy Of Rebirth, at once. Nothing happens, silently, when none is within a distance of 3.5.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI:ArcannaseEffigyOfRebirth[all]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ArcannaseEffigyOfRebirth

OgreBotAPI:DoVDebuff[fw, mob, allowMoving=setting]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI
  what: Queues your archetype's raid debuff on the mob: Demoralizing Swipe (fighter), Slice of Despair (scout), Pall of the Elements (mage) or Divine Despair (priest). It is skipped when the ability is 5 seconds or more from ready, or the mob is out of range and moving is not allowed; a missing mob, ability or archetype echoes a line and does nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg mob (string): The mob: an actor ID, or a name (the nearest actor whose name contains it).
  arg allowMoving (bool, default: setting): TRUE walks into range first when the mob is too far away (the range is the ability export's); FALSE skips the cast instead. Left out, the DoV raid debuff "allow moving" setting decides.
  example: OgreBotAPI:DoVDebuff[all,${Target.ID}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:DoVDebuff

OgreBotAPI:DoVDebuff_Half[fw, mob, archetype=auto, odd=TRUE, allowMoving=setting]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI
  what: Like DoVDebuff, but only characters of one archetype cast, and only half of them: the odd or even ranks when that archetype's raid members (group members outside a raid) are ordered by character ID. Most refusals are silent - a different archetype, the other half, or no DoV debuff found on the mob when archetype is auto.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg mob (string): The mob: an actor ID, or a name (the nearest actor whose name contains it).
  arg archetype (string, default: auto): fighter, scout, mage or priest - the archetype that casts. auto reads the mob's effects for a DoV raid debuff icon and uses that archetype.
  arg odd (bool, default: TRUE): TRUE: the odd ranks (1st, 3rd, ...) cast; FALSE: the even ranks.
  arg allowMoving (bool, default: setting): TRUE walks into range first when the mob is too far away; FALSE skips the cast instead. Left out, the DoV raid debuff "allow moving" setting decides.
  example: OgreBotAPI:DoVDebuff_Half[all,${Target.ID},auto,TRUE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:DoVDebuff_Half

OgreBotAPI:F2PWindow_SetOptions[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI
  what: Ticks the Settings tab option that closes the All-Access upsell window, which the bot then checks about every 100 seconds, and echoes that the watcher is enabled; with no OgreBot profile loaded the option is not ticked, though the echo still prints.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI:F2PWindow_SetOptions[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:F2PWindow_SetOptions

OgreBotAPI:GetFlag[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI
  what: Queues a job that talks to the guild strategist and takes a tactical rally banner (conversation reply 3). It echoes and stops when no strategist is within a distance of 10 or you already carry a banner.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI:GetFlag[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:GetFlag

OgreBotAPI:NoTarget[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI
  what: Clears your target at once (the game's /target_none).
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI:NoTarget[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:NoTarget

OgreBotAPI:Prepare_TankSwapping[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI
  what: Gets the group ready for tank swapping: Guardians turn off Recapture, Bruisers turn off and cancel Hostility and Alternate: Shiftiness, and fighters tick the option to cast no force-target abilities. Everyone also cancels Subtle Strikes, drops the TankSwap no-offensive hold and clears the threat ignore list, all at once (not queued).
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI:Prepare_TankSwapping[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Prepare_TankSwapping

OgreBotAPI:Remove_Prepare_TankSwapping[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI
  what: Undoes Prepare_TankSwapping: Guardians turn Recapture back on, Bruisers turn Hostility and Alternate: Shiftiness back on in the cast stack (they are not recast), and fighters untick the no force-target option. Everyone also cancels Subtle Strikes, drops the TankSwap no-offensive hold and clears the threat ignore list.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI:Remove_Prepare_TankSwapping[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Remove_Prepare_TankSwapping

OgreBotAPI:ResetFor_Intercept[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI
  what: Turns back on exactly the cast stack entries SetUpFor_Intercept turned off on this character, so an Intercept that was already off stays off. The Guardian entry is touched on a Guardian only.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI:ResetFor_Intercept[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ResetFor_Intercept

OgreBotAPI:Scribe_Empyral[fw, nameFilter=Empyral]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI
  what: Queues a job that scribes every scribeable item in your bags whose name contains nameFilter, one at a time, then opens and closes the knowledge book so new recipes show. Pass * to scribe everything scribeable; when nothing matches it echoes that and does nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg nameFilter (string, default: Empyral): Text the item name must contain (case-insensitive), or * for every scribeable item.
  example: OgreBotAPI:Scribe_Empyral[${Me.Name},Empyral]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Scribe_Empyral

OgreBotAPI:SetUpFor_Intercept[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI
  what: Turns the Intercept ability off in the cast stack on every class, and on a Guardian also the Guardian ability, cancelling the Guardian buff it is maintaining. The bot does this itself before it casts Intercept when the game says a groupmate needs it; ResetFor_Intercept puts back what this turned off.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI:SetUpFor_Intercept[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:SetUpFor_Intercept

OgreBotAPI:Special[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI
  what: Double-clicks the nearest interactable actor whose type contains "special" (a clickable object), at once. There is no range limit, and nothing happens when there is none.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI:Special[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Special, call Obj_OgreIH.Specialwait, call Obj_OgreUtilities.HandleClickActor_Special

OgreBotAPI:Target[fw, target]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI
  what: Targets an actor once, at top priority, on the bot's next pulse (even while paused); it does not hold the target, so auto-target or assist may change it later. me or your own name targets yourself; a blank target or one that resolves to nothing does nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg target (string): Who to target: an actor ID, me, an @role, pet:<owner>, or a name (the nearest actor whose name contains it).
  example: OgreBotAPI:Target[all,${Target.ID}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Target, call Obj_OgreUtilities.DoTarget

OgreBotAPI:TargetLock[fw, target=clear]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI
  what: Locks your target onto one actor and keeps it there, above auto-target and assist, until you clear it, a LetsGo runs or you change zone; a new lock replaces the old one. clear, off, 0 or a blank target releases the lock, and a target that resolves to nothing leaves the current lock as it is.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg target (string, default: clear): The actor to lock onto: an actor ID, an @role, pet:<owner>, or a name (the nearest actor whose name contains it); clear, off or 0 releases the lock.
  example: OgreBotAPI:TargetLock[all,${Target.ID}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:TargetLock

OgreBotAPI:UpdateNPCTarget[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI
  what: Re-reads your NPC target right now: your target if it is a live NPC, otherwise your target's target. The bot already does this every frame in the world, so a script only needs it to see a target change within the same frame.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI:UpdateNPCTarget[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:UpdateNPCTarget

OgreBotAPI:UseFlag[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI
  what: Queues a job that talks to the guild strategist and picks reply 2, which sends you to your guild's rally point. It echoes and stops when no strategist is within a distance of 10; a Brigand's Safehouse is cancelled first.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI:UseFlag[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:UseFlag


== OgreBotAPI.Abilities ==

${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.CanCastOn[ability,target]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Tells you whether you could cast an ability on a target right now, and if not, why. It runs the bot's own castability check (range measured edge to edge, power, cooldown, position, stealth, line of sight, target type), so a script never has to rebuild it.
  arg ability (ability name or id): the ability to check
  arg target (actor name or id): who to cast it on; blank = yourself
  returns: string: "eligible" when it can be cast now. Otherwise the reason: "no ability given", "unresolved" (ability not found), "no valid target" (also when not in the world), "no target", "target gone", "cannot target self", "wrong target type", "target type unreadable", "ability not known", "on cooldown", "just cast this line", "not enough power", "not flanking", "not behind", "position unreadable", "requires stealth", "moving", "distance unreadable", "out of range", "line of sight unknown" or "line of sight blocked".
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.CanCastOn["Intercept",${Target.ID}]}

${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.CancelCurrentCast}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Reads the cancel-current-cast flag that :SetCancelCurrentCast raises. It stays TRUE until the next cast starts or ends, then clears itself.
  returns: bool: TRUE while a cancel of the current cast is pending, FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.CancelCurrentCast}

${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.Count}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: The number of usable abilities in the loaded export: one per ability line, the highest rank your level allows.
  returns: int: the number of usable abilities, one per line. 0 when no export is loaded.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.Count}

${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.FindCastableHOIconAbilityID[iconId,options...]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Finds an ability you own that matches a heroic opportunity icon and can be cast now, and gives its id without casting it. Your "no stuns"-style settings are honoured; -offensive keeps only hostile abilities, and -ActorID <id> (or -HOTarget <id>) checks against that actor instead of your current NPC target.
  arg iconId (number, default: 0): the heroic opportunity icon id
  arg options... (text): -offensive, -ActorID <id> or -HOTarget <id>, and the -No options, each on top of your settings boxes: -NoStun, -NoDaze, -NoFear, -NoStifle, -NoInterrupt, -NoDispel, -NoRoot, -NoSnare, -NoCures, -NoGroupCures, -NoForceTargets, -NoThreatIncreases, -NoThreatDecreases. The console names any other option once, and it is ignored.
  returns: int64: the id of the ability to cast. 0 when nothing you own matches the icon or can be cast now.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.FindCastableHOIconAbilityID[3,-offensive]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_HOIconAbility

${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.FindCastableID[query...]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Picks an ability that is ready now by its properties instead of its name and gives its id without casting it; all terms have to match. Your "no stuns"-style settings still rule abilities out, except for the property you searched on, and a bad query is reported in the console.
  arg query... (text): query terms, each member, comparison, value (such as "IsInterrupt","=","TRUE"), plus options such as -NPCRequired or -ActorID <id> that check against a target
  returns: int64: the id of the matching ability (fastest cast time wins). 0 when nothing matches, when the query is refused, or when no export is loaded.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.FindCastableID["IsInterrupt","=","TRUE","-NPCRequired"]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_AbilityTypeID, OgreBotAPI.Get_AbilityTypeID_Ref, OgreBotAPI.Get_AbilityVia

${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.FindCastableInterruptID[actor]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Picks the interrupt you would use right now (an interrupt that is not beneficial, ready, and usable on the target; fastest cast time wins) and gives its id without casting it. With no actor it checks against your current NPC target; a bad query is reported in the console.
  arg actor (actor name or id): who to interrupt; blank = current NPC target
  returns: int64: the id of the interrupt to cast. 0 when you have none usable right now.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.FindCastableInterruptID}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_InterruptID

${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.HaveMaintained[name...]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Checks your maintained window for any of the names you give; names match partially and ignore case by default. An ability id is turned into the full name of the rank you hold.
  arg name... (ability name or id): maintained names or ability ids to look for; put -exact (or TRUE) before names that must match exactly and -partial (or FALSE) to switch back
  returns: bool: TRUE when any of the names is in your maintained window, FALSE when none is.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.HaveMaintained[-exact,"Sprint"]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.HaveMaintained

${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.ID[name]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Looks an ability up in your loaded export and gives its id. A short name ("Assault"), any rank's full name ("Assault X") or any rank's id all give the best rank you can use now; name matching ignores case.
  arg name (ability name or id): the ability to look up
  returns: int64: the id of the best usable rank. A number that is not in your export comes back unchanged. 0 when the name matches nothing or no export is loaded.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.ID["Sprint"]}
  oldbot: Abilities.Ability, Abilities.GetIndexBy, Abilities.GetIndexByID

${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.Info[nameOrId, field]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Reads one field of an ability from your loaded export, for the best rank you can use. Flags the export leaves out (false flags are omitted) read as empty, not FALSE.
  arg nameOrId (ability name or id): the ability to read
  arg field (text): export field name, e.g. Name or CastingTime
  returns: string: the field's value as text (TRUE/FALSE for flags). Empty when the ability or the field is not found, or no export is loaded.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.Info["Sprint",CastingTime]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_AbilityInfo, SpellOb.AllowRaid, SpellOb.CastingTime

${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.InfoRaw[nameOrId]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Gives the whole export record of an ability (best rank you can use) as JSON, for reading several fields at once with jsonvalue.
  arg nameOrId (ability name or id): the ability to read
  returns: string: the record as a JSON object. {} when the ability is not found or no export is loaded.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.InfoRaw["Assault"]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_AbilityInfo_RawData

${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.Loaded}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Tells you whether an ability export is loaded for this character. Name lookups (casting by name, Info, ShortName and the rest) need a loaded export.
  returns: bool: TRUE when an ability export is loaded, FALSE when none is.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.Loaded}

${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.RawCount}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: The number of entries in the loaded export before it is reduced to one rank per line, so every rank of every ability counts.
  returns: int: the total number of entries in the export file. 0 when no export is loaded.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.RawCount}

${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.Ready[fw,ability,actor]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Asks whether an ability is ready. Without an actor it checks only that the ability is off cooldown; with an actor it runs the full can-I-cast-this-on-them check (range, power, position, line of sight, target type), the same check as CanCastOn.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg ability (ability name or id): the ability to check
  arg actor (actor name or id): who you would cast it on; blank = cooldown only
  returns: bool: TRUE when the ability is ready (and castable on the actor, if one is given). FALSE when it is not, when the ability or actor cannot be found, when you are not in the world, or when the for-who does not include this character.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.Ready[all,"Assault"]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.AbilityReady

${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.ScrollMaintainedDuration[name]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Gives the time left on the first maintained effect whose name ends with the text you give (case ignored). With no text it looks for Painlink.
  arg name (text, default: Painlink): end of the maintained effect's name
  returns: int: seconds remaining on that maintained effect. -1 when none matches.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.ScrollMaintainedDuration[Painlink]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.ScrollOf_Get_MaintainedDuration

${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.ShortName[nameOrId]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Gives the line name of an ability, without its rank: "Assault X" or an Assault id gives "Assault". Reads your loaded export.
  arg nameOrId (ability name or id): the ability to name
  returns: string: the ability line name. Empty when the ability is not found or no export is loaded.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.ShortName["Sprint"]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_AbilityShortName, SpellOb.AbilityName, SpellOb.GetAbilityShortName

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:AbilityDetails[fw, name or id]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Opens the Ability Details window, which shows what your export holds for an ability, and selects the one you name. It also opens at character select.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg name or id (ability name or id): the ability to select; blank selects nothing
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:AbilityDetails[${Me.Name},"Assault"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:SpewAbility

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:AddEmbargo[fw, id, durationSec]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Embargoes an ability: the cast stack skips it for that many seconds while the Enable Ability Embargo setting is ticked. Both the ability and the duration are required (an error is printed otherwise); 0 seconds expires at once.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg id (ability name or id): the ability to embargo
  arg durationSec (number): embargo length in seconds
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:AddEmbargo[all,"Assault",30]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:AbilityEmbargo_AddRotateTimer

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:AnnounceCasted[fw, caster, seconds]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Tells the bot sessions that a caster has put up a cast-while-moving effect: every session (this one too) in the caster's group lets its rotation cast while moving for that many seconds. A blank caster, or seconds that are missing, 0 or less, or not a number, is refused with a console line and nothing is sent.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg caster (player name): who cast the effect (required)
  arg seconds (number): how long the effect lasts, more than 0 (required)
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:AnnounceCasted[all,${Me.Name},30]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CastedCastOnTheMove

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:AnnounceCasting[fw, seconds]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Like AnnounceCasted with you as the caster: every session in your group (this one too) lets its rotation cast while moving for that many seconds. Seconds that are missing, 0 or less, or not a number are refused with a console line and nothing is sent.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg seconds (number): how long the effect lasts, more than 0 (required)
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:AnnounceCasting[${Me.Name},30]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CastingCastOnTheMove

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CancelCasting[fw, except..., -HOAbility, -HOAbilityUI, -CastTime s, -CastAbility ability, -CastAbilityOnPlayer ability player, -CastHOAbilityIconID iconId, -CastAbilityOnNPC ability mob, -UnlessCasting ability]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Cancels the spell you are casting, unless it is one of the abilities you name (any rank) or a guard option says to keep it. -CastAbility, -CastAbilityOnPlayer, -CastAbilityOnNPC and -CastHOAbilityIconID queue that cast first; any other -option cancels nothing (a warning is printed once).
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg except... (ability name or id): abilities never to cancel
  arg -HOAbility (flag): cancel only an ability that has a heroic opportunity icon
  arg -HOAbilityUI (flag): cancel a heroic opportunity ability only when your settings disable it
  arg -CastTime s (flag + number): cancel only when at least s seconds of the cast remain
  arg -CastAbility ability (flag + ability name or id): queue this ability first, then cancel
  arg -CastAbilityOnPlayer ability player (flag + ability + player): queue this ability on that player first, then cancel
  arg -CastHOAbilityIconID iconId (flag + number): queue the ability with this heroic opportunity icon id first, then cancel
  arg -CastAbilityOnNPC ability mob (flag + ability + mob name or id): queue this ability on that mob first, then cancel
  arg -UnlessCasting ability (flag + ability name or id): the same as naming the ability plainly: never cancel it
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CancelCasting[all,-CastTime,0.5,-HOAbilityUI]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CancelCasting

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CancelGroupWaterBreathing[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Cancels your class's group water-breathing maintained buff. Skipped (noted in the log) when your class has none.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CancelGroupWaterBreathing[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CancelGroupWaterBreathing, Obj_OgreIH:CancelGroupWaterBreathing

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CancelInvis[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Breaks invisibility: if you are invisible and Transmute is ready, it casts Transmute and presses Esc half a second later to close its window. Does nothing when you are not invisible or Transmute is not ready.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CancelInvis[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: call OgreBotAPI.CancelInvis

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CancelMaintained[ability...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Cancels each maintained ability you list on this character. It takes no for-who: every argument is an ability name or id, and a short name cancels whichever rank is up.
  arg ability... (ability name or id): maintained abilities to cancel
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CancelMaintained["Sprint"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CancelMaintained

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CancelMaintainedFor[fw, ability...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Cancels each maintained ability you list, on the characters the for-who names. A short name cancels whichever rank is up.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg ability... (ability name or id): maintained abilities to cancel
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CancelMaintainedFor[igw:${Me.Name},"Sprint"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CancelMaintainedForWho

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CancelOnCast[fw, abilityName]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Runs your Cancel On Cast list as if you had just cast this ability: any row that ability triggers cancels its maintained buff, held until combat ends when the row says so.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg abilityName (ability name or id): the ability to treat as just cast
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CancelOnCast[${Me.Name},"Assault"]

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:Cast[fw, ability, calledFrom=OgreBotAPI]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Queues a cast of an ability at your current target; it is asynchronous and goes off when the cast bar is free. Nothing is queued when the ability cannot be found or is not ready.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg ability (ability name or id): the ability to cast
  arg calledFrom (text, default: OgreBotAPI): label shown in the cast debug log
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:Cast[${Me.Name},"Sprint"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CastAbility, call Obj_OgreUtilities.CastAbilityID

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastBulwark[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Casts Bulwark of Order right now: queues it ahead of the rotation, cancels any other cast in progress, and tries again a second later if it has not gone off. If the ability is missing from your export or not ready, it broadcasts a notice (at most every 30 seconds) and does nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastBulwark[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CastBulwarkImmediately

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastGroupWaterBreathing[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Casts your class's group water-breathing ability through :Cast. Skipped (noted in the log) when your class has none or your export does not have it.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastGroupWaterBreathing[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CastGroupWaterBreathing, Obj_OgreIH:CastGroupWaterBreathing

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastHOIcon[fw, iconId, calledFrom=CastHOIcon]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Casts an ability you own that matches a heroic opportunity icon and can be cast now (the same pick as FindCastableHOIconAbilityID), through :Cast. No icon id is refused with a console line; -2, or an icon no ready ability matches, does nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg iconId (number): the heroic opportunity icon id (required); -2 casts nothing
  arg calledFrom (text, default: CastHOIcon): label for the cast log
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastHOIcon[${Me.Name},5]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CastHOIconID

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastInSeconds[fw, ability, delay, calledFrom=OgreBotAPI]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Casts an ability after a delay by running :Cast when the time is up, so the ready check happens then. A bare number is seconds; "500ms" or "2m" style values are also accepted, and a bad delay is reported in the console.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg ability (ability name or id): the ability to cast
  arg delay (number or duration): how long to wait; bare number = seconds
  arg calledFrom (text, default: OgreBotAPI): label for the cast log
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastInSeconds[${Me.Name},"Sprint",5]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CastAbilityInSeconds

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastInterrupt[fw, mobNameOrId="", calledFrom=Cast_Interrupt]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Casts an interrupt at a mob: it picks a non-beneficial interrupt usable on that mob right now and, unless you are already casting an interrupt, cancels your current cast first. With no mob it uses your current NPC target (a name must match exactly); the console says when there is no mob or no interrupt available.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg mobNameOrId (actor name or id, default: ""): the mob to interrupt; blank = current NPC target
  arg calledFrom (text, default: Cast_Interrupt): label for the cast log
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastInterrupt[igw:${Me.Name},${Target.ID}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Cast_Interrupt

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastNoChecks[fw, ability, calledFrom=OgreBotAPI]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Queues a cast of an ability at your current target without checking first that it is ready. The cast is still dropped if the ability is not ready by the time it reaches the cast bar.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg ability (ability name or id): the ability to cast
  arg calledFrom (text, default: OgreBotAPI): label for the cast log
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastNoChecks[${Me.Name},"Sprint",MyScript]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CastAbilityNoChecks

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastNoExport[fw, ability, calledFrom=CastAbilityNoExport]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Queues a cast of an ability at your current target, like :Cast, but checks only that you have the ability and it is off cooldown. Asynchronous: it goes off when the cast bar is free.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg ability (ability name or id): the ability to cast
  arg calledFrom (text, default: CastAbilityNoExport): label for the cast log
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastNoExport[${Me.Name},${OgreBotAPI.Abilities.ID["Sprint"]}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CastAbilityNoExport

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastOnNPC[fw, ability, mob=target]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Targets a mob, waits until it is your target, casts the ability at it and puts your target back. Nothing is cast if the mob is not given or cannot be found, you are dead, or the ability is not ready.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg ability (ability name or id): the ability to cast
  arg mob (actor name or id): the mob to cast on, by name or id; required
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastOnNPC[${Me.Name},"Assault",${Target.ID}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CastAbilityOnNPC

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastOnPlayer[fw, ability, player=me, calledFrom=AbilityExportCastFromUplinkOnPlayer]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Queues a cast of an ability on a named player without changing your target, after checking that it can be cast on them (ready, power, range, line of sight and the rest - the same check as CanCastOn); when it cannot, nothing is cast and the reason goes to the log file. The player can be a name or a role alias such as @Healer1, defaults to you, and must be you or in your group or raid; calledFrom is the label shown in the cast debug log.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg ability (ability name or id): the ability to cast
  arg player (player name or alias, default: me): who to cast it on
  arg calledFrom (text, default: AbilityExportCastFromUplinkOnPlayer): label for the cast log
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastOnPlayer[igw:${Me.Name},"Intercept",${Target.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CastAbilityOnPlayer

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastOnPlayerInSeconds[fw, ability, player, seconds, calledFrom=OgreBotAPI]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Casts an ability on a player after a delay by running :CastOnPlayer when the time is up. A bare number is seconds ("500ms" style values also work); with no player it uses the sending character.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg ability (ability name or id): the ability to cast
  arg player (player name or alias): who to cast it on
  arg seconds (number or duration): how long to wait; bare number = seconds
  arg calledFrom (text, default: OgreBotAPI): label for the cast log
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastOnPlayerInSeconds[${Me.Name},"Intercept",${Target.Name},3]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CastAbilityOnPlayerInSeconds

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastOnPlayerNoChecks[fw, ability, player, calledFrom=OgreBotAPI]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Queues a cast of an ability on a named player without the checks CastOnPlayer makes first (ready, power, range, line of sight); it is still dropped if not ready when it reaches the cast bar. The player defaults to you and must be you or in your group or raid.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg ability (ability name or id): the ability to cast
  arg player (player name or alias): who to cast it on; blank = you
  arg calledFrom (text, default: OgreBotAPI): label for the cast log
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastOnPlayerNoChecks[${Me.Name},"Intercept",${Target.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CastAbilityOnPlayerNoChecks

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastRescue[fw, calledFrom=CastRescue, ...opts]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Casts a rescue: an ability that raises your threat position, or, if you have none, a force-target ability (-NoForceTargets skips that fallback). It checks against your current NPC target unless -TargetID <id> (or -ActorID <id>) names one; other words are added to the ability query.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg calledFrom (text, default: CastRescue): label for the cast log
  arg ...opts (text): -NoForceTargets, -NPCRequired, -TargetID <id> / -ActorID <id>, or extra query terms
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:CastRescue[${Me.Name},MyScript,-NoForceTargets]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CastRescue

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:Clear[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Unloads the ability export. Until you :Load again, Loaded is FALSE and anything that looks an ability up by name finds nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:Clear[${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:ClearAllEmbargos[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Removes every ability embargo. Item embargoes are not touched.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:ClearAllEmbargos[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:AbilityEmbargo_ResetAllAbilityEmbargos

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:ClearEmbargo[fw, ability]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Removes the embargo on one ability. Does nothing when the ability cannot be found or is not embargoed; item embargoes are not touched.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg ability (ability name or id): the ability to release
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:ClearEmbargo[${Me.Name},"Sprint"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:AbilityEmbargo_ResetAbilityEmbargo

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:DispellNPC[fw, mob, op]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Queues a dispel on a mob that runs as soon as your cast bar is free, and each call queues another. Characters with no dispel for the chosen op do nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg mob (actor name or id): the mob to dispel (required)
  arg op (text): how to dispel: any (your class dispel, else a dispel item; the default), ability or spell (class dispel only), item (dispel item only)
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:DispellNPC[igw:${Me.Name},${Target.ID},any]

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:Dump[fw, path]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Writes the loaded ability list (one usable rank per line) to a file as JSON, replacing the file if it exists. Nothing is written when no path is given.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg path (text): file to write the JSON to
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:Dump[${Me.Name},"abilities.json"]

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:FindAndCast[fw, query...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Picks an ability by its properties and casts it: the same query as FindCastableID (terms like "IsInterrupt","=","TRUE" plus options such as -NPCRequired). A refused query is reported in the console; if nothing matches, nothing is cast.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg query... (text): query terms (member, comparison, value) and options
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:FindAndCast["all","IsInterrupt","=","TRUE","-NPCRequired"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CastAbility_Via

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:Load[fw, toon=me, level=myLevel]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Loads a character's ability export and keeps, for each ability line, the highest rank at or below the level, then prints a loaded or failed line to the console. Outside the world you must give both toon and level.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg toon (text, default: me): character whose export to load; left out = your own name (must be given outside the world)
  arg level (number, default: myLevel): highest ability level to keep; left out = your own level (must be given outside the world)
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:Load[${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:Rebuff[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Cancels every maintained buff from your export that lasts until cancelled (links such as Powerlink are kept), so the rotation casts them again fresh. The recast only happens while the bot is casting.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:Rebuff[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Rebuff

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:SetAOEsDisabled[fw, disable=TRUE, -verbose, -allowcounters, -AllowEncounters, -aggressive]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Stops (TRUE) or allows (FALSE) AE casting: it sets the ignore-PBAE, ignore-encounter-nukes and ignore-counter-abilities options, casts Singular Focus (Focus Offensive on a Guardian) and cancels class buffs that proc AEs; FALSE cancels the focus buff instead. -allowcounters keeps counter abilities and counter buffs, -AllowEncounters leaves encounter nukes on while disabling, -verbose announces the setting changes, and -aggressive does nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg disable (true/false, default: TRUE): TRUE stops AEs, FALSE allows them
  arg -verbose (flag): announce the setting changes
  arg -allowcounters (flag): leave counter abilities and counter buffs alone
  arg -AllowEncounters (flag): keep encounter nukes when disabling
  arg -aggressive (flag): accepted, does nothing
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:SetAOEsDisabled[igw:${Me.Name},TRUE,-allowcounters]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Set_DisableAllAOEs

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:SetCancelCurrentCast[fw, on=TRUE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: TRUE asks the bot to abort the cast it has in progress and raises the CancelCurrentCast flag; FALSE lowers the flag and withdraws an abort not yet acted on. The flag clears itself at the next cast start or end.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg on (true/false, default: TRUE): TRUE cancels, FALSE withdraws
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:SetCancelCurrentCast[igw:${Me.Name},TRUE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CancelCurrentCast

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:SetDispellsEnabled[fw, on=TRUE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Turns the bot's dispel casting on or off through the "no dispels" setting. A value that is not a yes/no word changes nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg on (true/false, default: TRUE): TRUE enables dispels, FALSE disables them
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:SetDispellsEnabled[igw:${Me.Name},FALSE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Enable_Dispells, OgreBotAPI:Disable_Dispells

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:SetInterruptsEnabled[fw, on=TRUE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Turns the bot's interrupt casting on or off through the "no interrupts" setting; a value that is not a yes/no word changes nothing. Enabling also turns Daring Advance back on in the cast stack, and disabling on a Rogue turns Daring Advance off and cancels it.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg on (true/false, default: TRUE): TRUE enables interrupts, FALSE disables them
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:SetInterruptsEnabled[igw:${Me.Name},FALSE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Enable_Interrupts, OgreBotAPI:Disable_Interrupts

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:SetStunsEnabled[fw, on=TRUE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Turns the bot's stun casting on or off through the "no stuns" setting; a value that is not a yes/no word changes nothing. Enabling also turns Blessed Weapon back on in the cast stack, and disabling on a Paladin turns Blessed Weapon off and cancels it.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg on (true/false, default: TRUE): TRUE enables stuns, FALSE disables them
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:SetStunsEnabled[igw:${Me.Name},FALSE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Disable_Stuns, OgreBotAPI:Enable_Stuns

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:SetUpForDispells[fw, on=TRUE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Sets the cast stack up for a dispel fight: TRUE turns the Absorb Magic, Tease and Cuss entries on, FALSE turns them back off. Nothing is cancelled either way, and a value that is not a yes/no word changes nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg on (true/false, default: TRUE): TRUE sets up, FALSE resets
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:SetUpForDispells[igw:${Me.Name},TRUE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:SetUpFor_Dispells, OgreBotAPI:ResetFor_Dispells

OgreBotAPI.Abilities:TrackerAdd[fw, ability]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Abilities
  what: Adds an ability to the Ability Tracker watch list in the open profile (an id is stored as its name). The change is not saved until you save the profile; the console says if it is already on the list.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg ability (ability name or id): the ability to watch
  example: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:TrackerAdd[${Me.Name},"Sprint"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:AbilityTracker_Add


== OgreBotAPI.Access ==

${OgreBotAPI.Access.UnauthPCsNearMe[dist]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Access
  what: TRUE when another player character closer to you than dist is not one of the characters saved in your accounts list (EQ2Chars), matched by name ignoring case. Your own character never counts, a nearby player whose name has not loaded counts as not yours, and a dist that is not a number reads as 0, which is always FALSE.
  arg dist (float, default: 999): range from you; a player counts only when strictly closer than this
  returns: bool: TRUE when at least one player character within dist is not one of your saved characters; FALSE when no other player is within dist or every one of them is yours.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Access.UnauthPCsNearMe[200]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.UnauthPCsNearMe

OgreBotAPI.Access:SetLevel[fw, value, silent=FALSE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Access
  what: Sets this session's access level to value at once, clamped between 0 and the highest level your account has; asking for more than that uses your highest level and prints a warning. The new level is announced in the console only when it actually changed, and silent TRUE hides both the warning and the announcement; it also works at the character select screen.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg value (int): the level to set; below 0 becomes 0, above your highest level becomes your highest level, and a value that is not a number counts as 0
  arg silent (bool, default: FALSE): TRUE hides the over-the-maximum warning and the level-changed announcement
  example: OgreBotAPI.Access:SetLevel[${Me.Name},0]


== OgreBotAPI.Actors ==

${OgreBotAPI.Actors.CountByName[name,...]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Actors
  what: Counts the actors around you with this name, an exact match in any case unless -partial is given. Optional flags narrow it by distance and type, and the count is 0 when nothing matches.
  arg name (string): the actor name to count; case does not matter
  arg ... (flags): any of: -partial (or -substring) to count names that contain the text; -distance F to count only actors within F (999 or more means no limit, the default); -Type S to count only actors whose Type is S, any case
  returns: int: how many actors match; 0 when none do.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Actors.CountByName["a gnoll",-partial,-distance,30]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.GetActorCountByName

${OgreBotAPI.Actors.CountByType[type,-distance,distance]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Actors
  what: Counts the actors of one Type (NPC, NamedNPC, PC, Corpse and so on, any case), optionally only those within a distance; the type may be a lone word or follow -Type, and each flag and its value are separate arguments. With no type given it counts Type Special, and PC never counts you, because your own Type is Me.
  arg type (string, default: Special): the actor Type to count, any case; -Type and then the type works the same
  arg -distance (string): the word -distance, when a distance follows it
  arg distance (float, default: 999): count only actors within this distance; 999 or more means no limit
  returns: int: how many actors of that type are in range; 0 when none are.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Actors.CountByType[NPC,-distance,20]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.GetActorCountByType

${OgreBotAPI.Actors.IsPC[actorType]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Actors
  what: Tells you whether an actor Type word means a player character. Pass the actor's Type, not its name or id.
  arg actorType (string): an actor's Type, such as the value of ${Target.Type}
  returns: bool: TRUE when the type is Me or PC (any case); FALSE for anything else.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Actors.IsPC[${Target.Type}]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.IsAPC

${OgreBotAPI.Actors.MobID[name]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Actors
  what: Returns the id of the nearest actor whose name matches exactly, in any case. A number is handed back only when that actor is here, and the usual target words (@ aliases, pet:<owner>, a class word for a group or raid member) are understood too.
  arg name (string): the actor's full name, or an actor id
  returns: int64: the actor id; 0 when no actor matches, the name is blank or that id is not here.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Actors.MobID["a goblin scout"]}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb.ActorToID, GetInfoOb.GetMobID, Obj_OgreIH.Get_NPC_ID

${OgreBotAPI.Actors.NPCsWithin[distance]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Actors
  what: Counts the living NPCs and named NPCs within the distance, aggro or not, measured edge to edge: your own model size and each mob's size widen the reach, as an area spell around you does. A distance of 0 or less counts nothing and prints a console warning.
  arg distance (float): the radius around you, above 0
  returns: int: how many living NPCs and named NPCs are in reach; 0 when none are, when the distance is not above 0, or when the actor list is not ready yet.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Actors.NPCsWithin[10]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.NPCsWithinRange

OgreBotAPI.Actors:ApplyVerb[fw, actor, verb]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Actors
  what: Applies a verb at once to the actor whose id you give, else the nearest one whose name contains the text, or of that type when the text is a type word, using the game's apply_verb command. A blank actor or verb gets one line, and so does an actor that does not match.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg actor (string): the actor's name or part of it, any case, its actor id, or a type word: npc, namednpc, nokillnpc, pc, special, chest, resource, door
  arg verb (string): the verb as it shows on the actor's right-click menu
  example: OgreBotAPI.Actors:ApplyVerb[igw:${Me.Name},"Strange Device","Use"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ApplyVerbForWho, OgreBotAPI:ApplyVerbIDForWho, OgreBotAPI:ApplyVerb

OgreBotAPI.Actors:ApplyVerbQueued[fw, actor, verb, waitDs=40]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Actors
  what: Queues a verb on the actor whose id you give, else the nearest one whose name contains the text, or of that type when the text is a type word, then waits out the cast it starts, exactly as ApplyVerbIDQueued does. The actor is looked up when you call it; a blank actor or verb, or no match, gets one line and queues nothing, and one gone by its turn is dropped with a console line.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg actor (string): the actor's name or part of it, any case, its actor id, or a type word: npc, namednpc, nokillnpc, pc, special, chest, resource, door
  arg verb (string): the verb as it shows on the actor's right-click menu
  arg waitDs (int, default: 40): the longest wait for the cast to end, in tenths of a second
  example: OgreBotAPI.Actors:ApplyVerbQueued[igw:${Me.Name},"Strange Device","Use"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ApplyVerbIDQueuedForWho, OgreBotAPI:ApplyVerbQueuedForWho

OgreBotAPI.Actors:Click[fw, nameOrId, ...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Actors
  what: Double-clicks an actor at once: an id as given, or else the nearest interactable actor whose name contains the text (or matches it exactly when the third argument is TRUE). Nothing happens, with no message, when no actor is found.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg nameOrId (string): an actor id, or a name to search for among interactable actors
  arg ... (bool): exact: TRUE matches the whole name (any case) instead of any name containing it; default FALSE
  example: OgreBotAPI.Actors:Click[${Me.Name},"Strange Lever"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Actor_Click, call Obj_OgreUtilities.HandleClickActor

OgreBotAPI.Actors:ClickQueued[fw, nameOrId, ...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Actors
  what: Queues a double-click on an actor found the same way as Click, then waits out the cast the click starts. At its turn it waits up to 5 seconds for a free cast bar, clicks once, and holds the cast bar until that cast ends or the wait runs out; an actor gone by then is dropped with a console line.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg nameOrId (string): an actor id, or a name to search for among interactable actors
  arg ... (bool, int): exact, then waitDs: exact TRUE matches the whole name instead of any name containing it (default FALSE); waitDs is the longest wait for the cast to end, in tenths of a second (default 40)
  example: OgreBotAPI.Actors:ClickQueued[${Me.Name},"Ancient Altar",FALSE,60]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Actor_ClickQueued, OgreBotAPI:AltarOfTheAncients, OgreBotAPI:TargetAndDoubleClickActor

OgreBotAPI.Actors:Hail[fw, nameOrId]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Actors
  what: Queues a hail: target the actor, face it, then hail, about 0.3 seconds apart, and the hail is abandoned if the target does not change to that actor within 1 second. A blank or 0 hails the nearest nokill NPC within 10 (nothing happens when there is none); a name that finds nobody, or an id that is not here, says so on the console and hails nobody.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg nameOrId (string): an actor id, a name (any actor whose name contains it, nearest first), an @ alias or pet:<owner>; blank or 0 uses the nokill NPC fallback
  example: OgreBotAPI.Actors:Hail[${Me.Name},${Target.ID}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:HailNPC, call Obj_OgreUtilities.DoHail, call Obj_OgreUtilities.DoHailID

OgreBotAPI.Actors:SetCastMonitoring[fw, -watch "<mob>" ..., -unwatch "<mob>, -clear, -radius N]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Actors
  what: Adds or removes the mob names this script asks NPC cast monitoring to watch, or sets the scan radius, for this zone; -watch and -radius also tick NPC Cast Monitoring, and watched mobs in range raise OgreEvent_CastMonitoring_CastingStarted and OgreEvent_CastMonitoring_CastingEnded. Flags run in the order written with one console line each, watches added by the zone or an encounter are never touched, and one bad flag refuses the whole call.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg -watch "<mob>" ... (string): -watch followed by a mob name to watch, matched as a whole name in any case; repeat the pair for more mobs; it ends at the next zone or when NPC Cast Monitoring is unticked, and the tick stays
  arg -unwatch "<mob> (string): -unwatch followed by a mob name to stop watching (only a watch a script added)
  arg -clear (flag): drops every watch scripts added
  arg -radius N (int): -radius followed by the scan radius, a whole number from 5 to 500 (default 50); it beats the zone's own radius and ends at the next zone or when NPC Cast Monitoring is unticked
  example: OgreBotAPI.Actors:SetCastMonitoring[${Me.Name},-watch,"a ravenous gnoll",-radius,60]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:NPC_CastMonitoring


== OgreBotAPI.Assist ==

${OgreBotAPI.Assist.InControl}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Assist
  what: Whether this character picks its own target instead of following someone else's. With the Auto Assist box off nobody drives this character, so it reads TRUE.
  returns: bool: TRUE when auto-target is on, the Auto Assist box is off, you are the assist anchor, or no assist rule names anyone to follow; FALSE when you follow another player, and FALSE when not in the world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Assist.InControl}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.InControlOfAssisting

${OgreBotAPI.Assist.IsAssisting}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Assist
  what: The exact opposite of InControl: whether this character follows someone else's target. It reads FALSE whenever the Auto Assist box is off.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the Auto Assist box is on and you follow another player's target; FALSE when you pick your own target, and FALSE when not in the world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Assist.IsAssisting}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb.IsAssisting, OgreBotAPI.IsAssisting

${OgreBotAPI.Assist.TargetID}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Assist
  what: The assist decision as one number: who this character would take its target from right now. It is read fresh on each call and reports the decision even when the Auto Assist box is off or auto-target is on.
  returns: int64: greater than 0 is the ID to target (with Direct Assist Targeting on, the assisted player's target; otherwise the assisted player, which is your own ID when you are the anchor); 0 when you pick your own target; -1 when your current target should be left alone (Direct Assist Targeting on and the player you assist has no live target); NULL when not in the world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Assist.TargetID}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.GetAssistID

OgreBotAPI.Assist:Anchor[fw, who=me]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Assist
  what: Sets who this character takes its kill target from: a group or raid member's name or alias, an actor ID, blank for yourself, or off to clear it (the literal word me is looked up as a name and sets nothing). It does not target anything itself - the bot retargets on its pulse while Auto Assist is ticked, a name not in your group or raid sets nothing and says so in the console, and the anchor clears when you zone into a different zone.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg who (string, default: me): The player to assist: a name, an alias, an actor ID, or off to clear the anchor; blank anchors on yourself
  example: OgreBotAPI.Assist:Anchor[igw:${Me.Name},${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:AssistForWho, OgreBotAPI:Assist


== OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt ==

${OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt.Active}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt
  what: TRUE when AutoHunt is switched on in Hunt mode. It reflects the mode only, so it stays TRUE while the hunt sits idle because OgreBot is closed or the bot is paused.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the mode is Hunt; FALSE when it is Off.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt.Active}

${OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt.AllowMovement}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt
  what: TRUE when AutoHunt is letting this character move: a camp spot pulls again and the path picked on the Auto-Hunt tab walks on. It is FALSE while it holds position because a safety check tripped or a mob or an add is being dealt with, and TRUE while the character flies, since AutoHunt holds nothing in the air; it is updated on each hunt tick, and it reads FALSE after the mode is set to Off.
  returns: bool: TRUE when AutoHunt has released its hold on movement; FALSE when it is holding position or AutoHunt is Off.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt.AllowMovement}

${OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt.FreezeReason}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt
  what: Which safety check stopped the hunt on its last tick, or None when it was safe or the character was flying (the checks are not read in the air). It is not cleared when the mode is set to Off, so it can still show the last reason after AutoHunt is turned off.
  returns: string: None, Aggro, Dead, LowHP, LowMana or ExquisiteChest. Only the first check that tripped is named, and a group or raid member who is not in the zone counts as Dead or LowHP when those checks are on.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt.FreezeReason}

${OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt.LastAction}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt
  what: What AutoHunt decided to do on its last tick. It reads None after the mode is set to Off and keeps the last value while the hunt sits idle.
  returns: string: None, Walk, HoldPosition, MoveGroupToCamp, Prebuff, AcquireTarget, Pull or Cleanup. Walk means no mob is in reach, or the character is flying and AutoHunt pulls nothing in the air, so the character may walk on. None while the character is dead: AutoHunt holds as it stands.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt.LastAction}

${OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt.Mode}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt
  what: The AutoHunt mode this character is in: Off or Hunt. It starts as Off when the extension loads and is not saved, and it still reads Hunt while the hunt sits idle because OgreBot is closed or the bot is paused.
  returns: string: Off or Hunt.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt.Mode}

${OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt.PullTargetID}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt
  what: The actor ID of the mob the last Hunt tick picked to pull, or 0 when none was found in the scan radius or the character is flying (no pull in the air); a different answer counts only after it has held for 0.3 seconds. It is 0 after the mode is set to Off, and an add already attacking the group is handled first but is not shown here.
  returns: int64: the actor ID picked to pull on the last tick; 0 when there was none.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt.PullTargetID}

${OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt.SafetyTripped}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.AutoHunt
  what: TRUE when one of the AutoHunt safety checks (aggro, dead, low health, low power, exquisite chest) stopped the hunt on its last tick. It keeps the last tick's value while the hunt sits idle and reads FALSE after the mode is set to Off.
