  returns: bool: TRUE when SetNoReqBowAbilities turned the flag on; FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Combat.NoReqBowAbilities}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.CheckNoReqBowAbilities, OgreBotAPI.bNoReqBowAbilities

${OgreBotAPI.Combat.Zoning}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Combat
  what: TRUE while a zone change is in progress, including the short wait after arriving before the character is settled. FALSE once you are in a zone and settled.
  returns: bool: TRUE while zoning or not yet settled after a zone; FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Combat.Zoning}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Zoning

OgreBotAPI.Combat:AddNoOffensive[fw, mobName, exactOnly=TRUE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Combat
  what: Adds a mob name to the no-offensive list: while your current NPC target matches an entry, NoOffensive is TRUE and the bot holds off offensive abilities and auto-attack. Matching ignores case, adding a name already listed replaces its exactOnly setting, and the list is kept until ClearNoOffensive, LetsGo or the bot closing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg mobName (string): The mob name to add. A blank name is ignored.
  arg exactOnly (bool, default: TRUE): TRUE matches the whole name only; FALSE matches any target whose name contains mobName.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Combat:AddNoOffensive[all,"a shield of Yothshaval",TRUE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:AddNoOffensiveOn

OgreBotAPI.Combat:ClearNoOffensive[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Combat
  what: Empties the no-offensive list built by AddNoOffensive. Reasons set with SetNoOffensive are not touched.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Combat:ClearNoOffensive[all]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ClearNoOffensiveOn

OgreBotAPI.Combat:Countdown[fw, seconds=10]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Combat
  what: When this character is grouped and is the group leader, runs the game's countdown for the given seconds; on anyone else it does nothing. A number below 1 counts down from 1 and one over 30 from 30, with a console line saying so.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg seconds (int, default: 10): Seconds to count down, 1 to 30. A word that is not a number reads as 0, so it counts down from 1. The -countdown console row passes 1 when its time is left blank.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Combat:Countdown[igw:${Me.Name},5]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Countdown

OgreBotAPI.Combat:RemoveNoOffensive[fw,mobName]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Combat
  what: Takes a mob name off the no-offensive list that Combat:AddNoOffensive adds to; the name is matched ignoring case. A name not on the list changes nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg mobName (string): The mob name to take off the list. A blank name is ignored.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Combat:RemoveNoOffensive[all,"a shield of Yothshaval"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:RemoveNoOffensiveOn

OgreBotAPI.Combat:SetNoDefensive[fw, on=TRUE, reason=""]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Combat
  what: Turns no-defensive on or off by reason: on adds the reason (manual when blank), off with a reason removes just that one, and off with no reason clears them all. While any reason is held the bot skips defensive abilities; LetsGo and reopening the bot clear every reason.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg on (bool, default: TRUE): TRUE adds the reason; FALSE removes it, or every reason when reason is blank. A word that is not yes or no changes nothing.
  arg reason (string, default: ""): A name for why it is on, so several callers can hold it at once. Blank means manual when adding and every reason when removing.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Combat:SetNoDefensive[igw:${Me.Name},FALSE,"tank swap"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:SetNoDefensive

OgreBotAPI.Combat:SetNoOffensive[fw, on=TRUE, reason=""]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Combat
  what: Turns no-offensive on or off by reason: on adds the reason (manual when blank), off with a reason removes just that one, and off with no reason clears them all. While any reason is held the bot skips offensive abilities and turns auto-attack off; LetsGo and reopening the bot clear every reason.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg on (bool, default: TRUE): TRUE adds the reason; FALSE removes it, or every reason when reason is blank. A word that is not yes or no changes nothing.
  arg reason (string, default: ""): A name for why it is on, so several callers can hold it at once. Blank means manual when adding and every reason when removing.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Combat:SetNoOffensive[igw:${Me.Name},TRUE,"tank swap"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:SetNoOffensive

OgreBotAPI.Combat:SetNoReqBowAbilities[fw, on=TRUE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Combat
  what: Sets the flag NoReqBowAbilities reports, and needs the character in the world. While it is on the cast stack skips abilities that need a bow; LetsGo and closing the bot turn it off.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg on (bool, default: TRUE): TRUE turns the flag on; FALSE turns it off. A word that is not yes or no leaves it as it is.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Combat:SetNoReqBowAbilities[${Me.Name},FALSE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:SetNoReqBowAbilities

OgreBotAPI.Combat:ThreatIgnoreAdd[fw, name...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Combat
  what: Adds fighter names to the threat ignore list: a fighter on it holding aggro does not count as a fighter already tanking, so your taunts and threat abilities are still used. Matching ignores case, blank and NULL names are skipped, and the list is cleared when the bot is opened or closed.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg name... (string): One or more fighters' character names to add.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Combat:ThreatIgnoreAdd[igw:${Me.Name},${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ThreatFighterIgnoreList_Add

OgreBotAPI.Combat:ThreatIgnoreClear[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Combat
  what: Empties the threat ignore list. Needs the character in the world.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Combat:ThreatIgnoreClear[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ThreatFighterIgnoreList_Clear

OgreBotAPI.Combat:ThreatIgnoreList[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Combat
  what: Prints the threat ignore list to the console: a ThreatFighterIgnoreList -- Start -- line, then one name per line. There is no end line, and the character must be in the world.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Combat:ThreatIgnoreList[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.ThreatFighterIgnoreList, OgreBotAPI:ThreatFighterIgnoreList_List

OgreBotAPI.Combat:ThreatIgnoreRemove[fw, name...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Combat
  what: Removes each named fighter from the threat ignore list, in any case. A name that is not on the list is ignored, and the character must be in the world.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg name... (string): One or more character names to remove.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Combat:ThreatIgnoreRemove[igw:${Me.Name},${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ThreatFighterIgnoreList_Remove


== OgreBotAPI.Comms ==

${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Dispatched}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: How many received events at least one of the bot's own handlers acted on. Events no handler wants, and events dropped by for-who, are not counted.
  returns: int64: events handled
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Dispatched}

${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Errors}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: How many received events were thrown away as unreadable: bad base64, bad JSON, not an event, a newer envelope version, no name, or a name unfit for a script event. For-who drops and a full inbox are not counted here.
  returns: int64: unreadable events
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Errors}

${OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery[fw,question...]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: With arguments, starts a groupQuery on this session and returns it - every read of this form asks again; with no arguments it is the handle whose .Last, .Done[id] and .Result[id] read queries. Answers come over this PC's relay group only, so group or raid members on other PCs show as missing, and a bad question prints a groupQuery error.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg question... (string): one JSON object, or -key,value pairs: -question (itemCount, abilityReady, slotResolve or LavishScript["${...}"]), -item, -ability or -slot, -compare with -value, -sendTo (default igw:<me>), -limitMs (default 3000), -askAgainIfBlank
  returns: groupquery object: its text is the new query id (read .Done and .Result on it); NULL when the for-who does not name this character or the question is refused. With no arguments: the handle with .Last, .Done[id], .Result[id]
  returns object: OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery (its members and methods are listed under it)
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery[all,-question,itemCount,-item,"Mechanized Platinum Repository of Reconstruction"]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Ask, OgreBotAPI.Ask_AllFalse, OgreBotAPI.Ask_AllTrue

${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Query_Active[id]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: TRUE while a query is still collecting replies, before its timeout. An empty id reads the last query (Query_Last); an unknown or cleared id reads FALSE.
  arg id (string): the query id from Query_Last; empty = the last query
  returns: bool: TRUE while the query is collecting replies; FALSE once it is done, or for an unknown id
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Query_Active[${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Query_Last}]}

${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Query_Count[id]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: How many characters have replied to a query; an unknown id reads 0. Only in-world sessions on this PC answer, and this session answers its own question.
  arg id (string): the query id from Query_Last; empty = the last query
  returns: int: replies so far (final once Query_Done); 0 for an unknown id
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Query_Count[${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Query_Last}]}

${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Query_Done[id]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: TRUE once a query's timeout has passed and its tally is final. The tally stays readable for 60 seconds after that, then the query is forgotten and this reads FALSE again.
  arg id (string): the query id from Query_Last; empty = the last query
  returns: bool: TRUE when the query has finished; FALSE while it runs, after it is forgotten, or for an unknown id
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Query_Done[${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Query_Last}]}

${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Query_Json[id]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Every reply to a query as one JSON object of responder name to raw answer: the item count, seconds until the ability is ready, the equipped item name, or the expression's text. An empty id reads the last query.
  arg id (string): the query id from Query_Last; empty = the last query
  returns: string: JSON such as {"Name1":"5","Name2":"0"}; {} when nobody replied or the id is unknown
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Query_Json[${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Query_Last}]}

${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Query_Last}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: The id of the last query this session started with Comms:Query; the bot's own group, loot and quest questions do not change it, and a refused :Query leaves the previous id in place.
  returns: string: the query id; empty before any query started
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Query_Last}

${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Query_TrueCount[id]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: How many replies to a query answered TRUE: has the item, ability ready, slot filled, or the expression read true. An empty id reads the last query; an unknown id reads 0.
  arg id (string): the query id from Query_Last; empty = the last query
  returns: int: TRUE replies so far; 0 for an unknown id
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Query_TrueCount[${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Query_Last}]}

${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Queued}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: How many received events are waiting to be handled right now. They are handled on the next pulse, so this is normally 0.
  returns: int64: events waiting
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Queued}

${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Received}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: How many events this session has received from its relay group since it loaded or since the last ResetStats, counting its own events and events its for-who then dropped. It stays 0 when the uplink's OgreConsoleHub is not loaded, because then nothing comes back.
  returns: int64: events received
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Received}

${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Stats}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: This session's comms counters as one line: received, queued, handled, dropped by for-who, sent, and errors by kind. It is a local read that sends nothing, and echo ${OgreBotAPI.Comms} prints the same line.
  returns: string: the counter line, e.g. recv=12 q=0 proc=12 disp=10 nosub=2 refired=12 cfwdrop=0 emit=5 err[b64=0 json=0 type=0 ver=0 name=0 refname=0] of=0 tid[recv=... pulse=...]
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.Stats}

${OgreBotAPI.Comms.UplinkName}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Inner Space's uplink name for this PC, read from ${InnerSpace.Uplink}. A local read; every session on the PC reads the same text.
  returns: string: the value of ${InnerSpace.Uplink}
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.UplinkName}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb.UplinkName, OgreBotAPI.UplinkName

OgreBotAPI.Comms:AddAnnounce[fw, ability, to, text]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Adds a row to this character's Announce tab and saves it in the loaded profile like a panel edit; from then on, casting the ability sends text to the to place (group or raid chat, a tell to the target, a game command, or a console command). An unknown ability or place, empty text, a duplicate row or no loaded profile is refused with a console line, and nothing announces while the Announce tab is switched off.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg ability (string): the ability's name (any rank) or id, from this character's ability export
  arg to (string): where to announce: Group, Raid, Tell To Target, In-Game Command or Execute In Console (any case)
  arg text (string): the announce text; everything after to is joined back with commas, so it need not be quoted
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:AddAnnounce[${Me.Name},Rescue,Group,"Rescue on *Target*"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Announce_AddEntry

OgreBotAPI.Comms:Broadcast[fw, text, -tab name..., -sound ding|alarm]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Sends the text to every session in this PC's relay group, this one included; each shows "[Notify] <sender>: <text>" in its OgreConsole (and the -tab tab) and plays the -sound. fw picks which sessions send, not who receives; it never leaves the PC, and with no OgreConsoleHub in the uplink nobody shows it, not even this session.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg text (string): the line to show; commas in it are kept
  arg -tab name... (string): followed by an OgreConsole tab name - each receiver also puts the line in that tab; may be repeated
  arg -sound ding|alarm (string): followed by ding or alarm - each receiver plays that sound; a bare -sound is ding
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:Broadcast[${Me.Name},"Named is up",-sound,alarm]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Message_Relay

OgreBotAPI.Comms:ConversationBubble[fw, num=1]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Clicks reply number num in the NPC conversation window open on this session; needs a character in the world. When no conversation is open or it has no such reply nothing is clicked, and only the log file says so.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg num (int, default: 1): which reply to click, counting from 1 as SpewConversationBubbles numbers them
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:ConversationBubble[igw:${Me.Name},2]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ConversationBubble, OgreBotAPI:OptNum, call Obj_OgreUtilities.DoConversation

OgreBotAPI.Comms:Emit[fw, name, cfw="", dest="", ev=1, dataJson=""]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Sends a named event to every session in this session's relay group on this PC, this one included; each session whose for-who matches cfw runs its handlers and fires the script event OgreComms_<name> with the event JSON. It never leaves the PC and needs OgreConsoleHub in the uplink - without it nothing arrives anywhere and, a few seconds on, a "comms egress is BLIND" warning prints; an empty name gets a refusal line and invalid dataJson is refused (log file only).
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg name (string): the event name (required); letters, digits and _ up to 64 characters, or no OgreComms_ script event fires
  arg cfw (string, default: ""): for-who checked by each receiving session; empty = every session. A session not in the world (login screen, character select, zoning) takes in only what needs no game - messages, tag changes, group and key-bind updates - and throws momentary requests (casts, script events) away; a changed MCP file is kept once and read when it reaches the world; the OgreComms_ script event fires only in the world
  arg dest (string, default: ""): the relay group to deliver to; empty = this session's relay group (Relay Groups tab)
  arg ev (int, default: 1): the data version number stamped on the event
  arg dataJson (string, default: ""): a JSON value carried as the event's data; must be valid JSON
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:Emit[${Me.Name},MyEvent]

OgreBotAPI.Comms:ExecuteEvent[fw, name, ...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Runs Event["name"]:Execute[...] on this session with the remaining arguments joined by commas, as written (not quoted). Local only - nothing is sent; needs a character in the world.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg name (string): the LavishScript event to fire
  arg ... (string): arguments passed to the event, in order
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:ExecuteEvent[${Me.Name},MyScript_Pull,${Target.ID}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ExecuteEvent_JSON, OgreBotAPI:ExecuteEvent

OgreBotAPI.Comms:GroupQuery[fw, question...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Starts a groupQuery: asks group or raid members a question and judges the answers; read the id from ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery.Last} and the result JSON from .Result[id], which also fires OgreEvent_GroupQueryDone. Answers come over this PC's relay group only, so members on other PCs show as missing, and a bad question prints a groupQuery error to the console.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg question... (string): one JSON object, or -key,value pairs: -question (itemCount, abilityReady, slotResolve or LavishScript["${...}"]), -item, -ability or -slot, -compare with -value, -sendTo (default igw:<me>), -limitMs (default 3000), -askAgainIfBlank
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:GroupQuery[${Me.Name},-question,abilityReady,-ability,Rescue,-sendTo,igw:${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Comms:Ingest[fw, wire]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Hands a base64 event envelope to this session's comms receiver as if it had arrived from the relay group; it is handled on the next pulse. Nothing is sent anywhere, and unreadable input only adds to Errors.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg wire (string): the base64-encoded event envelope JSON
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:Ingest[${Me.Name},eyJ2IjoxLCJmcm9tIjoiaXMxIiwiZGVzdGluYXRpb24iOiJvZ3JlX2V2ZXJxdWVzdDIiLCJ0eXBlIjoiZXZlbnQiLCJhcmdzIjp7Im5hbWUiOiJNeUV2ZW50IiwiZXYiOjF9fQ==]

OgreBotAPI.Comms:InjectChat[fw, chat=Nothing]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Feeds the text into this session's own chat handling as a raid-chat line from the bot's built-in speaker OgreIRCSession, on the next pulse, so chat triggers and chat commands act on it. Nothing is said in game or sent anywhere; needs a character in the world.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg chat (string, default: Nothing): the chat text to inject
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:InjectChat[${Me.Name},"burn now"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:InjectChat

OgreBotAPI.Comms:IrcAuthIfInRaid[nick, toon]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: If toon is in this character's raid, tells this PC's IRC bridge to accept commands from the IRC nick nick, marked as learned through the raid so IrcRaidUnauth can take it back. There is no for-who - every in-world session checks and prints a line saying whether toon is in its raid; nothing happens if the IRC bridge is not loaded in the uplink.
  arg nick (string): the IRC nick to accept, as written
  arg toon (string): the character whose raid membership decides it
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:IrcAuthIfInRaid[${Me.Name}_IRC,${Group[1].Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:OgreIRC_AuthIfInRaid

OgreBotAPI.Comms:IrcConnect[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Loads the IRC bridge (OgreIRCHub) in this PC's uplink if it is not loaded and connects it to IRC with the saved settings; already connected = no change. It prints "irc: connecting" either way, and if the settings file cannot be read the bridge says so and does not connect.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:IrcConnect[${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Comms:IrcDisconnect[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Asks this PC's IRC bridge to disconnect from IRC; the bridge stays loaded and idle. It prints "irc: asking the uplink OgreIRCHub to disconnect (it stays loaded)." and the bridge reports the result on the uplink.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:IrcDisconnect[${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Comms:IrcRaidAuth[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Asks, over IRC, every IRC bridge whose PC has a character in this raid to accept commands from each other's nicks; characters outside the raid take no part. Needs a character in a raid and IRC connected - otherwise it prints why and asks nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:IrcRaidAuth[${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Comms:IrcRaidCheck[fw, ask, toon]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Answers this PC's IRC bridge: if toon is in this character's raid, it reports this character's name back for question number ask. It says nothing when toon is not in the raid, when ask is not all digits, or out of the world; the bridge calls this itself.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg ask (int): the bridge's question number (digits only)
  arg toon (string): the character that asked; must be a plain name
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:IrcRaidCheck[all,12,${Group[1].Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Comms:IrcRaidUnauth[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Asks, over IRC, every IRC bridge in this raid to drop the nicks it accepted through the raid; nicks accepted any other way stay. Needs a character in a raid and IRC connected - otherwise it prints why and asks nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:IrcRaidUnauth[${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Comms:IrcReload[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Makes this PC's IRC bridge re-read its settings and reconnect with them, but only if it is connected - an idle bridge stays idle. It prints "irc: reloading the uplink hub config."; a settings file that does not read is only written to the bridge's log.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:IrcReload[${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Comms:LogStats[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Prints the Stats counter line to this session's console and writes it to the log file. Local only.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:LogStats[all]

OgreBotAPI.Comms:Message[fw, text, -tab name..., -sound ding|alarm]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Prints "[Message] <text>" in this session's OgreConsole (the Inner Space console when OgreConsole is not available); nothing goes to other sessions, IRC or game chat. -tab also puts it in that OgreConsole tab and -sound plays the sound here; an unknown sound name warns and plays nothing, and an empty text does nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg text (string): the line to show; commas in it are kept
  arg -tab name... (string): followed by an OgreConsole tab name - the line also lands in that tab; may be repeated
  arg -sound ding|alarm (string): followed by ding or alarm - plays that sound with the line; a bare -sound is ding
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:Message[${Me.Name},"Pull in 10 seconds",-sound,ding]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Message, OgreBotAPI:Message_NT

OgreBotAPI.Comms:Pushover[fw, message..., -title t, -priority n]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Sends a push notification through the Pushover service from this session; every word that is not a flag becomes the message. Not configured (no app token or user key), switched off in the profile, or no message = nothing sent and a warning, and -sound, -device, -retry and -expire are accepted but ignored.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg message... (string): the notification text; unflagged words are joined with spaces
  arg -title t (string): followed by the notification title
  arg -priority n (int, default: 0): followed by a Pushover priority, -2 to 2
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:Pushover[${Me.Name},"Raid wiped",-title,EQ2,-priority,1]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Pushover, Obj_Pushover.PushoverSendMsg, Obj_Pushover

OgreBotAPI.Comms:Query[fw, kind, cfw="", timeoutMs=0, paramsJson=""]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Asks every in-world session in this PC's relay group a typed question and tallies the replies; read the new id from Query_Last, then Query_Count, Query_TrueCount and Query_Json once Query_Done. Sessions on other PCs never answer (it does not use IRC), with no OgreConsoleHub in the uplink nobody answers, not even this session, and an unknown kind or one of the bot's own (lootBid, questSteps) is refused (log file only).
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg kind (string): the question: itemCount, abilityReady, slotResolve or eval (required)
  arg cfw (string, default: ""): for-who checked by each session before it answers; empty = every session
  arg timeoutMs (int, default: 0): how long to collect replies in milliseconds; 0 or less = 3000, capped at 60000
  arg paramsJson (string, default: ""): the question's JSON: itemCount {"item":"name"}, abilityReady {"ability":"name or id"}, slotResolve {"slot":"slot name or number"}, eval {"expr":"a LavishScript expression"}; missing or wrong = nobody answers
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:Query[${Me.Name},itemCount,all,5000,{"item":"Mechanized Platinum Repository of Reconstruction"}]

OgreBotAPI.Comms:Query_Clear[fw, id=""]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Forgets a query and its tally on this session; its Query_* reads go back to FALSE, 0 and {}. Leave id empty for the last Comms:Query - an unknown id does nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg id (string, default: ""): the query id to forget; empty = the last query (the word last itself is not recognised)
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:Query_Clear[${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Comms:ReportVersion[fw, compareTo]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Says this character's bot version in IRC: "VERSION: <name> (<version>)" when compareTo is empty, else "SAME: <name> (<version>)" or "DIFFERENT: <name> - Mine: <version> Requested: <compareTo>". Needs a character in the world; while IRC is not connected the IRC bridge holds the line and sends it once it connects.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg compareTo (string): the version to compare against; empty = just report the version
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:ReportVersion[all,""]

OgreBotAPI.Comms:ResetStats[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Zeroes this session's comms counters (Stats, Received, Dispatched, Errors) and restarts the silent-hub warning's clock. Local only; prints nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:ResetStats[all]

OgreBotAPI.Comms:SendTell[fw, target, message]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Sends an in-game /tell from this character to target, in game chat; needs a character in the world. If target or message contains NULL the tell is not sent and an "Unable to send" line goes to IRC instead (the IRC bridge holds it until IRC connects).
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg target (string): the character to send the tell to
  arg message (string): the tell's text; commas in it are kept
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:SendTell[${Me.Name},${Group[1].Name},"Ready when you are"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Send_Tell

OgreBotAPI.Comms:SpewConversationBubbles[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Prints the replies the open NPC conversation window offers to this session's console, numbered the way ConversationBubble clicks them. With no conversation open it prints "no conversation window open."
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:SpewConversationBubbles[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ConversationBubbleSpew

OgreBotAPI.Comms:SpewRelayGroup[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Sends "<name>: OgreRelayGroup: <group>" to every session in this PC's relay group, naming the relay group this session uses now. Same path as Broadcast - nobody shows it without OgreConsoleHub in the uplink - and it needs a character in the world.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:SpewRelayGroup[all]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Spew_RelayGroup

OgreBotAPI.Comms:TTS[fw, text]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Comms
  what: Speaks the text aloud on this PC through Inner Space (uplink speak). An empty for-who means is1, not all, so by default only session is1 speaks; empty text does nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg text (string): the words to speak
  example: OgreBotAPI.Comms:TTS[${Me.Name},"Tank is low"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:TTS


== OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery ==

${OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery.Done[id]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery
  what: Whether a group query has finished. With no id it reads the query this object was started as, else the last one; an id from another session matches nothing.
  arg id (string): The query id from Last (like gq:is1:4); blank reads the bound or last query
  returns: bool: TRUE once the query has finished; FALSE while it runs, for an id this session did not start, and again 60 seconds after it finished, when the result is dropped.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery.Done[${OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery.Last}]}

${OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery.Last}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery
  what: The id of the last group query this session started, from ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery[fw,...]} or OgreBotAPI.Comms:GroupQuery. Pass it to Done and Result to read that query.
  returns: string: the id, like gq:is1:4; "" when this session has not started one.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery.Last}

${OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery.Result[id]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery
  what: The result of a finished group query, as JSON. With no id it reads the query this object was started as, else the last one; the result stays readable for 60 seconds after the query finishes.
  arg id (string): The query id from Last (like gq:is1:4); blank reads the bound or last query
  returns: string: the result JSON once finished; "" while it runs, for an id this session did not start, and after the 60 seconds are up.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery.Result[${OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery.Last}]}


== OgreBotAPI.Consumables ==

OgreBotAPI.Consumables:AddMercenaries[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Consumables
  what: Queues, for every item in your bags, Overseer bag and harvest bag whose name contains "Mercenary: ", an examine that answers the "What would you like to do?" dialog with its first choice and closes the examine window. It echoes how many it is adding, or that there are none.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Consumables:AddMercenaries[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Mercenary_AddMercenaries

OgreBotAPI.Consumables:CheckFamiliar[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Consumables
  what: Summons your familiar at once with summon_familiar, unless your Summon Familiar buff is already maintained. After a summon it ignores further calls for 2 seconds.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Consumables:CheckFamiliar[all]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Check_Familiar

OgreBotAPI.Consumables:CheckMercenaryTraining[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Consumables
  what: Queues a check that resumes your mercenary if needed, opens Persona on the Mercenary tab and starts training when the button is enabled (it reports training already running or max level instead), then closes Persona, and suspends the mercenary again only when this check summoned it. It refuses in a full group of 6, reports every step to the console, and a new call replaces an earlier one.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Consumables:CheckMercenaryTraining[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CheckMercenaryTraining

OgreBotAPI.Consumables:CheckMountTraining[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Consumables
  what: Queues a check that opens Persona on the Mounts tab and starts training your current mount when the Start Training button is showing, answering the confirm popup (it declines when the popup says training will be carried over from another mount), then closes Persona. You must be on a mount that is not a flight transport or it stops with a console line, and a new call replaces an earlier one.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Consumables:CheckMountTraining[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CheckMountTraining

OgreBotAPI.Consumables:CoV[fw, travel=Teleport, toon, allowSameZone=FALSE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Consumables
  what: Uses Call of the Veteran to bring up the veteran reward porter (or uses one already within 15, or a selection window already open), then picks the travel option and the named group or raid member in its two popups. It is skipped with a console line when you are in combat, name yourself, the member is not in your group (raid when you are in one), the member is already in your zone without allowSameZone, or there is no porter, no open window and the item is not ready.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg travel (string, default: Teleport): the option to pick in the first popup, matched by its label in any case; the default takes you to the member, Summon brings the member to you
  arg toon (string): the group or raid member to pick in the second popup, by full name; blank echoes that no toon was named and does nothing
  arg allowSameZone (bool, default: FALSE): TRUE goes ahead even when the member is already in your zone; FALSE skips that case
  example: OgreBotAPI.Consumables:CoV[${Me.Name},Summon,${Group[1].Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CoV

OgreBotAPI.Consumables:DrinkAlcohol[fw, item]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Consumables
  what: Drinks the named item from your bags at once, using the game's drink_alcohol command on it. With no item named it says so on the console, and so does an item that is not in your bags.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg item (string, default: ""): the item's full name (case does not matter); it must be in your bags, not the bank; required
  example: OgreBotAPI.Consumables:DrinkAlcohol[${Me.Name},"Flask of Ale"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Drink_Alcohol

OgreBotAPI.Consumables:MountDown[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Consumables
  what: Queues a forced dismount: sit, toggle summon_mount once, then stand, about 3 seconds in all. It does nothing if you are moving when its turn comes, and with one line if you are not mounted.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Consumables:MountDown[all]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Force_MountOff

OgreBotAPI.Consumables:MountUp[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Consumables
  what: Queues a forced mount-up: sit, toggle summon_mount, stand, then toggle summon_mount again, about 4 seconds in all. It does nothing if you are moving when its turn comes, and with one line if you are already mounted.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Consumables:MountUp[all]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Force_MountOn

OgreBotAPI.Consumables:RekindleHeartstone[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Consumables
  what: Applies the Rekindle Bond verb at once to the nearest actor whose name contains "Heartstone". Nothing happens, with no message, when there is none or it is more than 6 away.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Consumables:RekindleHeartstone[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Heartstone_RekindleBond

OgreBotAPI.Consumables:ReplenishFoodDrink[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Consumables
  what: Opens the nearest Food & Drink Depot (it must be within 11) and tops your equipped food and drink up to stacks of 100, equipping a bag copy into the slot before and after the pull, then closes the depot window. It uses the names in your Food and Drink slots, or the configured fallback names when a slot is empty, runs in the background over a few seconds, and only one depot run can be in flight at a time (a second call echoes that it is busy).
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Consumables:ReplenishFoodDrink[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:FoodDrink_Replenish, OgreBotAPI:Get_FoodDrink

OgreBotAPI.Consumables:ReplenishStatPotions[fw, potion=""]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Consumables
  what: Opens the nearest Poison, Potion, & Totem Depot (it must be within 11) and pulls one potion until your bags hold 100 of it, then closes the depot window. Each step reports to the console (already stocked, depot out, depot low, no depot nearby), and only one depot run can be in flight at a time.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg potion (string, default: ""): the potion's name as the depot lists it; blank uses the statPotion name from replenish-names.json (your OgreSave/EQ2/Replenish/custom copy wins over the shipped one)
  example: OgreBotAPI.Consumables:ReplenishStatPotions[${Me.Name},"Planar Elixir of intellect"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Get_StatPotions, OgreBotAPI:StatPotions_Replenish, OgreBotAPI:Get_Poisons

OgreBotAPI.Consumables:ScrollOf[fw, name=Prowess, cancelIfDurationLessThan=0, useBest=FALSE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Consumables
  what: Keeps one scroll buff up: if a buff of that family is already maintained it does nothing (or cancels and recasts it when it has fewer than cancelIfDurationLessThan minutes left), otherwise it casts the family's ability already in your spellbook, or scribes one from your bags first when none is, and checks that it landed. It is queued, reports each outcome to the console, and a new call replaces one still running.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg name (string, default: Prowess): the scroll family, any case: Prowess, forcelink, Pain, painlink, Power or powerlink; anything else is refused with a console warning
  arg cancelIfDurationLessThan (int, default: 0): minutes; a maintained buff of the family with less time left than this is cancelled and recast, 0 leaves any maintained one alone
  arg useBest (bool, default: FALSE): only used when none of the family is in your spellbook yet: TRUE scribes the first bag scroll found from the bottom of the family's scroll list, FALSE from the top
  example: OgreBotAPI.Consumables:ScrollOf[igw:${Me.Name},Prowess,10,TRUE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ScrollOf

OgreBotAPI.Consumables:SummonFamiliar[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Consumables
  what: Sends summon_familiar at once, with no check of whether a familiar is already out. Use CheckFamiliar to summon only when needed.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Consumables:SummonFamiliar[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Summon_Familiar


== OgreBotAPI.Craft ==

OgreBotAPI.Craft:AddLastScribedRecipe[fw, qty=1]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Craft
  what: Adds the recipe you last scribed this session (by the bot or by hand) to the craft setup queue. With nothing scribed yet it prints a warning and adds nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg qty (int, default: 1): How many to craft; 0 or less becomes 1.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Craft:AddLastScribedRecipe[${Me.Name},5]
  oldbot: OgreCraft:AddLastScribedRecipe, OgreCraftAPI:AddLastScribedRecipe

OgreBotAPI.Craft:AddRecipe[fw, nameOrID|lastknownrecipe, qty=1]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Craft
  what: Adds a recipe to the craft setup queue by full name, by part of a name that matches only one recipe (4 letters or more), by recipe ID, or lastknownrecipe for the recipe last scribed this session. A recipe not in your recipe book prints a warning and adds nothing; if the book has not been read yet the add waits and runs once it has.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg nameOrID|lastknownrecipe (string): The recipe name, its ID (plain digits), or lastknownrecipe. A name may also be passed as several arguments; they are joined with spaces.
  arg qty (int, default: 1): How many to craft. Read only when it is the last argument and a whole number; 0 or less becomes 1.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Craft:AddRecipe[${Me.Name},"Tempered Iron",2]
  oldbot: OgreCraft:AddRecipeNameForWho, OgreCraftAPI:AddRecipeNameForWho

OgreBotAPI.Craft:BuyAllTinkeringRecipes[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Craft
  what: Buys every tinkering recipe book you do not already know or carry from Fizza Cogsworth. It is refused unless you carry at least 3 platinum, are in Steamfont Mountains and are within 10 meters of her, and also while a crafting flow or merchant errand is running.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Craft:BuyAllTinkeringRecipes[${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Craft:CompleteNavigation[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Craft
  what: Answers craft's OgreCraft_NavigationRequired event (sent only when the craft setting to use events for movement is on) to say your script has moved the character; craft then checks the distance again and carries on. If no request is waiting it prints a warning.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Craft:CompleteNavigation[${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Craft:DeferNavigation[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Craft
  what: Answers craft's OgreCraft_NavigationRequired event to say your script will not move the character, so craft uses its own movement. If no request is waiting it prints a warning.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Craft:DeferNavigation[${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Craft:ScribeRecipe[fw, name|all=all]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Craft
  what: Scribes recipe scrolls from your bags one at a time, then opens and closes the tradeskill book. A name scribes only scrolls whose full item name matches it in any case (a name with a comma arrives whole), nothing matching prints a line and does nothing, and a call while scribing adds the new scrolls to the run.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg name|all (string, default: all): The scroll's full item name in any case, or all for every scribeable scroll in your bags. Left empty it scribes all.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Craft:ScribeRecipe[${Me.Name},all]
  oldbot: OgreCraft:ScribeRecipe, OgreCraftAPI:ScribeRecipe

OgreBotAPI.Craft:Start[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Craft
  what: Starts crafting the setup queue. It is refused with a console line when you are not in the world, a crafting flow is already running, or the setup queue is empty, and a refused start changes nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Craft:Start[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreCraft:Start, OgreCraftAPI:Start

OgreBotAPI.Craft:StartLLL[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Craft
  what: Starts low level leveling: rounds of buying recipe books, crafting the highest standard recipe at or below your tradeskill level, and selling or destroying what was made when the panel's settings say so. It stops at tradeskill level 9 or 19, and is refused when a crafting flow is already running or you are not in the world.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Craft:StartLLL[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreCraftAPI:StartLLL

OgreBotAPI.Craft:StartQuest[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Craft
  what: Crafts the recipe steps of the quest selected in your journal, one of each per pass, until no craftable step is left. It is refused when no quest is selected, a crafting flow is already running, or you are not in the world, and a refused start changes nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Craft:StartQuest[${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Craft:StartTinker[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Craft
  what: Starts auto tinkering: rounds of buying recipe books, crafting the highest-level tinkering recipe you know, and selling or destroying what was made when the panel's settings say so, until tinkering is maxed. It stops if the character has no tinkering skill, and is refused when a crafting flow is already running or you are not in the world.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Craft:StartTinker[${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Craft:StartWrits[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Craft
  what: Starts the rush order (writ) run for the number of writs set in the craft settings. It is refused below tradeskill level 20, when a crafting flow is already running, or when you are not in the world, and a refused start changes nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Craft:StartWrits[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreCraftAPI:StartWrits

OgreBotAPI.Craft:Stop[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Craft
  what: Stops the running crafting run (queue, writs, quest, Low Level Leveling or Auto Tinkering) on the characters the for-who names, the same as ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Stop. With nothing running it drops a pause and prints that nothing was running.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Craft:Stop[igw:${Me.Name}]


== OgreBotAPI.Cures ==

${OgreBotAPI.Cures.CurseCalled[victim]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: TRUE while a cure-curse call is open for that character, made by RequestCurse or by Request with kind curse. With no argument it asks about you, and any asks whether a call is open for anyone.
  arg victim (character name): who to ask about; blank means you; any means anyone
  returns: bool: TRUE while a cure-curse call is open (a call lasts at most 8 seconds); FALSE otherwise, and FALSE out of world when no name is given.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Cures.CurseCalled[${Group[1].Name}]}
  oldbot: Obj_CureCurseCalled.CastCureCurse

${OgreBotAPI.Cures.CursedID[-archetype X...,-uncurable,-uncurableonly,-GroupOnly]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: The actor ID of the first cursed member found, searching the raid when you are in one and otherwise the group with you first. By default only curable curses count; 0 when nobody matches.
  arg -archetype X... (flag + word): only members of this archetype: fighter, priest, mage or scout, any case. Repeat the switch to allow more than one archetype.
  arg -uncurable (flag): also accept a member whose curse cannot be cured
  arg -uncurableonly (flag): accept only a member whose curse cannot be cured
  arg -GroupOnly (flag): search your group even when you are in a raid
  returns: int64: the actor ID of the first matching member; 0 when nobody matches.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Cures.CursedID[-archetype,priest,-uncurable]}
  oldbot: Obj_CureCurseCalled.GetID_CursedMember, Obj_CureCurseCalled.GetID_GroupCursedMember, Obj_CureCurseCalled.GetID_RaidCursedMember

${OgreBotAPI.Cures.Detrimental[main,back,actorId,field]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: One field of a detrimental, found by its main and backdrop icon IDs, on you or another actor, as a number. The default field, exists, reads 1 or 0; a detrimental that is not there reads 0.
  arg main (int, default: 0): the detrimental's main icon ID
  arg back (int, default: 0): the detrimental's backdrop icon ID
  arg actorId (int64, default: 0): whose effects to look at: 0 or your own ID is you. Any other actor ID reads only that actor's first 10 effects, and there duration and maxduration always read 0.
  arg field (text, default: exists): exists, iseffectinfoavailable, id, mainiconid, backdropiconid, currentincrements, duration or maxduration, any case. Any other word is read from the effect's examine info, and text such as Name reads 0 here - use DetrimentalText. cancel removes the detrimental from you and reads 0.
  returns: float: the field's value; exists reads 1 or 0; 0 when the detrimental is not found or the field is text.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Cures.Detrimental[279,315,${Target.ID},exists]}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb.CurrentIncrements, GetInfoOb.CurrentIncrements_ref, GetInfoOb.DetrimentalInfo

${OgreBotAPI.Cures.DetrimentalText[main,back,actorId,field]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: The same read as Detrimental, returned as text, so examine-info fields such as Name and Description can be read. Reads "" when the detrimental is not found.
  arg main (int, default: 0): the detrimental's main icon ID
  arg back (int, default: 0): the detrimental's backdrop icon ID
  arg actorId (int64, default: 0): whose effects to look at: 0 or your own ID is you. Any other actor ID reads only that actor's first 10 effects, and there duration and maxduration always read 0.
  arg field (text, default: exists): exists (1 or 0), iseffectinfoavailable, id, mainiconid, backdropiconid, currentincrements, duration, maxduration, or an examine-info field such as Name or Description. Examine-info text can be empty on the first read, so wait for iseffectinfoavailable to read 1. cancel removes the detrimental from you and reads "".
  returns: string: the field's value; "" when the detrimental is not found.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Cures.DetrimentalText[279,315,0,exists]}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb.DottedDescription_ref, GetInfoOb.DottedName_ref, OgreBotAPI.DetrimentalInfo_String

${OgreBotAPI.Cures.GroupCurses}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: How many living group members, you included, have a curse that can be cured. Uncurable curses are not counted here - GroupUncurable counts those.
  returns: int: the number of living group members with a curable curse; 0 when nobody has one.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Cures.GroupCurses}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb.CursesInGroup, GroupCureOb.NumOfPCsCursed, Obj_CureCurseCalled.GroupCurseCount

${OgreBotAPI.Cures.GroupUncurable}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: How many group members, you included, carry a curse that cannot be cured. Curable curses are not counted.
  returns: int: the number of group members with an uncurable curse; 0 when nobody has one.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Cures.GroupUncurable}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_GroupUncurableCurseCount

${OgreBotAPI.Cures.GroupUncurableIDs}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: The actor IDs of the group members, you included, who carry an uncurable curse, as a JSON array sorted lowest first. Reads [] when there are none.
  returns: string: a JSON array of actor IDs, for example [1234,5678]; [] when nobody has an uncurable curse.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Cures.GroupUncurableIDs}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_GroupUncurableCurses_JSON

${OgreBotAPI.Cures.HaveSickness}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: TRUE while you have revive sickness (the detrimental with main icon 279 and backdrop icon 315). FALSE out of world.
  returns: bool: TRUE when you have revive sickness; FALSE when you do not or out of world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Cures.HaveSickness}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.HaveSickness

${OgreBotAPI.Cures.PotionAvailable[type]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: TRUE when you carry a Cure <type> potion that is ready to use. It does not check whether you are afflicted.
  arg type (text): arcane, elemental, noxious or trauma, matched as part of the item name. Any other word answers FALSE.
  returns: bool: TRUE when a ready potion of that type is in your bags; FALSE when not, when it is still cooling down, when type is not one of the four, or out of world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Cures.PotionAvailable[noxious]}

${OgreBotAPI.Cures.PotionNeeded}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: The cure type to drink a potion for right now: the first of arcane, elemental, noxious and trauma that is ticked in the cure potion settings, is on you, and has a ready Cure <type> potion in your bags. Reads "" when none qualifies or out of world.
  returns: string: arcane, elemental, noxious or trauma; "" when no potion is both needed and ready.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Cures.PotionNeeded}

${OgreBotAPI.Cures.RaidCursedIDs}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: The actor IDs of every raid member with a curse, curable or not, as a JSON array sorted lowest first. Out of a raid it lists the group members with a curse, curable or not.
  returns: string: a JSON array of actor IDs, for example [1234,5678]; [] when nobody matches or out of world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Cures.RaidCursedIDs}
  oldbot: Obj_CureCurseCalled.ic_CursedToons, OgreBotAPI.Get_RaidCurableOrUncurableCurses_JSON

${OgreBotAPI.Cures.RaidCurses}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: How many raid members are alive and have a curse that can be cured. Out of a raid it gives the group count, the same as GroupCurses.
  returns: int: the number of living raid members with a curable curse (the group count when not in a raid); 0 when nobody has one.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Cures.RaidCurses}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_RaidCurseCount, OgreBotAPI.NumRaidWithCurses

${OgreBotAPI.Cures.RaidUncurable}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: How many raid members carry a curse that cannot be cured. Out of a raid it gives the group count, the same as GroupUncurable, and it reads 0 out of world.
  returns: int: the number of raid members with an uncurable curse (the group count when not in a raid); 0 when nobody has one or out of world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Cures.RaidUncurable}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_RaidUncurableCurseCount

${OgreBotAPI.Cures.RaidUncurableIDs}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: The actor IDs of the raid members who carry an uncurable curse, as a JSON array sorted lowest first. Out of a raid it lists your group instead; [] when there are none or out of world.
  returns: string: a JSON array of actor IDs, for example [1234,5678]; [] when nobody has an uncurable curse or out of world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Cures.RaidUncurableIDs}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_RaidUncurableCurses_JSON

${OgreBotAPI.Cures.Uncurable[type,-GroupOnly]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: The actor ID of the first member whose affliction of this type cannot be cured: the raid when you are in one, else the group with you first, else just you. 0 when nobody has one or out of world.
  arg type (text, default: Cursed): the affliction to check, as the game names it: Cursed, Arcane, Noxious, Elemental or Trauma. Blank means Cursed.
  arg -GroupOnly (flag): search your group even when you are in a raid
  returns: int64: the actor ID of the first member with an uncurable affliction of that type; 0 when nobody has one or out of world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Cures.Uncurable[Cursed,-GroupOnly]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_Uncurable

OgreBotAPI.Cures:CancelDetrimental[fw, mainId, backdropId]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: Cancels the detrimental with this main and backdrop icon ID on each matching character. Prints a console line when there is no such detrimental, and does nothing when both IDs are 0.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg mainId (int): the detrimental's main icon ID
  arg backdropId (int): the detrimental's backdrop icon ID
  example: OgreBotAPI.Cures:CancelDetrimental[igw:${Me.Name},279,315]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CancelDetrimental, GetInfoOb:CancelEffect, GetInfoOb:CancelEffect_ref

OgreBotAPI.Cures:CancelRequests[fw, victimOrTag]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: Cancels, on each character the for-who matches, every curse, cure and group-cure request whose victim or -tag is the given name (any letter case). Says how many went when any did.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg victimOrTag (text): the toon the requests were for, or the -tag they were given; a blank one is refused with one console line
  example: OgreBotAPI.Cures:CancelRequests[igw:${Me.Name},${Group[1].Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Cures:ItemCure[fw, type]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: Drinks a cure potion now on each matching character, if a ready one is in their bags. With a type it drinks that potion whether or not you are afflicted or the type is ticked; with no type, or any, it drinks the one PotionNeeded names.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg type (text): arcane, elemental, noxious or trauma; blank or any drinks whatever the cure potion settings need. Any other word prints a console line and does nothing.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Cures:ItemCure[igw:${Me.Name},trauma]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:AutoItemCure

OgreBotAPI.Cures:ReplenishPotions[fw, all|arcane|elemental|noxious|trauma]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: Tops up cure potions, up to a full stack, from a Poison, Potion, & Totem Depot within 11 meters, on each matching character. A type is restocked only if one of its potions is already in your bags; a blank or unknown type prints a console line and does nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg all|arcane|elemental|noxious|trauma (word): all four cure types, or just one of them, any case
  example: OgreBotAPI.Cures:ReplenishPotions[igw:${Me.Name},all]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CurePotions_Replenish, OgreBotAPI:Get_CurePotions

OgreBotAPI.Cures:Request[fw, victim, kinds...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: Records a cure request for the victim on each character the for-who matches, and their cure casting serves it. A request lasts 8 seconds unless -AutoRemove says otherwise, and is not sent anywhere else, so use oc !c to reach other characters.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg victim (character name): who to cure; a blank one is refused with one console line
  arg kinds... (words): which cures: arcane (a), noxious (n), elemental (e), trauma (t), curse, confrontfear or sickness, one per argument or comma-separated. None means the four basic kinds (arcane, noxious, elemental, trauma). Then the options -AutoRemove <seconds> (how long the request lasts, 1 to 600, default 8) and -tag <name> (a name Cures:CancelRequests can cancel it by). Any other word refuses the whole request with one console line naming it. confrontfear and sickness are kept only on a dirge.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Cures:Request[igw:${Me.Name},${Group[1].Name},noxious,trauma,-AutoRemove,20]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:AutoCure, Obj_CureCalled:AutoAdd, Obj_CurseCalled:AutoAdd

OgreBotAPI.Cures:RequestCurse[fw, victim, options...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: Records a cure-curse request for the victim on each character the for-who matches, for their cure casting to serve. The request lasts 8 seconds unless -AutoRemove says otherwise, and is not sent anywhere else; a blank victim, or a word it does not know, refuses it with one console line.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg victim (character name): who to cure of the curse; a blank one is refused with one console line
  arg options... (words): -AutoRemove <seconds> (how long the request lasts, 1 to 600, default 8) and -tag <name> (a name Cures:CancelRequests can cancel it by). Any other word refuses the request with one console line naming it.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Cures:RequestCurse[igw:${Me.Name},${Group[1].Name},-AutoRemove,20]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:AutoCurse, OgreBotAPI:Cursed, Obj_CureCurseCalled:Add

OgreBotAPI.Cures:RequestGroup[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: Asks each matching character to cast its class group cure within the next 2 seconds, when that ability is ready and someone in the group, you included, has an arcane, noxious, elemental or trauma detrimental. Curses are not group cured.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Cures:RequestGroup[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:GroupCure

OgreBotAPI.Cures:RequestGroupWatch[fw, words...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: Watches for a group cure on each matching character: the class group cure goes out as soon as it is ready and enough of the group, you included, carry one of the named kinds, each counted on its own (curses are not group cured). The watch lasts 8 seconds unless -AutoRemove says otherwise, and several can run at once.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg words... (words): kinds: arcane (a), noxious (n), elemental (e), trauma (t), one per argument or comma-separated; none means any of the four. Options: -count <n> (at least n of you and the group carry the kind, 1 to 6, default 1), -AutoRemove <seconds> (how long to watch, 1 to 600, default 8), -tag <name> (a name Cures:CancelRequests can cancel it by). Any other word refuses the request with one console line naming it.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Cures:RequestGroupWatch[igw:${Me.Name},arcane,trauma,-count,3]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:AutoGroupCure

OgreBotAPI.Cures:RequestItem[fw, type]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: Queues a potion cure on each matching character, drunk once the cast bar is free; a potion only ever cures the one who drinks it. The request waits up to 8 seconds for a ready potion.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg type (text): arcane, elemental, noxious or trauma. Blank or any picks the needed type when the request is served. Any other word prints a console line and queues nothing.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Cures:RequestItem[igw:${Me.Name},arcane]

OgreBotAPI.Cures:SetEnabled[fw, on=TRUE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Cures
  what: Turns cures on or off on each matching character: the Disable CS_Cure setting and, for a Templar, Warden, Mystic or Monk, that class's cure ability in the Cast Stack. At character select it prints a line and changes nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg on (bool, default: TRUE): TRUE turns cures on, FALSE turns them off. Off also unticks Enable Auto Cure Potions and cancels the running class ability (Mana Cure, Tranquility, Ancestral Balm or Will of the Heavens). The 'Use these while stunned / stifled / rooted' option is left as you set it. A word that is not yes or no changes nothing.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Cures:SetEnabled[igw:${Me.Name},FALSE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Enable_Cures, OgreBotAPI:Disable_Cures


== OgreBotAPI.Debug ==

${OgreBotAPI.Debug.CheckVersion[fw,compareTo]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Debug
  what: Compares this session's version with compareTo and returns a one-line verdict that names the character. It returns "" when the for-who does not match this character or the character is not in the world.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg compareTo (string): the version to compare with, as ${ISXOgreEQ2.Version} gives it; blank just reports this session's version
  returns: string: "SAME: <name> (<version>)" when they match; "DIFFERENT: <name> - Mine: <version> Requested: <compareTo>" when they do not; "VERSION: <name> (<version>)" when compareTo is blank; "" when the for-who does not match or the character is not in the world
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Debug.CheckVersion[all,${ISXOgreEQ2.Version}]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.CheckVersion

${OgreBotAPI.Debug.DebugPrefix}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Debug
  what: A time-stamped prefix for your own debug lines: the current time followed by ": OgreBot:". The bot does not add it to anything for you, :DebugEcho included.
  returns: string: "<time>: OgreBot:", for example "14:03:22: OgreBot:"
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Debug.DebugPrefix} checking loot
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.DebugMessage, OgreBotDebug.Prefix

OgreBotAPI.Debug:BroadcastStat[fw, type, value, where=oc]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Debug
  what: Reads one fact about this character, sends "<name> --> <label> <value>" to where `where` says and fires the OgreEvent_SpewStats event with the same data. An unknown type or stat sends a "SpewStat:" error line instead, and faction, currency and recipe open a game window, so their answer comes a moment later.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg type (string): what to report: stat, item, missingitem, abilityready, abilityidready, abilityidcd, marked, faction, currency, recipe or ascension (a leading - is allowed); quest and missingquest answer with a not-yet error
  arg value (string): what to look up for that type: a stat key such as potency or haste, an item name, an ability id, a faction name or all, a currency name (eth and loyalty are short names), or a recipe name; leave blank for marked and ascension. An item you have none of sends nothing
  arg where (string, default: oc): where the line goes: oc (the Ogre console on every session), irc, or event (no line, only the event); any other word goes to oc
  example: OgreBotAPI.Debug:BroadcastStat[all,stat,potency,oc]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.SpewStat, OgreBotAPI:Get_Faction

OgreBotAPI.Debug:DebugEcho[fw, a, b]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Debug
  what: Echoes a and b, joined by a space, to this session's console, but only while debug mode is on (see :SetDebugMode). With debug mode off, which is the default, it prints nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg a (string): the first part of the line
  arg b (string): the second part, printed after a space
  example: OgreBotAPI.Debug:DebugEcho[${Me.Name},"Target:",${Target.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Debug:Echo[fw, text, text2=""]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Debug
  what: Echoes text and text2, joined by a space, to this session's console. Only characters the for-who matches print it, and it works out of the world too.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg text (string): the first part of the line
  arg text2 (string, default: ""): the second part, printed after a space
  example: OgreBotAPI.Debug:Echo[${Me.Name},"Pull ready","waiting on tank"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Echo, OgreBotDebug:Echo

OgreBotAPI.Debug:SetDebugMode[fw, on=TRUE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Debug
  what: Turns debug mode on or off; while it is on, :DebugEcho prints its lines. Debug mode starts off, and a word that is not a yes/no word leaves it as it is.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg on (bool, default: TRUE): TRUE turns debug mode on, FALSE turns it off
  example: OgreBotAPI.Debug:SetDebugMode[all,TRUE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:SetDebugMode

OgreBotAPI.Debug:SpewInternalVariables[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Debug
  what: Echoes every internal variable as "name -> value" to this session's console, in name order. These are the values stored with OgreBotAPI.Vars:SetInternal; an empty store prints nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Debug:SpewInternalVariables[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Spew_InternalVariables

OgreBotAPI.Debug:SpewResearchWindow[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Debug
  what: Queues a job that opens the Knowledge window's research page if it is not up, broadcasts every row to every session as "<label> -> <status>", then closes the window if it opened it. It needs the character in the world, and with no rows it echoes a note to the console instead.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Debug:SpewResearchWindow[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Spew_BoZ_Research

OgreBotAPI.Debug:SpewSubscriptionStatus[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Debug
  what: Reads the game's All Access membership status from the tooltip of the Marketplace window's All Access button and broadcasts it to every session as Good, Need to claim, Need more time, Not a member or Unknown, followed by the tooltip text. It does not open the window, and a tooltip it cannot read reports as Unknown.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Debug:SpewSubscriptionStatus[all]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:SpewSubscriptionStatus

OgreBotAPI.Debug:SpewVariables[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Debug
  what: Echoes every script variable as "name -> value" to this session's console, in name order. These are the values stored with OgreBotAPI.Vars:Set; an empty store prints nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Debug:SpewVariables[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Spew_Variables


== OgreBotAPI.Encounter ==

OgreBotAPI.Encounter:List[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Encounter
  what: Prints in this character's console the encounter coding for the current zone: one line per fight with its named mobs, (DISABLED) when switched off, and its file. With none it prints "No encounter coding for this zone"; the Settings tab's No Available Setups box does not silence it.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Encounter:List[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:DisplayAvailableSetups


== OgreBotAPI.Events ==

OgreBotAPI.Events:AddChatEntry[fw, text, oc, ding, code]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Events
  what: Adds a row to the Chat Events tab of the loaded profile: when a line in the chat window contains text (any case), it announces in OgreConsole (oc), plays the ding sound (ding) and runs code as a command, in that order, with no arguments passed to the code. The row is unsaved until Save, only fires while the tab is ticked on the Settings tab (it warns if not), a blank text or an identical enabled row is refused with a console line, and every session's console is told it was added.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg text (string): Text to watch for - matched as a case-insensitive substring of each incoming chat-window line
  arg oc (bool): TRUE to send `<name> -> <kind> event -> (<text>) found -> <match>` to OgreConsole when it fires
  arg ding (bool): TRUE to play the ding sound when it fires
  arg code (string): A command line to run when it fires (run on the next frame, may be empty); any extra arguments after it are joined back on with commas
  example: OgreBotAPI.Events:AddChatEntry[igw:${Me.Name},"tells you",TRUE,TRUE,"echo got a tell"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ChatEvent_AddEntry

OgreBotAPI.Events:AddDespawnEntry[fw, text, oc, ding, code]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Events
  what: Adds a row to the Despawn Events tab of the loaded profile: when an actor despawns whose name contains text (case-sensitive), it announces in OgreConsole (oc), plays the ding sound (ding) and runs code as a command, in that order, with no arguments passed to the code. The row is unsaved until Save, only fires while the tab is ticked on the Settings tab (it warns if not), a blank text or an identical enabled row is refused with a console line, and every session's console is told it was added.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg text (string): Text to watch for - matched as a case-sensitive substring of the despawning actor's name
  arg oc (bool): TRUE to send `<name> -> <kind> event -> (<text>) found -> <match>` to OgreConsole when it fires
  arg ding (bool): TRUE to play the ding sound when it fires
  arg code (string): A command line to run when it fires (run on the next frame, may be empty); any extra arguments after it are joined back on with commas
  example: OgreBotAPI.Events:AddDespawnEntry[${Me.Name},"a cursed spirit",TRUE,FALSE,"echo spirit is gone"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:DespawnEvent_AddEntry

OgreBotAPI.Events:AddSpawnEntry[fw, text, oc, ding, code]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Events
  what: Adds a row to the Spawn Events tab of the loaded profile: when an actor spawns whose name contains text (case-sensitive), it announces in OgreConsole (oc), plays the ding sound (ding) and runs code as a command, in that order, with no arguments passed to the code. The row is unsaved until Save, only fires while the tab is ticked on the Settings tab (it warns if not), a blank text or an identical enabled row is refused with a console line, and every session's console is told it was added.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg text (string): Text to watch for - matched as a case-sensitive substring of the spawning actor's name
  arg oc (bool): TRUE to send `<name> -> <kind> event -> (<text>) found -> <match>` to OgreConsole when it fires
  arg ding (bool): TRUE to play the ding sound when it fires
  arg code (string): A command line to run when it fires (run on the next frame, may be empty); any extra arguments after it are joined back on with commas
  example: OgreBotAPI.Events:AddSpawnEntry[${Me.Name},"a cursed spirit",TRUE,TRUE,"echo spirit is up"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:SpawnEvent_AddEntry

OgreBotAPI.Events:RemoveChatEntry[fw, text=all]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Events
  what: Removes every Chat Events row whose text equals text (any case, disabled rows included), or every row for all, and tells every session's console which rows went. The change is unsaved until Save; no match, no loaded profile or a text passed but empty each print a console line and remove nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg text (string, default: all): The watch text of the rows to remove, or all for every row
  example: OgreBotAPI.Events:RemoveChatEntry[igw:${Me.Name},"tells you"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ChatEvent_RemoveEntry

OgreBotAPI.Events:RemoveDespawnEntry[fw, text=all]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Events
  what: Removes every Despawn Events row whose text equals text (any case, disabled rows included), or every row for all, and tells every session's console which rows went. The change is unsaved until Save; no match, no loaded profile or a text passed but empty each print a console line and remove nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg text (string, default: all): The watch text of the rows to remove, or all for every row
  example: OgreBotAPI.Events:RemoveDespawnEntry[${Me.Name},all]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:DespawnEvent_RemoveEntry

OgreBotAPI.Events:RemoveSpawnEntry[fw, text=all]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Events
  what: Removes every Spawn Events row whose text equals text (any case, disabled rows included), or every row for all, and tells every session's console which rows went. The change is unsaved until Save; no match, no loaded profile or a text passed but empty each print a console line and remove nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg text (string, default: all): The watch text of the rows to remove, or all for every row
  example: OgreBotAPI.Events:RemoveSpawnEntry[${Me.Name},"a cursed spirit"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:SpawnEvent_RemoveEntry


== OgreBotAPI.ForWho ==

${OgreBotAPI.ForWho.Alias[name]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.ForWho
  what: Returns the character name an alias points to right now, or "" when it names nobody present. It reads @me, @Tank, @Healer1 to @Healer3, @DPS1 to @DPS3, @Bard, @Enchanter, @Fighter / @Priest / @Mage / @Scout with an optional rank, @PCTarget, @NPCsTarget, *<your alias> (only while the OgreBot enable-aliases setting is on and you are in the world) and *Team:<group> (its first member present); a plain character name or class word returns "".
  arg name (string): the alias to resolve, with its @ or * (any case)
  returns: string: the character name the alias resolves to; "" when it resolves to nobody, is not an alias, or no argument is given.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.ForWho.Alias[@Healer1]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_Alias, GetInfoOb.Alias

${OgreBotAPI.ForWho.AliasesJSON}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.ForWho
  what: Returns the loaded OgreBot profile's own alias list as JSON text, one object per row with its starred name, For (what it points to) and, when set, NR (no raid) and a disabled marker. Returns "[]" when no OgreBot profile is loaded or it has no aliases.
  returns: string: a JSON array of alias rows; "[]" when there are none or no profile is loaded.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.ForWho.AliasesJSON}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_Aliases_JSON

${OgreBotAPI.ForWho.Me[expr]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.ForWho
  what: Answers whether a call with this for-who would run on this character - the same test every OgreBotAPI method makes on its first argument. While zoning or at character select it answers from what it already knows: words that need a live read (id:, a bare actor id, eval_num_me:, @PCTarget, @NPCsTarget, *aliases) do not match, and group words use your last settled zone.
