  arg expr (string): a for-who expression, one word with no spaces or commas. | separates alternatives (any one group matching is enough), + joins words that must all match, and a leading - or ! negates a word. Words, any case: all, auto, @all, @group, @raid (everyone); me, @me; a character name; your InnerSpace session name (is1); an archetype fighter, priest, mage, scout, or healer, melee, caster (plurals too), and not<archetype> such as notfighter; a class or subclass (predator, ranger); an ascension class (geomancer); g1 to g4 (your raid group); groups:<digits> (your raid group number appears in the digits); groupleader; igw:<name> (that character is you or in your group), with irw: also counting the raid, igzw: / irzw: also needing them in your zone, and a bn ending (igwbn:, irzwbn:) leaving yourself out; not:<name>; id:<actor id> or a bare actor id; ToonFlagged:<n>; eval_num_me:<member><op><value> with op < <= > >= = or ==; @Tank, @Healer1 to @Healer3, @DPS1 to @DPS3, @Bard, @Enchanter; @Fighter, @Priest, @Mage, @Scout with an optional rank (@Scout2); @PCTarget, @NPCsTarget; *<alias> (your own aliases) and *Team:<group>. A word that is none of these simply does not match.
  returns: int: 1 when the expression selects this character; 0 when it does not, including an empty expression (an empty for-who on a method means all); NULL with no argument.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.ForWho.Me[igw:${Me.Name}+healer]}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb.CommandForMe, GetInfoOb.CommandForMe_Check, GetInfoOb.CommandForMe_Eval_Me

${OgreBotAPI.ForWho.Member[expr,name]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.ForWho
  what: Answers whether a for-who expression selects a given member of your group or raid, using the same words as ForWho.Me with that member in your place. The member must be in your current group or raid; g1 to g4, groups:, groupleader, session names and ascension words never match a member, and eval_num_me: only reads Health, HealthPct, Power and PowerPct.
  arg expr (string): a for-who expression, the same grammar and words as ForWho.Me
  arg name (string): the group or raid member to test, by character name (any case)
  returns: int: 1 when the expression selects that member; 0 when it does not, when the name is not in your group or raid, or when you are not in the world; NULL with fewer than two arguments.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.ForWho.Member[priest,${Group[1].Name}]}

OgreBotAPI.ForWho:AddAlias[fw, alias, value, noRaid=FALSE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.ForWho
  what: Adds a row to the loaded OgreBot profile's alias list, so *<alias> names the first character present that value matches: you, a group member by name, a raid member by name, then whoever of you, the group and the raid first fits value as a class word. Several rows may share one name (the first that resolves wins) but an exact repeat is refused with a warning; with no OgreBot profile loaded nothing happens and one console line says so, and the change is kept in memory until the profile is saved.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg alias (string): the alias name; a leading * is added when you leave it off
  arg value (string): what the alias points to: a character name or a class word (archetype, class or subclass)
  arg noRaid (bool, default: FALSE): TRUE = only you and your group count, raid members are not matched
  example: OgreBotAPI.ForWho:AddAlias[${Me.Name},MainHealer,${Group[1].Name},TRUE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Alias_AddEntry

OgreBotAPI.ForWho:ChangeAlias[fw, from, to, silent=FALSE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.ForWho
  what: Points the first alias row named from at to instead (a blank to clears it, so the alias names nobody), and announces the change in the Ogre console unless silent is TRUE. When no alias of that name exists nothing changes and one console line says so (not when silent); with no OgreBot profile loaded nothing happens and one console line says so.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg from (string): the alias to change (with or without its *)
  arg to (string): the new character name or class word it points to
  arg silent (bool, default: FALSE): TRUE = make the change without the Ogre console announce
  example: OgreBotAPI.ForWho:ChangeAlias[${Me.Name},MainHealer,Templar]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Alias_ChangeEntry

OgreBotAPI.ForWho:ForceUpdate[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.ForWho
  what: Drops the cached alias answers, so the next *alias is worked out against the group and raid as they are now. The cache lasts about a second and every alias edit already drops it, so this matters only straight after the group changes.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.ForWho:ForceUpdate[all]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ForceAliasUpdate

OgreBotAPI.ForWho:RemoveAlias[fw, name|all]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.ForWho
  what: Removes the first alias row with that name from the loaded OgreBot profile, or every alias row when the name is all or blank. With no OgreBot profile loaded nothing happens and one console line says so; the change is kept in memory until the profile is saved.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg name|all (string): the alias to remove (with or without its *), or all to clear the whole list
  example: OgreBotAPI.ForWho:RemoveAlias[${Me.Name},MainHealer]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Alias_RemoveEntry

OgreBotAPI.ForWho:RenameAlias[fw, from, to, silent=FALSE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.ForWho
  what: Renames the first alias row named from to to (stars added when missing), keeping what it points to, and announces it in the Ogre console unless silent is TRUE. The row keeps its place and its no-raid and disabled settings; a blank name, no alias named from or a to name already taken gets one line and renames nothing, and with no OgreBot profile loaded nothing happens.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg from (string): the alias to rename (with or without its *)
  arg to (string): the new alias name (with or without its *)
  arg silent (bool, default: FALSE): TRUE = rename without the Ogre console announce
  example: OgreBotAPI.ForWho:RenameAlias[${Me.Name},MainHealer,BackupHealer]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Alias_ChangeEntryAlias


== OgreBotAPI.HOs ==

${OgreBotAPI.HOs.DoEnabled}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: TRUE while this character is running OgreBot's solo HO (started with DoSetup or DoSetEnabled); session only, never saved, and FALSE after a reload. It turns FALSE when the HO count is reached, the timeout runs out, the target dies or goes away, DoSetEnabled[...,FALSE] is called, or another group member takes over the solo HO.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the solo HO is running on this character; FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.HOs.DoEnabled}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.DoHO_Get_Enabled

${OgreBotAPI.HOs.DoHOerID}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: The actor ID of the OTHER group member who is running the solo HO, as that character announced it. Session only; 0 when this character is the one running it, or nobody is.
  returns: int64: the other HO'er's actor ID; 0 when it is this character or nobody.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.HOs.DoHOerID}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.DoHO_Get_HOerID

${OgreBotAPI.HOs.DoPrimed}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: TRUE once the solo HO has made its first full setup pass on this character (the group's HO settings set, stale casts cancelled, the HO'er announced); a later enable while primed only turns this character's own HO settings back on. Session only, and cleared by DoReset, by a disable, and when another session takes over.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the solo HO setup has been applied; FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.HOs.DoPrimed}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.DoHO_Get_Primed

${OgreBotAPI.HOs.DoTargetID}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: The actor ID given to DoSetup with -TargetID, the mob the solo HO is aimed at; 0 when no target was given, or after DoReset or a new DoSetup without one. Session only - note the casing: DoTargetID.
  returns: int64: the solo HO's target actor ID; 0 when none is set.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.HOs.DoTargetID}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.DoHo_Get_TargetID

${OgreBotAPI.HOs.MyArchetypeStart}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: TRUE when the starter window is up and the heroic opportunity's centre icon is this character's own archetype, so the starter in progress is ours. FALSE when no starter is showing or it belongs to another archetype.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the starter showing is this character's archetype; FALSE otherwise, including when no heroic opportunity is up.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.HOs.MyArchetypeStart}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:MyArchetypeHOStart

${OgreBotAPI.HOs.MyWheelTimeRemaining}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: Seconds left on the HO timer, but only while the wheel is up and it is this character's archetype's wheel. Returns 0 when no heroic opportunity is up, it is still in the starter phase, or the wheel belongs to another archetype.
  returns: float: seconds left on this character's archetype's wheel; 0 otherwise.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.HOs.MyWheelTimeRemaining}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:MyArchetypeWheelTimeRemaining

${OgreBotAPI.HOs.StarterClass}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: Which archetype's starter is up, from the starter window's centre icon, in lower case: fighter, priest, mage or scout. Empty when the starter window is not showing or no heroic opportunity is up.
  returns: string: fighter, priest, mage or scout; "" when no starter is showing.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.HOs.StarterClass}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.HO_Starter_Class

${OgreBotAPI.HOs.StarterClassAvailable[class]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: TRUE when the starter chain currently offers an icon that the given archetype can use. FALSE when the starter window is not up, no heroic opportunity is up, or class is not fighter, priest, mage or scout (any case).
  arg class (string, default: my archetype): Archetype to check: fighter, priest, mage or scout (any case). Blank or left out means this character's own archetype.
  returns: bool: TRUE when that archetype has an icon on the starter chain now; FALSE otherwise, including when no heroic opportunity is up.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.HOs.StarterClassAvailable[scout]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.HO_Starter_Class_Available

${OgreBotAPI.HOs.StarterVisible}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: TRUE while the HO starter window (the chain of icons before the wheel) is showing. FALSE when no heroic opportunity is up or it has moved on to the wheel.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the starter window is up; FALSE otherwise, including when no heroic opportunity is up.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.HOs.StarterVisible}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.HO_Starter_Visible

${OgreBotAPI.HOs.TargetID}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: The actor ID the bot recorded as the HO target: set when this character's bot casts an HO start, and when another group member's bot announces one. Returns 0 when no heroic opportunity is up or that actor no longer exists.
  returns: int64: the HO target's actor ID; 0 when no heroic opportunity is up, the actor is gone, or no start has been recorded.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.HOs.TargetID}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.HO_TargetID

${OgreBotAPI.HOs.Visible}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: TRUE while a heroic opportunity is up in any phase (starter, wheel or finishing); FALSE when none is up or out of world. The HO reads are refreshed at most every 250 ms, so a value can be up to a quarter second old.
  returns: bool: TRUE when a heroic opportunity is up; FALSE when none is up or not in world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.HOs.Visible}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.HO_Visible

${OgreBotAPI.HOs.WheelClassAvailable[class]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: TRUE when the wheel currently has a step the given archetype can complete right now. FALSE when the wheel is not up, no heroic opportunity is up, or class is not fighter, priest, mage or scout (any case).
  arg class (string, default: my archetype): Archetype to check: fighter, priest, mage or scout (any case). Blank or left out means this character's own archetype.
  returns: bool: TRUE when that archetype has a completable step on the wheel now; FALSE otherwise, including when no heroic opportunity is up.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.HOs.WheelClassAvailable[mage]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.HO_Class_Available, OgreBotAPI.HO_Wheel_Class_Available

${OgreBotAPI.HOs.WheelName}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: The heroic opportunity name shown on the wheel, read from the HO window itself. Empty when no heroic opportunity is up; it can also be empty or stale during the starter phase, so check WheelVisible first.
  returns: string: the wheel's HO name; "" when no heroic opportunity is up.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.HOs.WheelName}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.HO_Wheel_Name

${OgreBotAPI.HOs.WheelVisible}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: TRUE while the HO wheel is showing. FALSE when no heroic opportunity is up or it is still in the starter phase.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the wheel is up; FALSE otherwise, including when no heroic opportunity is up.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.HOs.WheelVisible}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.HO_Wheel_Visible

OgreBotAPI.HOs:Advance[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: Takes one turn on an open wheel, casting each of this character's abilities once for the wheel steps its archetype can complete now; it follows "Offensive Only" and "HO - Change Target", works while the bot is paused, and suits scripts that keep "HO Wheel" off and drive the wheel themselves. It does nothing with no heroic opportunity or wheel up, no step for this archetype, "Last to Complete" on while other archetypes still have steps, "HO - allow unknown target" off with no known HO target, or within 1 second of the last advance.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.HOs:Advance[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:HO_Advance, OgreBotAPI:HO_Wheel_Advance

OgreBotAPI.HOs:AllowIcon[fw, icon]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: Adds an HO icon ID to the allow list; while the list has any icon, cast stack abilities that carry a different HO icon are skipped (abilities with no HO icon are not affected, the disable list wins over it, and the bot's own HO starter and wheel casts are not steered). Session only - never saved to the profile, kept until cleared, LetsGo or the extension reloads.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg icon (int): HO icon ID: fighter 0-5, priest 12-17, mage 24-29, scout 36-41. Required; an icon already in the list does nothing. A missing icon, or a word that is not a whole number, is refused with a console line and changes nothing.
  example: OgreBotAPI.HOs:AllowIcon[${Me.Name},25]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Set_Allow_HOICon

OgreBotAPI.HOs:CancelStarter[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: Cancels the HO starter window right away by sending the game's cancel HO starter command. Does nothing when no heroic opportunity is up or the starter window is not showing (a running wheel is never cancelled).
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.HOs:CancelStarter[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:HO_Cancel_Starter

OgreBotAPI.HOs:ClearAllowIcon[fw, icon]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: Removes one HO icon ID from the allow list (session only). When the list becomes empty, no ability is skipped for its HO icon by this list.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg icon (int): HO icon ID to remove from the allow list. Required; an icon not in the list does nothing. A missing icon, or a word that is not a whole number, is refused with a console line and changes nothing.
  example: OgreBotAPI.HOs:ClearAllowIcon[${Me.Name},25]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Clear_Allow_HOICon

OgreBotAPI.HOs:ClearAllowIcons[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: Empties the HO icon allow list (session only), so the cast stack no longer skips abilities for being outside it. The disable list is not touched.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.HOs:ClearAllowIcons[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Clear_Allow_HOICons

OgreBotAPI.HOs:ClearDisableIcon[fw, icon]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: Removes one HO icon ID from the disable list, so abilities with that icon can be cast again (subject to the allow list). Session only; an icon not in the list does nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg icon (int): HO icon ID to remove from the disable list. Required. A missing icon, or a word that is not a whole number, is refused with a console line and changes nothing.
  example: OgreBotAPI.HOs:ClearDisableIcon[${Me.Name},14]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Clear_Disable_HOICon

OgreBotAPI.HOs:ClearDisableIcons[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: Empties the HO icon disable list (session only). The allow list is not touched, and the per-icon disable checkboxes in the profile are a separate setting and stay as they are.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.HOs:ClearDisableIcons[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Clear_Disable_HOICons

OgreBotAPI.HOs:DisableIcon[fw, icon]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: Adds an HO icon ID to the disable list, so cast stack abilities that carry that HO icon are skipped even if the icon is also in the allow list; the bot's own HO starter and wheel casts are not steered. Session only - never saved to the profile, kept until cleared, LetsGo or the extension reloads.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg icon (int): HO icon ID: fighter 0-5, priest 12-17, mage 24-29, scout 36-41. Required. A missing icon, or a word that is not a whole number, is refused with a console line and changes nothing.
  example: OgreBotAPI.HOs:DisableIcon[${Me.Name},14]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Set_Disable_HOICon

OgreBotAPI.HOs:DoReset[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: Clears this character's solo HO record (session only): target, HO count and completions, the leave-open and cast stack options, the other HO'er's ID and the primed flag. It does not turn the solo HO on or off, change the timeout, or change any settings.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.HOs:DoReset[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:DoHO_Reset

OgreBotAPI.HOs:DoSetEnabled[fw, on=TRUE, option...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: Turns OgreBot's solo HO on or off on this character without clearing its record (use DoSetup to set the target and count); calling it with the state it already has does nothing unless -Force, and a value that is not a yes/no word does nothing. On/off is session only, and the settings it writes are profile options in memory, kept on disk only if the profile is saved before they are put back.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg on (bool, default: TRUE): TRUE to run the solo HO here: makes this character the HO'er, tells the rest of the group to stand down, cancels another archetype's starter if one is up, writes the group's HO settings, cancels group casts with more than 0.5 seconds left, holds the first start for -DelayStart seconds (default 1) and extends the timeout to at least 25 seconds (or sets it to -TimeOut n). FALSE to stop it: puts back this character's HO settings and asks the group to put back theirs.
  arg option... (flags): Any of -Force (run even if already in that state), -NoEnable / -PrimeOnly / -NoStart (set the group up but leave this character's HO settings off), -NoHoAbilities (on FALSE, keep HO abilities disabled on the rest of the group), -TimeOut n, -DelayStart n. Unknown words are ignored.
  example: OgreBotAPI.HOs:DoSetEnabled[${Me.Name},FALSE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:DoHO_Set_Enable

OgreBotAPI.HOs:DoSetup[fw, option...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: Starts OgreBot's solo HO with this character as the one who starts it (no HO needs to be up): it clears the previous record, starts a 25 second timeout and enables it as DoSetEnabled[fw,TRUE,...] with the same options, turning HO Start, Starter and Wheel off for the group and on for this character and setting the group's HO helper settings. It ends after -NumHOsToComplete completions (default 1), on timeout, or when the -TargetID mob dies or goes away, and every session then puts back the HO settings it had; the record is session only, and the changed HO settings are profile options in memory, written to disk only if the profile is saved while they are changed.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg option... (flags): Any of -TargetID id, -NumHOsToComplete n, -TimeOut n (instead of 25 seconds), -LeaveStartOpen, -LeaveWheelOpen, -AllowCastStack (keep this character's cast stack on), -NoModifyOptions (change no settings), -Force (when the solo HO is already running, apply the settings again instead of only recording the new options), -NoEnable, -DelayStart n, -NoHoAbilities, in any order; the DoSetEnabled options work here too. Unknown words are ignored.
  example: OgreBotAPI.HOs:DoSetup[${Me.Name},-TargetID,${Target.ID},-NumHOsToComplete,1,-TimeOut,30]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:DoHO_Setup

OgreBotAPI.HOs:RestoreSetUpFor[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: Puts "Heroic Surge (ROC Adorn)" back to the value SetUpFor remembered, quietly, and forgets it. Does nothing if SetUpFor was not called since the last restore, or the extension was reloaded in between.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.HOs:RestoreSetUpFor[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Restore_SetUpFor_HOs

OgreBotAPI.HOs:SetUpFor[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: Readies a fight that needs HOs controlled, with or without an HO up: remembers the current "Heroic Surge (ROC Adorn)" setting (only on the first call before a RestoreSetUpFor), then turns it off quietly so the adornment cannot start or advance HOs on its own. The remembered value is session only; the setting itself is a profile option changed in memory, so saving the profile before RestoreSetUpFor keeps it off on disk.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.HOs:SetUpFor[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:SetUpFor_HOs

OgreBotAPI.HOs:Start[fw, -ActorID id, -SkipTimer]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: Casts this character's archetype HO starter ability (Fighting Chance, Lucky Break, Divine Providence or Arcane Augur) once, immediately, even while the bot is paused, and tells the group which actor the HO is on. Nothing happens within 1 second of the last start unless -SkipTimer is given, or when the ability is not ready, out of range or the cast bar is busy - call it again to retry.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg -ActorID id (flag + number): Start the HO on this actor ID instead of the current target; -TargetID id is the same flag. Without it the cast goes at the current target and does nothing while any heroic opportunity is already up. With it, nothing happens if that actor is gone or a wheel is already running, and if another archetype's starter is up it is cancelled and the cast goes on the actor once the starter closes and the ability is ready (giving up after about 8 seconds).
  arg -SkipTimer (flag): Ignore the 1 second wait after the last start.
  example: OgreBotAPI.HOs:Start[${Me.Name},-ActorID,${Target.ID}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:HO_Start

OgreBotAPI.HOs:Starter[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.HOs
  what: Takes one turn on an open starter chain, casting this character's abilities for the starter icons its archetype is offered; it follows "HO - Change Target" and works while the bot is paused. It does nothing when no heroic opportunity or starter window is up, this archetype has no icon in the chain, "HO - allow unknown target" is off and no HO target is known, or within 1 second of the last starter cast.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.HOs:Starter[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:HO_Starter, OgreBotAPI:HO_Starter_Advance


== OgreBotAPI.IM ==

${OgreBotAPI.IM.EndWhenFinished}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: Whether -end is armed, so the Inventory Manager window closes itself once the work has been idle for about 1.5 seconds. Only the console arms it (the -end flag of an `ogre im` line); there is no method for it, and closing the window clears it.
  returns: bool: TRUE while -end is armed; FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.IM.EndWhenFinished}

${OgreBotAPI.IM.IsOpen}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: Whether the Inventory Manager window is up on this session - the window is the session, so this is what a script waits on after starting it with -end. It reads FALSE when the UI host is not available, even while modes run from the console.
  returns: bool: TRUE while the Inventory Manager window really exists; FALSE when it is closed or could not open.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.IM.IsOpen}

${OgreBotAPI.IM.IsRunning}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: Whether the Inventory Manager is doing work right now - a mode (depot, sell, destroy, tse, restock, trade, quiver), a chain of them, or a depot withdraw started anywhere. It is FALSE while the window sits open and idle and can be FALSE just before a mode starts, so to wait for work to finish poll IsOpen with -end instead.
  returns: bool: TRUE while any Inventory Manager mode or chain is working; FALSE when idle.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.IM.IsRunning}

${OgreBotAPI.IM.Mode}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: The Inventory Manager mode working right now: depot, sell, destroy, tse, restock, trade, quiver or withdraw (a depot withdraw from anywhere). It reads chain when only a chain is busy between modes, and empty when idle.
  returns: string: the busy mode's name, "chain", or "" when nothing is running.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.IM.Mode}

${OgreBotAPI.IM.Status}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: One line saying what the Inventory Manager is doing, the same line `echo ${OgreBotAPI.IM}` prints. It reads "closed", "open, idle", "open, running sell", "open, running withdraw" or "closed (running headless), running restock", with "; will close when finished (-end)" added while -end is armed.
  returns: string: the status line, such as "open, idle" or "closed".
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.IM.Status}

OgreBotAPI.IM:Chain[fw, words...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: Prints what each -<mode> flag expands to. `reload` reads the chain defaults from disk again.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg words... (string): reload. Optional.
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Chain[all,reload]

OgreBotAPI.IM:Close[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: Closes the Inventory Manager window, clears a pending -end, and closes the merchant window unless a sell run is using it. It does not stop work that is running - use Stop for that.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Close[${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.IM:Console[fw, word]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: The window's activity log: always, running or never sets when the strip shows, and clear empties it. With no word it prints the setting and how many lines it holds.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg word (string): always, running, never or clear. Optional.
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Console[all,running]

OgreBotAPI.IM:Depot[fw, words...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: Runs the depot mode, deposits into the nearest house or guild hall depots, and brings the window up; with no flags it runs the line saved on the Depot tab, or warns if nothing is saved. The words after it are read as one `ogre im` line, so `ogre im depot status` is `ogre im status`.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg words... (string): The depot flags, one argument each, such as -harvest all -nearestdepot. `ogre im help` lists them. Optional.
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Depot[all,-harvest,all,-nearestdepot]

OgreBotAPI.IM:Destroy[fw, words...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: The destroy mode: with no words, or flags first, it brings the window up and destroys what is on the destroy list; a name or an item id destroys that one item. The other first words are in the param.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg words... (string): stop, status, reload, preview (or plan), list [all], add <name> or remove <name>; or flags; or an item. One argument each. Optional.
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Destroy[all,preview]

OgreBotAPI.IM:End[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: Stops whatever the Inventory Manager is running and closes the window, the same as `ogre end im` and the window's X. It stops first, so a script polling IsOpen never reads FALSE while work is still going.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:End[all]

OgreBotAPI.IM:Examine[fw, box]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: Fills the named box of the window with the item in the open item examine window; you still pick the quantity and add it. It warns when no item examine window is open.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg box (string): restock or trade: the tab whose box it fills.
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Examine[all,restock]

OgreBotAPI.IM:Flags[fw, words...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: Takes the words no other method spells: a line wholly of mode flags is a chain, run in that order, with -end to close the window when it finishes. Any other line goes to the depot parser, which says what it cannot read.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg words... (string): The line, one argument each.
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Flags[all,-destroy,-tse,-end]

OgreBotAPI.IM:Help[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: Prints the `ogre im` usage to the console: the depot flags, every other mode, chains, the queue and the settings.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Help[all]

OgreBotAPI.IM:Open[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: Opens the Inventory Manager window on the characters named; calling it while the window is up just refreshes it. If the UI host is not available it prints a warning and IsOpen stays FALSE.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Open[${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.IM:Pane[fw, words...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: Builds the editor list for a tab and prints how many rows it holds: sell or destroy, destroy when no name is given. `sell reopen` opens the merchant again first if its window is shut, as the Sell list tab's Refresh button does.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg words... (string): The tab name, then reopen for sell. Optional.
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Pane[all,destroy]

OgreBotAPI.IM:Probe[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: Prints what the open depot's tier dropdown holds, for checking a depot window against the depot tables. It changes nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Probe[all]

OgreBotAPI.IM:Queue[fw, mode]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: Adds a mode to the run queue and brings the window up: it runs when the current work finishes. With no mode it prints what is waiting, and a word that is not a mode is refused.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg mode (string): depot, sell, destroy, tse, restock, trade or quiver. Optional.
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Queue[all,sell]

OgreBotAPI.IM:Reload[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: Reloads the depot tables from disk: the depot kinds, the ammo rows and the shared resource table.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Reload[all]

OgreBotAPI.IM:Restock[fw, words...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: The restock mode: with no words, or a profile name, it brings the window up and tops up from the depots, and -forwho <expr> runs it only on the characters named. A word short of its arguments is read as a profile name.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg words... (string): A profile, or one of stop, status, reload, list (or profiles), show <profile>, preview (or plan) [profile], set <profile> <qty> <item>, forwho <profile> <who> <item>, drop <profile> <item>. Optional.
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Restock[all,"Raid night",-forwho,${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.IM:Sell[fw, words...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: The sell mode: with no words it brings the window up and sells what is on the sell list, opening a nearby merchant if none is open. The other first words are in the param; any other words go to the run.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg words... (string): stop, status, reload, preview (or plan), list [all], add <name> or remove <name>, then its arguments. Optional.
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Sell[all,preview]

OgreBotAPI.IM:Settings[fw, words...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: With no words, prints the saved settings; too few words prints the usage and changes nothing. Otherwise it changes one setting, as the param says.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg words... (string): One of: bag <tse|destroy> <1-6|overseer|harvest|sharedtradeskill> <on|off>; tse <option> <on|off|number>; quiver <arrow|bolt|throwing> <name|clear|examine>; depot <flags>; reload. One argument each. Optional.
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Settings[all,tse,minlevel,120]

OgreBotAPI.IM:Status[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: Prints the session line to the console, then the chain if one runs and one summary line each for depot, sell, destroy, restock and trade. For one line a script can read, use ${OgreBotAPI.IM.Status}.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Status[all]

OgreBotAPI.IM:Stop[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: Stops whatever the Inventory Manager is running (the chain, every busy mode, or a depot withdraw still in flight) and leaves the window open. When nothing is running it prints "im: nothing is running." to the console.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Stop[igw:${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.IM:Trade[fw, words...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: The trade mode: with no words it brings the window up and runs the queue. The other first words are in the param.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg words... (string): add <player> <qty|all> <item>, remove <n> (or delete), list, clear, preview (or plan), status or stop, then its arguments. Optional.
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Trade[all,add,Tobbin,5,"Rare Ore"]

OgreBotAPI.IM:Transmute[fw, words...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: Brings the window up and transmutes one named item, or an item by id.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg words... (string): The item name or id. A name may be several arguments; they are joined with spaces.
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Transmute[all,"Rusted Greatsword"]

OgreBotAPI.IM:Tse[fw, words...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.IM
  what: The transmute, salvage and extract mode: `stop` stops it, and anything else brings the window up and runs. It starts from the options saved on the TSE tab, and flags such as -salvage or -stopafter 5 change that run.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg words... (string): stop, or the run's flags, one argument each. Optional.
  example: OgreBotAPI.IM:Tse[all,-stopafter,5]


== OgreBotAPI.Inventory ==

${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.AdornmentColour[iconId]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Looks up the colour of an adornment from its icon id, using the bot's built-in table of known adornment icons.
  arg iconId (number): the adornment's icon id
  returns: string - White, Red, Blue, Cyan, Green, Purple or Black. Empty when the icon id is not in the table.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.AdornmentColour[3877]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.AdornmentIconIDColour, OgreBotAPI.Get_AdornmentColour

${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.AdornToRemoveSlot[adorn]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: The reverse of AdornToSlot: takes the slot number out of an adornment entry name, so _ADORN_<slot>_<name> becomes _ADORN_<name>. Text that is not in that form comes back unchanged.
  arg adorn (text): the adornment entry name, _ADORN_<slot>_<name>
  returns: string - the entry name without the slot, or the input unchanged when it is not in the _ADORN_<slot>_<name> form.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.AdornToRemoveSlot["_ADORN_21_Raid Rune: Void Flow III"]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.ConvertAdornToRemoveSlot

${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.AdornToSlot[adorn, slot=21]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Puts a slot number into an adornment entry name: _ADORN_<name> becomes _ADORN_<slot>_<name>. Text that is not in the _ADORN_<name> form (with no other underscores) comes back unchanged.
  arg adorn (text): the adornment entry name, _ADORN_<name>
  arg slot (number, default: 21): the slot number to insert
  returns: string - the entry name with the slot inserted, or the input unchanged when it is not in the _ADORN_<name> form.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.AdornToSlot["_ADORN_Raid Rune: Void Flow III",21]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.ConvertAdornToSlot

${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.Count[itemName, exact|contains]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Counts how many of an item you are carrying, adding up every stack in your bags and your Harvest Bag. The name match ignores case; it is exact unless you pass contains.
  arg itemName (item name): the item to count
  arg exact|contains (text, default: exact): exact = the whole name must match, contains = any item whose name contains the text
  returns: int - the total quantity on hand. 0 when nothing matches, the name is empty, you are not in the world, or the match word is not exact or contains (that last case also prints a line).
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.Count[Ingot,contains]}
  oldbot: Obj_OgreUtilities.ItemCount, OgreBotAPI.ItemCount

${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.CurrentImmunityRune}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Names the immunity rune on the belt you are wearing; it only reads your own character. It needs the belt's item details: an empty answer means they are still loading (the read asks the game for them), so ask again shortly - never treat empty as no rune.
  returns: string - Stun, Stifle, Mez, Fear or Medic for the rune worn. Unknown when the details are loaded and no known rune is on the belt. Empty when the details are not loaded yet or you are not in the world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.CurrentImmunityRune}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_CurrentImmunityRune

${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.IsAdornmentColour[iconId, colour]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: TRUE when an adornment icon id is a known icon of the given colour. The colour match ignores case, and a blank colour means White.
  arg iconId (number): the adornment's icon id
  arg colour (text, default: White): White, Red, Blue, Cyan, Green, Purple or Black
  returns: bool - TRUE when the icon is in the table with that colour. FALSE when the colour differs or the icon id is not in the table.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.IsAdornmentColour[3877,White]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.IsAdornmentColour

${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.PackPonyRunning}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: TRUE while a pack pony run is in progress, whether CheckPackPony or the bot's own pack pony chore started it.
  returns: bool: TRUE while a pack pony run is in progress; FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.PackPonyRunning}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_APIPackPonyRunning, OgreBotAPI.Get_PackPonyRunning, OgreBotAPI.bAPIPackPonyRunning

${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.SlotAvailable[slot name]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: TRUE when the item worn in the named equipment slot can be used (activated) right now - for example, a clicky cloak on cooldown reads FALSE. It does not tell you whether the slot is empty or can hold an item.
  arg slot name (text): one of: primary, secondary, head, cloak, chest, shoulders, forearms, hands, legs, feet, left_ring, right_ring, ears, ears2, neck, left_wrist, right_wrist, ranged, ammo, waist, activate1, activate2, event_slot, food, drink (any case)
  returns: bool - TRUE when the item in that slot is usable now. FALSE when it is not, when the name is not one of the slot names (a warning is printed), or when the slot could not be read.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.SlotAvailable[cloak]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.EquipmentSlotAvailable

${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.SlotModifier[slot, modifier]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Reads one stat modifier from the item equipped in a slot, matching the modifier name without regard to case. It reads the item's detail record, which the game may have to fetch first, so it can return empty until that has loaded.
  arg slot (slot name or number): the equipment slot, as the game's equipment list accepts it
  arg modifier (text): the modifier name, e.g. Potency
  returns: string - the modifier's value. Empty when the item has no such modifier, its details are not loaded yet, or you are not in the world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.SlotModifier[primary,Potency]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_EquipmentModifierValue

${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.SlotName[n=1]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Turns one of the bot's slot numbers (1 to 22) into the bot's short slot name: primary, secondary, head, chest, shoulders, Forearms, Hands, legs, feet, LRing, RRing, ear, ear2, neck, lwrist, rwrist, ranged, ammo, waist, cloak, Activate1, Activate2.
  arg n (number, default: 1): the slot number, 1 to 22
  returns: string - the slot name. Empty when n is outside 1 to 22.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.SlotName[20]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_SlotNum_To_SlotNames, OgreBotAPI.SlotNum_SlotNames, OgreBotAPI.Slot_SlotNames

${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.SlotNumAvailable[slot number 1-22]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: The same check as SlotAvailable, with the slot given as a number from 1 to 22 in the bot's own numbering (not the game's equipment index): 1 primary, 2 secondary, 3 head, 4 chest, 5 shoulders, 6 forearms, 7 hands, 8 legs, 9 feet, 10 left_ring, 11 right_ring, 12 ears, 13 ears2, 14 neck, 15 left_wrist, 16 right_wrist, 17 ranged, 18 ammo, 19 waist, 20 cloak, 21 activate1, 22 activate2.
  arg slot number 1-22 (number): the slot, in the bot's numbering (whole digits only)
  returns: bool - TRUE when the item in that slot is usable now. FALSE when it is not, when the number is not 1 to 22 (a warning is printed), or when the slot could not be read. event_slot, food and drink have no number; use SlotAvailable for them.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.SlotNumAvailable[20]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.EquipmentSlotNumAvailable

${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.SlotUIName[n=1]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Turns one of the bot's slot numbers (1 to 22) into the slot's name as the game's character window spells it: primary, secondary, head, chest, shoulders, Forearms, Hands, legs, feet, left_ring, right_ring, ears, ears2, neck, left_wrist, right_wrist, ranged, ammo, waist, cloak, Activate1, Activate2.
  arg n (number, default: 1): the slot number, 1 to 22
  returns: string - the window's slot name. Empty when n is outside 1 to 22.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Inventory.SlotUIName[10]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_SlotNum_EQ2UIPageSlotNames, OgreBotAPI.SlotNum_EQ2UIPageSlotNames

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:AddEmbargo[fw, linkId, durationSec]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Stops the bot's casting from using an item, given by its LinkID, for a number of seconds (while item embargo is enabled in the bot's settings). Both arguments are required; a new embargo on the same item only ever extends it, and the signed and unsigned forms of a LinkID both work.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg linkId (number): the item's LinkID, a whole number from -2147483648 to 4294967295
  arg durationSec (number): how long, in seconds; 0 expires at once
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:AddEmbargo["all",-1112810742,30]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ItemEmbargo_AddRotateTimer

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:AutoConsumeFamiliarXP[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Uses "(Temporary 4 hour) Familiar Experience" from your bags up to 10 times, waiting while you are in combat or moving. Only one temporary auto-consume run (this, mount training or research) runs at a time; a new call replaces the one before.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:AutoConsumeFamiliarXP[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:AutoConsumeTemporaryFamiliarExperience

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:AutoConsumeFoodDrink[fw, value=TRUE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Turns auto-consume on or off for the food and drink in your equipped provision slots, flipping only a slot whose setting differs from what you asked. It is queued, with a 1-second pause after.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg value (true/false or word, default: TRUE): TRUE = on, FALSE = off, toggle = flip, report = change nothing; any other word means TRUE
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:AutoConsumeFoodDrink[igw:${Me.Name},TRUE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Change_FoodDrinkAutoConsume, OgreBotAPI:FoodDrink_AutoConsume

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:AutoConsumeMountTraining[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Checks that mount training is running, then uses "(Temporary 4 hour) Mount Training Reduction" from your bags up to 10 times, waiting while you are in combat or moving. If training is not running nothing is consumed; a new call replaces any temporary auto-consume run already going.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:AutoConsumeMountTraining[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:AutoConsumeTemporaryMountTrainingReduction

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:AutoConsumeResearch[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Uses "(Temporary 4 hour) Research Reduction" from your bags up to 10 times, waiting while you are in combat or moving. It opens the research window if needed and stops when research is complete or nothing is being researched; a new call replaces any temporary auto-consume run already going.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:AutoConsumeResearch[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:AutoConsumeTemporaryResearchReduction

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:AutoConsumeStatPotions[fw, value=TRUE, potion=""]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Turns auto-consume on or off for a stat potion in your bags (exact name); with no potion named it uses the bot's configured stat potion. It flips only when the setting differs from what you asked, is queued with a 1-second pause after, and prints a line if the potion is not in your bags.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg value (true/false or word, default: TRUE): TRUE = on, FALSE = off, toggle = flip, report = change nothing; any other word means TRUE
  arg potion (item name, default: ""): the potion; blank = the configured stat potion
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:AutoConsumeStatPotions[igw:${Me.Name},TRUE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Change_StatPotionsAutoConsume, OgreBotAPI:StatPotions_AutoConsume, OgreBotAPI:Change_PoisonAutoConsume

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:ChangeBeltAdorn[fw, adornType, unequip=TRUE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Applies an immunity rune from your bags to your belt; it is queued and refuses while you are moving or in combat. A rune it replaces is accepted back and moved next to where the new rune was.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg adornType (text): Stun, Stifle, Mez, Fear or Medic
  arg unequip (true/false, default: TRUE): TRUE takes the belt off, applies the rune and puts the belt back on; FALSE applies the rune to the worn belt
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:ChangeBeltAdorn[${Me.Name},Stun,TRUE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ChangeBeltAdorn

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:CheckGear[fw, threshold=100]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Checks the condition of the item in your primary slot and prints "<name> gear N%" when it is at or below the threshold (and always at 30, 20, 10 and 0). It is queued, waits up to 5 seconds for the item's details to load, and fires the gear-condition event on every check.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg threshold (number, default: 100): the percent at or below which to print; TRUE means 100
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:CheckGear[igw:${Me.Name},90]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CheckGear

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:CheckPackPony[fw, forceCheck=FALSE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Runs the Artisan's Pack Pony chore now: summons the pony, works through its conversation and dismisses it, pausing the bot for the run (and resuming it after, if it was not already paused). It does not need the pack pony settings enabled, but it waits out the re-check interval unless forced, and prints why if it cannot start (already running, not in the world, no pack pony ability, in combat).
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg forceCheck (true/false, default: FALSE): TRUE = run even within the re-check interval
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:CheckPackPony[${Me.Name},TRUE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CheckPackPony

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:ClearAllEmbargos[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Removes every item embargo. Ability embargoes are not touched.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:ClearAllEmbargos["all"]

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:ClearEmbargo[fw, linkId]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Removes the item embargo on one item, by the same LinkID AddEmbargo took. Does nothing if that item has no embargo.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg linkId (number): the item's LinkID
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:ClearEmbargo["all",-1112810742]

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:ConsumeFamiliars[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Goes through each familiar already loose in your bags: one not yet in your collection is added, one you already have is consumed for familiar experience. It does not unpack Familiar Cages - UnpackConsumeFamiliars does both.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:ConsumeFamiliars[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Consume_Familiars

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:ConsumeList[fw, -fc, -all, -st]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Runs the bot's Consume Items list once: it uses the first entry that is ready and in your bags, or every one with -all. It skips disabled entries, in-combat-only entries outside combat and entries whose own timer has not run out, and stops if you are dead or moving.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg -fc (flag): force combat: ignore the in-combat-only setting and the in-combat wait between items
  arg -all (flag): use every eligible entry, not just the first
  arg -st (flag): skip timers: ignore each item's own timer
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:ConsumeList[igw:${Me.Name},-all]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ConsumeItems_ProcessList

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:ConsumeStatusIngots[fw, amount=99999]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Targets yourself and consumes status ingots - every bag item whose name contains Ingot - by examining each and confirming, until the amount is used. An item that fails twice in a row is skipped (tradeskill ingots match the name too); it is queued, stops if you lose the target, makes at most 250 tries a run, and sends a finished line to every session.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg amount (number, default: 99999): how many to consume; 0 or less means all
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:ConsumeStatusIngots[${Me.Name},10]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Consume_Status_Ignots, OgreBotAPI:Consume_Status_Ingots

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:ConsumeStatusTokens[fw, amount=99999]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Targets yourself and consumes Status Token items, then Status Coin items, by examining each and confirming. Every try counts toward the amount whether or not it consumed one; it is queued, stops if you lose the target, makes at most 250 tries a run, and sends a finished line to every session.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg amount (number, default: 99999): how many tries to make; 0 or less means all
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:ConsumeStatusTokens[${Me.Name},10]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Consume_Status_Tokens

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:DestroyItem[fw, itemName, charges=0]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Destroys an item in your carried bags by name, but only when it has no charges or its charges equal the number you give, so a partly used charged item is kept. It is queued, waits a second for the item's details to load and refuses with a line if they did not arrive; the destroy cannot be undone.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg itemName (item name): the item to destroy
  arg charges (number, default: 0): the charge count the item must have to be destroyed
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:DestroyItem[${Me.Name},"Rusty Dagger",0]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:DestroyItem

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:DestroyItemNoChecks[fw, itemName]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Destroys an item in your carried bags (not the bank) whose name matches exactly, ignoring case - the whole stack, with no charge check. This cannot be undone; use DestroyItem to keep a partly used charged item safe.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg itemName (item name): the item to destroy
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:DestroyItemNoChecks[${Me.Name},"Rusty Dagger"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:DestroyItem_NoChecks

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:EquipCharm[fw, slot=1]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Equips the item set as charm option 1 or 2 in the bot's Equipment settings, finding it in your bags by name. This only asks the game to equip it; the game can still refuse (slot rules, relic limits).
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg slot (number, default: 1): which charm option to equip, 1 or 2
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:EquipCharm[igw:${Me.Name},2]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:EquipCharm

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:Examine[fw, item=DoesNotExist]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Opens the examine window for an item in your main bags, matched by exact name. Does nothing when no such item is there.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg item (item name, default: DoesNotExist): the item to examine
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:Examine[${Me.Name},"Spirit of the Cat"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ExamineInventoryItem, Obj_OgreIH:ExamineInventoryItem

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:ExamineAll[fw, item...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Examines every carried item whose name contains any of the given texts (main bags, Overseer Bag and Harvest Bag), each stack as many times as its quantity plus two, closing the examine window after each stack. It is queued and reads the bags when it runs; it prints a line if nothing matches.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg item... (item names): one or more name texts to match (contains, any case)
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:ExamineAll[${Me.Name},Potion]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ExamineAllOfItem

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:InitAdornmentInfo[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Fills the adornment icon colour table that AdornmentColour and IsAdornmentColour read. The table is filled automatically, so a script does not normally need this.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:InitAdornmentInfo[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Initialize_AdornmentInfo

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:RedeemKrono[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Redeems a Krono from the Krono page of your character window and confirms it, then prints whether it worked and fires the Krono redemption event. With no Krono to redeem it prints a line and stops.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:RedeemKrono[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:RedeemKrono

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:SpewSlotNames[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Prints one console line per gear slot 1 to 22: the slot number, the bot's name for that number, and the item equipped there (NULL when nothing reads).
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:SpewSlotNames[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Spew_SlotNum_To_SlotNames

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:Unpack[fw, item, ...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Unpacks an item in your bags (exact name), with flags after the item in any order: -qty N unpacks N (1 to 1000), -all keeps going until none is left (up to 1000), and -pick <number | name | lowest> chooses the reward when the window offers a choice (lowest = the choice you hold the fewest of). It is queued and waits out an open reward window; a bad flag is refused with one line before anything is queued.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg item (item name): the item to unpack
  arg ... (flags): -qty N or -all, and -pick <number | name | lowest>
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:Unpack[${Me.Name},"Reward Crate",-all,-pick,lowest]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Unpack, OgreBotAPI:Unpack_EmpyralStones, OgreBotAPI:Unpack_PlanarStones

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:UnpackConsumeFamiliars[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Unpacks every Familiar Cage in your bags, then goes through each familiar in your bags: one not yet in your collection is added, one you already have is consumed for familiar experience (summoning a familiar if one is needed). A finished line is sent to every session when it is done.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:UnpackConsumeFamiliars[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Unpack_Consume_Familiars

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:UnpackFamiliars[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Unpacks every Familiar Cage in your bags, one at a time (up to 20). It is queued, and prints a line if there is no Familiar Cage.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:UnpackFamiliars[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Unpack_Familiars

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:UpgradeItem[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Moves the adornments from the old item in bag 1 slot 1 onto the new item in bag 1 slot 2, moves the old item to the end of bag 1 and equips the new one. Both must be for the same slot and the new one must have no adornments; an adornment with no free slot of its colour goes back on the old item.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:UpgradeItem[${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:Use[fw, item, ...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Uses an item by name: equipped items (gear, food and drink) are checked first, then your carried bags (exact name, any case). The use is queued and fires when the cast bar is free; an item that is not found prints a line, and an empty name or Nothing does nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg item (item name): the item to use
  arg ... (any): extra arguments are ignored
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:Use[${Me.Name},"Spirit of the Cat"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:UseItem

OgreBotAPI.Inventory:UseOnPlayer[fw, item, player=me, ...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Inventory
  what: Uses an item on another player: it targets that player, uses the item (equipped first, then bags) and puts your old target back. It does nothing if the item is on cooldown, if an effect the item is known to give is already maintained by you, or if the cast bar is busy; an item or player that is not found prints a line.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg item (item name): the item to use
  arg player (player name or actor id, default: me): who to use it on
  arg ... (any): extra arguments are ignored
  example: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:UseOnPlayer[${Me.Name},"Spirit of the Cat",${Target.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:UseItemOnPlayer


== OgreBotAPI.Loot ==

${OgreBotAPI.Loot.ItemCount}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Loot
  what: How many distinct item names have a SmartLoot cap in the loaded loot files. It is 0 until the loot files have been loaded.
  returns: int: the number of capped item names; 0 when nothing is loaded.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Loot.ItemCount}

${OgreBotAPI.Loot.Loaded}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Loot
  what: TRUE once the SmartLoot item caps file has been read, which happens on every profile load and on :Load or :Reload. Answers about this session only.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the item caps file (ItemLootData) was read; FALSE before a load or when that file is missing or unreadable.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Loot.Loaded}

${OgreBotAPI.Loot.WindowExists}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Loot
  what: Whether a loot window is open on this session. With two loot windows open it answers about the topmost one.
  returns: bool: TRUE when a loot window is open; FALSE when none is.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Loot.WindowExists}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.LootWindowExists

${OgreBotAPI.Loot.WindowID}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Loot
  what: The id of the open loot window, or 0 when there is none. With two loot windows open it is the topmost one.
  returns: int64: the loot window id; 0 when no loot window is open.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Loot.WindowID}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_LootWindowID

OgreBotAPI.Loot:BuildToonItemsToBeZeroed[fw, toon, item, ...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Loot
  what: Adds character and item pairs to a list of SmartLoot counts to reset to 0, ready for :ProcessToonItemsToBeZeroed. It can be called several times to build a long list, and a character left without an item is dropped with a warning.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg toon (string): the character whose count for the item is reset
  arg item (string): the item name for that character; colour codes are removed
  arg ... (string): more character and item pairs, in the same order
  example: OgreBotAPI.Loot:BuildToonItemsToBeZeroed[${Me.Name},${Me.Name},"Gleaming Crown",${Group[1].Name},"Gleaming Crown"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:SmartLoot_BuildToonItemsToBeZeroed

OgreBotAPI.Loot:Config[fw, mode=open]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Loot
  what: Opens the SmartLoot config panel, or closes it when mode is close. Opening a panel that is already open does nothing, so unsaved edits in it are kept.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg mode (string, default: open): close closes the panel; any other value opens it
  example: OgreBotAPI.Loot:Config[${Me.Name},close]

OgreBotAPI.Loot:Decide[fw, execute=FALSE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Loot
  what: Works out what SmartLoot would do with every open loot window in turn and prints the plan for each item of a Leader Only one; by default it is a dry run that clicks nothing. With execute it records the counts and assigns or loots for real on the next pulse, and it does nothing but print a line when OgreBot has no profile, is paused or has no loot window open, or for each window that is not Leader Only.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg execute (bool, default: FALSE): execute, force or a true word (TRUE, 1, yes, on) performs the plan; anything else, or nothing, is a dry run
  example: OgreBotAPI.Loot:Decide[${Me.Name},execute]

OgreBotAPI.Loot:LootAll[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Loot
  what: Clicks Loot All on the open loot window. Does nothing when no loot window is open.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Loot:LootAll[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:LootWindowLootAll

OgreBotAPI.Loot:Migrate[fw, overwrite=FALSE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Loot
  what: Converts the older XML loot files into the JSON loot store and prints how many files were written, blocked or missing. JSON files that already exist are left alone unless overwrite is given, and the loot data is reloaded when anything was written.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg overwrite (bool, default: FALSE): overwrite, force or a true word (TRUE, 1, yes, on) replaces JSON files that already exist; anything else leaves them alone
  example: OgreBotAPI.Loot:Migrate[${Me.Name},overwrite]

OgreBotAPI.Loot:ProcessToonItemsToBeZeroed[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Loot
  what: Sets every collected character and item count to 0, which makes those characters eligible for the item again, saves the loot counts file and empties the list. It prints how many were reset, and with nothing collected or an unreadable counts file it saves nothing and says so.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Loot:ProcessToonItemsToBeZeroed[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:SmartLoot_ProcessToonItemsToBeZeroed

OgreBotAPI.Loot:Reload[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Loot
  what: Reads the SmartLoot item caps and per-character loot counts from the saved loot files again and prints the cap count. Use it after editing the loot files by hand.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Loot:Reload[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:SmartLoot_ReloadDataFromFile

OgreBotAPI.Loot:ResetLootedActors[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Loot
  what: Forgets which actors auto-loot has already looted or opened, so the next scan can try them again. The same reset happens by itself on every zone change.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Loot:ResetLootedActors[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ResetActorsLooted

OgreBotAPI.Loot:SetAutoLootMode[fw, mode]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Loot
  what: Sets this character's own auto-loot mode in the game, 0 none, 1 auto-greed or 2 auto-decline; out of the world nothing is sent. A missing mode prints a console line and sends nothing, and any other value sets 0 with a line saying so.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg mode (text): 0, 1 or 2, or the words AN, AG or AD that Loot:SetOptions takes
  example: OgreBotAPI.Loot:SetAutoLootMode[${Me.Name},1]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:SetAutoLootMode

OgreBotAPI.Loot:SetOptions[fw, token, ...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Loot
  what: Sets the group loot method, rarity and auto-loot mode from short loot words, one per argument and in any order; a kind you do not name is left as it is. The group leader opens the group options window and applies them through the action queue, while anyone else only sets their own auto-loot mode; out of the world nothing is sent.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg token (string): one loot word: method LO, FFA, Lotto, NBG or RR (the long names such as Leader Only or Round Robin work too); rarity All, T, L or F (with or without +); auto-loot AN, AG or AD. An unknown word is ignored with a console warning
  arg ... (string): more loot words of the same kinds
  example: OgreBotAPI.Loot:SetOptions[${Me.Name},LO,T+,AN]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ChangeLootOptions


== OgreBotAPI.Merchant ==

OgreBotAPI.Merchant:Buy[fw, item, qty=1]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Merchant
  what: With a merchant window already open, buys qty of the named item from the merchant's list, right away, and accepts the purchase prompt if one comes up. No item, no merchant window, or an item the merchant does not carry each get one line.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg item (string): Name of the item on the merchant's list
  arg qty (int, default: 1): How many to buy
  example: OgreBotAPI.Merchant:Buy[${Me.Name},"Fishing Bait",20]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:BuyFromMerchant, Obj_OgreIH:BuyFromMerchant

OgreBotAPI.Merchant:OpenAndBuy[fw, merchant, item, qty=1]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Merchant
  what: Queued: opens the merchant window by double-clicking the nearest actor whose name contains merchant (unless a merchant window is already open), waits up to 3 seconds for it, buys qty of item and accepts the purchase confirmation. A missing name prints a console line, a window that never opens or an item the merchant does not carry prints a line and buys nothing, and no matching actor stops it silently.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg merchant (string): Name (or part of the name) of the merchant to open
  arg item (string): Name of the item on the merchant's list
  arg qty (int, default: 1): How many to buy
  example: OgreBotAPI.Merchant:OpenAndBuy[${Me.Name},"Provisioner","Fishing Bait",20]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:OpenAndBuyFromMerchant

OgreBotAPI.Merchant:OpenAndBuyXTimes[fw, merchant, item, qty, times]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Merchant
  what: Queued: does OpenAndBuy times times in a row - each round opens the merchant if needed, buys qty of item and accepts the confirmation. A missing merchant or item name, or times of 0 or less, prints a console line and nothing runs.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg merchant (string): Name (or part of the name) of the merchant to open
  arg item (string): Name of the item on the merchant's list
  arg qty (int): How many to buy each round (1 when blank)
  arg times (int): How many rounds to buy (1 when blank)
  example: OgreBotAPI.Merchant:OpenAndBuyXTimes[${Me.Name},"Provisioner","Fishing Bait",100,3]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:OpenAndBuyFromMerchantXTimes

OgreBotAPI.Merchant:Repair[fw, force=FALSE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Merchant
  what: Queued: unless force is TRUE, checks your primary and chest items and stops with "no repair needed" when both are at 100% condition. Otherwise finds a known mender within 10m (prints "no mender within 10m" if none), stops auto-attack, opens it, repairs everything and closes the window.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg force (bool, default: FALSE): TRUE to repair even when primary and chest are already at 100%
  example: OgreBotAPI.Merchant:Repair[igw:${Me.Name},FALSE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:RepairGear

OgreBotAPI.Merchant:Sell[fw, item, qty=1]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Merchant
  what: With a merchant window already open, sells qty of the named item from your bags, right away. No item, no merchant window, or an item not in the sell list each get one line.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg item (string): Name of the item in your bags
  arg qty (int, default: 1): How many to sell
  example: OgreBotAPI.Merchant:Sell[${Me.Name},"Rough Ruby",5]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:SellToMerchant, Obj_OgreIH:SellToMerchant


== OgreBotAPI.Movement ==

${OgreBotAPI.Movement.Active}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: TRUE while the bot's mover is driving your character anywhere. That includes Movement:ToLoc, Come2Me and Move2Area, but also follow, the camp spot and nav trips.
  returns: bool: TRUE while a move is in progress; FALSE when the mover is idle.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Movement.Active}

${OgreBotAPI.Movement.AllowMovement}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: TRUE when no movement block is held, the exact opposite of Blocked with no reason. It does not count the camp spot holds left by Come2Me, Move2Area or JoustIn.
  returns: bool: TRUE when no block is held; FALSE when at least one is.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Movement.AllowMovement}
  oldbot: Obj_CampSpot.AllowCampSpot, Obj_Movement.AllowCampSpot, Ogre_CampSpot.AllowCampSpot

${OgreBotAPI.Movement.AlreadyFacing[id]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: TRUE when your heading is within 45 degrees of the heading to the actor with this ID. FALSE when you are not in the world or the actor is not known.
  arg id (int64): The actor ID to measure against (a number, such as ${Target.ID}). A name is not looked up.
  returns: bool: TRUE when you are roughly facing the actor; FALSE when you are not, are not in the world, or the actor is not known.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Movement.AlreadyFacing[${Target.ID}]}

${OgreBotAPI.Movement.BehindLoc[id,dist]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: A point the given distance directly behind the actor, based on the way the actor is facing, at the actor's height. Returns an empty string when the actor is not found.
  arg id (int64): The actor ID to measure against (a number, such as ${Target.ID}). A name is not looked up.
  arg dist (float, default: 5): How far from the actor the point is, in meters.
  returns: string: "x,y,z" behind the actor; "" when the actor is not found.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Movement.BehindLoc[${Target.ID},5]}

${OgreBotAPI.Movement.BlockCount}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: How many different movement blocks are held right now. Adding the same reason twice counts once.
  returns: int: the number of distinct block reasons held; 0 when movement is free.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Movement.BlockCount}
  oldbot: Obj_CampSpot.uAllowMovement, Obj_Movement.uAllowMovement, Ogre_CampSpot.uAllowMovement

${OgreBotAPI.Movement.Blocked[reason]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: With a reason, TRUE when that named movement block is held; with the reason left blank, TRUE when any block is held. Reason names are case-sensitive, and the bot's own movers add blocks too while they run.
  arg reason (string): The block name to check, as given to Movement:Block. Leave it blank to ask whether any block is held.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the named block (or, with no reason, any block) is held; FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Movement.Blocked[MyScript]}
  oldbot: Obj_CampSpot.Disabled, Obj_Movement.Disabled, Ogre_CampSpot.Disabled

${OgreBotAPI.Movement.BlockReasons}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: The names of every movement block held right now, so you can see what is stopping a character. This includes blocks the bot's own movers hold while they run.
  returns: string: the block reasons separated by commas; "" when no block is held.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Movement.BlockReasons}
  oldbot: Obj_CampSpot.sc_ItemsAffectingMovement, Obj_Movement.sc_ItemsAffectingMovement, Ogre_CampSpot.sc_ItemsAffectingMovement

${OgreBotAPI.Movement.Distance2DTo[id]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: The flat distance from you to the actor with this ID, ignoring height (X and Z only). Returns -1 when the ID is 0, is not a number, or no such actor is nearby.

OgreBotAPI.Movement:Block[fw, reason]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: Adds a named movement block and stops the move in progress. While any block is held the camp spot, follow, new nav trips and queued moves all stay still, but a direct Movement:ToLoc, Come2Me or Move2Area still moves; a blank reason prints a line and adds nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg reason (string): A name for this block, so Movement:Unblock can release exactly this one. Case-sensitive.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Movement:Block[${Me.Name},MyScript]
  oldbot: Obj_CampSpot:Disable, Obj_Movement:Disable, Ogre_CampSpot:Disable

  example: OgreBotAPI.Movement:CallGH[${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Movement:Come2Me[fw, toWho=me, precision=3]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: Runs to where the named character is standing at the moment of the call, stopping within the precision; it needs OgreBot open (or Movement:UseWithoutOgreBot) and prints a line when it is not, and a character with Allow Camp Spot off stays put and prints a line. On arrival the character stays there instead of going back to its camp spot until JoustOut or LetsGo, a name that matches nobody here prints a line and does nothing, and after 10 seconds stuck the move stops with one line.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg toWho (string, default: me): Who to run to: a name (part of a name works), an actor ID or an @ alias. Blank means yourself.
  arg precision (float, default: 3): How close counts as arrived, in meters.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Movement:Come2Me[${Me.Name},${Group[1].Name},3]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Come2Me

OgreBotAPI.Movement:Evac[fw, mode=""]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: Queues your class evacuation spell when you have one and it is ready (Escape for scouts, Shadowy Elusion for Shadowknights, Depart for Wizards, Verdurous Journey for Wardens). With mode totem, a character without a ready class evac uses a Totem of Escape from its bags instead, and prints a line when it has none or it is on cooldown; without totem it prints one line saying why it did not evacuate.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
