OgreBotAPI.Movement:FaceLoc[fw, x, y, z]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: Turns you to face the location using X and Z; the height is not used. A missing x or z prints an error, and nothing turns while a face lock is held.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg x (float or name): X of the location, or the whole location as one word: the name of a point of interest in this zone, or x,y,z. An unknown name prints one line and does nothing.
  arg y (float): Y (height). Ignored - a heading is flat - and kept so a location pastes in as x,y,z (${Me.Loc} as is).
  arg z (float): Z of the location. Not read when x holds the whole location.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Movement:FaceLoc[${Me.Name},100,20,-250]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:FaceLoc, Obj_OgreIH:FaceLoc

OgreBotAPI.Movement:FaceLock[fw, nameOrId, ttlSeconds=0]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: Turns you to the actor and holds that heading, turning again when you drift more than 45 degrees (at most once a second); while held, nothing else can turn you, movement waits and the game's /follow is stopped. The lock ends after ttlSeconds, on Movement:FaceUnlock, LetsGo, zoning, death or camping, or when the actor is gone, and an actor that is not found takes no lock.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg nameOrId (string): The actor's exact name, its actor ID, or an @ alias.
  arg ttlSeconds (int, default: 0): How long the lock lasts, in seconds. 0 or blank means 15; the most is 120.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Movement:FaceLock[${Me.Name},${Target.ID},10]

OgreBotAPI.Movement:FaceLockLoc[fw, x, z, ttlSeconds=0]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: Turns you toward the location and holds that heading, the same way Movement:FaceLock does for an actor. A missing x or z prints an error, and the lock ends after ttlSeconds, on Movement:FaceUnlock, LetsGo, zoning, death or camping.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg x (float or name): X of the location to face, or the whole location as one word: the name of a point of interest in this zone, or x,y,z. An unknown name prints one line and does nothing.
  arg z (float): Z of the location to face. Not read when x holds the whole location.
  arg ttlSeconds (int, default: 0): How long the lock lasts, in seconds. 0 or blank means 15; the most is 120.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Movement:FaceLockLoc[${Me.Name},100,-250,10]

OgreBotAPI.Movement:Follow[fw, leader=off, minDistance=8, maxDistance=200, breakWithNoTarget=FALSE, backOffDistance=0]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: Follows the leader with the bot's own follow, moving up when farther than minDistance and stopping when the leader is beyond maxDistance; it stops the game's /follow and needs OgreBot open (or Movement:UseWithoutOgreBot) to start. A leader of off, blank or your own name turns follow off, as does off given as the for-who; an unknown leader or bad distances print a line.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg leader (string, default: off): Who to follow: a character name, an actor ID, or off to stop following.
  arg minDistance (float, default: 8): Follow moves up when the leader is farther than this, in meters. Must be above 0.
  arg maxDistance (float, default: 200): Follow stops chasing when the leader is this far or farther. Must be above minDistance.
  arg breakWithNoTarget (bool, default: FALSE): TRUE to turn follow off the first time it needs to move up while you have no target.
  arg backOffDistance (float, default: 0): Back away from a leader closer than this, in meters. 0 is off; otherwise at least 1 less than minDistance.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Movement:Follow[${Me.Name},${Group[1].Name},8,200,FALSE,0]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:OFollow

OgreBotAPI.Movement:FollowDistanceDown[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: Takes 2 meters off the follow distances: minDistance never goes below 1, and maxDistance is left alone when minDistance hits that floor. A back-off distance shrinks with them and turns off when there is no room left.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Movement:FollowDistanceDown[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:OFolDecDistance

OgreBotAPI.Movement:FollowDistanceUp[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: Adds 2 meters to both follow distances (and to the back-off distance when one is set).
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Movement:FollowDistanceUp[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:OFolIncDistance

OgreBotAPI.Movement:JumpRoute[fw, start, jump, end, completed="", flag...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: Walks to start, then on to end, pressing jump once when passing within 2 meters of the jump point, and on arrival sets the camp spot to completed (or to end). It runs in the background and gives up after 10 seconds by default; a bad point or flag, or a route already running, prints why.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg start (string): The first point to walk to, as "x,y,z".
  arg jump (string): Where to jump on the way to end, as "x,y,z".
  arg end (string): Where the route ends, as "x,y,z".
  arg completed (string, default: ""): The camp spot to set on arrival, as "x,y,z". Blank, or an X of 0, uses end.
  arg flag... (string): Optional flags, one per argument, each followed by its value: -JumpDistance meters (default 2), -MaxTimer seconds per try (default 10), -Attempts 1 to 10, -RetryDelay seconds, -AboveY height that counts as success, -RunMode walk or run.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Movement:JumpRoute[${Me.Name},"100,20,-250","104,20,-246","110,25,-240","",-JumpDistance,1,-MaxTimer,12]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Set_CampSpotJump_Handle, Obj_CampSpotJump:Handle, Obj_CampSpotJump:HandleAdvanced

OgreBotAPI.Movement:NavTo[fw, x, y, z, mode=walk]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: Starts a nav trip over the navmesh to the location, replacing any trip under way; it waits while OgreBot is paused and stops when OgreBot closes. It leaves an encounter's trip alone and prints a line saying so, a missing x, y or z or one that is not a number prints an error, and a trip that cannot start prints why.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg x (float or name): X of the location, or the whole location as one word: the name of a point of interest in this zone, or x,y,z. An unknown name prints one line and does nothing.
  arg y (float): Y (height) of the location. Not read when x holds the whole location.
  arg z (float): Z of the location. Not read when x holds the whole location.
  arg mode (string, default: walk): fly to fly there; any other word walks.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Movement:NavTo[${Me.Name},100,20,-250,walk]
  oldbot: call Obj_OgreUtilities.NavTo, call Obj_OgreUtilities.NavToLoc

OgreBotAPI.Movement:SetRunMode[fw, run]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: Sets running (TRUE) or walking (FALSE), pressing the game's run toggle only when the current mode is the other one. A blank value, or a word that is not yes or no, prints a line and changes nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg run (bool): TRUE to run, FALSE to walk. Required.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Movement:SetRunMode[${Me.Name},TRUE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:RunWalk

OgreBotAPI.Movement:Stand[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: Stands you up when you are feigning death. Does nothing otherwise.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Movement:Stand[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Stand

OgreBotAPI.Movement:Stop[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: Stops the move in progress right away and lets go of the movement keys. Follow, the camp spot or a nav trip can start a new move on their next pulse, so use Movement:Block to keep a character still.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Movement:Stop[${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Movement:StopFollow[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: Pauses follow (the leader is kept), stops the game's /follow and stops the move in progress right away. LetsGo, JoustIn or a new Movement:Follow resumes follow, and the camp spot still pulls the character back.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Movement:StopFollow[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:HoldUp, OgreBotAPI:NoMove

OgreBotAPI.Movement:StopJumpRoute[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: Stops the jump route that is running. Does nothing when none is running.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Movement:StopJumpRoute[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: Obj_CampSpotJump:Stop

OgreBotAPI.Movement:ToLoc[fw, x, y, z, precision=0]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: Runs straight to the location and stops once within the precision, measured flat (X and Z); it returns at once and the move carries on in the background, with OgreBot closed too (Movement:Stop ends it). A missing x, y or z, or one that is not a number, prints an error and does nothing, and the move does not hold the camp spot, so a character with a camp spot can walk back afterwards.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg x (float or name): X of the location, or the whole location as one word: the name of a point of interest in this zone, or x,y,z. An unknown name prints one line and does nothing.
  arg y (float): Y (height) of the location. Not read when x holds the whole location.
  arg z (float): Z of the location. Not read when x holds the whole location.
  arg precision (float, default: 0): How close counts as arrived, in meters. 0 or blank uses 2.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Movement:ToLoc[${Me.Name},100,20,-250,3]

OgreBotAPI.Movement:Unblock[fw, reason]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: Releases the named movement block and leaves any others in place. A reason that is not held does nothing; a blank reason prints a line.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg reason (string): The block name given to Movement:Block. Case-sensitive.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Movement:Unblock[${Me.Name},MyScript]
  oldbot: Obj_CampSpot:Enable, Obj_Movement:Enable, Ogre_CampSpot:Enable

OgreBotAPI.Movement:UseWithoutOgreBot[fw, 1|0=0]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: Lets Come2Me, Move2Area, follow and the camp spot move the character while OgreBot is not open (1 or TRUE), or puts back the need for OgreBot to be open (0 or FALSE). Left blank it turns the option off, a word that is not yes or no leaves it as it is, and it lasts until the session ends.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg 1|0 (bool, default: 0): 1 or TRUE to allow movement without OgreBot open; 0 or FALSE to require OgreBot.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Movement:UseWithoutOgreBot[${Me.Name},1]

OgreBotAPI.Movement:Waypoint[fw, x, y, z]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Movement
  what: Sends the game's /waypoint command for the location, which shows the in-game waypoint trail to it. A missing x, y or z prints an error and does nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg x (float or name): X of the location, or the whole location as one word: the name of a point of interest in this zone, or x,y,z. An unknown name prints one line and does nothing.
  arg y (float): Y (height) of the location. Not read when x holds the whole location.
  arg z (float): Z of the location. Not read when x holds the whole location.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Movement:Waypoint[${Me.Name},100,20,-250]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Waypoint


== OgreBotAPI.Options ==

${OgreBotAPI.Options.Value[id]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Options
  what: Reads a stored OgreBot option for this character by its control id, matching the id in any case. Needs no for-who; an id the profile does not hold reads the same as an empty value.
  arg id (string): The option's control id, as saved in the profile
  returns: string: the option's current value (a checkbox reads TRUE or FALSE); "" when the id is absent, empty, or no id is given
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Options.Value[checkbox_settings_enable_chatevents]}
  oldbot: OgreOSA.Enabled, OgreOSA.ScanRadius, OgreOSA.TargetsOnly

OgreBotAPI.Options:LoadProfile[fw, name]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Options
  what: Loads the named OgreBot profile for this character, opening OgreBot first if it is not open; Use_UI reloads the current profile. A missing name gets one line and loads nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg name (string): Profile name, or Use_UI for the current profile. Required.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Options:LoadProfile[${Me.Name},Raid]
  oldbot: ProfileConfig:LoadProfileForWho, OgreBotAPI:LoadProfile, ProfileConfig:LoadProfile

OgreBotAPI.Options:Revert[fw, source]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Options
  what: Puts back every option that scripts, commands or encounters changed since the last revert, then forgets those changes; changes you made yourself in the OgreBot window are never reverted. Prints "options: reverted N" with the source in the console.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg source (string): Which writer's changes to put back: an encounter's key, command for typed and script changes, or all / empty for every source
  example: OgreBotAPI.Options:Revert[${Me.Name},all]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:RevertOptions, Obj_LICH:HODefaultSettings

OgreBotAPI.Options:Set[fw, silent|loud|verbose="", (id,value)..., silent=FALSE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Options
  what: Writes one or more OgreBot options by control id in the loaded profile, prints each real change in OgreConsole unless silenced, and remembers the old value so Revert can put it back. The write is unsaved until Save, and does nothing when no profile is loaded.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg silent|loud|verbose (string, default: ""): Optional, before an id: silent turns the change lines off, loud or verbose turns them on
  arg (id,value)... (string): Pairs of control id and new value; a TRUE or FALSE after a value, with more pairs after it, sets silent too
  arg silent (bool, default: FALSE): A TRUE or FALSE at the very end: TRUE makes the whole call silent
  example: OgreBotAPI.Options:Set[all,checkbox_settings_enable_chatevents,TRUE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ChangeOgreBotUIOption, OgreBotAPI:UplinkOptionChange, Obj_OgreUtilities:Set_EQ2_onQuestOffered

OgreBotAPI.Options:WarnBeforeSave[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Options
  what: Shows a warning beside Save in this character's OgreBot window saying the Instance Controller has run and settings may have changed, until a profile is loaded. Save still works while it is up; the Instance Controller sends this to its group itself.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Options:WarnBeforeSave[igw:${Me.Name}]


== OgreBotAPI.Overseer ==

OgreBotAPI.Overseer:AddAgents[fw, destroy=TRUE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Overseer
  what: Adds every Overseer agent card in your bags and Overseer bag to your agent collection, one card per pulse, and prints a count of added, duplicate, converted and destroyed cards when done. With destroy TRUE a duplicate is converted when that gives items and destroyed otherwise (one whose item details do not load in time is left); with FALSE duplicates are kept, and a second call while a pass runs is refused with a console warning.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg destroy (bool, default: TRUE): TRUE converts or destroys duplicate cards; FALSE keeps them (any word that is not a yes word counts as FALSE)
  example: OgreBotAPI.Overseer:AddAgents[igw:${Me.Name},FALSE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Overseer_AddAgentsToCollection

OgreBotAPI.Overseer:AutoAddQuests[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Overseer
  what: Uses every Overseer mission scroll in your bags and Overseer bag - the same add pass the daily run does, on its own. It is refused with a console warning while the daily run or another add pass is going.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Overseer:AutoAddQuests[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Overseer_AutoAddOverseerQuests

OgreBotAPI.Overseer:BuyMissions[fw, flag...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Overseer
  what: Queues an Overseer mission buy run at the merchant, started on the next pulse; with no flags it uses this character's own Overseer Buy tab, and flags such as -season 3, -colour Blue, -num 2, -amount 5, -replenishonly, -noscribe or -destroy override it, each as its own argument (a first word that is not a flag gets one line and starts nothing, a later unknown word is skipped). It needs OgreBot open with a profile loaded and is refused with a console warning when a buy run is already going, and a second call before the next pulse replaces the first.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg flag... (string): Option flags for the run, one per argument, with a flag's value as the next argument (-season, 3); none uses this character's Overseer Buy tab
  example: OgreBotAPI.Overseer:BuyMissions[igw:${Me.Name},-replenishonly]

OgreBotAPI.Overseer:CheckQuests[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Overseer
  what: Starts the daily Overseer run now instead of waiting for the bot to start it; the run then works through its steps on the pulse. It is refused with a console warning when a run or an add-missions pass is already going or when 'Do not touch overseer at all no matter what' is ticked, and with OgreBot closed it runs on the default options.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Overseer:CheckQuests[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Overseer_CheckQuests


== OgreBotAPI.Paths ==

${OgreBotAPI.Paths.Count}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Paths
  what: How many saved paths the zone you are in has. It reads 0 in a zone with none, while you are not settled in a zone and while the travel data loads.
  returns: int: the current zone's saved paths.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Paths.Count}

${OgreBotAPI.Paths.Running}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Paths
  what: TRUE while a path is being walked on this character, a Paths:Start walk or AutoHunt's. It is FALSE again once the walk finishes, is stopped or ends at a zone.
  returns: bool: TRUE while a walk is in flight on this character.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Paths.Running}

OgreBotAPI.Paths:AddPoint[fw, name, point]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Paths
  what: Adds a point to the end of a saved path of the zone you are in, and a new name makes the path, walked by nav with no loop. A POI name is not looked up here, so its POI can come later: Paths:Start checks every point.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names. Paths are shared by every box on the PC, so a line that reaches several boxes names one, or each box it lands on does it.
  arg name (string): The path's name, in any case.
  arg point (string): A POI name, or x,y,z. A script that writes x,y,z without quotes gets the same point.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Paths:AddPoint[${Me.Name},autohuntpath1,bell]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:AutoHunt_AddPath, OgreBotAPI:AutoHunt_AddPoint

OgreBotAPI.Paths:Clear[fw, name]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Paths
  what: Takes every point off a saved path of the zone you are in. The path stays, with its mover and its loop setting.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names. Paths are shared by every box on the PC, so a line that reaches several boxes names one, or each box it lands on does it.
  arg name (string): The path's name, in any case.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Paths:Clear[${Me.Name},autohuntpath1]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:AutoHunt_ClearPoints

OgreBotAPI.Paths:Delete[fw, name]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Paths
  what: Deletes a saved path of the zone you are in. An unknown name prints one line and changes nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names. Paths are shared by every box on the PC, so a line that reaches several boxes names one, or each box it lands on does it.
  arg name (string): The path's name, in any case.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Paths:Delete[${Me.Name},autohuntpath1]

OgreBotAPI.Paths:InsertPoint[fw, name, at, point]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Paths
  what: Puts a point into a saved path of the zone you are in at a place in the list, and the point at that place and the ones after it move down one. An unknown path, a place outside the list or a point that cannot be one prints one line and changes nothing, and a walk under way keeps the points it had at its Start.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names. Paths are shared by every box on the PC, so a line that reaches several boxes names one, or each box it lands on does it.
  arg name (string): The path's name, in any case. It must exist: a place is a place in a list, so this never makes a path.
  arg at (number): The place the point takes, counted from 1. One past the last point puts it on the end.
  arg point (string): A POI name, or x,y,z. A script that writes x,y,z without quotes gets the same point.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Paths:InsertPoint[${Me.Name},autohuntpath1,2,bell]

OgreBotAPI.Paths:MovePoint[fw, name, from, to]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Paths
  what: Moves a point of a saved path of the zone you are in to another place in the list, and the points between shift one place. An unknown path or a place outside the list prints one line and changes nothing, and a walk under way keeps the points it had at its Start.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names. Paths are shared by every box on the PC, so a line that reaches several boxes names one, or each box it lands on does it.
  arg name (string): The path's name, in any case.
  arg from (number): The place of the point to move, counted from 1.
  arg to (number): The place it ends at, counted from 1. Moving a point to the place it holds changes nothing.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Paths:MovePoint[${Me.Name},autohuntpath1,5,2]

OgreBotAPI.Paths:RemovePoint[fw, name, point]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Paths
  what: Takes the first point of that text off a saved path of the zone you are in, so a path that passes a point twice keeps the later one. An unknown path or point prints one line and changes nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names. Paths are shared by every box on the PC, so a line that reaches several boxes names one, or each box it lands on does it.
  arg name (string): The path's name, in any case.
  arg point (string): The point as the path holds it, in any case: a POI name, or x,y,z.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Paths:RemovePoint[${Me.Name},autohuntpath1,bell]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:AutoHunt_RemovePoint

OgreBotAPI.Paths:Start[fw, name]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Paths
  what: Walks a saved path of the zone you are in, point by point, by the path's own mover, in place of any walk under way and through a pause of OgreBot; a point that does not resolve stops it before anything moves, and OgreBot must be open. It waits while something else has the character (a fight, a death, an AutoHunt pull, a movement block) and goes on from the same point, and one line says when it finishes, cannot reach a point, or ends at a zone or OgreBot closing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg name (string): The path's name, in any case. A path of one point goes there and finishes, looping or not. A path walked by camp spot leaves the camp spot at its last point when it finishes, and no earlier camp spot comes back.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Paths:Start[${Me.Name},autohuntpath1]

OgreBotAPI.Paths:Stop[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Paths
  what: Stops the path being walked, a Paths:Start walk or AutoHunt's: the character stands where it is, and a walk by camp spot has its camp spot cleared. With no walk it prints one line.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Paths:Stop[${Me.Name}]


== OgreBotAPI.Pet ==

OgreBotAPI.Pet:Assist[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Pet
  what: Sends the game command /pet autoassist right away, which toggles your pet assisting you. There is no check that you have a pet, and nothing happens when not in the world or the for-who does not name this character.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Pet:Assist[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:PetAssist

OgreBotAPI.Pet:Attack[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Pet
  what: Sends the game command /pet attack right away, so your pet attacks your current target. There is no check that you have a pet, and nothing happens when not in the world or the for-who does not name this character.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Pet:Attack[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:PetAttack

OgreBotAPI.Pet:GetLost[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Pet
  what: Sends the game command /pet getlost right away, which dismisses your pet. There is no check that you have a pet, and nothing happens when not in the world or the for-who does not name this character.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Pet:GetLost[all]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:PetGetLost

OgreBotAPI.Pet:Off[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Pet
  what: Sends the game command /pet backoff right away, so your pet stops attacking. There is no check that you have a pet, and nothing happens when not in the world or the for-who does not name this character.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Pet:Off[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:PetOff


== OgreBotAPI.POI ==

${OgreBotAPI.POI.Count}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.POI
  what: How many points of interest the current zone has, shipped and your own together. It reads 0 in a zone with none, while you are not settled in a zone and while the travel data loads.
  returns: int: the current zone's total. A POI of yours that overrides a shipped one counts once.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.POI.Count}

${OgreBotAPI.POI.Loc[name]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.POI
  what: Where a point of interest of the current zone is, shipped or your own. It reads empty for an unknown name, for a POI that names only an actor, while you are not settled in a zone and while the travel data loads.
  arg name (string): The POI's name, in any case.
  returns: string: x,y,z to two decimals, or empty when there is no such location.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.POI.Loc[bell]}

OgreBotAPI.POI:Add[name, x, y, z, sender]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.POI
  what: Saves a named point of interest in the zone you are in, where you stand or at x,y,z, for every character on this PC. A shipped name is overridden, a name of your own moves to the new spot, and a refusal prints one line and saves nothing.
  arg name (string): The name, in any case. It cannot be empty, hold a comma or read as a number.
  arg x (float): X of the spot. Leave x, y and z out to use where you stand. With any of them given all three are needed, and 0,0,0 is refused.
  arg y (float): Y (height) of the spot.
  arg z (float): Z of the spot.
  arg sender (string): Leave this out in a script. The -POI_Add row fills it with the box that sent the line, and every other box does nothing.
  example: OgreBotAPI.POI:Add["Quest giver",100,20,-250]

OgreBotAPI.POI:Remove[name]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.POI
  what: Removes a point of interest of your own from the zone you are in, and a shipped POI it was overriding is back. A shipped POI cannot be removed: that and an unknown name print one line and change nothing.
  arg name (string): The POI's name, in any case.
  example: OgreBotAPI.POI:Remove["Quest giver"]

OgreBotAPI.POI:Rename[old, new]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.POI
  what: Renames a point of interest of your own in the zone you are in. A shipped POI, an unknown name and a new name that another POI here holds each print one line and change nothing.
  arg old (string): The POI's name now, in any case.
  arg new (string): The new name. It cannot be empty, hold a comma or read as a number.
  example: OgreBotAPI.POI:Rename["Quest giver","Quest giver east"]


== OgreBotAPI.Position ==

${OgreBotAPI.Position.ActorModelSize[nameOrId]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Position
  what: Returns an actor's model size: its collision radius times its collision scale. Returns 0 when the argument is blank or the actor cannot be found.
  arg nameOrId (string): the actor: an actor id, an @alias or *alias, pet:<owner>, a class word (the first group or raid member it fits) me or your own name (you), or a name (the nearest actor whose name contains it)
  returns: float: the actor's collision radius times its collision scale; 0 when it is not found.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Position.ActorModelSize[${Target.ID}]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.GetActorModelSize

${OgreBotAPI.Position.AtAngle[angle,actorNameOrId,dist=3]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Position
  what: Returns the point at angle degrees around an actor, measured from the actor's heading, dist plus your model size plus the actor's model size away, at the actor's height plus 0.5. Returns "" when the actor cannot be found; it only computes a point and moves nothing.
  arg angle (int): whole degrees around the actor from its heading: 0 is directly behind it and 180 directly in front, 90 and -90 its two sides (a fraction is dropped)
  arg actorNameOrId (string): the actor: an actor id, an @alias or *alias, pet:<owner>, a class word (the first group or raid member it fits) me or your own name (you), or a name (the nearest actor whose name contains it)
  arg dist (float, default: 3): the gap between the two bodies, before the model sizes are added
  returns: string: "x,y,z" with two decimals; "" when the actor is not found.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Position.AtAngle[90,${Target.ID},5]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.PointAtAngle

${OgreBotAPI.Position.AtAngleNoTargetSize[angle,actorNameOrId,dist=3]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Position
  what: Same as Position.AtAngle, but the distance adds only your own model size, not the actor's. Returns "" when the actor cannot be found.
  arg angle (int): whole degrees around the actor from its heading: 0 is directly behind it and 180 directly in front, 90 and -90 its two sides (a fraction is dropped)
  arg actorNameOrId (string): the actor: an actor id, an @alias or *alias, pet:<owner>, a class word (the first group or raid member it fits) me or your own name (you), or a name (the nearest actor whose name contains it)
  arg dist (float, default: 3): the distance before your model size is added
  returns: string: "x,y,z" with two decimals; "" when the actor is not found.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Position.AtAngleNoTargetSize[180,${Target.ID},3]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.PointAtAngleNoSize

${OgreBotAPI.Position.DistanceToActor[nameOrId=Target]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Position
  what: Returns your distance to an actor as the game reports it (the actor's Distance), using your current target when no actor is given. Returns -1 when the actor cannot be found or you are not in the world.
  arg nameOrId (string, default: Target): the actor: an actor id, an @alias or *alias, pet:<owner>, a class word (the first group or raid member it fits) me or your own name (you), or a name (the nearest actor whose name contains it); blank = your current target
  returns: float: the distance to the actor; -1 when it is not found or you are not in the world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Position.DistanceToActor[${Target.ID}]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.GameDistanceToActor

${OgreBotAPI.Position.FarthestActorFrom[anchorNameOrId,actorName,minDist=20]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Position
  what: Returns the id of the actor named exactly actorName (any case) that is farthest, in straight-line 3D distance, from an anchor actor, as long as it is more than minDist away. Returns 0 when the anchor or no actor of that name is found, or when even the farthest one is not past minDist.
  arg anchorNameOrId (string): the actor to measure from: an actor id, an @alias or *alias, pet:<owner>, a class word or a name (the nearest actor whose name contains it)
  arg actorName (string): the full name of the actors to choose among (whole-name match, any case)
  arg minDist (float, default: 20): the winner must be farther than this from the anchor, or the answer is 0
  returns: int64: the chosen actor's id; 0 when there is none.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Position.FarthestActorFrom[${Target.ID},"a void tentacle",20]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.GetFarthestActorFrom, OgreBotAPI.GetFarthestActorFrom_ref

${OgreBotAPI.Position.FarthestGroupDistance}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Position
  what: Returns the distance to the farthest other member of your group. Returns 0 when you are solo or not in the world.
  returns: float: the largest distance from you to another group member; 0 when there is none.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Position.FarthestGroupDistance}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.GetFarthestGroupDistance, Obj_OgreUtilities.GroupWithinDistance

${OgreBotAPI.Position.MyModelSize}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Position
  what: Returns your model size: your collision radius times your collision scale, the body edge the bot adds to its distances.
  returns: float: your collision radius times your collision scale.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Position.MyModelSize}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.GetMyModelSize

${OgreBotAPI.Position.Toward[fx,fy,fz,tx,ty,tz,dist=15]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Position
  what: Returns the point dist away from the first point in the direction of the second, measured flat (x and z only), with the second point's y. It does not stop at the second point when dist is longer than the gap, and returns "" when fewer than six coordinates are given.
  arg fx (float): the starting point's x
  arg fy (float): the starting point's y (not used in the result)
  arg fz (float): the starting point's z
  arg tx (float): the point to head toward, x
  arg ty (float): the point to head toward, y (becomes the result's y)
  arg tz (float): the point to head toward, z
  arg dist (float, default: 15): how far from the starting point to go
  returns: string: "x,y,z" with two decimals; "" when fewer than six coordinates are given.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Position.Toward[${Me.X},${Me.Y},${Me.Z},${Target.X},${Target.Y},${Target.Z},10]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.PointTowardDist


== OgreBotAPI.Quest ==

${OgreBotAPI.Quest.ActorHas[actorId]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Quest
  what: Whether the actor with this id is within a distance of 10 and offers a quest or has a quest update or hand-in for you. With no id it prints a console line and answers FALSE.
  arg actorId (int64): the actor id to check; required
  returns: bool: TRUE when that actor is within 10 and has a quest offer, update or hand-in; FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Quest.ActorHas[${Target.ID}]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.ActorHasQuest

${OgreBotAPI.Quest.Have[name]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Quest
  what: Whether a quest with this exact name, in any case, is in your active quest journal. No name, or not being in the world, answers FALSE.
  arg name (string): the full quest name to look for; case does not matter
  returns: bool: TRUE when the quest is in your active journal; FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Quest.Have["Feathers For Sethis"]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.HaveQuest, Obj_OgreIH.Check_Quest_Exists

OgreBotAPI.Quest:Accept[fw, questName=""]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Quest
  what: Clicks Accept on an offered new quest window, never a quest reward window, and does nothing when none is offered. It accepts whether or not the Settings Do not auto accept quests box is ticked, since that box stops only the automatic accept; given a name, a group leader with auto share on shares that quest two seconds later.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg questName (string, default: ""): the quest to share after accepting; blank accepts with no share
  example: OgreBotAPI.Quest:Accept[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:AcceptQuest, Obj_OgreUtilities:AcceptQuest

OgreBotAPI.Quest:CheckKunarkAscending[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Quest
  what: Opens and closes the quest journal, then prints which Kunark Ascending prerequisite quests you have not completed: the languages, the heritage quest, the signature line and an Epic 1.0 quest. It runs in turn on the action queue and ends with a completed line.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Quest:CheckKunarkAscending[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CheckKunarkAscendingRequirements

OgreBotAPI.Quest:CompareUpdate[fw, questName, sender]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Quest
  what: Reads your own steps for a quest and asks other characters to compare theirs; a character on a different step says so in its own console and you get a tally. The character that runs it asks, the for-who is who is asked, and all or blank asks the rest of your group.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: which characters are asked; all or blank is your group but you
  arg questName (string): the quest to compare; a missing one prints a console line
  arg sender (character name): the character that asks; the -CompareQuest console line fills it. Leave it out in a script: the character running it asks, and any other name makes the call do nothing
  example: OgreBotAPI.Quest:CompareUpdate[all,"Feathers For Sethis"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CompareQuestUpdate

OgreBotAPI.Quest:Delete[fw, questName]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Quest
  what: Deletes one quest from your own journal straight away and prints the result. There is no group leader check, and a quest that is not in the journal or has moved in it is not deleted.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg questName (string): the exact quest name, any case
  example: OgreBotAPI.Quest:Delete[${Me.Name},"Feathers For Sethis"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:DeleteQuest, Obj_OgreUtilities:DeleteQuest, Obj_OgreUtilities:DeleteQuestActual

OgreBotAPI.Quest:ShareAllMissions[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Quest
  what: Shares every active mission in your journal with the group, waiting up to 5 minutes for the group to gather within 30 and then 3 seconds between shares. With all only the group leader shares, and it says so in the console when you are not grouped or have no missions.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Quest:ShareAllMissions[all]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ShareAllMissions

OgreBotAPI.Quest:ShareMission[fw, questName]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Quest
  what: Like :ShareQuest, but the quest must be a mission (its journal category starts with Mission). It says so in the console when it is not an active mission, the name is blank or you are not grouped.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg questName (string): the exact mission name, any case
  example: OgreBotAPI.Quest:ShareMission[all,"Feathers For Sethis"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ShareMission

OgreBotAPI.Quest:ShareQuest[fw, questName]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Quest
  what: Shares one quest from your journal with the group, after waiting up to 5 minutes for the group to gather within 30. With all only the group leader shares, and it says so in the console when the name is blank, the quest is not in your journal or you are not grouped.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg questName (string): the exact quest name, any case
  example: OgreBotAPI.Quest:ShareQuest[all,"Feathers For Sethis"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ShareQuest

OgreBotAPI.Quest:ShareQuestWhenAble[fw, questName, zoneName]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Quest
  what: Shares one quest once the group has gathered (waiting up to 5 minutes), but only while you are in zoneName - leaving that zone first stops the share with a console line. With all only the group leader shares.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg questName (string): the exact quest name, any case
  arg zoneName (string): the zone the share is for; blank means the zone you are in now
  example: OgreBotAPI.Quest:ShareQuestWhenAble[all,"Feathers For Sethis","${Zone.Name}"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ShareQuestWhenAble

OgreBotAPI.Quest:ShowMissionInfo[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Quest
  what: Prints the hot zone mission rotation for this server to the console: what is current, what comes next and the time until it changes. It runs on every addressed character, with no group leader check.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Quest:ShowMissionInfo[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:DisplayEtherealMissionInfo

OgreBotAPI.Quest:ShowWiki[fw, name=""]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Quest
  what: Opens the EverQuest 2 wiki page for a quest in your web browser; a blank name uses the quest selected in the quest journal, and with none selected a console line says so and nothing opens. A blank for-who means is1 here, not all.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg name (string, default: ""): the quest to look up; blank uses the quest selected in the journal
  example: OgreBotAPI.Quest:ShowWiki[${Me.Name},"Feathers For Sethis"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ShowWikiForQuest

OgreBotAPI.Quest:SpewMissionTimers[fw, ...searches]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Quest
  what: Opens the quest journal on its Mission Timers tab and sends one oc line per mission whose name contains a search word, with the time to reset and whether it is completed. With no search word it prints a reminder and nothing else, and it closes the journal when done.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg ...searches (string): one or more words; a mission matches when its name contains any of them, in any case
  example: OgreBotAPI.Quest:SpewMissionTimers[${Me.Name},Weekly,Daily]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Spew_MissionTimerInfo


== OgreBotAPI.Roster ==

${OgreBotAPI.Roster.ArchetypeOf[class]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: The archetype of a subclass name, in lower case: fighter, priest, mage or scout. An actor ID is also accepted and that actor's class is used; a class tier name such as warrior, or anything unknown, reads an empty string.
  arg class (string): A subclass name such as templar (any case), or an actor ID.
  returns: string - fighter, priest, mage or scout, empty when unknown.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.ArchetypeOf[${Target.ID}]}
  oldbot: ClassInfo.Archetype, GetArchetypeFromClass, GetInfoOb.Archetype

${OgreBotAPI.Roster.BaseClassOf[class]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: The class tier of a subclass name, in lower case: templar reads cleric, berserker reads warrior. An actor ID is also accepted and that actor's class is used; anything that is not a subclass reads an empty string.
  arg class (string): A subclass name such as berserker (any case), or an actor ID.
  returns: string - the class tier (warrior, cleric, bard and so on), empty when unknown.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.BaseClassOf[berserker]}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb.GetBaseClass, GetInfoOb.GetClass, OgreBotAPI.Get_BaseClass

${OgreBotAPI.Roster.CountGroupBy[mode,search]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Counts the members of your group, you included, that match mode and search. Only player characters count: a member whose type reads as anything else (a corpse, for example) is skipped; with no mode it matches by Class, and a mode word the list does not know matches nobody.
  arg mode (string, default: Class): How to match: All (everyone; search ignored), Class (exact subclass, e.g. templar), RawClass or ParentClass (class tier, e.g. cleric), Archetype, NotArchetype, Role (tank, priest, enchanter, bard, dps), Cursed (search ignored), KraletusCharmers (coercers and troubadors, search ignored). Empty means Class; any other word matches nobody.
  arg search (string): The class, tier, archetype or role name to match, any case.
  returns: int - number of matching group members, 0 when none match.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.CountGroupBy[Archetype,priest]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.CountGroupBy, GetInfoOb.CountGroupBy_, CheckGroupSetup

${OgreBotAPI.Roster.CountRaidBy[mode,search]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Counts the members of your raid, you included, that match mode and search; in a raid every member counts, corpses too. When you are not in a raid it answers exactly as CountGroupBy does.
  arg mode (string, default: Class): How to match: All, Class, RawClass or ParentClass, Archetype, NotArchetype, Role, Cursed, KraletusCharmers. Empty means Class; any other word matches nobody.
  arg search (string): The class, tier, archetype or role name to match, any case.
  returns: int - number of matching raid members (group members when not in a raid).
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.CountRaidBy[Role,priest]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.CountRaidBy, GetInfoOb.CountRaidBy_

${OgreBotAPI.Roster.Flagged[n=1]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: TRUE when flag number n is set on this character. Flags are kept by this session only, are set with Roster:Flag, and can be read anywhere, even outside the world; flag 24 is the same state as Marked.
  arg n (int, default: 1): The flag number to check.
  returns: bool - TRUE when flag n is set.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.Flagged[2]}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb.FlaggedToon, GetInfoOb:ToonFlagged, OgreBotAPI.ToonFlagged

${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GroupIDBy[mode,search,rank=1]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: The actor ID of the rank-th group member, you included, that matches mode and search, with matches sorted alphabetically by name. Only player characters are considered (a corpse is skipped); reads 0 when nobody matches or rank is past the last match.
  arg mode (string, default: Class): How to match: All, Class, RawClass or ParentClass, Archetype, NotArchetype, Role, Cursed, KraletusCharmers. Empty means Class; any other word matches nobody.
  arg search (string): The class, tier, archetype or role name to match, any case.
  arg rank (int, default: 1): Which match to return, counting from 1 in name order.
  returns: int64 - the member's actor ID, 0 when there is no such match.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GroupIDBy[Class,templar,1]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.GetGroupIDBy, GetInfoOb.GetGroupIDBy_

${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GroupIDPreferred[search,rank=1]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: The actor ID of the rank-th group member, you included, whose archetype or role matches search, ordered by how useful that class is to spare (for dps the order is flipped so pure damage classes come first). Only player characters are considered (a corpse is skipped), a member matching any of the listed pools counts, ties go to the pool listed first and then to name, and it reads 0 when nobody matches.
  arg search (string): One or more archetypes or roles separated by |, for example scout, dps or scout|mage.
  arg rank (int, default: 1): Which match to return, counting from 1 in preferred order.
  returns: int64 - the member's actor ID, 0 when there is no such match.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GroupIDPreferred[scout|mage,1]}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb.GetGroupIDPreferred_, OgreBotAPI.GetGroupIDPreferred

${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GroupNameBy[mode,search,rank=1]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: The name of the rank-th group member, you included, that matches mode and search, with matches sorted alphabetically by name. Only player characters are considered (a corpse is skipped), as in GroupIDBy, so the same rank names the same member in both; reads an empty string when nobody matches or rank is past the last match.
  arg mode (string, default: Class): How to match: All, Class, RawClass or ParentClass, Archetype, NotArchetype, Role, Cursed, KraletusCharmers. Empty means Class; any other word matches nobody.
  arg search (string): The class, tier, archetype or role name to match, any case.
  arg rank (int, default: 1): Which match to return, counting from 1 in name order.
  returns: string - the member's name, empty when there is no such match.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GroupNameBy[Class,templar,1]}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb.GetGroupInformation, GetInfoOb.GetGroupNameBy_, OgreBotAPI.GetGroupNameBy

${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GroupNamePreferred[search,rank=1]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: The name of the rank-th group member, you included, whose archetype or role matches search, in the same preferred order as GroupIDPreferred, so the same rank names the same member in both (a corpse is skipped). search can list several pools with |; reads an empty string when nobody matches.
  arg search (string): One or more archetypes or roles separated by |, for example scout, dps or scout|mage.
  arg rank (int, default: 1): Which match to return, counting from 1 in preferred order.
  returns: string - the member's name, empty when there is no such match.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GroupNamePreferred[dps,1]}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb.GetGroupNamePreferred_, OgreBotAPI.GetGroupNamePreferred

${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GroupSize}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: How many people are in your group, counting you, so a solo character reads 1. Reads NULL when you are not in the world.
  returns: int - group members including you.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GroupSize}

${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GuildFlagLocation}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: The text the game shows for your guild's flag location. Reads NULL when you are not in the world, and an empty string when the game has no value.
  returns: string - the guild flag location as the game labels it.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.GuildFlagLocation}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.GuildFlagLocation

${OgreBotAPI.Roster.InCombat}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: TRUE when anyone in your group is in combat mode, you included, so a solo character reads its own; it checks your group only, never the rest of a raid, and a member in another zone counts as out of combat. Reads NULL when you are not in the world; for your character alone, hated included, use ${OgreBotAPI.Combat.InCombat}.
  returns: bool - TRUE when any member of your group, you included, is in combat mode; FALSE when nobody is.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.InCombat}
  oldbot: Obj_OgreUtilities.GroupInCombat

${OgreBotAPI.Roster.InEQ2Chars[speaker,fullAccountOnly=FALSE]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: TRUE when speaker is on the list the chat commands trust: every character saved in your account list, on any account (characters not yet assigned to one included), and the name OgreIRCSession, matched in any case. With fullAccountOnly TRUE it is TRUE only when that character also has complete account details saved, the kind a login needs; it works outside the world.
  arg speaker (string): The character name to look up.
  arg fullAccountOnly (bool, default: FALSE): TRUE to require complete saved account details for that character, not just its name on the list.
  returns: bool - TRUE when the name is on that list.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.InEQ2Chars[${Target.Name}]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.InEQ2Chars

${OgreBotAPI.Roster.InRaid}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: TRUE when you are in a raid. Reads NULL when you are not in the world (character select, zoning).
  returns: bool - TRUE in a raid, FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.InRaid}

${OgreBotAPI.Roster.InZone[within=0]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: TRUE when every other member of your group is in this zone and alive, and, when within is above 0, no farther away than within. Solo reads TRUE, outside the world reads FALSE; it checks your group only, never the rest of a raid.
  arg within (float, default: 0): The farthest a member may be from you. 0 skips the distance check.
  returns: bool - TRUE when the whole group is here.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.InZone[50]}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb.GroupInZone, OgreBotAPI.GroupInZone, call Obj_OgreUtilities.CheckIfGroupInSameZone

${OgreBotAPI.Roster.IsGroupLeader}

${OgreBotAPI.Roster.Marked}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Roster

${OgreBotAPI.Roster.NearestOfClass[class,range=50,scope=auto,includeMe=TRUE]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: The actor ID of a group or raid member of the given class who is within range, or 0 when there is none. A match is the subclass, its class tier or its archetype (warrior finds a berserker, fighter finds any fighter); you are checked first and returned with no distance test when includeMe is TRUE, then the closest member in range wins.
  arg class (string): A subclass, class tier or archetype name, any case. Empty reads 0.
  arg range (float, default: 50): The farthest a member may be. Members whose distance reads 0 are never matched.
  arg scope (string, default: auto): auto (your raid when in one, else your group), raid, or any other word for your group.
  arg includeMe (bool, default: TRUE): TRUE to answer with your own ID when your class matches.
  returns: int64 - the matching member's actor ID, 0 when none is in range.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.NearestOfClass[priest,30,auto,FALSE]}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb.Class

${OgreBotAPI.Roster.SortGroupByID[mode,search,exclude]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Your own position, counting from 1, among the group members that match mode and search, ordered by actor ID read as text (so 100 sorts before 99). Every character in the group gets a different number, which is what makes it useful for picking spots; reads 0 when you do not match yourself.
  arg mode (string, default: Class): How to match: All, Class, RawClass or ParentClass, Archetype, NotArchetype, Role, Cursed, KraletusCharmers. Empty means Class; any other word matches nobody.
  arg search (string): The class, tier, archetype or role name to match, any case.
  arg exclude (string): A character name to leave out of the ordering, any case. Empty leaves nobody out.
  returns: int - your 1-based position among the matches, 0 when you are not one of them.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.SortGroupByID[Archetype,scout]}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb:Get_GroupIDs, GetInfoOb.SortGroupByIDBy_, OgreBotAPI.SortGroupByIDBy

${OgreBotAPI.Roster.SortRaidByID[mode,search,exclude]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Your own position, counting from 1, among the raid members that match mode and search, ordered by actor ID read as text. When you are not in a raid it answers exactly as SortGroupByID does; reads 0 when you do not match yourself.
  arg mode (string, default: Class): How to match: All, Class, RawClass or ParentClass, Archetype, NotArchetype, Role, Cursed, KraletusCharmers. Empty means Class; any other word matches nobody.
  arg search (string): The class, tier, archetype or role name to match, any case.
  arg exclude (string): A character name to leave out of the ordering, any case. Empty leaves nobody out.
  returns: int - your 1-based position among the matches, 0 when you are not one of them.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Roster.SortRaidByID[Role,dps]}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb.SortRaidByIDBy_, OgreBotAPI.SortRaidByIDBy

OgreBotAPI.Roster:CheckMemberLevel[fw, onlyNonMembers=FALSE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Each selected character prints "<name> Membership level: <level>" on the InnerSpace console, using the game's subscription level. With onlyNonMembers TRUE, characters whose level reads Member print nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg onlyNonMembers (bool, default: FALSE): TRUE to print only for characters that are not Member.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Roster:CheckMemberLevel[all,TRUE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CheckMemberLevel

OgreBotAPI.Roster:Disband[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Each selected character sends the game's /disband, which takes it out of its group. It needs the character in the world.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Roster:Disband[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Disband

OgreBotAPI.Roster:Flag[fw, n=1]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Sets flag number n on each selected character. When the flag was not already set, a line saying so goes to OgreConsole; setting a flag that is already set is silent, a number outside 1 to 24 is refused with a console line, and it works outside the world.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg n (int, default: 1): The flag number to set, 1 to 24. Flag 24 is the same state as Mark.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Roster:Flag[${Me.Name},2]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:FlagToon, GetInfoOb:FlagToon

OgreBotAPI.Roster:FlagNextPerson[fw, mark=1, via=any, search..., -GroupOnly]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Finds the next character after you and tells that character, over IRC and over oc to every session on this PC, to set flag mark on itself. A group goes in actor id order, so every box agrees on who is next, and a raid in slot order; both wrap round, and nothing is sent when nobody passes.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg mark (int, default: 1): The flag number the next person sets.
  arg via (string, default: any): any, archetype or baseclass: who may be next. Any other word means any.
  arg search... (string): the archetypes or base classes to match; left out, your own
  arg -GroupOnly (switch): use the group even when you are in a raid
  example: OgreBotAPI.Roster:FlagNextPerson[${Me.Name},3]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:FlagNextPerson, OgreBotAPI:FlagToonNextPerson

OgreBotAPI.Roster:Invite[fw, who]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Each selected character sends a group invite to who; an alias such as @Healer1 is turned into that character's name first. Nobody already in your group or raid is invited (silently); a missing name, or one that is not plain letters, is refused with one line on the InnerSpace console.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg who (string): The character to invite, by name or alias; me means you, who are always skipped. Required.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Roster:Invite[${Me.Name},${Target.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Invite

OgreBotAPI.Roster:Inviter[fw, toon...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Each selected character invites a list of characters in order, about one second apart, skipping anyone already with it; names may also be split by spaces or commas. Put -r (or -ri, -raidinvite) before a name to raid-invite that one; -from, -i and -inviter are not supported here and skip the name after them with a warning, and starting a new list stops one that is still running.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg toon... (string): The names (or aliases) to invite, in order, each optionally led by -r for a raid invite. Any other word starting with - is skipped.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Roster:Inviter[${Me.Name},${Target.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Inviter

OgreBotAPI.Roster:Kick[fw, who]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Each selected character kicks who from its group; an alias is turned into a name first. A missing name, or one that is not in the group (you are never in the list), prints one line on the InnerSpace console and kicks nobody.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg who (string): The group member to kick, by name or alias.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Roster:Kick[${Me.Name},${Group[1].Name}]

OgreBotAPI.Roster:MakeLeader[fw, leader]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Each selected character that leads its group hands leadership to leader; an alias is turned into a name first. Nothing happens, silently, when leader is the running character, it is not the leader, or leader is not in its group; a missing name, or one that is not plain letters, is refused with one line on the InnerSpace console.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg leader (string): The group member to make leader, by name or alias; me means you, which does nothing. Required.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Roster:MakeLeader[${Me.Name},${Group[1].Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:MakeLeader

OgreBotAPI.Roster:Mark[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Marks each selected character, which is the same as setting flag 24. A line goes to OgreConsole when the character was not already marked; it works outside the world.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Roster:Mark[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:MarkToon, GetInfoOb:MarkToon

OgreBotAPI.Roster:Mentor[fw, name]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Each selected character mentors the group member name, but only when that member is in its group, is lower level, and neither of them is already mentoring. An alias is turned into a name first; a missing name gets one line, and any other case does nothing, silently.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg name (string): The group member to mentor, by name or alias. Required.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Roster:Mentor[${Me.Name},${Group[1].Name}]
  oldbot: Mentor, OgreBotAPI:Mentor

OgreBotAPI.Roster:RaidInvite[fw, who]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Each selected character sends a raid invite to who; an alias is turned into a name first. Nobody already in your raid or your own group is invited (silently); a missing name, or one that is not plain letters, is refused with one line on the InnerSpace console.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg who (string): The character to raid-invite, by name or alias; me means you, who are always skipped. Required.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Roster:RaidInvite[${Me.Name},${Target.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:RaidInvite

OgreBotAPI.Roster:SetClassValue[fw, member, value]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Forces one of the bot's class checks to TRUE or FALSE for each selected character, for example IsFighter TRUE so a non-fighter runs fighter logic, and auto removes the override. The setting lasts until another character is loaded in that session; a missing argument, a member that is not a class name, or a value that is not TRUE, FALSE or auto prints one line on the InnerSpace console and changes nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg member (string): The class check to force: an archetype, class tier or subclass name, with or without Is (IsFighter, Fighter, IsTemplar).
  arg value (string): TRUE or FALSE (yes/no style words also work), or auto to remove the override.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Roster:SetClassValue[${Me.Name},IsFighter,TRUE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ClassInfo_ChangeValue

OgreBotAPI.Roster:SpewFlags[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Each selected character sends one OgreConsole line per flag it holds, in number order, reading "<name> Flagged <n>". A character with no flags says nothing; it needs the character in the world.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Roster:SpewFlags[all]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:SpewFlags, GetInfoOb:SpewFlags

OgreBotAPI.Roster:SpewMarked[fw, where]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Each selected character reports whether it is marked, as a line reading "<name> --> Marked: TRUE" (or FALSE), and also raises the stat-report event. The line goes to OgreConsole unless where says otherwise and needs the character in the world; today it always reads FALSE, even for a marked character.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg where (string): oc (OgreConsole), irc, or event (no visible line, only the event). Empty or any other word means oc.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Roster:SpewMarked[all,oc]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ToonMarked

OgreBotAPI.Roster:Unflag[fw, n=1]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Clears flag number n on each selected character. When the flag was set, a line saying so goes to OgreConsole; clearing a flag that is not set is silent, a number outside 1 to 24 is refused with a console line, and it works outside the world.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg n (int, default: 1): The flag number to clear, 1 to 24.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Roster:Unflag[all,2]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:UnflagToon, GetInfoOb:UnflagToon

OgreBotAPI.Roster:UnflagAll[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Clears every flag on each selected character, the mark (flag 24) included. One OgreConsole line is written for each flag that was set; nothing is written when none were.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Roster:UnflagAll[all]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:UnflagAll, GetInfoOb:UnflagAll

OgreBotAPI.Roster:Unmark[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Removes the mark (flag 24) from each selected character. A line goes to OgreConsole when the character was marked; otherwise it is silent.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
