OgreBotAPI.Roster:Unmentor[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Roster
  what: Each selected character stops mentoring, but only when its effective level differs from its level; otherwise nothing is sent.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Roster:Unmentor[all]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Unmentor


== OgreBotAPI.Session ==

${OgreBotAPI.Session.AtCharacterSelect}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Session
  what: Whether the character select screen is showing. It works with no character logged in.
  returns: bool: TRUE while the character select screen is visible; FALSE otherwise
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Session.AtCharacterSelect}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.AtCharacterSelect

${OgreBotAPI.Session.CharacterName}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Session
  what: This character's name. It returns "" when not in the world, for example at character select.
  returns: string: the character's name; "" out of the world
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Session.CharacterName}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.CurrentCharacter

${OgreBotAPI.Session.ReviveLocation[option,exact]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Session
  what: While you are dead, finds the revive point named by option in the death window and returns its row number. It returns 0 when you are alive, not in the world, give no option, or no revive point matches.
  arg option (string): a row number, or a revive point name such as Entrance, compared case-insensitively with the text before the bracket; a row that is not a revive point is never chosen
  arg exact (bool, default: FALSE): TRUE: the name must match in full; FALSE: the name may be part of the revive point's name
  returns: int: the row number (from 1) of the matching revive point; 0 when there is none
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Session.ReviveLocation[Entrance,FALSE]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_ReviveLocation

OgreBotAPI.Session:CollectShiny[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Session
  what: Targets the nearest collectible shiny, by the Loot tab's own test (an actor named only a question mark or an exclamation mark, or a resource whose name has a question mark), and collects it if it is within 10 meters. Nothing happens when none is that close; this runs on demand and is separate from the Loot tab's own shiny collecting.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Session:CollectShiny[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Question

OgreBotAPI.Session:Harvest[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Session
  what: Targets the nearest harvest node and collects from it, if that node is within 10 meters. Nothing happens when no node is that close, and the collect is sent at once, not queued.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Session:Harvest[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Resource

OgreBotAPI.Session:ImmRes[fw, howManyDead=2]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Session
  what: Queues a cast of Immaculate Revival when it is ready and enough of the group is dead: each dead group member counts 1, while a dead fighter or priest, or being dead yourself, counts 6. It does nothing for a character without the ability.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg howManyDead (int, default: 2): the count it takes before it casts; below 1 it never casts
  example: OgreBotAPI.Session:ImmRes[igw:${Me.Name},3]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ImmRes

OgreBotAPI.Session:LogToonIn[forToon, toon, server="", class=""]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Session
  what: Logs toon in on the one session forToon names, from the login screen, from character select, or from the world on another character (camping out first, unless in combat). It needs a saved login for toon on this PC and says so on the console when there is none.
  arg forToon (string): the session that should act: its InnerSpace session name or its character's name, case-insensitive - at character select or the login screen, the character it last played (so a box a zone dropped to character select answers to its toon), and mid-zone only the session name; all, classes and groups do not match, and a blank gets one line
  arg toon (string): the character to log in; a blank gets one line
  arg server (string): the server, by name or short form (ior, md), for a character saved on more than one; blank uses its default server
  arg class (string): the class to log in as, like ranger; blank logs in whatever class it was
  example: OgreBotAPI.Session:LogToonIn[is2,${Group[1].Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:LogToonIn, OgreBotAPI:LoginAtCharacterSelect

OgreBotAPI.Session:PlayAtCharacterSelect[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Session
  what: Presses the Play button on the character select screen. It does nothing unless that screen is showing, and it works with no character in the world.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Session:PlayAtCharacterSelect[all]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:PlayAtCharacterSelect

OgreBotAPI.Session:Res[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Session
  what: Lets the cast stack cast res abilities again by unchecking Disable CS_Res. It is silent, and it turns ressing on even if you turned it off by hand.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Session:Res[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Res

OgreBotAPI.Session:ResStone[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Session
  what: Queues this class's res stone spell when it is ready: Divine Awakening for a cleric, Spirit Guide for a shaman, Favor of the Phoenix for a druid, Channel Soul for a channeler. Any other class does nothing, so it is safe to send to the whole group.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Session:ResStone[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ResStone

OgreBotAPI.Session:Revive[fw, option=0, exact=FALSE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Session
  what: With option 0, presses Revive on the death window when you are dead (a living character clicks nothing); with a row number or revive point name, picks that point and presses Revive half a second later, or the last revive point the window lists when none matches, saying on the console which points there are. A dead character that revives this way has its camp spot cleared, because it comes back away from where it fell.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg option (string, default: 0): 0 for the death window's default revive, or a revive point row number or name, matched as ${OgreBotAPI.Session.ReviveLocation} matches it; when nothing matches, the last revive point the window lists is used (no revive only when it lists none)
  arg exact (bool, default: FALSE): TRUE: a name must match in full; FALSE: it may be part of the revive point's name
  example: OgreBotAPI.Session:Revive[igw:${Me.Name},Entrance]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Revive, Revive, call Obj_OgreUtilities.Revive

OgreBotAPI.Session:StopRes[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Session
  what: Stops the cast stack casting res abilities by checking Disable CS_Res. It is silent; :Res turns ressing back on.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Session:StopRes[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:StopRes


== OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns ==

${OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns.IsOpen}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns
  what: Returns whether the Temp Adornments window is open on this session.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the Temp Adornments window is open; FALSE when it is not.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns.IsOpen}

${OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns.Profiles}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns
  what: Returns how many temporary-adornment profiles are saved - one profile file is shared by every character on this PC. The first read loads that file and, when there is none yet, creates it with the default profiles CBOC, Pot and HP plus any profiles saved by the classic Temp Adorns window.
  returns: int: the number of saved profiles; 0 when there are none or the profile file could not be read.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns.Profiles}

OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns:Apply[fw, profile]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns
  what: Queues putting a profile's temporary adornments on your gear: each listed piece gets its adornment from your bags, even a piece that already has it with time left; it skips only pieces with nothing equipped and adornments you do not carry. A blank or unknown profile name, or not being in the world, prints one console line and queues nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg profile (string): the saved profile to apply, any case (CBOC, Pot and HP exist by default); a two-handed primary row in it is used for Primary when your primary weapon is a two-hander
  example: OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns:Apply[igw:${Me.Name},CBOC]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ApplyTempAdorn, OgreBotAPI:PoP_TempAdorns

OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns:Close[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns
  what: Closes the Temp Adornments window. Nothing happens when it is not open.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns:Close[${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns:List[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns
  what: Prints every saved temporary-adornment profile to the console, one line each with its gear pieces and their adornments. Says so when there are no profiles.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns:List[${Me.Name}]

OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns:Open[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns
  what: Opens the Temp Adornments window, where profiles are built, saved, deleted and applied. Works at character select too, and does nothing when the window is already open.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.TempAdorns:Open[${Me.Name}]


== OgreBotAPI.Travel ==

${OgreBotAPI.Travel.ZoneDoorValue[option]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Travel
  what: Reads the row that ZoneDoor would pick for an option in the zone-door destination window that is open now, without clicking anything. It reads the window only when it is open and answers 0 otherwise.
  arg option (string): A row number, a destination name (the whole name in any case, with or without its instance number), or LAST_ENTRY for the last listed row.
  returns: int: the 1-based row of that destination in the open window; 0 when no window is open, the option is empty, no row matches, or a row number is past the end of the list.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Travel.ZoneDoorValue[LAST_ENTRY]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Travel_Get_ZoneDoorValue

OgreBotAPI.Travel:Bell[fw, toWhere, exact=FALSE, mzo=LAST_ENTRY]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Travel
  what: Double-clicks a bell within reach (15 units unless the travel data says otherwise), picks toWhere on its map, clicks the zone button, answers the window that follows and closes the map. It runs in the background, replaces any travel in progress, and gives up with a console line when no bell is in reach or the destination is still missing after a second look.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg toWhere (string): The destination button to pick, matched case-insensitively against the map's button labels as part of a label; the first match wins. When it is not found the console line lists every destination the bell offers.
  arg exact (bool, default: FALSE): TRUE to match the whole label (still any case) instead of part of it.
  arg mzo (string, default: LAST_ENTRY): When a zone-door destination window follows the zone button, the row to pick there: a row number, a destination name, or LAST_ENTRY for the last row. When a zone's sub-map follows instead, the last location on it is picked.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Travel:Bell[${Me.Name},"Antonica"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:TravelBell

OgreBotAPI.Travel:Druid[fw, toWhere, exact=FALSE, mzo=LAST_ENTRY]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Travel
  what: Double-clicks a druid ring within reach, or in a guild hall talks to the guild hall druid, if there is one, and uses the ring that conversation brings up, then picks toWhere on its map, clicks the zone button and closes the map. It runs in the background, replaces any travel in progress, and gives up with a console line when nothing opens or the destination is still missing after a second look.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg toWhere (string): The destination button to pick, matched case-insensitively against the map's button labels as part of a label; the first match wins. When it is not found the console line lists every destination the ring offers.
  arg exact (bool, default: FALSE): TRUE to match the whole label (still any case) instead of part of it.
  arg mzo (string, default: LAST_ENTRY): When a zone-door destination window follows the zone button, the row to pick there: a row number, a destination name, or LAST_ENTRY for the last row. When a zone's sub-map follows instead, the last location on it is picked.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Travel:Druid[${Me.Name},"Steamfont"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:TravelDruid

OgreBotAPI.Travel:Fast[fw, toWhere, flag...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Travel
  what: Opens the game's fast travel map, picks toWhere, clicks the zone button, answers the window that follows and closes the map. It runs in the background, replaces any travel in progress, and gives up with a console line when the map does not open or the destination is still missing after a second look.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg toWhere (string): The destination button to pick, matched case-insensitively as part of a label unless -em is given; the first match wins. When it is not found the console line lists every destination the map offers.
  arg flag... (string): Optional switches in any order. -em (or -exactmatch) matches the whole label. -mto <option> picks that number of sub-map location, counting from 1, the one whose description contains that text, Random, or Last; without it the last location is picked. -loc <x,y,z> (or -mtl) picks the sub-map location nearest that point. -mzo <option> picks the zone-door row: a number, a name, or LAST_ENTRY (the default). -report echoes the sub-map's locations instead of picking one. Unknown words are ignored.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Travel:Fast[${Me.Name},"Antonica",-mto,Random]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:FastTravel, call Obj_OgreUtilities.FastTravel, Obj_OgreUtilities.Obj_Travel

OgreBotAPI.Travel:Mesh[fw, zone, poi=""]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Travel
  what: Plans a route from this zone to zone across the travel network (zone doors, bells, spires, druid rings, the travel map, guild hall amenities and travel items such as call-to-home), echoes its hops, then walks and travels it hop by hop. A trip asked for while zoning starts once the zone settles, a new route replaces the one in progress only when it can be planned, and the route ends when OgreBot ends; a bot you paused stays paused on arrival.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg zone (string): The destination zone: its display name in any case, or its travel-data id. An empty zone echoes "no destination zone given", and an unknown one echoes a "did you mean" list.
  arg poi (string, default: ""): A named point inside the destination zone to walk to at the end. A point the zone does not declare gets a console line and the route still goes to the zone.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Travel:Mesh[${Me.Name},"Antonica"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:TravelMesh

OgreBotAPI.Travel:MeshFeatures[fw, flag="", on=""]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Travel
  what: With no flag, echoes the account travel features the route planner knows for this character (the Friends and Family unlocks) and starts a scan for any still unanswered. With a flag and a yes or no, saves your answer for this character, which the planner then trusts and never scans again; a flag with no answer prints an error and saves nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg flag (string, default: ""): The feature id to set: sod_friends_and_family or roc_friends_and_family, in any case. Empty lists every feature instead of setting one; an id that is not one of those prints a line naming them and saves nothing.
  arg on (bool): TRUE when the character holds the feature, FALSE when it does not. Needed with a flag; a word that is not a yes or no word leaves the feature as it is.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Travel:MeshFeatures[${Me.Name},sod_friends_and_family,TRUE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:TravelMeshFeatures

OgreBotAPI.Travel:MeshGroup[fw, zone, poi=""]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Travel
  what: Starts the same route as Mesh on this character, then sends it to the rest of the group as a console command, and each member plans its own route from where it stands, staggered so the group does not move as one. Addressed to more than one character each plans its own route and nothing is sent, and when this character cannot plan the route nothing is sent.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg zone (string): The destination zone: its display name in any case, or its travel-data id. An empty zone echoes "no destination zone given", and an unknown one echoes a "did you mean" list.
  arg poi (string, default: ""): A named point inside the destination zone to walk to at the end, sent to every member. A point the zone does not declare gets a console line and the route still goes to the zone.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Travel:MeshGroup[${Me.Name},"The Commonlands"]
  oldbot: Obj_OgreIH.Obj_OgreTravelMesh, OgreBotAPI:TravelMeshGroup

OgreBotAPI.Travel:MeshPreview[fw, zone]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Travel
  what: Plans the route from here to zone and echoes it, a summary line with the hop count and rough time and then one line per hop, without moving. When there is no route it echoes why, and the first use loads the travel data, which can take a moment.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg zone (string): The destination zone: its display name in any case, or its travel-data id. An unknown one echoes a "did you mean" list.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Travel:MeshPreview[${Me.Name},"Antonica"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:TravelMeshPreview

OgreBotAPI.Travel:MeshStop[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Travel
  what: Stops the route in progress, and a trip still waiting for its zone to settle, whoever started it. It echoes "travel: gave up (stopped by request)" when a route was running and is silent otherwise.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Travel:MeshStop[all]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:TravelMeshStop

OgreBotAPI.Travel:SpewZoneDoorOptions[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Travel
  what: Echoes every destination in the open zone-door destination window as "[#n] name", numbered by row so the number works with ZoneDoor and ZoneDoorValue. With no window open it says so and reads nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Travel:SpewZoneDoorOptions[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:SpewZoneDoorOptions

OgreBotAPI.Travel:Spires[fw, toWhere, exact=FALSE, mzo=LAST_ENTRY]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Travel
  what: Double-clicks a wizard spire within reach, picks toWhere on its map, clicks the zone button, answers the window that follows and closes the map. It runs in the background, replaces any travel in progress, and gives up with a console line when no spire is in reach or the destination is still missing after a second look.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg toWhere (string): The destination button to pick, matched case-insensitively against the map's button labels as part of a label; the first match wins. When it is not found the console line lists every destination the spire offers.
  arg exact (bool, default: FALSE): TRUE to match the whole label (still any case) instead of part of it.
  arg mzo (string, default: LAST_ENTRY): When a zone-door destination window follows the zone button, the row to pick there: a row number, a destination name, or LAST_ENTRY for the last row. When a zone's sub-map follows instead, the last location on it is picked.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Travel:Spires[${Me.Name},"The Commonlands"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:TravelSpires

OgreBotAPI.Travel:ToGuildHall[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Travel
  what: Double-clicks the nearest actor within 15 units whose name contains "Magic Door to the Guild Hall", the city door that takes you to your guild hall. With no such door in reach it prints one line.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Travel:ToGuildHall[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:PortalToGuildHall

OgreBotAPI.Travel:Travel[fw, toWhere, exact=FALSE, mzo=LAST_ENTRY]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Travel
  what: Picks toWhere on a travel map that is already open, clicks the zone button, answers the window that follows and closes the map, so open the map first (a griffon station's map, for example). It runs in the background, replaces any travel in progress, and gives up with a console line when no map is up within 5 seconds or the destination is still missing after a second look.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg toWhere (string): The destination button to pick, matched case-insensitively against the map's button labels as part of a label; the first match wins. When it is not found the console line lists every destination the map offers.
  arg exact (bool, default: FALSE): TRUE to match the whole label (still any case) instead of part of it.
  arg mzo (string, default: LAST_ENTRY): When a zone-door destination window follows the zone button, the row to pick there: a row number, a destination name, or LAST_ENTRY for the last row. When a zone's sub-map follows instead, the last location on it is picked.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Travel:Travel[${Me.Name},"The Commonlands"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Travel

OgreBotAPI.Travel:ZoneDoor[door=1]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Travel
  what: Picks a destination in the zone-door destination window that is already open and confirms it half a second later. It takes no for-who and runs on the session that calls it, and with no window open, or a destination not in the list, it does nothing and echoes why (listing what the window offers).
  arg door (string, default: 1): A row number, a destination name (the whole name in any case, with or without its instance number), or LAST_ENTRY for the last row. SpewZoneDoorOptions shows the rows.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Travel:ZoneDoor[LAST_ENTRY]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ZoneDoor

OgreBotAPI.Travel:ZoneDoorFor[fw, door=1]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Travel
  what: The for-who form of ZoneDoor: picks door in the zone-door destination window that is already open and confirms it half a second later. With no window open, or a destination not in the list, it does nothing and echoes why (listing what the window offers).
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg door (string, default: 1): A row number, a destination name (the whole name in any case, with or without its instance number), or LAST_ENTRY for the last row. SpewZoneDoorOptions shows the rows.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Travel:ZoneDoorFor[igw:${Me.Name},LAST_ENTRY]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ZoneDoorForWho, call Obj_OgreUtilities.HandleZoneDoor


== OgreBotAPI.Util ==

${OgreBotAPI.Util.Between[v,lo,hi]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: TRUE when v is from lo to hi with both ends included, compared as whole numbers, so decimals are cut off before comparing. If lo is greater than hi the answer is always FALSE.
  arg v (int64, default: 0): The number to test.
  arg lo (int64, default: 0): The lowest allowed value, included.
  arg hi (int64, default: 0): The highest allowed value, included.
  returns: bool: TRUE when lo <= v <= hi; FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.Between[${Me.Level},50,60]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Between

${OgreBotAPI.Util.BetweenFloat[v,lo,hi]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: TRUE when v is from lo to hi with both ends included, compared as decimal numbers. If lo is greater than hi the answer is always FALSE.
  arg v (float, default: 0): The number to test.
  arg lo (float, default: 0): The lowest allowed value, included.
  arg hi (float, default: 0): The highest allowed value, included.
  returns: bool: TRUE when lo <= v <= hi; FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.BetweenFloat[${Target.Distance},0,7.5]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.BetweenFloat

${OgreBotAPI.Util.Clean[s]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: Tidies a name: when it has a dot, only the part after the last dot is kept, otherwise the brackets ( and ) are removed. A name starting with Skyshrine Infiltrator or Skyshrine Guardian comes back as Skyshrine_Infiltrator or Skyshrine_Guardian.
  arg s (string): The name to tidy, usually an actor or effect name.
  returns: string: the tidied name.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.Clean[${Target.Name}]}
  oldbot: Obj_OgreUtilities.CleanName, OgreBotAPI.CleanNameWithSpaces, GetInfoOb.Clean

${OgreBotAPI.Util.FileExists[path]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: TRUE when the file exists, also trying it with .iss added; a path without a colon is looked up under the Inner Space Scripts folder. A folder is not a file, and an empty path returns FALSE.
  arg path (string): A full path, or a path relative to the Scripts folder such as EQ2OgreBot/OgreBot. The .iss ending may be left off.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the file exists, as given or with .iss added; FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.FileExists["EQ2OgreBot/OgreBot"]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.FileExists

${OgreBotAPI.Util.Hours[n]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: Returns the hours part of a number of seconds, wrapped at 24 so whole days are dropped. 90000 seconds (25 hours) gives 1.
  arg n (int64, default: 0): The number of seconds.
  returns: int64: the hours, 0 to 23.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.Hours[7500]}
  oldbot: Obj_OgreUtilities.Get_Hours, OgreBotAPI.Get_Hours

${OgreBotAPI.Util.IEquals[a,b]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: TRUE when the two texts are the same, ignoring upper and lower case. Two empty texts count as equal.
  arg a (string): The first text.
  arg b (string): The second text.
  returns: bool: TRUE when a and b match ignoring case; FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.IEquals[${Target.Name},${Me.Name}]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.PE_ThisMember

${OgreBotAPI.Util.MD5[s]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: Returns the MD5 hash of the text as 32 lowercase hex characters. With no argument it hashes empty text.
  arg s (string): The text to hash, exactly as given.
  returns: string: the 32-character lowercase hex MD5 of the text.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.MD5["hello"]}
  oldbot: ISXOgre.MD5, OgreBotAPI.MD5

${OgreBotAPI.Util.Minutes[n]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: Returns the minutes part of a number of seconds, 0 to 59. 7500 seconds gives 5.
  arg n (int64, default: 0): The number of seconds.
  returns: int64: the minutes, 0 to 59.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.Minutes[7500]}
  oldbot: Obj_OgreUtilities.Get_Minutes, OgreBotAPI.Get_Minutes

${OgreBotAPI.Util.RomanToInt[s]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: Reads a Roman numeral made of I, V, X and L (upper or lower case) and returns its value, so XLIV gives 44. Any other character, including C, D, M or a space, makes the whole answer 0.
  arg s (string): The Roman numeral, for example XLIV. Only I, V, X and L are understood.
  returns: int: the value of the numeral; 0 when the text is empty or has any other character.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.RomanToInt[XLIV]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.RomanToInt

${OgreBotAPI.Util.RoundToNearest[value,step,incBy]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: Rounds a whole number to the nearest multiple of step, then adds incBy; an exact half rounds up, so 45 with step 10 gives 50 and 44 gives 40. 0 and negative values are rounded the same way, and a step below 1 is used as 1.
  arg value (int, default: 0): The number to round. Decimals are cut off; 0 and negatives are kept.
  arg step (int, default: 1): Round to a multiple of this, for example 10. Anything below 1 is used as 1.
  arg incBy (int, default: 0): Added to the rounded result.
  returns: int: the rounded value plus incBy.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.RoundToNearest[${Me.Level},10,0]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.RoundNumToNearestValue

${OgreBotAPI.Util.Seconds[n]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: Returns the seconds part of a number of seconds, 0 to 59. 7530 seconds gives 30.
  arg n (int64, default: 0): The number of seconds.
  returns: int64: the seconds, 0 to 59.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.Seconds[7530]}
  oldbot: Obj_OgreUtilities.Get_Seconds, OgreBotAPI.Get_Seconds

${OgreBotAPI.Util.SecondsToHMS[n]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: Formats a number of seconds as timer text in days, hours, minutes and seconds, like "1d 2h 5m 30s". A part that is 0 is left out, so 300 gives "5m" and 45 gives "45s".
  arg n (int64, default: 0): The number of seconds to format.
  returns: string: the time, for example "2h 5m"; "0s" for 0 or less.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.SecondsToHMS[7500]}
  oldbot: Obj_OgreUtilities.ConvertSecondsToHMS, OgreBotAPI.ConvertSecondsToHMS

${OgreBotAPI.Util.SlotArrayToSlot[n]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: Returns n plus 1, turning a 0-based equipment slot position (the item Slot member) into a 1-based slot number. Nothing is looked up or checked.
  arg n (int, default: 0): The 0-based slot position.
  returns: int: n + 1.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.SlotArrayToSlot[0]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.ConvertSlotArrayToSlot

${OgreBotAPI.Util.StripColourCodes[s]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: Removes one colour code from the start of the text (#RRGGBB, or \#RRGGBB in its escaped form) and returns the rest; colour codes later in the text are left alone. With no argument it uses the current zone name, which is empty when you are not in the world.
  arg s (string): The text to strip. Leave it out to use ${Zone.Name}.
  returns: string: the text without its leading colour code; unchanged when it does not start with one.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.StripColourCodes[${Zone.Name}]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.RemoveColourCode

${OgreBotAPI.Util.StripZoneNumber[s]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: Returns the text with a leading #RRGGBB colour code, every #00FF00 and /c colour token, and any trailing spaces and digits removed, so "Antonica 2" gives Antonica. With no argument it uses the current zone name, which is empty when you are not in the world.
  arg s (string, default: ${Zone.Name}): The zone name to clean. Leave it out to use ${Zone.Name}.
  returns: string: the zone name without colour codes or its trailing number.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.StripZoneNumber[${Zone.Name}]}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb.RemoveZoneNumber, OgreBotAPI.RemoveZoneNumber

${OgreBotAPI.Util.StripZoneNumberOnly[s]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: Returns the text with any trailing spaces and digits removed, so "Antonica 2" gives Antonica, and leaves colour codes in place. With no argument it uses the current zone name, which is empty when you are not in the world.
  arg s (string, default: ${Zone.Name}): The zone name to clean. Leave it out to use ${Zone.Name}. The first character is always kept.
  returns: string: the text without its trailing spaces and digits.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.StripZoneNumberOnly[${Zone.Name}]}
  oldbot: Obj_OgreUtilities.RemoveZoneNumber, OgreBotAPI.RemoveZoneNumberOnly

${OgreBotAPI.Util.ToFloat[s]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: Turns text into a decimal number, dropping commas first; text that does not start with a number gives 0. Quote a value that has commas in it, or the comma splits it into a second argument.
  arg s (string): The text to read, for example "1,234.5".
  returns: float: the number read from the text; 0 when it does not start with a number.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.ToFloat["1,234.5"]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.To_Float

${OgreBotAPI.Util.ToInt[s]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: Turns text into a whole number, dropping commas first; reading stops at the first character that is not a digit, and text that does not start with a number gives 0. Quote a value that has commas in it, or the comma splits it into a second argument.
  arg s (string): The text to read, for example "1,234,567". Leading spaces and a + or - sign are allowed.
  returns: int64: the number read from the text; 0 when it does not start with a number.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.ToInt["1,234,567"]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.To_Int, SpellOb.ConvertToInt64

${OgreBotAPI.Util.ToNumber[s]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: Returns the text with every comma and percent sign removed, so "1,234%" comes back as 1234. It does not check that what is left is a number.
  arg s (string): The text to clean, for example "1,234%". Quote it when it has commas.
  returns: string: the text without commas or percent signs.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Util.ToNumber["1,234%"]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.To_Number

OgreBotAPI.Util:CheckResearch[fw, forceReport=FALSE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: Queues a look at the research (Knowledge) window, opening it first when it is not up, and echoes "Research: <name> --> <progress>." to the console. Without forceReport it echoes only when the research reads Complete.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg forceReport (bool, default: FALSE): TRUE echoes the progress whatever it says; FALSE echoes only when it is Complete.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Util:CheckResearch[igw:${Me.Name},TRUE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CheckResearch

OgreBotAPI.Util:CheckResearchMaterials[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: Queues a pass over every Advancement, Companion, Mount, Tradeskill, Upgrade and General Research Material in your bags: each is examined and the first choice in the window it opens is picked, or the windows are closed with a console line when it has no eligible research. With none in the bags it echoes that and does nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Util:CheckResearchMaterials[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Research_Material_Check

OgreBotAPI.Util:DelayedAction[fw, delay, command...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: Runs a console command after a delay on each character the for-who picks at the time of the call; the timer is dropped if that character zones before it fires. Give the command as one quoted argument (escape any comma inside it), and note that a bare number for the delay is milliseconds.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg delay (string): How long to wait: a bare whole number is milliseconds, or add a unit - 500ms, 10s, 1.5s, 2m, 1h. Anything else (30x, "30 s", -5) echoes an error and nothing is armed.
  arg command... (string): The command to run, quoted as one argument, for example "eq2execute sit". If it arrives in several pieces they are joined back with commas and a warning is echoed; an empty command echoes an error and nothing is armed.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Util:DelayedAction[igw:${Me.Name},10s,"eq2execute sit"]

OgreBotAPI.Util:OnScreenTimer[fw, time=30, slot=1, message="Timer:", minUpdate=1]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: Shows a message with a live countdown in one of the ten on-screen timer slots, opening the on-screen display if it is closed; the line is removed 5 seconds after the countdown ends. A slot below 1 uses slot 1 and one above 10 uses slot 10, and a slot that was set less than minUpdate seconds ago silently keeps its old timer.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg time (float, default: 30): Seconds to count down from. Decimals are cut off.
  arg slot (int, default: 1): Which timer line to use, 1 to 10. A number outside is moved to the nearest of them.
  arg message (string, default: "Timer:"): The text shown before the countdown. Empty uses "Timer:".
  arg minUpdate (int, default: 1): Seconds after this call during which a new timer for the same slot is refused. 0 allows an immediate replacement.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Util:OnScreenTimer[igw:${Me.Name},45,2,"Adds in:",1]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:OnScreenTimer

OgreBotAPI.Util:OnScreenTimerReset[fw, slot=1]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Util
  what: Clears one on-screen timer slot; the line disappears within a second. It does not lift the minUpdate hold of the timer it clears, so a new timer for that slot inside that time is still refused.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg slot (int, default: 1): Which timer line to clear, 1 to 10. A number outside is moved to the nearest of them.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Util:OnScreenTimerReset[igw:${Me.Name},2]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:OnScreenTimerReset


== OgreBotAPI.Vars ==

${OgreBotAPI.Vars.Bool[name]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Vars
  what: Reads the script variable name as a yes/no: TRUE only when its whole value is 1, true, yes or on in any case. A missing variable, an empty value or any other text (2, enabled, a value with spaces around it) reads FALSE.
  arg name (string): The variable name, case-sensitive.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the stored value is a yes word; FALSE otherwise, including when the variable is missing.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Vars.Bool[UseCampSpot]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_Variable_Bool

${OgreBotAPI.Vars.Exists[name]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Vars
  what: TRUE when a variable called name is in this session's script variable store, even if its value is empty. Use it to tell a missing variable from an empty one, since Get returns an empty string for both.
  arg name (string): The variable name, case-sensitive.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the variable is stored; FALSE when it is missing or name is blank.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Vars.Exists[PullCount]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_VariableExists

${OgreBotAPI.Vars.Get[name]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Vars
  what: The value stored under name in this session's script variable store (set with OgreBotAPI.Vars:Set), or an empty string when there is no such variable. Names ignore case, and the store lives in memory on this session only: it is not shared with other characters, not saved, and lasts until it is cleared or the extension is unloaded.
  arg name (string): The variable name; case does not matter.
  returns: string: the stored value; empty when the variable is missing or was set to an empty value.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Vars.Get[PullCount]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_Variable, OgreBotAPI.Variables

${OgreBotAPI.Vars.GetInternal[name]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Vars
  what: The value stored under name in the internal variable store (set with OgreBotAPI.Vars:SetInternal), or an empty string when there is no such variable. It is a separate store from Get and Set but lives the same way: in memory on this session only, not shared, not saved; names ignore case.
  arg name (string): The internal variable name; case does not matter.
  returns: string: the stored value; empty when the variable is missing or was set to an empty value.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Vars.GetInternal[LastZone]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_InternalVariable, OgreBotAPI.InternalVariables

${OgreBotAPI.Vars.InternalExists[name]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Vars
  what: TRUE when a variable called name is in this session's internal variable store, even if its value is empty. It only looks at the internal store, not the one Get and Set use.
  arg name (string): The internal variable name, case-sensitive.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the internal variable is stored; FALSE when it is missing or name is blank.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Vars.InternalExists[LastZone]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_InternalVariableExists

OgreBotAPI.Vars:Clear[fw, name]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Vars
  what: Removes the variable name from the script variable store on each matching character, so Exists then reads FALSE and Get an empty string. Nothing happens when name is blank or the variable is missing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg name (string): The variable name to remove, case-sensitive.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Vars:Clear[${Me.Name},PullCount]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Clear_Variable

OgreBotAPI.Vars:ClearAll[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Vars
  what: Removes every variable from the script variable store on each matching character. The internal store is not touched (use ClearAllInternal).
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Vars:ClearAll[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Clear_Variables

OgreBotAPI.Vars:ClearAllInternal[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Vars
  what: Removes every variable from the internal variable store on each matching character. The store Get and Set use is not touched.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Vars:ClearAllInternal[igw:${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Clear_InternalVariables

OgreBotAPI.Vars:ClearInternal[fw, name]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Vars
  what: Removes the variable name from the internal variable store on each matching character, so InternalExists then reads FALSE. Nothing happens when name is blank or the variable is missing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg name (string): The internal variable name to remove, case-sensitive.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Vars:ClearInternal[${Me.Name},LastZone]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Clear_InternalVariable

OgreBotAPI.Vars:Set[fw, name, value]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Vars
  what: Stores value under name in the script variable store on each matching character, replacing any earlier value; a blank value is stored as an empty string. Nothing happens when name is blank, and a successful set prints nothing.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg name (string): The variable name; case does not matter. Blank does nothing.
  arg value (string): The text to store. Blank stores an empty value.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Vars:Set[igw:${Me.Name},PullCount,3]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Set_Variable

OgreBotAPI.Vars:SetInternal[fw, name, value]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Vars
  what: Stores value under name in the internal variable store on each matching character, replacing any earlier value. Nothing happens when name is blank, and the store Get and Set use is not touched.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg name (string): The internal variable name; case does not matter. Blank does nothing.
  arg value (string): The text to store. Blank stores an empty value.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Vars:SetInternal[${Me.Name},LastZone,antonica]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Set_InternalVariable


== OgreBotAPI.Windows ==

${OgreBotAPI.Windows.CastingWindowVisible}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Windows
  what: Whether the game's casting bar is on screen. Always FALSE while you are not in the world.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the casting bar is visible; FALSE when it is hidden or you are not in the world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Windows.CastingWindowVisible}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.IsCastingWindowVisible

${OgreBotAPI.Windows.ReplyExists[text]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Windows
  what: Which reply of the open reply dialog (the window a clicked item or object opens) contains the text, in any case. It answers a number, not TRUE/FALSE, so test it with > 0; it does not look at the NPC conversation window.
  arg text (string): Text to look for inside each reply. Matches anywhere in the reply, any case.
  returns: int: the 1-based number of the first reply that contains the text; 0 when no reply dialog is open, nothing matches, or the text is empty.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Windows.ReplyExists[Yes]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.ReplyDialog_ReplyExists

${OgreBotAPI.Windows.RewardID[num|name,windowId]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Windows
  what: The number of one reward on a reward window, picked by number or by item name the same way AcceptReward picks it. A number past the window's reward count, a name that matches no row, an empty selection, or no reward window all answer 0.
  arg num|name (number or text): The reward to pick: its number on the window (1 = the first), or its item name (trimmed, any case, first match). Empty or 0 picks nothing.
  arg windowId (int, default: 0): The reward window id to read. Empty or 0 = the active reward window (the oldest one the bot saw open that is still up).
  returns: int: the 1-based reward number; 0 when there is no reward window or nothing matches.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Windows.RewardID[2,0]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_RewardID

${OgreBotAPI.Windows.RewardLinkID[num|name,windowId]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Windows
  what: The LinkID of one reward on a reward window, picked by number or by item name the same way AcceptReward picks it. Empty when there is no reward window, nothing matches, or the game has no LinkID for that row.
  arg num|name (number or text): The reward to pick: its number on the window (1 = the first), or its item name (trimmed, any case, first match). Empty or 0 picks nothing.
  arg windowId (int, default: 0): The reward window id to read. Empty or 0 = the active reward window (the oldest one the bot saw open that is still up).
  returns: string: that reward's LinkID; empty when there is no window or no match.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Windows.RewardLinkID[1,0]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_RewardLinkID

${OgreBotAPI.Windows.RewardName[num|name,windowId]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Windows
  what: The item name of one reward on a reward window, picked by number or by item name. Empty when there is no reward window, nothing matches, or the row does not read.
  arg num|name (number or text): The reward to pick: its number on the window (1 = the first), or its item name (trimmed, any case, first match). Empty or 0 picks nothing.
  arg windowId (int, default: 0): The reward window id to read. Empty or 0 = the active reward window (the oldest one the bot saw open that is still up).
  returns: string: that reward's item name; empty when there is no window or no match.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Windows.RewardName[1,0]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Get_RewardName

${OgreBotAPI.Windows.RewardWindowID}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Windows
  what: The id of the active reward window: the oldest reward window the bot saw open that is still up, or with none held, the one open now. It reads 0 when no reward window is up.
  returns: int64: the active reward window's id; 0 when none is open or you are not in the world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Windows.RewardWindowID}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.RewardWindow_Get_WindowID

${OgreBotAPI.Windows.SelectOption[n]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Windows
  what: Which option of the open select window matches, without clicking anything and without printing anything, so a script may read it as often as it likes. Options count from 1 (OldBot's numbers were one higher).
  arg search... (number or text): The option to find: a number is that option's position; text must match the option name exactly (any case). Add -substring as another argument to match text anywhere in the name.
  returns: int: the 1-based option position; 0 when no select window is open, nothing matches, or no argument is given.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Windows.SelectOption[1]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.Select_Window_GetOption

OgreBotAPI.Windows:AcceptNoChoiceReward[fw, windowId=0]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Windows
  what: Presses Receive on a reward window that offers no choice. It refuses, with a console line, a window that offers a choice, a 'New Quest!' offer, or a window whose reward pack is not shown.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg windowId (int, default: 0): The reward window id. Empty or 0 = the active reward window (the oldest one the bot saw open that is still up).
  example: OgreBotAPI.Windows:AcceptNoChoiceReward[${Me.Name},0]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:AcceptNoChoiceReward

OgreBotAPI.Windows:AcceptReward[fw, num|name=0, windowId=0]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Windows
  what: Takes a reward from a reward window: on a choice window it accepts the reward you name, and on a single or no-choice window it presses Receive whatever you pass, but never on a 'New Quest!' offer. Each outcome, including no window or no match, prints a line to the console.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg num|name (number or text, default: 0): The reward to take on a choice window: its number (1 = the first) or its item name (any case). Ignored on a single-reward window.
  arg windowId (int, default: 0): The reward window id. 0 = the active reward window (the oldest one the bot saw open that is still up).
  example: OgreBotAPI.Windows:AcceptReward[${Me.Name},1,0]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:AcceptReward, Obj_OgreIH:AcceptReward

OgreBotAPI.Windows:Choice[fw, option=1]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Windows
  what: Clicks one of the choice window's buttons: 1 is the first button, 2 the second. Another number is clamped to the nearer of the two, with a console line saying which it chose; does nothing when no choice window is open.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg option (int, default: 1): Which button to click: 1 or 2 (below 1 is 1, above 2 is 2).
  example: OgreBotAPI.Windows:Choice[${Me.Name},1]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ChoiceWindow

OgreBotAPI.Windows:Close[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Windows
  what: Closes the top-most game window, exactly as the /close_top_window command does. Does nothing when you are not in the world.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Windows:Close[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CloseWindow

OgreBotAPI.Windows:CloseExamine[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Windows
  what: Clicks the close button of the item examine window once. It closes one examine window per call, and it clicks even when none is open.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Windows:CloseExamine[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:CloseAllExamine, OgreBotAPI:CloseExamineWindow, OgreBotAPI:CloseExamine

OgreBotAPI.Windows:InputTextAccept[fw]

OgreBotAPI.Windows:Reply[fw, number|text=1]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Windows
  what: Picks a reply in the open reply dialog (the window a clicked item or object opens): a number picks that reply, text picks the first reply that contains it in any case. When no dialog is open or nothing matches, nothing is clicked and a warning listing the replies goes to the console.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg number|text (number or text, default: 1): A reply number (1 = the first), or text to find inside a reply (any case).

  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ReplyDialogClose

OgreBotAPI.Windows:Select[fw, search...]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Windows
  what: Picks an option in the open select window and then presses its OK. The match happens at once but the clicks are queued: the option first, then OK about 0.3 seconds later; each pick and each miss prints a line to the console.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg search... (number or text): The option to pick: a number is its position (1 = the first real option); text must match the option name exactly, any case. Flags may come before or after it as their own arguments: -substring (match text anywhere in the name), -test (click the option but not OK), -reportonly (say which option matches, click nothing) and -spew (list the options).
  example: OgreBotAPI.Windows:Select[${Me.Name},1]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Select_Window

OgreBotAPI.Windows:SelectCancel[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Windows
  what: Clicks Cancel on the open select window. Does nothing, silently, when the Cancel button is not visible.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Windows:SelectCancel[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Select_Window_Cancel

OgreBotAPI.Windows:SelectSpew[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Windows
  what: Prints every option of the open select window to the console, numbered from 1, with the row template it found. Prints a 'no select window open' line instead when there is none.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Windows:SelectSpew[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Select_Window_Spew

OgreBotAPI.Windows:ShowConsole[fw, on=TRUE]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Windows
  what: Opens the OgreConsole window, or closes it for a no word (FALSE, 0, no or off). Empty, a yes word, or any other word opens it, so a typo never closes the console.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg on (bool, default: TRUE): FALSE, 0, no or off closes the console; anything else, empty included, opens it.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Windows:ShowConsole[${Me.Name},TRUE]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ShowOgreConsole

OgreBotAPI.Windows:SpewRewardWindowIDs[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Windows
  what: Prints every reward window id the bot has seen open, oldest first, and whether each is still up. It keeps at most the last 16 windows.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Windows:SpewRewardWindowIDs[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:RewardWindow_Spew_WindowIDs

OgreBotAPI.Windows:ToggleConsole[fw, value=toggle]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Windows
  what: Flips the OgreConsole window between open and closed. A yes word (TRUE, 1, yes, on) always opens it and a no word (FALSE, 0, no, off) always closes it.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg value (string, default: toggle): TRUE opens, FALSE closes, anything else (or nothing) flips.
  example: OgreBotAPI.Windows:ToggleConsole[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ToggleConsoleWindow

OgreBotAPI.Windows:ToggleMain[fw]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Windows
  what: Hides the main OgreBot window if it is shown, or shows it if it is hidden. It does not close OgreBot, and it does nothing when OgreBot is not open.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  example: OgreBotAPI.Windows:ToggleMain[${Me.Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ToggleMainWindow


== OgreBotAPI.Zone ==

${OgreBotAPI.Zone.CityRestrictions}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Zone
  what: TRUE in one of the bot's 17 city zones, such as The City of Freeport or Qeynos Province District, unless Allow City Casting is ticked. FALSE out of world.
  returns: bool: TRUE in a listed city with Allow City Casting unticked; FALSE otherwise or out of world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Zone.CityRestrictions}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.CityRestrictions

${OgreBotAPI.Zone.CleanName[name]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Zone
  what: The same cleaned name as Name, made safe for file and setting names: spaces become underscores and the characters , [ ] : ' and ` are removed. Reads "" out of world when no name is passed.
  arg name (text, default: ${Zone.Name}): a zone name to clean; blank means the zone you are in
  returns: string: the cleaned zone name with underscores for spaces; "" out of world when no name is given.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Zone.CleanName}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.CleanZoneName, Ogre_Instance_Controller.CleanZoneName

${OgreBotAPI.Zone.InGuildHall}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Zone
  what: TRUE when the zone's short name contains guildhall, except the Island of Mara Estate (guildhall_mara). FALSE out of world.
  returns: bool: TRUE in a guild hall; FALSE elsewhere or out of world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Zone.InGuildHall}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb.InGuildHallZone, Obj_OgreUtilities.InGuildHallZone, OgreBotAPI.InGuildHallZone

${OgreBotAPI.Zone.InHouse}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Zone
  what: TRUE when you look to be inside a house: not in a guild hall, and a Magic Door to the Guild Hall or a market bulletin board is in the zone. It is a guess from those two objects; FALSE out of world.
  returns: bool: TRUE when either object is in the zone and it is not a guild hall; FALSE otherwise or out of world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Zone.InHouse}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb.InHouseZone, OgreBotAPI.InHouseZone

${OgreBotAPI.Zone.InHouseAccess}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Zone
  what: TRUE in one of the eight zones the bot treats as house-access zones: Antonica, Halas, the two Qeynos zones, Timorous Deep, Greater Faydark, Neriak and Freeport. This is the outdoor zone, not the house itself; FALSE out of world.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the zone's short name is antonica, halas, qeynos_combined01, qeynos_combined02, exp04_rgn_timorous_deep, exp03_rgn_greater_faydark, neriak or freeport_combined; FALSE otherwise or out of world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Zone.InHouseAccess}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb.InHouseAccessZone, OgreBotAPI.InHouseAccessZone

${OgreBotAPI.Zone.InInstance}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Zone
  what: TRUE when the zone name contains a [ (instances are named like that, such as [Heroic] or [Solo]) and you are not in a guild hall. FALSE out of world.
  returns: bool: TRUE in an instance; FALSE in an open zone, a guild hall, or out of world.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Zone.InInstance}
  oldbot: GetInfoOb.InAInstance, OgreBotAPI.InInstance

${OgreBotAPI.Zone.Name[name]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Zone
  what: The zone name with colour codes and the trailing instance number removed. Every trailing digit and space is stripped, so a name that really ends in a number loses it; "" out of world when no name is passed.
  arg name (text, default: ${Zone.Name}): a zone name to clean; blank means the zone you are in
  returns: string: the cleaned zone name; "" out of world when no name is given.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Zone.Name}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.ZoneName

${OgreBotAPI.Zone.ResetReady}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Zone
  what: TRUE once the Zone Reuse table has been read at least once and no re-read is asked for or running. Wait for it after ResetUpdateInfo before reading ResetZoneData.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the table is in and not being re-read; FALSE before the first read or while a re-read is pending.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Zone.ResetReady}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.ZoneReset_IsReady

${OgreBotAPI.Zone.ResetUpdating}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Zone
  what: TRUE while a Zone Reuse re-read is asked for or running.
  returns: bool: TRUE while a re-read is pending or running; FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Zone.ResetUpdating}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.ZoneReset_IsUpdating

${OgreBotAPI.Zone.ResetZoneData[zone,field]}
  kind: member of OgreBotAPI.Zone
  what: One zone's entry from the Zone Reuse window, as last read by ResetUpdateInfo. A zone that is not in the table reads FALSE, and an unknown field prints a console line and reads FALSE.
  arg zone (text): the zone name exactly as the Zone Reuse window shows it, any case
  arg field (text): blank reads TRUE when the zone has an entry; otherwise ZoneName, IsSet (TRUE when its timer state is known), Resettable, TimeLeft (seconds) or TextTimeLeft
  returns: bool, int64 or string by field: TRUE/FALSE for blank, IsSet and Resettable; seconds for TimeLeft; text for ZoneName and TextTimeLeft. FALSE when the zone is not in the table.
  example: echo ${OgreBotAPI.Zone.ResetZoneData["${OgreBotAPI.Zone.Name}",Resettable]}
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI.ZoneReset_Get_ZoneData

OgreBotAPI.Zone:ChampionsResetter[fw, zone]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Zone
  what: Resets one zone with your Champion's Zone Lockout Reset item: examines it, then picks the zone in the window it opens. Prints a console line when the item is not in your bags, is on cooldown, or does not list the zone.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg zone (text): the zone name as the item's window lists it
  example: OgreBotAPI.Zone:ChampionsResetter[${Me.Name},"${OgreBotAPI.Zone.Name}"]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Champions_Zone_Resetter

  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg toWho (character name): the group member whose instance to join
  example: OgreBotAPI.Zone:ChangeZoneTo[${Me.Name},${Group[1].Name}]
  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:ChangeZoneTo, Obj_OgreIH:ChangeZoneTo

  arg zone (text): the zone name as the Zone Reuse window shows it

OgreBotAPI.Zone:ResetAll[fw, allowRaid=FALSE]

  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg zone (text): the zone name as the Zone Reuse window shows it

  oldbot: OgreBotAPI:Select_Zone_Version

OgreBotAPI.Zone:ShareQuestsForZone[fw, zone=""]
  kind: method of OgreBotAPI.Zone
  what: Shares, one at a time after the group has gathered, the Hot Zones missions in your journal that belong to this zone. It works only while you are in that zone, and with for-who all only the group leader shares.
  arg fw (for-who): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names
  arg zone (text, default: ""): the zone the missions are for; blank means the zone you are in. Another zone prints a console line and shares nothing.
