== ISXOgreEQ2.Class ==

${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.Archetype}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Class
  what: The local character's archetype in lowercase: fighter, priest, mage or scout. It is read from the game the first time it is asked for once in world and refreshed on every zone load; it is empty before any character has been read, and a ChangeValue override does not change it (only Is does).
  returns: string: fighter, priest, mage or scout; empty when no character has been read yet or the game's value is not recognised
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.Archetype}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.AscensionClass}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Class
  what: The local character's ascension class: Thaumaturgist, Elementalist, Etherealist or Geomancer, in that capitalisation. Empty when the character has no ascension class or none of those names is found in the game's ascension label.
  returns: string: Thaumaturgist, Elementalist, Etherealist or Geomancer; empty when none is found
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.AscensionClass}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.ClassTier}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Class
  what: The local character's class grouping, the level between archetype and subclass, in lowercase: warrior, crusader, brawler, cleric, druid, shaman, shaper, sorcerer, enchanter, summoner, bard, rogue, predator or animalist. Empty before any character has been read.
  returns: string: the lowercase class grouping; empty when no character has been read yet or the game's value is not recognised
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.ClassTier}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.HasEpic2}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Class
  what: TRUE for a ranger who owns the ranger epic 2.0 ability, FALSE otherwise. The buff is hidden and kept up, so owning it is taken to mean it is on.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the character is a ranger who owns the epic 2.0 ability; FALSE otherwise
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.HasEpic2}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.Is[name]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Class
  what: TRUE when name matches the local character's archetype, class grouping or class, case-insensitive, with an optional leading Is ignored, so Is[Scout], Is[predator] and Is[IsRanger] all answer TRUE for a ranger. A value forced with ChangeValue for that name wins over the real class, and no argument returns FALSE.
  arg name (string): An archetype, class grouping or class name, optionally prefixed with Is (fighter, crusader, paladin, IsPaladin)
  returns: bool: TRUE when the name matches the character (or a ChangeValue override for it is TRUE); FALSE otherwise or when no name is given
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.Is[templar]}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.OnBGServer}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Class
  what: TRUE when the current server is the Battlegrounds server. The server name match is case-insensitive.
  returns: bool: TRUE on Battlegrounds; FALSE on any other server or before the server has been read
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.OnBGServer}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.OnKaladimServer}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Class
  what: TRUE when the current server is Kaladim. Kaladim also counts as TLE, so OnTLEServer is TRUE there too.
  returns: bool: TRUE on Kaladim; FALSE on any other server or before the server has been read
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.OnKaladimServer}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.OnTLEServer}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Class
  what: TRUE when the current server is a Time Locked Expansion server: Kaladim, Varsoon, Fallen Gate, Stormhold, Deathtoll, Zarrakon or Wuoshi. The server is read with the class identity (first read and every zone load) and again by UpdateServer.
  returns: bool: TRUE on one of the listed TLE servers; FALSE on any other server or before the server has been read
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.OnTLEServer}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.OnVarsoonServer}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Class
  what: TRUE when the current server is Varsoon. Varsoon also counts as TLE, so OnTLEServer is TRUE there too.
  returns: bool: TRUE on Varsoon; FALSE on any other server or before the server has been read
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.OnVarsoonServer}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.Ruleset}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Class
  what: The current server's ruleset as one word: Battlegrounds, TLE or Live. Any server not on the TLE or Battlegrounds list answers Live, including before the server has been read.
  returns: string: Battlegrounds, TLE or Live
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.Ruleset}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.Subclass}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Class
  what: The local character's final class in lowercase, such as templar, ranger or shadowknight (one of the 26 classes). Empty before any character has been read.
  returns: string: the lowercase class name; empty when no character has been read yet or the game's value is not recognised
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.Subclass}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.WaterBreathingAbility}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Class
  what: The name of the group water-breathing ability the bot uses for the local character's class: Water Spirit for a mystic, Abominus for a defiler. Every other class, channeler included, answers empty.
  returns: string: Water Spirit, Abominus, or empty for every other class
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Class.WaterBreathingAbility}

ISXOgreEQ2.Class:ChangeValue[member,value]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Class
  what: Forces Is[member] to answer value for the local character, so ChangeValue[IsFighter,TRUE] makes a non-fighter run fighter logic, and auto removes the override so it reads what the game says again; it lasts across zones until set again or a different character is read. A missing argument, a member that is not an archetype, class or subclass, or a value that is not TRUE, FALSE or auto prints one line and stores nothing, the same line as OgreBotAPI.Roster:SetClassValue.
  arg member (string): The class name to force, with or without a leading Is (IsFighter, fighter, IsTemplar): an archetype, class or subclass
  arg value (string): TRUE or FALSE (also 1/0, yes/no, on/off) to force it, or auto to remove the override
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Class:ChangeValue[IsFighter,TRUE]

ISXOgreEQ2.Class:Update
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Class
  what: Re-reads the local character's name, class, ascension class and server from the game right away; out of world the read is held and happens on the first Class read once in world. ChangeValue overrides survive for the same character but are dropped when a different character is read, and a console line says so whenever the identity changes.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Class:Update

ISXOgreEQ2.Class:UpdateServer
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Class
  what: Re-reads the server name now and resets OnTLEServer, OnKaladimServer, OnVarsoonServer, OnBGServer and Ruleset from it. Class values are not touched.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Class:UpdateServer


== ISXOgreEQ2.Codex ==

ISXOgreEQ2.Codex:End
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Codex
  what: Stops a running Codex inspect pass: drops the names still waiting, closes the inspect window and prints how many were not inspected - the same as ogre end codexinspect. Players already uploaded keep their cooldown; with no pass running it does nothing.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Codex:End

ISXOgreEQ2.Codex:Inspect[names,setting]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Codex
  what: Queues the named players to be inspected one at a time, 3 s apart, each one an inspect request to the game server (a server request), and each uploaded to Codex as an active raid member - the same as ogre codexinspect. A name inspected in the last 5 minutes (by default) is skipped, reset clears the active raid roster on Codex, status (or ?) or no argument prints the status line, and the console says how many were queued.
  arg names (string): a comma-separated list of player names, or reset, or status / ?
  arg setting (string, default: ""): optional; leave it out
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Codex:Inspect[status]

ISXOgreEQ2.Codex:Toon[word]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Codex
  what: Inspects your own character and uploads its snapshot to Codex - the same as ogre codextoon: it sends the game an inspect request for you (a server request), then uploads over the web and prints the result when the upload answers. With status (or ?) it only prints the Codex status line, and it refuses with a message when Codex is not set up, you are not in the world, or an upload is already running.
  arg word (string, default: ""): status or ? prints the Codex status line instead of uploading; leave it out to upload
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Codex:Toon[status]


== ISXOgreEQ2.Collection ==

${ISXOgreEQ2.Collection.Running}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Collection
  what: TRUE while an `ogre cm` collection run is in progress, from the depot or from your bags. Starting another while one runs is refused with a busy warning.
  returns: bool: TRUE while a collection run is going; FALSE when idle.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Collection.Running}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Collection.Status}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Collection
  what: Progress of the running collection run, or "idle". It is the same text `${ISXOgreEQ2.Collection}` returns.
  returns: string: "idle", "cm (done/total, n added)" for a depot run or "cm -inventory (done/total, n added)" for a bag scan.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Collection.Status}

ISXOgreEQ2.Collection:Run[flags...]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Collection
  what: The engine behind `ogre cm`: opens the collectible depot within 10 m, turns Hide Grey on, then withdraws each listed piece one at a time, examines it and clicks the quest journal's Add button; the final result line goes to OgreConsole prefixed with your name. With -inventory it scans your bags instead and MAKES A SERVER CALL PER ITEM (`.ToItemInfo.IsCollectible` and `.AlreadyCollected`, waiting up to 5 s for each item's info), so it is slow.
  arg flags... (string): none = the nearest depot whose name contains Collectible Depot, else a Personal Collectible Stash; -small = exactly Collectible Depot; -large = exactly Collectible Depot (Large) (a named depot that is not found refuses the call); -inventory (also 1 or -1) scans your bags instead; unknown words are ignored
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Collection:Run[-large]

ISXOgreEQ2.Collection:Stop
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Collection
  what: Stops a running collection run, closes the depot window if it is open and prints "cm: stopped.". Does nothing when idle.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Collection:Stop


== ISXOgreEQ2.Commands ==

ISXOgreEQ2.Commands:Close
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Commands
  what: Closes the Commands window and drops any clicks it had not run yet.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Commands:Close

ISXOgreEQ2.Commands:Open
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Commands
  what: Opens the Commands window, which lists the ogre console commands with their usage and lets you run or end one with a click. If the window cannot open, a warning goes to the console.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Commands:Open


== ISXOgreEQ2.ContentBuilder ==

ISXOgreEQ2.ContentBuilder:End
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.ContentBuilder
  what: Closes the Content Builder window (the same as `ogre end contentbuilder` and the window's X). Changes that were not saved are kept and offered back the next time the window opens, and a run it started goes on.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.ContentBuilder:End

ISXOgreEQ2.ContentBuilder:Open[tier,path]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.ContentBuilder
  what: Opens the Content Builder window (the same as `ogre contentbuilder`), on a zone file when you name one. A window that is already open comes to the front, and asks before it opens that file over unsaved changes; without the Ogre UI desktop it prints a warning.
  arg tier (string, default: none): The root the zone file is in: default or custom. Leave both out to open the window as it was.
  arg path (string, default: none): The zone file's path inside that root, ending in .json. A path with spaces may be quoted or written as several words.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.ContentBuilder:Open[custom,"My_Zone.json"]
  more: https://kannkor.github.io/ISXOgre/EQ2/bot/developer/zone-files/builder


== ISXOgreEQ2.Craft ==

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Crafted}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: How many crafts the current queue has made: a writ or loop run crafts queue after queue, and this counts the one crafting now. Once nothing is running it reads the count from the last queue that ran, so a finished run does not drop to 0.
  returns: int: crafts made so far in the current queue, or in the last queue once idle; 0 before any run.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Crafted}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.CraftTotal}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: How many crafts the current queue plans to make: a writ or loop run crafts queue after queue, so this is one queue's total, not the whole run's. Once nothing is running it reads the total of the last queue that ran.
  returns: int: the planned craft count of the current queue, or of the last queue once idle; 0 before any run.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.CraftTotal}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Details}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: The whole crafting picture as one JSON string: running, paused, flow, stage, status, crafted, craftTotal, recipe, row, rows, lastError, and short (a list of name / need / have / fuel for what the latest resource count came up short on). recipe is "" and row / rows are 0 when no queue row is being crafted.
  returns: string: a JSON object with the fields listed above.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Details}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Flow}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Which crafting run is going: idle, queue, writs, autotinkering, lowlevelleveling or quest. It goes back to idle when the run finishes.
  returns: string: "idle", "queue", "writs", "autotinkering", "lowlevelleveling" or "quest".
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Flow}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.IsReady}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Whether the crafting engine has started up, which happens on its first pulse after the extension loads. It does not mean the recipe book has been read - see ScanActive and QueueUpdated.
  returns: bool: TRUE once the crafting engine has started; FALSE before that.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.IsReady}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.LastError}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: The last refusal or failure the crafting engine reported, the same line the panel shows in red. It is cleared only when a run passes its start checks.
  returns: string: the last error or refusal text; "" when there has been none since the last good start.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.LastError}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.LastScribedRecipeId}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: The recipe id of the recipe you scribed most recently, by this engine or by hand, filled in when the recipe book is read again after the game's "put in recipe book" message, so it lags the name briefly. If that name is not found in the re-read book the id keeps the previous recipe's, so it can disagree with LastScribedRecipeName.
  returns: int64: the last scribed recipe's id; 0 when none has been seen since the extension loaded.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.LastScribedRecipeId}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.LastScribedRecipeName}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: The name of the recipe you scribed most recently, by this engine or by hand, taken from the game's "put in recipe book" message.
  returns: string: the last scribed recipe's name; "" when none has been seen since the extension loaded.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.LastScribedRecipeName}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Lite}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Whether craft lite is on - the reaction engine that casts the crafting reaction arts during a craft, also for crafts you start by hand. Opening the panel or starting any run turns it on.
  returns: bool: TRUE when craft lite (crafting reactions) is on; FALSE when it is off.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Lite}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.MissingResources}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Whether the latest queue's resource count came up short of something it needs. It stays set after the run ends and resets when the next count starts; Details lists what is short.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the latest resource count was short; FALSE before any count and when nothing was short.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.MissingResources}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.NavigationDetails}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: The most recent navigation request as a JSON string, the same payload OgreCraft_NavigationRequired passes: requestID, action, category, key, displayName, customNamedPoint, precision, zone, characterName, targetFound, and targetID / targetName / targetX / targetY / targetZ / targetDistance when the target was found. It keeps the last request after it is answered and is "" before the first one.
  returns: string: the last navigation request's JSON; "" when no request has been made since the extension loaded.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.NavigationDetails}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Paused}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Whether the crafting pause is on. A pause turned on with no run going still reads TRUE but holds nothing, and the next start clears it.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the crafting pause is on; FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Paused}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.QueueUpdated}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Whether every recipe add and queue load you asked for has landed in the setup queue. An add or load asked while the recipe book is still being read waits for the read, and this is FALSE until it lands.
  returns: bool: TRUE when no add or queue load is waiting for the recipe book; FALSE while one waits.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.QueueUpdated}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Recipes}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: How many recipes the engine has indexed from your recipe book. It is 0 until the book has been read; a read starts when a run starts, when you scribe a recipe or on Scan, and also when the panel opens or craft lite turns on unless Do NOT load recipes on startup is ticked.
  returns: int: the number of recipes indexed by the last recipe-book read; 0 before the first read.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Recipes}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.RecipesInQueue}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: How many recipe rows are in the setup queue (the queue Start crafts). It counts rows, not the quantity to craft.
  returns: int: the number of rows in the setup queue; 0 when it is empty.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.RecipesInQueue}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Running}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Whether a crafting run is going: a setup-queue run, writs, auto tinkering, low level leveling or quest crafting. A paused run still counts as running.
  returns: bool: TRUE while any crafting run is going (paused or not); FALSE when crafting is idle.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Running}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.ScanActive}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Whether the engine is reading your recipe book right now. Runs wait for the read to finish before they resolve any recipe.
  returns: bool: TRUE while the recipe book is being read; FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.ScanActive}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Setting[id]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: One crafting panel setting, read by its id, as the raw stored text. An id that has never been saved returns "" (the built-in default is not filled in), and a call with no id returns NULL.
  arg id (string): The panel setting id, such as slider_craft_writcount or checkbox_craft_useevents.
  returns: string: the stored value of that setting; "" when it is not set.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Setting[slider_craft_writcount]}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Stage}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: One word for what crafting is doing right now, such as countingResources, findingStation, walking, crafting, findingWrit, turningIn, buyingBooks or disposing. It reads idle when nothing is running.
  returns: string: the current stage word; "idle" when no run is going.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Stage}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Status}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: The crafting engine's status line, the same text the panel shows, such as "idle", "crafting <recipe>", "scanning recipes", "paused" or "waiting for your navigation script (...)". A refused start does not change it - the reason is in LastError.
  returns: string: the current status text; "idle" when nothing is running.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.Status}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.WaitingForNavigation}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Whether the crafting engine is waiting for your script to move the character, after it fired OgreCraft_NavigationRequired. This happens only with the "use events" setting (checkbox_craft_useevents) on; the wait has no time limit and Stop ends it.
  returns: bool: TRUE while a navigation request is waiting for CompleteNavigation or DeferNavigation; FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.WaitingForNavigation}

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:AddLastScribedRecipe[qty]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Adds the recipe you last scribed this session (by the bot or by hand) to the craft setup queue, waiting for the recipe book to be read first when needed. With nothing scribed yet it prints a warning and adds nothing; it is the same as OgreBotAPI.Craft:AddLastScribedRecipe.
  arg qty (int): How many to craft; left out, 0 or less it is 1.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:AddLastScribedRecipe[2]

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:AddRecipe[nameOrID|lastknownrecipe, qty]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Adds a recipe to the craft setup queue by full name, by part of a name that matches only one recipe (4 letters or more), by recipe ID, or lastknownrecipe for the recipe last scribed this session; a recipe already queued gets the quantity added. A recipe not in your book prints a warning and adds nothing, an add made before the book is read waits for it, and this is OgreBotAPI.Craft:AddRecipe without the for-who.
  arg nameOrID|lastknownrecipe (string): The recipe name, its ID (plain digits), or lastknownrecipe. A name may also be passed as several arguments; they are joined with spaces.
  arg qty (int): How many to craft. Read only when it is the last of two or more arguments and a whole number; left out it is 1, and 0 or less becomes 1.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:AddRecipe["Tempered Iron",2]

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:AddRecipeListFromFile[file]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Adds the recipes of one of your saved craft queues to the setup queue (the panel's Load Queue replaces it instead), warning about any recipe not in this character's book. The name is a queue in your queues folder, any path is cut off and a .json or .xml ending dropped, a missing name or file prints a warning, and a queue that needs the recipe book waits for the book to be read.
  arg file (string): The saved queue's name, with or without .json, as saved from the craft panel; a folder in front of it is ignored.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:AddRecipeListFromFile["MyQueue.json"]

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:BuyAllTinkeringRecipes[]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Buys every tinkering recipe book you do not already know or carry from Fizza Cogsworth, then scribes the ones your skill allows when the Scribe recipes setting is on. It is refused unless you carry at least 3 platinum, are in Steamfont Mountains and are within 10 meters of her, and also while a crafting flow or merchant errand is running (the same as OgreBotAPI.Craft:BuyAllTinkeringRecipes).
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:BuyAllTinkeringRecipes

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Catalog[]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Prints how much the craft data files loaded: devices, universal devices, merchant types, recipe book series, conversions and partial conversions. The files are loaded first if they were not yet.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Catalog

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Clear[]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Empties the craft setup queue, whether or not a flow is running, and prints setup queue cleared. Each row it drops fires OgreCraft_RecipeQueueUpdated as a removed row, as a remove does.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Clear

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:CompleteNavigation[]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Answers craft's OgreCraft_NavigationRequired event (sent only when the craft setting to use events for movement is on) to say your script has moved the character; craft then takes the nearest station or NPC of the same name within 100 m and checks the distance again. If no request is waiting it prints a warning, and it is the same as OgreBotAPI.Craft:CompleteNavigation.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:CompleteNavigation

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:DeferNavigation[]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Answers craft's OgreCraft_NavigationRequired event to say your script will not move the character, so craft walks there with its own movement. If no request is waiting it prints a warning, and it is the same as OgreBotAPI.Craft:DeferNavigation.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:DeferNavigation

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:End[]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Closes the craft window and ends all of crafting: the running flow, craft's own movement, a merchant errand, a summoned station, and craft lite. It is the same as ogre end craft and the window's X; use Stop to stop a run and keep the window.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:End

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Help[]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Prints the ogre craft console words and their arguments to the console. It changes nothing.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Help

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Lite
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Turns craft lite on, so the crafting reactions are cast for you during crafting rounds, and prints a console line when the state changes; turned on in the world with the recipe book not yet read, it also starts reading the book unless the "Do NOT load recipes on startup" setting is ticked. Opening the panel and starting any crafting flow turn it on as well.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Lite

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:LiteOff
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Turns craft lite off, so no crafting reactions are cast, drops any reaction waiting to be cast, and prints a console line when the state changes. Starting any crafting flow turns it back on.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:LiteOff

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Minimize[]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Rolls the craft window up to its header while crafting carries on; Open brings it back. With the window not open it does nothing.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Minimize

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Open
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Opens the crafting panel, or brings back a minimized one, and turns craft lite on - the same as a bare `ogre craft`. A panel that cannot open prints why and leaves craft as it was, and with the "Do NOT load recipes on startup" setting ticked an unread recipe book stays unread.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Open

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Pause[on|off]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Pauses or resumes crafting: off resumes, and on, any other word or no argument pauses. A craft already begun finishes and nothing new starts while paused, and a pause made with no flow running is dropped when the next flow starts.
  arg on|off (string, default: on): off resumes; on, any other word, or nothing pauses.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Pause[on]

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Queue[]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Prints each row of the craft setup queue to the console as quantity, recipe name and recipe ID, or setup queue is empty. It changes nothing.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Queue

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Reload
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Writes any setting changed in the last second, then reloads the craft settings from disk and the craft data files (devices, merchants, recipe books and reaction arts), printing what the data files loaded.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Reload

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Save
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Writes changed craft settings to disk now instead of waiting for the automatic save, and prints settings saved or settings NOT saved (saved also when nothing had changed and nothing was written). It refuses to write over a settings file that could not be read.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Save

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Scan
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Re-reads your recipe book from the start, opening the book so the client lists every recipe, and restarts a scan already in progress. Out of the world it does nothing and prints nothing.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Scan

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:ScribeRecipe[name|all=all]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Scribes recipe scrolls from your bags one at a time, then opens and closes the tradeskill book so the new recipes are listed. A name scribes only scrolls whose full item name matches it in any case (a name with a comma arrives whole), nothing matching prints a line, and a call while scribing adds the new scrolls to the run (the same as OgreBotAPI.Craft:ScribeRecipe).
  arg name|all (string, default: all): The scroll's full item name in any case, or all for every scribeable scroll in your bags. Left empty it scribes all.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:ScribeRecipe[all]

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Set[key,value]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Changes one craft setting by its key and prints the new value; it is saved by itself about a second later. Both arguments are required, and a key that is not a craft setting (any case is accepted) prints a warning and saves nothing.
  arg key (string): The setting's key, the panel control's id such as checkbox_craft_scriberecipes.
  arg value (string): The new value, stored as given (TRUE or FALSE for a checkbox).
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Set[checkbox_craft_scriberecipes,TRUE]

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Start
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Starts crafting the setup queue, the same as `ogre craft start` and OgreBotAPI.Craft:Start (without the for-who). It is refused with a console line and LastError when you are not in the world, a run is already going, or the setup queue is empty, and a refused start changes nothing.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Start

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:StartLLL
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Starts low level leveling, a loop that crafts low-level recipes round after round and stops when your tradeskill level is 9, or 19 or higher - the same as `ogre craft lll` and OgreBotAPI.Craft:StartLLL. It is refused when you are not in the world or a run is already going.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:StartLLL

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:StartQuest[]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Crafts the recipe steps of the quest selected in your journal, one of each per pass, until no craftable step is left; it keeps to that quest even if you select another one mid-run. It is refused when no quest is selected, a crafting flow is already running, or you are not in the world, and is the same as OgreBotAPI.Craft:StartQuest.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:StartQuest

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:StartTinker
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Starts auto tinkering, a loop that crafts tinkering recipes round after round and ends when you have no tinkering skill or it is at its maximum - the same as `ogre craft tinker` and OgreBotAPI.Craft:StartTinker. It is refused when you are not in the world or a run is already going.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:StartTinker

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:StartWrits
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Starts a writs (rush order) run for as many writs as the writ count setting (default 10), the same as `ogre craft writs` and OgreBotAPI.Craft:StartWrits. It is refused below tradeskill level 20, when you are not in the world, or when a run is already going.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:StartWrits

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Status[]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Prints the crafting state to the console: craft lite on or off, the flow, the status text, crafted of total, the number of recipes read from your book, and the last error when there is one. It changes nothing.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Status

ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Stop
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Craft
  what: Stops the running crafting run and drops a pause, printing "craft: stopping (Craft:Stop)." to the console, while the panel stays open (End closes it). With no run going it drops a pause and prints that nothing is running, the same as `ogre craft stop`.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:Stop


== ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm ==

ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm:Close
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm
  what: The same as :End: closing this window never leaves a run going. It takes no arguments.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm:Close

ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm:End
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm
  what: Stops a run and closes the window, the same as `ogre end craftgm` and the window's X. It takes no arguments.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm:End

ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm:Open[words]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm
  what: Opens the Craft Grandmasters window and does nothing else, the same as bare `ogre craftgm`. A word it cannot read prints why and the usage, and nothing changes.
  arg words (string): A level range such as 131-135 or all, to seed the boxes, and depot or nodepot for the Scroll Depot box, one argument each. Optional.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm:Open

ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm:Queue[words]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm
  what: Opens the window, seeds it the same way, scans, then replaces the Ogre Craft queue with the Grandmaster recipes and stops - nothing is crafted, the Scroll Depot is never used, and the Craft window opens on the queue.
  arg words (string): A level range, one argument. Optional. depot is refused: Queue never pulls from the Scroll Depot.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm:Queue[131-135]

ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm:Scan[words]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm
  what: Opens the window, seeds it the same way, and scans. It queues nothing and crafts nothing.
  arg words (string): A level range and depot or nodepot, one argument each. Optional.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm:Scan[131-135,depot]

ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm:Start[words]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm
  what: Opens the window, seeds it the same way, then scans, queues and crafts.
  arg words (string): A level range and depot or nodepot, one argument each. Optional.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm:Start[all,nodepot]

ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm:Status
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm
  what: Prints the state, filter, queue and Scroll Depot counters to the console. It takes no arguments.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm:Status

ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm:Stop
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm
  what: Stops a run and leaves the window as it is, so you can see what happened. It takes no arguments.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.CraftGm:Stop


== ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats ==

${ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats.Keys}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats
  what: The keys of the loaded lists, comma separated - each key is also the flag that picks that list in Get and Plan (the shipped ones are cd, ka, mm, pop and vov). Re-reads the list files first if any changed on disk.
  returns: string: the loaded list keys joined with ", "; "" when none loaded
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats.Keys}

${ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats.Lists}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats
  what: How many crafting-mats lists are loaded: the shipped ones plus your own from OgreSave/EQ2/CraftingMats/custom. Reading it first re-reads the list files if any changed on disk; any load warnings are in Warnings, and Get, Plan and Reload print them.
  returns: int: number of loaded lists; 0 when no list files were found
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats.Lists}

${ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats.Warnings}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats
  what: The warnings the last load of the list files produced, such as an unreadable file; Get, Plan and Reload also print them each time they run. Re-reads the list files first if any changed on disk.
  returns: string: the warnings joined with " | "; "" when the load was clean
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats.Warnings}

ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:End
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats
  what: Stops a depot withdraw that a crafting-mats run started (only that one) and closes the editor window; unsaved edits are kept for the next Open. This is what `ogre end craftingmats` and the window's X do.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:End

ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:Get[flags...]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats
  what: Works out the mats for the chosen lists and categories, prints any list-file warnings and the plan, then starts pulling them from the Harvesting Supply Depot and buying any fuel at the Guild Fuel Merchant on the pulse after the call returns (the same as `ogre craftingmats -<flags>`). No flags pulls the Visions of Vetrovia signature line; nothing is pulled when not in world, when another depot errand is running, or when only unknown words were given, and the run stops if no depot is within 11 of you.
  arg flags... (string): Any mix, dash optional, any case: a list key (-vov, -cd, -mm, -pop, -ka or your own list's key), -sig / -s, -daily / -d, -weekly / -w, -plan to print only, help. A list with no category uses its own signature line (daily + weekly for Kunark's Ascending), a category with no list uses Visions of Vetrovia, and unknown words are ignored with one warning.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:Get[-vov,-daily,-weekly]

ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:Help
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats
  what: Prints the `ogre craftingmats` usage to the console: the list and category flags, the defaults, the script calls and where to put your own lists so updates never overwrite them.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:Help

ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:Open
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats
  what: Opens the Crafting Mats list editor window, where you change a list and save it to your own custom file (the same as bare `ogre craftingmats`). Calling it while the window is open changes nothing, and without the Ogre UI desktop it prints a warning instead.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:Open

ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:Plan[flags...]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats
  what: Prints any list-file warnings and the shopping list Get would use - the mats to pull from the depot and the fuel to buy - and touches neither the depot nor the merchant. Takes the same flags as Get; no flags plans the Visions of Vetrovia signature line.
  arg flags... (string): Any mix, dash optional, any case: a list key (-vov, -cd, -mm, -pop, -ka or your own list's key), -sig / -s, -daily / -d, -weekly / -w, -plan to print only, help. A list with no category uses its own signature line (daily + weekly for Kunark's Ascending), a category with no list uses Visions of Vetrovia, and unknown words are ignored with one warning.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:Plan[-ka]

ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:Reload
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats
  what: Re-reads every list file from disk now, prints any warnings the load produced, then "craftingmats: reloaded -" with the list count and keys. Rarely needed: the lists are re-read by themselves whenever a list file changes.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.CraftingMats:Reload


== ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer ==

${ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer.Running}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer
  what: TRUE while a house-to-guild-hall, guild-hall-to-house or small-to-large depot transfer is running. Only one transfer runs at a time; starting another is refused with a busy warning.
  returns: bool: TRUE while a depot transfer is running; FALSE when idle.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer.Running}

${ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer.Status}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer
  what: The running transfer's current depot type, its place in the list and how many withdrawals have been made, or "idle". It is the same text `${ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer}` returns.
  returns: string: "idle", or "<type> (n/total, k pulled)" where type is harvest, ammo, adorn, food, lore, potion, collectible, fuel or scroll.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer.Status}

ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer:GHToHouse[flags...]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer
  what: The engine behind `ogre ghtohouse`: must start in your guild hall, then withdraws each chosen guild hall depot and deposits it into the matching personal house depot, travelling back and forth until that depot is empty (at most 40 trips per type). If a house depot says it cannot hold any more, the rest goes back into the guild hall depot and that type is skipped; each house depot must be within 8 m of where you arrive in the house.
  arg flags... (string): -all (the eight shared depot types, not scroll), or any of -harvest/-h, -ammo, -adorn, -food, -lore, -potion, -collect/-collectible/-c, -fuel, each with a -no twin (-noharvest/-nh, -nocollect/-nocollectible/-nc, -nofuel ...); read left to right so `-all -nofuel` is all but fuel; a bare word is the house owner to enter (default your own name); an unknown flag is warned about and ignored; at least one depot type must end up selected or the call is refused; -scroll adds the scroll depot, which -all does not include
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer:GHToHouse[-harvest,-scroll]

ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer:HouseToGH[flags...]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer
  what: The engine behind `ogre housetogh`: empties the chosen personal house depots into the matching guild hall depots, travelling between the guild hall and the house as often as needed (at most 40 trips per depot type), and pulling Superior Rune items one at a time. Started in the guild hall it first deposits what you carry there; each guild hall depot must be within 11 m of where you arrive, and a missing door or depot stops the run with a console warning.
  arg flags... (string): -all (the eight shared depot types, not scroll), or any of -harvest/-h, -ammo, -adorn, -food, -lore, -potion, -collect/-collectible/-c, -fuel, each with a -no twin (-noharvest/-nh, -nocollect/-nocollectible/-nc, -nofuel ...); read left to right so `-all -nofuel` is all but fuel; a bare word is the house owner to enter (default your own name); an unknown flag is warned about and ignored; at least one depot type must end up selected or the call is refused; -scroll is warned about as unknown here (there is no house scroll depot)
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer:HouseToGH[-all,-nofuel]

ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer:SmallToLarge[flags...]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer
  what: The engine behind `ogre smalldepottobigdepot`: in your guild hall, withdraws one depot type from "<type> Depot" and deposits it into "<type> Depot (Large)" (within 11 m), repeating until the small depot is empty. It is refused outside a guild hall or for an unknown type; with the do-not-deposit option it fills your bags once and stops.
  arg flags... (string, default: -harvest): one depot type: -harvest, -adorn/-adornment, -ammo, -scroll/-spell, -collectible/-collectable, -food/-drink, -fuel, -lore/-legend or -potion/-poison/-totem (the last one given wins); TRUE, 1 or -donotdeposit only fills your bags, FALSE or 0 turns that off again; any other word refuses the call
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer:SmallToLarge[-adorn]

ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer:Stop
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer
  what: Stops the running depot transfer and prints "depot transfer: stopped."; does nothing when idle. You stay where the transfer had got to, and items already withdrawn stay in your bags.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.DepotTransfer:Stop


== ISXOgreEQ2.Det ==

${ISXOgreEQ2.Det.DetrimentalInfo[mainIconID,backdropIconID,-actorID,-maxEffects,field]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Det
  what: One field of a detrimental effect matched by its icon pair: on you (no -actorID, or your own ID) it reads the bot's detrimental tracker, which refreshes about every 500 ms, and for any other actor it walks that actor's effect list live, the first 10 effects unless -maxEffects says otherwise. Numeric fields (exists, id, mainiconid, backdropiconid, currentincrements, duration, maxduration, iseffectinfoavailable) come back as a number - 0 when not found, duration in whole seconds, and always 0 for duration on another actor - while any other field name (Name, Description, Type...) reads the game's effect info, a server request, and the read is NULL out of the world or with fewer than two arguments.
  arg mainIconID (int): the effect's MainIconID
  arg backdropIconID (int): the effect's BackDropIconID
  arg -actorID (switch, default: 0 (you)): -actorID <id>: read this actor's effects instead of yours
  arg -maxEffects (switch, default: 10): -maxEffects <n>: how many of another actor's effects to walk; 0 walks them all; not used for you
  arg field (string, default: exists): the field to return; the last word that is not a switch wins. A read changes nothing: ISXOgreEQ2.Det:DetrimentalCancel is the way to cancel
  returns: int64 or string: exists is 1 or 0; id, icon ids, currentincrements, duration and maxduration are numbers (0 when not found); any other field is a string (empty when not found).
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Det.DetrimentalInfo[176,313,-actorID,${Target.ID},currentincrements]}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Det.DetrimentalInfo_JSON[mainIconID,backdropIconID,-actorID,-maxEffects,-ExtraFields]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Det
  what: A detrimental effect as JSON (ID, BackDropIconID, MainIconID, CurrentIncrements, Duration, MaxDuration): with no icon pair (or 0,0) a JSON array of every detrimental on you (or of another actor's first effects with -actorID), and with an icon pair that one effect as an object, {} when not found. The switches are read in any position and the first two other arguments are the icon pair; Duration and MaxDuration are always 0 for another actor, and the read is NULL out of the world.
  arg mainIconID (int, default: 0): the effect's MainIconID; 0 with backdropIconID 0 lists every effect
  arg backdropIconID (int, default: 0): the effect's BackDropIconID; with fewer than two icon arguments there is no pair (0,0)
  arg -actorID (switch, default: 0 (you)): -actorID <id>: read this actor's effects instead of yours
  arg -maxEffects (switch, default: 10): -maxEffects <n>: how many of another actor's effects to walk; 0 walks them all; not used for you
  arg -ExtraFields (switch, default: off): -ExtraFields: add Name, Description, Type, UsesRemaining, NumEffectStrings and EffectStrings to a matched effect (a server request); not applied to the whole list
  returns: string: a JSON array (every effect) or a JSON object (one matched effect, {} when not found).
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Det.DetrimentalInfo_JSON}

ISXOgreEQ2.Det:DetrimentalCacheClear
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Det
  what: Empties the bot's detrimental tracker, so its next scan sees every detrimental still on you as new. That fires OgreEvent_OnDetrimentalAdded again for each of them and echoes a +det line for each.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Det:DetrimentalCacheClear

ISXOgreEQ2.Det:DetrimentalCancel[mainIconID,backdropIconID]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Det
  what: Cancels the detrimental effect on you with this icon pair, immediately, and echoes a cancel line to the console when it finds it. It says nothing when no such effect is on you; OgreBotAPI.Cures:CancelDetrimental is the same cancel with a for-who and a not-found message.
  arg mainIconID (int): the effect's MainIconID
  arg backdropIconID (int): the effect's BackDropIconID
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Det:DetrimentalCancel[176,313]

ISXOgreEQ2.Det:Dump[mode,-noinfo]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Det
  what: The `ogre dets` console dump: lists every detrimental on you from the tracker (dets, the default), your maintained spells and their targets (m), or your target's effects (target), one line each. By default it also reads each detrimental's Name and Description, a server request per effect, which -noinfo skips; out of the world it only prints a warning.
  arg mode (string, default: dets): dets (or det, d), m (or maintained), target (or t); -h, -help or ? as the first word prints usage
  arg -noinfo (switch, default: off): skip the Name and Description reads; -info turns them back on
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Det:Dump[dets,-noinfo]

ISXOgreEQ2.Det:Set_DetrimentalScanTime[ms]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Det
  what: Sets how often, in milliseconds, the bot's detrimental tracker rescans your detrimentals (500 by default); every reader of the tracker sees the change. A value outside 100 to 5000 is refused with a console warning and the interval stays as it was, and the setting is not saved.
  arg ms (int): the scan interval in milliseconds, 100 to 5000
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Det:Set_DetrimentalScanTime[250]

== ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter ==

${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.ActiveCount}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter
  what: The number of encounters that are setting up or running right now.
  returns: int: encounters in setup or active; 0 when none.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.ActiveCount}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.Current}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter
  what: The encounters setting up or running right now, as a JSON array. Each entry has primary (the first named mob), state ("setup" or "active"), named (every named mob), expansion and zone.
  returns: string: a JSON array of the active encounters; "[]" when none.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.Current}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.IsActive[mob]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter
  what: Whether any loaded encounter naming that mob is setting up or running. The mob name is matched ignoring case, whatever zone you are in.
  arg mob (string): The named mob's name.
  returns: bool: TRUE when that mob's encounter is in setup or active; FALSE when it is not, when no encounter owns that name, or when no name is given.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.IsActive[${Target.Name}]}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.Loaded}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter
  what: The number of encounter files loaded, across every zone. It changes when a reload or a zone-in picks up new or edited files.
  returns: int: the number of loaded encounters.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.Loaded}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.Sequences}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter
  what: Every live encounter sequence as a JSON array, so you can see which step a fight is waiting on. Each entry names its encounter and holds either its condition rules or the list it is running (setup, a trigger and so on) with the current step.
  returns: string: a JSON array of live sequences; "[]" when none.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.Sequences}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.Validation}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter
  what: The answer of the last Encounter:Validate, as JSON: ok (true when the file would load), errors and warnings (how many), fileErrors and ruleErrors (the errors split: a file error stops the file from loading, a rule error does not), and issues - one for each line it printed, with the list, the rule and the step it belongs to (counted from 1), the message, and whether it is only a warning. Empty until Encounter:Validate has run.
  returns: string: JSON, for example {"ok":true,"errors":0,"warnings":0,"fileErrors":0,"ruleErrors":0,"issues":[]}; "" before the first Encounter:Validate.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter.Validation}
  more: https://kannkor.github.io/ISXOgre/EQ2/bot/developer/zone-files/builder

ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Debug[switch,value]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter
  what: Turns the console echo of encounter messages (comms) or step changes (steps) on or off, then prints both settings; with no switch it only prints them - the same as `ogre encounter debug`. Both are always written to the log; an unknown switch or a missing on/off prints a warning and changes nothing.
  arg switch (string, default: ""): comms or steps; blank just prints the current settings.
  arg value (string, default: ""): on or off; needed when switch is given.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Debug[steps,on]

ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Fire[mob]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter
  what: Sets up for an encounter on the next pulse: the fight of the named mob given, or with no name the nearest or engaged named in this zone; a setup already running is started again. It is OgreBotAPI.Bot:SetUpFor without the for-who, and it is ignored with a warning when Enable Raid Setups (raid zones) or Enable Heroic Setups (other zones) is off, or when no encounter owns that name.
  arg mob (string, default: ""): The named mob whose encounter to set up; blank picks the nearest or engaged named in this zone.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Fire[${Target.Name}]

ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Help
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter
  what: Prints the `ogre encounter` words (reload, debug and sequences) with one line each to the console, the same as typing a bare `ogre encounter`.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Help

ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:List
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter
  what: Prints this zone's encounter coding to the console: one line per fight with its named mobs, (DISABLED) when switched off, and its file. It always answers, even "No encounter coding for this zone", and is OgreBotAPI.Encounter:List without the for-who.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:List

ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Reload
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter
  what: Re-reads every encounter file from disk in the background and swaps the new set in when it is done, which ends every encounter setup and sequence in progress - the same as `ogre encounter reload`. It prints one line at once and a second with the loaded, scanned and error counts when the swap lands.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Reload

ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Sequences
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter
  what: Prints the Sequences JSON to the console, or "(none live)" when nothing is running - the same as `ogre encounter sequences`.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Sequences

ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Validate[root,path]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter
  what: Checks one fight file by the same rules the game uses when it loads fight files, and changes nothing: a file on disk by its root and path (the same as `ogre encounter validate`), or the base64 text of a fight file's JSON. It prints whether the file would load and each problem, and keeps the answer for Encounter.Validation.
  arg root (string): The root the fight file is in: default or custom. With no path, this one argument is read as the base64 text of a fight file's JSON, checked as a new file of your own.
  arg path (string, default: none): The fight file's path inside that root, ending in .json. A path with spaces may be quoted or written as several words.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Encounter:Validate[custom,"My Zone/My Mob.json"]
  more: https://kannkor.github.io/ISXOgre/EQ2/bot/developer/zone-files/builder


== ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder ==

ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:BuildPages[zone,rebuild]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder
  what: Builds the readable pages from every recording on this PC, the window's Build pages button; it needs Node.js. It returns at once, and the window and the console say how the build ended.
  arg zone (string, default: none): The word zone: only this zone's recordings. Leave it out for all of them.
  arg rebuild (string, default: none): The word rebuild: every pull is read and every page made again. Leave it out to make only what changed.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:BuildPages

ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:End
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder
  what: Stops everything - recording, an open fight's file and a page build this session started - and closes the window, the same as `ogre end er` and the window's X.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:End

ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:EveryDet[state]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder
  what: Whether every det is examined, not one for each pair of icons - for dets that share their icons. Saved for every box of this PC.
  arg state (string, default: none): on or off. Leave it out to be told what it is now.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:EveryDet["on"]

ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:Help
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder
  what: Prints the words of `ogre er` to the console.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:Help

ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:Mark[text]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder
  what: Writes a note on the fight's timeline, the same as `ogre er mark <text>`. Recording must be on.
  arg text (string, default: none): The note. Several arguments are joined with spaces.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:Mark["boss at 50%"]

ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:NpcEffects[state]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder
  what: Whether this session reads the names of effects on NPCs, saved for this session on this PC. The session is1 reads them unless switched off; no other session does unless switched on.
  arg state (string, default: none): on or off. Leave it out to be told what it is now.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:NpcEffects["on"]

ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:Off
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder
  what: Stops recording, the same as `ogre er off`: an open fight's file is ended. The window stays open.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:Off

ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:OffForWho
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder
  what: Sends `off` to every box the MCP For Who window names, the same way as :OnForWho.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:OffForWho

ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:On
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder
  what: Records every fight by itself from the pull on and opens the window, the same as `ogre er on`. It is never on by itself: each box is switched on after every login, and out of the world nothing happens.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:On

ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:OnForWho
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder
  what: Sends `on` to every box the MCP For Who window names, over oc or IRC as that window says. This box switches on only when the For Who names it too.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:OnForWho

ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:Open
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder
  what: Opens the Encounter Recorder window, the same as bare `ogre er`.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:Open

ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:Pets[state]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder
  what: Whether rows are written for pets, saved for every box of this PC. Off unless switched on.
  arg state (string, default: none): on or off. Leave it out to be told what it is now.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:Pets["on"]

ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:RecordTrash[state]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder
  what: "Record trash pulls": whether a fight with no named is written too, saved for every box of this PC. Off unless switched on, and it takes hold with the next fight.
  arg state (string, default: none): on or off. Leave it out to be told what it is now.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:RecordTrash["on"]

ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:Start
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder
  what: Begins a fight's file by hand, for an event that never puts you in combat; it ends on :Stop. Recording must be on.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:Start

ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:Status
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder
  what: Prints what it is doing, what it has written and its switches to the console, the same as `ogre er status`.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:Status

ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:Stop
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder
  what: Ends the open fight's file that :Start began, the same as `ogre er stop`.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:Stop

ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:UploadFights[state]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder
  what: The switch "Upload each finished fight", saved for every box of this PC: each box sends its own file to the raid's Encounters page a few seconds after the fight ends. On unless switched off; now sends this toon's files the raid does not have yet.
  arg state (string, default: none): on, off, or now. Leave it out to be told what it is now.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:UploadFights["now"]

ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:UploadRaid[slug]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder
  what: The raid whose Encounters page gets the recordings, saved for every box of this PC. With no raid named nothing is sent.
  arg slug (string, default: none): The last part of the raid page's address (lower-case letters, digits and -), or none for no raid. Leave it out to be told the raid.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:UploadRaid["my-raid"]

ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:UploadRaids
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder
  what: Asks the site for the raids this PC may send to, the window's Refresh. The answer comes a moment later, in the console and as a list under the window's raid field.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.EncounterRecorder:UploadRaids


== ISXOgreEQ2.Events ==

${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Count}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Events
  what: How many native game events the extension listens to, currently 14, numbered from 0 for the event argument of Received, Dispatched, Subscribers, EventName and NativeName.
  returns: int: the number of events (14 today)
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Count}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Dispatched[<event>]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Events
  what: How many arrivals of this game event have been handed out to the extension's features since it loaded, or the total for all events when the argument is left out. It trails Received only by what is still Pending, and an unknown event gives NULL.
  arg <event> (string): The event's 0-based number or its name, such as ActorSpawned; leave it out for the total across all events
  returns: int64: arrivals handed out for that event since load (or for all events); NULL for an unknown event
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Dispatched[ActorSpawned]}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Dropped}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Events
  what: Total game events thrown away since the extension loaded, because more than 4096 were waiting at once (oldest dropped first) or the event was not recognised. It never resets.
  returns: int64: events dropped since load
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Dropped}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.EventName[<event>]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Events
  what: The extension's name for a game event, such as IncomingChatText, looked up by its 0-based number or its name. A missing or unknown event gives NULL.
  arg <event> (string): The event's 0-based number (0 to Count minus 1) or its name
  returns: string: the event's name; NULL for a missing or unknown event
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.EventName[0]}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.NativeName[<event>]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Events
  what: The ISXEQ2 event a game event is read from, such as EQ2_onIncomingChatText, which is also the name a script attaches its own atom to. A missing or unknown event gives NULL.
  arg <event> (string): The event's 0-based number (0 to Count minus 1) or its name, such as IncomingChatText
  returns: string: the ISXEQ2 event name; NULL for a missing or unknown event
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.NativeName[IncomingChatText]}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Pending}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Events
  what: How many received game events are waiting to be handed to the extension's features; they are handed out every pulse, so this is normally 0. At most 4096 can wait, and beyond that the oldest are dropped and counted in Dropped.
  returns: int: events waiting to be handed out right now
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Pending}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Received[<event>]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Events
  what: How many times this game event has arrived since the extension loaded, or the total for all events when the argument is left out. The event is its 0-based number or its name in any case (IncomingChatText, ActorSpawned and so on), and an unknown event gives NULL.
  arg <event> (string): The event's 0-based number or its name, such as IncomingChatText; leave it out for the total across all events
  returns: int64: arrivals of that event since load (or of all events); NULL for an unknown event
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Received[IncomingChatText]}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Stats}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Events
  what: One summary line, such as attached=yes events=14 pending=0 dropped=0 recv=5120 disp=5120, with recv and disp totalled across all events. Echoing ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events} prints the same line after the word Events.
  returns: string: the summary line
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Stats}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.StatsJSON}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Events
  what: The full event table as one JSON object: attached, count, pending, dropped, and an events array giving each event's i, label, native, received, dispatched and subscribers.
  returns: string: a JSON object
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.StatsJSON}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Subscribers[<event>]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Events
  what: How many of the extension's own features are listening to this game event (such as the chat and spawn handling behind OgreBotAPI.Events), or the total when the argument is left out. Atoms a script attaches to the ISXEQ2 event itself are not counted, and an unknown event gives NULL.
  arg <event> (string): The event's 0-based number or its name, such as FinishedZoning; leave it out for the total across all events
  returns: int: listeners on that event (or on all events); NULL for an unknown event
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Events.Subscribers[FinishedZoning]}


== ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment ==

ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment:Boost[flag,count,...]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment
  what: Starts boosting the item already selected on the tradeskill window's Experiment tab, picking each queued stat and clicking Begin and the confirm dialog for every boost; it also turns on the crafting reaction handling. It refuses with a console line when you are not in the world, lack the Experiment AA, a run is already going or no stat is queued, and words it does not know are echoed and skipped.
  arg flag (string): the stat to boost: -p, -pot or -potency for potency, -cb or -critbonus for crit bonus, or -<stat> for any other stat label the game offers
  arg count (int): how many boosts of that stat to queue
  arg ... (string): more flag, count pairs, run in the order given
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment:Boost[-p,3,-cb,2]

ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment:Items
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment
  what: Lists the numbered item rows on the Experiment tab's item page to the console, briefly enlarging the tradeskill window to read them and then putting it back. It prints a warning instead when you are not in the world, lack the Experiment AA, a run is in progress or no list is showing.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment:Items

ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment:Run[row,flag,count,...]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment
  what: Boosts the item on row `row` of the Experiment item list (the numbers Items prints) with the same flags as Boost. A missing row, a row number out of range or no queued stat is refused with a console line and nothing starts.
  arg row (int): the item row number from Experiment:Items, starting at 1
  arg flag (string): the stat to boost: -p, -pot or -potency, -cb or -critbonus, or -<stat> for any other stat label
  arg count (int): how many boosts of that stat to queue
  arg ... (string): more flag, count pairs, run in the order given
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment:Run[2,-p,5]

ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment:Status
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment
  what: Prints the tradeskill experiment helper's state to the console: running or not, its last status, whether you have the Experiment AA, items done and skipped, boosts made, the last error and the usage lines. It is what a bare `ogre experiment` runs.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment:Status

ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment:Stop
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment
  what: Stops a running experiment and gives the tradeskill window back its size (the same as `ogre end experiment`). When nothing is running it only prints "experiment: not running" to the console.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Experiment:Stop


== ISXOgreEQ2.Export ==

${ISXOgreEQ2.Export.Busy}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Export
  what: TRUE from the moment an ability export starts until its file is written or the export is stopped. ISXOgreEQ2.Export:Abilities returns at once and runs in the background, so poll this to know when it is done.
  returns: bool: TRUE while an ability export is running; FALSE when none is.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Export.Busy}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Export.Processed}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Export
  what: How many abilities the running export has processed so far - the count its progress window shows. Reads 0 when no export is running.
  returns: int: abilities processed so far by the running export; 0 when idle.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Export.Processed}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Export.Total}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Export
  what: How many abilities the running export will process in all. Reads 0 when no export is running.
  returns: int: abilities the running export will process; 0 when idle.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Export.Total}

ISXOgreEQ2.Export:Abilities[flag...]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Export
  what: Starts the ability export in the background and returns at once: it reads each ability's game info one ability at a time (a server request per ability) and writes OgreSave/EQ2/OgreBot/AbilityExports/V3_<Name>_<SubClass>_<Server>_AbilityExport.json, the file OgreBotAPI.Abilities loads. With no flags it is the standard export (no passives, no tradeskill, merged into the existing file); a call while one is running is ignored with a console line, and when it finishes OgreBot reloads its abilities unless -noreloadbot or -nosave was given.
  arg flag... (string): optional flags in any order: -passive (include passives), -tradeskill (tradeskill export to the crafting XML files), -nodesc, -minlevel <n>, -maxlevel <n>, -j / -a / -e / -m / -gm / -ancient (lowest tier to keep), -new (fresh file, no merge), -na (only abilities not already in the file), -nosave (dry run, nothing written), -noreloadbot; a word that starts with - and is none of these is refused with one line and nothing starts; any other word is an ability ID or name to export only those (a name is looked up by name, a server request)
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Export:Abilities[-passive]

ISXOgreEQ2.Export:Config[word...]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Export
  what: The `ogre export` command: with no words it opens the Ability Export options panel, or brings it back if a run hid it. -start runs the export now with the panel's current options and no panel (a server request per ability, as Abilities does; refused while one is running), -default uses the default options for this call only without saving them, stop stops a running export, and any other word is named on the console and nothing happens.
  arg word... (string): optional words, any order, case-insensitive, leading dash optional: -default, -start, stop
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Export:Config[stop]

ISXOgreEQ2.Export:End
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Export
  what: Stops a running ability export (nothing is written, and abilities are not reloaded) and closes the export options window - the same as `ogre end export` or either window's X. When nothing is running and nothing is open it does nothing and says nothing.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Export:End

ISXOgreEQ2.ForWhoGroups:List
