== ISXOgreEQ2.MCP ==

${ISXOgreEQ2.MCP.ForWho}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.MCP
  what: The for-who text MCP buttons and bound keys use on this session, from the For Who picker or MCP:SetForWho. A button with its own for-who still uses its own.
  returns: string: the for-who text in force on this session; all when nothing has been picked (everyone).
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.MCP.ForWho}

${ISXOgreEQ2.MCP.IrcConnected}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.MCP
  what: Whether this session last heard that the IRC link is up. It starts FALSE on a new session and stays FALSE until the IRC hub reports in; while FALSE, MCP buttons that send over IRC go through OgreConsole instead.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the IRC hub last reported the link connected; FALSE when it reported it down or has not reported yet.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.MCP.IrcConnected}

ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:AddBind[key,buttonId,name,event]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MCP
  what: Links a keyboard key or mouse button (an InnerSpace key name such as G600-G9) to an MCP button, so pressing it runs MCP:Fire on that button. The bind is saved to Scripts/OgreSave/EQ2/OgreMCPBinds.json, armed at once, and every EQ2 session on this PC picks it up; a bind with the same name is replaced, and a button id that has no command yet only prints a note.
  arg key (string): The InnerSpace key name to bind, such as G600-G9 or F13.
  arg buttonId (string): The MCP button to run, as MCP:Buttons lists it.
  arg name (string, default: MCP_<key>_<buttonId> with every other character turned into _): A name for the bind, used by MCP:RemoveBind.
  arg event (string, default: press): release fires when the key is let go; anything else fires on press.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:AddBind[G600-G9,static:0_0,G9Heal,press]

ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Buttons
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MCP
  what: Prints every configured MCP button to the console with its id, label, page and command, so you can find the id to give MCP:Fire or MCP:AddBind. With no saved layout it prints a line saying there are no buttons yet.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Buttons

ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Close
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MCP
  what: Closes the Master Control Panel together with its For Who, Build command and Assign keys windows. It also cancels a key test that is still waiting for a press.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Close

ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Fire[buttonId]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MCP
  what: Runs an MCP button by its id, exactly as clicking it would: the button's command is read from the saved layout at that moment and sent with the button's own for-who, or this session's For Who when the button has none. A missing id, no saved layout, or a button with no command prints one console line and sends nothing.
  arg buttonId (string): The button's id as MCP:Buttons lists it: btn:<id> (follows the button when it moves), static:<row>_<col> or page:<page>:<row>_<col>.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Fire[static:0_0]

ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:FixHoistOrder
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MCP
  what: Repairs buttons that an older MCP:Migrate wrote with some arguments in the wrong order, touching only the affected buttons and writing OgreMCP.json.bak first. It runs once per file (a second call prints that it is already done), prints how many buttons were fixed or need checking by hand, and has every EQ2 session on this PC reload when anything changed.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:FixHoistOrder

ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:ListBinds
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MCP
  what: Prints every saved key bind to the console: its name, key, press or release, the button it runs, and whether it is disabled.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:ListBinds

ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Migrate[overwrite]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MCP
  what: Converts the old OgreBot MCP buttons (Scripts/EQ2OgreBot/MCP/MCPCustomSettings.xml) into the new panel's Scripts/OgreSave/EQ2/OgreMCP.json and prints a summary; button types with no command equivalent come across as label only. It refuses to replace an existing OgreMCP.json unless you pass overwrite, and on success every EQ2 session on this PC reloads the panel.
  arg overwrite (string, default: off - an existing file is kept): The word overwrite (or 1, TRUE, yes, on) replaces an existing OgreMCP.json, discarding its current layout.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Migrate

ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Open
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MCP
  what: Opens the Master Control Panel (MCP), the window of buttons that send commands to your characters, with its saved layout; the same as `ogre mcp`, and alt+backtick toggles it. Calling it while the panel is already open does nothing; if the in-game UI host is not running or a panel file cannot be read, nothing opens and one console line says which, and a missing command catalog opens the builder empty with a line.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Open

ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Reload
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MCP
  what: Re-reads Scripts/OgreSave/EQ2/OgreMCP.json and updates an open panel to match, which is how a change saved on one session shows up on the others. It is skipped when the file is exactly what this session just saved, or when the file is not valid JSON.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Reload

ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:ReloadBinds
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MCP
  what: Re-reads Scripts/OgreSave/EQ2/OgreMCPBinds.json, removes this session's live key binds and arms the saved ones again. Adding or removing a bind on any session runs this on every EQ2 session on the PC.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:ReloadBinds

ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:RemoveBind[name]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MCP
  what: Removes a saved key bind by name, disarms it and tells every EQ2 session on this PC to drop it. An unknown name prints a console line and changes nothing.
  arg name (string): The bind's name as MCP:ListBinds shows it.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:RemoveBind[G9Heal]

ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Send[message,-tab,tab,-rg,group,-cfw,who]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MCP
  what: With arguments it sends message exactly as ISXOgreX.Console:Send does (a leading !c or !ci makes it a command, anything else is a chat line). With no arguments it sends the button just clicked on this session, once, through the same route a click uses, and otherwise the console input box line.
  arg message (string, default: the button just clicked, or the input box line): The literal line to send; a leading !c or !ci makes it a command. Leave out every argument for the button just clicked, or the console input box line.
  arg -tab (switch, default: (none)): Also show the line in the console tab named by the next argument; may be given more than once.
  arg tab (string, default: (none)): The console tab name that follows -tab.
  arg -rg (switch, default: (none)): Send to the relay group named by the next argument instead of the bot's own relay group.
  arg group (string, default: the bot's relay group): The relay group name that follows -rg.
  arg -cfw (switch, default: (none)): Give the command a for-who, used by its commands whose own for-who is left as auto.
  arg who (for-who, default: everyone): for-who: this runs only when this character is one it names - the value that follows -cfw.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Send["!c -pause","-cfw","igw:${Me.Name}"]

ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:SetForWho[value]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MCP
  what: Sets the For Who that MCP buttons and bound keys use on this session only, held in memory (not saved, not shared, back to everyone after a restart). With a value it sets that as a custom For Who and shows it in the picker (spaces are removed; all or an empty value clears it back to everyone); with no value it takes the choice the For Who picker just made.
  arg value (string, default: (none) - the picker's choice): The for-who text to use, such as igw:<name> or several names joined with |. Leave it out to take the For Who picker's current choice.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:SetForWho[igw:${Me.Name}]

ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Toggle
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MCP
  what: Opens the Master Control Panel when it is closed and closes it when it is open. This is what alt+backtick runs.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Toggle


== ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft ==

ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft:Help
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft
  what: Prints the `ogre mc` usage lines to the console and does nothing else. It is what `ogre mc help` runs.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft:Help

ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft:List
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft
  what: Reads the recipes your TARGETED merchant sells and prints them numbered, for use with Start["#n"]. It is refused with a console warning when a run is already going, you are not in the world, the target is not a merchant within 9 m, or you lack the Summon Crafting Stations ability.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft:List

ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft:Start[words...]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft
  what: The engine behind `ogre mc <recipe> [count]`: for each round it buys the recipe from your targeted merchant (only if you do not know it), scribes it, summons the crafting station it needs, empties the craft engine's setup queue and crafts it 3 times. It has the same refusals as List and also refuses with no recipe or while a craft run is going; on a recipe not yet cached it MAKES A SERVER CALL (`.ToRecipeInfo`, to learn the crafting device), and only when the craft panel's "Allow recipe-info server call" option is on, which it is by default.
  arg words... (string): a partial recipe name (one or more words, first match wins) or "#n" for row n of List's numbering, then an optional trailing whole number = rounds (1 to 999, default 1; each round is 3 crafts)
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft:Start[ferrite,bracelet,4]

ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft:Status
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft
  what: Prints the merchant-craft state (running or idle, the current recipe and round, how many recipes the last scan found) and then the usage lines to the console. It is what bare `ogre mc` and `ogre mc status` run.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft:Status

ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft:Stop
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft
  what: Abandons the merchant-craft run and prints "mc: stopped.", or "mc: nothing is running." when idle. It does not stop a craft queue the run already started, and a summoned station stays.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantCraft:Stop


== ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps ==

${ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps.Running}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps
  what: TRUE while a buyfuel or buycrate run is in progress. Only one runs at a time; starting another is refused with a busy warning.
  returns: bool: TRUE while a fuel or crate purchase run is going; FALSE when idle.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps.Running}

${ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps.Status}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps
  what: One line naming the running merchant run and its progress, or "idle". It is the same text `${ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps}` returns.
  returns: string: "idle", "buyfuel '<fuel>' (round n)" or "buycrate (done/total)".
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps.Status}

ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps:BuyCrate[flags...]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps
  what: The engine behind `ogre buycrate`: targets and opens this zone's crate merchant (who must be nearby), buys one of each chosen heroic and raid crate, accepts the purchase prompt and closes the merchant. Only exp17_dun_fordel_midst and exp18_rgn_svarni_expanse have one (Svarni sells no heroic crate), and anywhere else, or when nothing matches the flags, the call is refused with a warning.
  arg flags... (string, default: -all): -r/-raid for the raid crate, -h/-heroic for the heroic crate, -all for both; read left to right, so `-raid -all` buys both and `-all -raid` only the raid crate; unknown words are ignored
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps:BuyCrate[-h]

ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps:BuyFuel[amount]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps
  what: The engine behind `ogre buyfuel`: at the guild hall Fuel Depot (within 11 m) it counts how much of the fuel you have EXAMINED the depot holds, buys the shortfall from the merchant titled Guild Fuel Merchant and deposits it, repeating for at most 10 rounds. It is refused when nothing is examined, a run is already going or you are not in the world, and stops with a console warning when the depot is missing, too far or does not open.
  arg amount (int, default: 90000): how much of the fuel the depot should end up holding; missing, not a whole number, or 0 or less uses 90000
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps:BuyFuel[20000]

ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps:Stop
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps
  what: Stops a running buyfuel or buycrate and prints "merchant: stopped."; does nothing when idle. Open depot or merchant windows are left as they are.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.MerchantOps:Stop


== ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate ==

ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate:Cancel[task]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate
  what: Backs out of a pending overwrite confirmation for one task, putting its row back to its normal state. It does nothing when that task is not waiting for a confirmation or the name is unknown.
  arg task (string): the task whose confirmation to cancel: accounts, imsettings, imlists, profiles, irc, mcp or isprofile
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate:Cancel[profiles]

ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate:Close
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate
  what: Closes the Migration Assistant window and cancels its pending auto-close. Nothing that has already run is undone.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate:Close

ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate:Open
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate
  what: Opens the Migration Assistant window (the same as `ogre migrate`), listing each migration task with its status and a re-run button. Before it opens it silently runs any task whose old file exists and whose new file does not, and when the window is already up it does nothing.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate:Open

ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate:RequestRerun[task]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate
  what: Puts one task's row in the Migration Assistant into its overwrite confirmation state, the same as clicking its re-run button; it reads and writes no files. It only does so when that task's old source data exists, otherwise nothing changes.
  arg task (string): the task to ask about: accounts, imsettings, imlists, profiles, irc, mcp or isprofile
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate:RequestRerun[accounts]

ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate:Run[task,overwrite]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate
  what: Runs one migration task now, copying old OgreBot data into the new store (your old XML files are kept); the isprofile task instead asks InnerSpace to add its game profile and ignores overwrite. Without overwrite a task whose new file already exists is not rewritten and its row asks you to confirm instead, an unknown task name does nothing, and the result shows in the Migration Assistant window and the log.
  arg task (string): the task to run: accounts, imsettings, imlists, profiles, irc, mcp or isprofile
  arg overwrite (string): the word overwrite (any case) to replace data that already exists; anything else, or leaving it out, keeps existing data
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Migrate:Run[irc]


== ISXOgreEQ2.Nav ==

${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavActive}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Nav
  what: TRUE while a nav trip is in progress - planning its route, waiting for this zone's navmesh, or moving. A paused trip still counts as in progress.
  returns: bool: TRUE while a trip is planning, waiting for its navmesh or moving; FALSE when idle or once the last trip has ended (Arrived, Stopped, Failed).
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavActive}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavDistance}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Nav
  what: Straight-line distance from the character to the trip's destination, refreshed every pulse while it moves, on foot or flying. It is -1 when idle, while a trip is still planning or waiting for its navmesh, and after a trip ends.
  returns: float: distance in game units to the destination; -1 when no trip is moving.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavDistance}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavMeshOn}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Nav
  what: TRUE unless nav has been switched off with Nav:Set[mesh,off] or `ogre nav -off`. While it is off, new trips are refused; the switch is not saved and starts TRUE each time the extension loads.
  returns: bool: TRUE when nav is allowed to move this character; FALSE when it is switched off.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavMeshOn}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavMeshPolys}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Nav
  what: How many walkable polygons the loaded navmesh has. It is 0 when no mesh is loaded in this zone yet.
  returns: int: polygon count of the loaded mesh; 0 when none is loaded.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavMeshPolys}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavMeshTiles}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Nav
  what: How many tiles the loaded navmesh has. It is 0 when no mesh is loaded in this zone yet.
  returns: int: tile count of the loaded mesh; 0 when none is loaded.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavMeshTiles}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavMeshZone}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Nav
  what: Name of the navmesh that is loaded - the zone's short name in lower case, or the base zone's name when this zone is a copy that uses it. It is "" until a mesh is loaded in this zone (see NavOnMap).
  returns: string: the loaded mesh's zone name; "" when none is loaded.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavMeshZone}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavOnMap}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Nav
  what: TRUE when a navmesh is loaded right now, so nav can plan a route without waiting. The mesh loads on the first trip or route request in a zone and is set aside on every zone change, so this reads FALSE after zoning until something asks for a route.
  returns: bool: TRUE when a navmesh is loaded; FALSE when none is loaded yet in this zone.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavOnMap}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavOnMesh}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Nav
  what: TRUE while the current trip is driven over a navmesh route. It is FALSE when idle, while a trip still waits for its navmesh or plans its first route, and once a trip ends.
  returns: bool: TRUE while a trip is driven over a navmesh route; FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavOnMesh}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavReason}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Nav
  what: Plain words about the trip: while it plans or moves, what the plan is doing; once it has ended or while it waits for a navmesh, why. It is empty before the first trip, and reads "already there" when a trip was asked for the spot the character already stands on.
  returns: string: the plan in force, or why the last trip ended; "" before any trip.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavReason}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavState}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Nav
  what: The trip's state as one word; Arrived, Stopped and Failed stay until the next trip starts, and a paused trip still reads Moving. Stopped means somebody ended the trip on purpose, Failed means nav gave up - NavReason says why.
  returns: string: a state word such as Idle, Planning, WaitingForMesh, Moving, Arrived, Stopped or Failed.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavState}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavWaypoint}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Nav
  what: The waypoint on the current route the character is heading for, counted from 1 (the first point after the start) up to NavWaypoints on the last leg. It is 0 when no route is being walked, a finished trip included.
  returns: int: the waypoint being walked to, 1 to NavWaypoints; 0 when no route is being walked.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavWaypoint}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavWaypoints}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Nav
  what: How many waypoints the current route has after its start point, so NavWaypoint reaches it on the last leg. It is 0 when no route is being walked, a finished trip included.
  returns: int: number of waypoints after the start; 0 when no route is being walked.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Nav.NavWaypoints}

ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:End
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Nav
  what: Ends the trip under way and closes the nav window, the same as `ogre end nav`, `ogre nav end` or the window's X. It prints "nav: stopped (...)" only when a trip was under way.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:End

ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Flags[flag...]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Nav
  what: Runs the `ogre nav -<flag> ...` line: -loc x,y,z (or -to) starts a trip and applies -precision, -nodoors/-doors and -reset with it (it ignores -set, -on/-off and -panel/-nopanel on the same line), while a line without -loc takes -set key value, -reset [key], -on/-off, -panel/-nopanel, -stop, -status or -help. With no flag it prints a warning and a bad or unknown flag prints an error naming it; -precision and -nodoors stay in force after the trip.
  arg flag... (string): The flags and their values, one per argument; a -loc point may be one "x,y,z" argument or three.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Flags[-loc,${Me.X},${Me.Y},${Math.Calc[${Me.Z}+30]},-precision,3]

ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Help
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Nav
  what: Prints the `ogre nav` command help to the console, one line at a time. This is bare `ogre nav` or `ogre nav help`.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Help

ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Open
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Nav
  what: Opens the nav panel (trip state with Stop and Pause buttons) now; if the window cannot open it prints "nav panel: <reason>". This is `ogre nav panel`.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Open

ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Set[key,value]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Nav
  what: Changes one nav setting for this session (not saved) and prints "nav: <key> = <value>"; an unknown key, or a value the setting refuses, prints an error and changes nothing. The key is case-insensitive, and `mesh` (alias `on`) never refuses: a yes word switches nav on and any other value switches it off.
  arg key (string): The setting's name, such as arrive, finalarrive, doors or avoid.
  arg value (string): The new value - a number for distances and counts, on or off for switches.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Set[arrive,4]

ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Status
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Nav
  what: Prints what nav is doing to the console - state, reason, paused, waypoint progress, the loaded mesh and every setting changed from its default. This is `ogre nav status`.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Status

ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Stop
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Nav
  what: Ends the trip under way (NavState becomes Stopped) and prints "nav: stopped"; the nav panel stays open. With no trip under way it changes nothing but still prints the line - this is `ogre nav stop`.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:Stop

ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:To[x,y,z]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Nav
  what: Starts a trip that moves the character to the point, replacing any trip already under way; it returns at once and the route is planned over the next frames (watch NavState). A missing value, or one that is not a number, prints an error and starts nothing, and a refusal (not in world, movement held by another system, no navmesh) prints "nav: <reason>".
  arg x (float): X of the destination.
  arg y (float): Y of the destination - Y is up in EQ2.
  arg z (float): Z of the destination.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Nav:To[${Me.X},${Me.Y},${Math.Calc[${Me.Z}+30]}]


== ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast ==

ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Capture
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast
  what: Asks for the cast your target is casting right now to be captured, the window's Capture button.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Capture

ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Clear
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast
  what: Empties your script watch list. Watches from zone data and encounters stay.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Clear

ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:End
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast
  what: Stops the Monitor and closes the window, the same as `ogre end npccast` and the window's X. The watch list is left alone.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:End

ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Import
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast
  what: Copies the shipped OldBot conversions into your own NPC cast data, never overwriting a file you have.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Import

ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Monitor[word]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast
  what: The Monitor: starts it on a set of mobs, stops it, or acts on its rows. No word starts it on your target, and any word it does not know prints its status.
  arg word (string): target, named, all or on start it; off or stop stop it; copy and clear act on its rows; status prints its state. Optional.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Monitor[named]

ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Open
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast
  what: Opens the NPC Cast Monitoring window, the same as bare `ogre npccast`.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Open

ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Radius[n]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast
  what: Sets the scan radius for the script watch list. With no value it prints one warning and changes nothing.
  arg n (int): The radius in meters; required.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Radius[80]

ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Reload
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast
  what: Asks for the zone data to be read from disk again.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Reload

ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Status
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast
  what: Prints the Monitor's state, the scan counters and the watch list to the console, with who holds each watch and whether it is casting.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Status

ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Unwatch[name]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast
  what: Takes a mob off your script watch list. With no name it prints one warning and changes nothing.
  arg name (string): The mob's name; several words are joined into one name; required.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Unwatch["Ancient Guardian"]

ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Watch[name]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast
  what: Adds a mob to your script watch list. With no name it prints one warning and changes nothing.
  arg name (string): The mob's name; several words are joined into one name; required.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Watch["Ancient Guardian"]

ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Zone
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast
  what: Prints what the zone data says for this zone to the console.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.NpcCast:Zone


== ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot ==

${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Character}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: The character whose OgreBot profile is loaded.
  returns: string: the character name; empty when nothing is loaded.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Character}

${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Count}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: How many single control values the loaded profile holds (checkboxes, text boxes, combo boxes). List sections such as the Cast Stack are not counted.
  returns: int: the number of stored control values; 0 when nothing is loaded.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Count}

${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Dirty}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: TRUE when the loaded profile has changes that are not saved to disk yet. Only Save writes them; closing OgreBot, Reload, or loading another profile drops them.
  returns: bool: TRUE when there are unsaved changes; FALSE when there are none or nothing is loaded.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Dirty}

${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.IsReady}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: TRUE when OgreBot is up: its main window or mini toolbar is open AND a profile is loaded - the check the bot's own features use before they act, and what ${OgreBotAPI.Combat.IsReady} reads too.
  returns: bool: TRUE when a window is open and a profile is loaded; FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.IsReady}

${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Loaded}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: TRUE while an OgreBot profile is loaded for this session. Closing OgreBot unloads the profile, so this goes FALSE on close.
  returns: bool: TRUE when a profile is loaded; FALSE when none is.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Loaded}

${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.PanelVisible}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: TRUE when the OgreBot main window or the mini toolbar is open, whether or not a profile is loaded. Use IsReady to ask whether the bot can run.
  returns: bool: TRUE when either window is open; FALSE when both are closed.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.PanelVisible}

${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Profile}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: The name of the loaded OgreBot profile, in the spelling stored in the profile file.
  returns: string: the profile name; empty when nothing is loaded.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Profile}

${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Value[id]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: The stored value of one OgreBot window control, read from the loaded profile in memory (unsaved changes included). The id must match exactly; OgreBotAPI.Options.Value is the case-insensitive version.
  arg id (string): the control id (the same id the profile saves it under), for example checkbox_settings_enablealiases
  returns: string: the control's value as text; empty when the id is not stored, no id is given, or nothing is loaded.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot.Value[checkbox_settings_enablealiases]}

ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Alias[verb,arg1,arg2,arg3,arg4]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: Edits the loaded profile's custom aliases in memory (Save keeps them) and refreshes the Aliases tab and Target list; names get a leading * if they lack one, and add refuses only the same name with the same For. Verbs are display (print what each alias resolves to now), add or edit (name,For,NoRaid), del (name), delat or toggle (index), editat (index,name,For,NoRaid) and move (from,to) with 0-based indexes, it does nothing with no profile loaded, and OgreBotAPI.ForWho:AddAlias and RemoveAlias use this same editor.
  arg verb (string): display, add, edit, del, delat, editat, toggle or move
  arg arg1 (string): the alias name (add, edit, del) or a 0-based row index (delat, editat, toggle, move)
  arg arg2 (string): the For value (add, edit; an empty one on edit clears it), the new name (editat) or the target index (move)
  arg arg3 (string): No-Raid as a yes/no word (add, edit) or the For value (editat)
  arg arg4 (bool): editat only: No-Raid
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Alias[add,Healer,${Group[1].Name},FALSE]

ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Close
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: Closes OgreBot entirely: both windows close, the profile is unloaded (unsaved changes are dropped with a warning in the console), travel routes stop, and follow and camp spots are cleared unless OgreBotAPI.Movement:UseWithoutOgreBot is on. It is the same close as the X on either window, `ogre end bot` and OgreBotAPI.Bot:End.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Close

ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:CreateProfile[name]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: Makes a new profile from the current settings, unsaved changes included, writes it to disk and switches to it. It fails with a console line when the name is already used (case does not matter).
  arg name (string): the new profile's name; a b64: prefix marks a base64 name
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:CreateProfile[Solo]

ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:DeleteProfile[name]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: Deletes a named profile from the character's profile file on disk. It refuses, with a console line, the loaded profile, the default profile, the last remaining profile and a name that does not exist.
  arg name (string): the profile name (case does not matter); a b64: prefix marks a base64 name
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:DeleteProfile[Solo]

ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Dump[path]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: Writes every stored control value of the loaded profile (unsaved changes included) to a JSON file and prints the count and path. List sections such as the Cast Stack are not included, and the file is overwritten each time.
  arg path (string): the file to write
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Dump["${LavishScript.HomeDirectory}/ogrebot_values.json"]

ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:List[section,op,arg1,arg2]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: Edits one list section of the loaded profile (the Cast Stack or any other ordered list tab) in memory; Save keeps it, and a Cast Stack edit reaches the running cast stack at once. Ops are add (entry), insert or update (index,entry), del or toggle (index) and move (from,to), with 0-based indexes and each entry as base64-encoded JSON; it does not refresh the open window and does nothing with no profile loaded.
  arg section (string): the profile section name, for example CastStack
  arg op (string): add, insert, update, del, move or toggle
  arg arg1 (string): the base64 JSON entry (add) or a 0-based row index (every other op)
  arg arg2 (string): the base64 JSON entry (insert, update) or the target index (move)
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:List[CastStack,toggle,0]

ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:LoadProfile[name]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: Switches to another named profile of the loaded character and refreshes the cast stack and window; if OgreBot is not open it opens it with that profile. Unsaved changes to the current profile are dropped, with one warning line unless you named the profile already loaded, a name that is not found prints a line and keeps the current profile, and OgreBotAPI.Options:LoadProfile calls this.
  arg name (string): the profile name (case does not matter); a b64: prefix marks a base64 name
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:LoadProfile[Raid]

ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Open[character,profile]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: Loads the character's profile from disk and opens the OgreBot main window and mini toolbar with it, then scans gear and inventory for the Items tab. Calling it while OgreBot is open loads the profile again and drops unsaved changes with one warning line; unlike the `ogre` command it leaves the pause state as it was, and a failed load (no character, profile not found) prints a line and changes nothing.
  arg character (string, default: ${Me.Name}): the character whose profile to load
  arg profile (string, default: the character's default profile): the profile name to load
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Open[${Me.Name},Group]

ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:OpenMini
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: Opens the OgreBot mini toolbar on its own, without loading a profile, and prints a line. If the mini toolbar is already open it does nothing.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:OpenMini

ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:RefreshTargets
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: Re-reads which aliases and targets resolve right now and sends them to the OgreBot window's Target dropdown. It does nothing when the main window is closed.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:RefreshTargets

ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Reload
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: Reads the loaded profile again from disk, dropping unsaved changes with one warning line, and refreshes the cast stack and the open window. It does nothing when no profile is loaded; OgreBotAPI.Bot:Reload is a different call that restarts the whole bot.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Reload

ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:ReloadKeyBinds
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: Reads the shared key binds file again (forward, backward and the other movement keys) and prints the new forward and backward keys. Another EQ2 session on this PC sends it after a key is changed.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:ReloadKeyBinds

ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:ReloadUi
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: Reloads the in-game window pages from disk, then reopens the OgreBot main window and mini toolbar if they were open, with the same profile and settings. Nothing in the bot is reloaded or reset; this is what `ogre ui reload` runs.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:ReloadUi

ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Research[mode]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: Runs the Ability Research check: it opens the Knowledge window and, with go or run, claims finished research and starts the next ability from the saved priority list, then closes the window. With no mode or any other word it only reads the window and says what it would do (trace also logs each window read), and a call while a check is running is ignored.
  arg mode (string, default: preview): go or run for the real run, trace for a logged preview; anything else is a preview
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Research[go]

ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Save
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: Writes the loaded profile's changes to disk and prints each file it wrote. With nothing loaded or nothing changed it prints that and writes nothing.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:Save

ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:SaveProfileAs[name]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: Overwrites another profile with the current settings, unsaved changes included, and switches to it. It fails with a console line when that profile does not exist or is the loaded one.
  arg name (string): the profile to overwrite; a b64: prefix marks a base64 name
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:SaveProfileAs[Solo]

ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:ScanItems
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: Asks for a scan of equipped gear, inventory and adornments on the next pulse, to fill the Items tab's source list. The request is dropped when no profile is loaded or the in-game UI is not ready, and opening OgreBot already runs one.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:ScanItems

ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:SetDefault[name]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: Makes a named profile the one this character loads by default, and writes that to the profile file at once. It fails with a console line when nothing is loaded or the profile does not exist.
  arg name (string): the profile name (case does not matter); a b64: prefix marks a base64 name
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:SetDefault[Group]

ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:UplinkConnect
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: Connects this PC's uplink to every PC on the Uplink Info list except this one, spaced out, and prints how many it did (or that there is nothing to do). A second connect or disconnect from the same session within 3 seconds is ignored and only written to the log.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:UplinkConnect

ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:UplinkDisconnect
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot
  what: Disconnects this PC's uplink from every PC on the Uplink Info list except this one, and prints how many it did (or that there is nothing to do). A second connect or disconnect from the same session within 3 seconds is ignored and only written to the log.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OgreBot:UplinkDisconnect


== ISXOgreEQ2.OSA ==

ISXOgreEQ2.OSA:Close
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OSA
  what: Closes the On-Screen Assistant window and stops its NPC scan, including an open that is still being retried. It does not untick the Enable On-Screen Assistant setting, so the window opens again only when that setting is next switched on (or at the next load while it is ticked).
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OSA:Close

ISXOgreEQ2.OSA:Open
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OSA
  what: Opens the On-Screen Assistant (OSA) window, the same as `ogre osa`: a live list of the NPCs around you, named NPCs first and then by distance, up to 35 rows, refreshed about 5 times a second within the Settings scan radius (50 until a value is set, at most 200). It does nothing while the window is already up, and it does not tick the Enable On-Screen Assistant setting, which opens and closes the window by itself whenever it changes.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OSA:Open

ISXOgreEQ2.OSA:Target[id]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.OSA
  what: Targets the actor with the given ID at once by sending the `target <id>` command, which is what clicking a row in the OSA window does. A call with no ID prints a line and targets nothing.
  arg id (int): ID of the actor to target
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.OSA:Target[${Target.Target.ID}]


== ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer ==

ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:BuyMissions[flag...]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer
  what: Starts a run that buys Overseer missions at the merchant on this session, using this character's Overseer Buy tab with any flags overriding it: -season N, -colour C, -num N, -amount N (at most 20), -replenishonly, -scribe or -noscribe, -destroy or -nodestroy, -gettogh or -nogettogh (go to the guild hall when done); unknown words are skipped. Refused with a console line when OgreBot is not open with a profile, a buy run is already going, or the first argument is not a -flag - the same run OgreBotAPI.Overseer:BuyMissions queues with a for-who.
  arg flag... (string): Optional flags, one per argument, each value as its own argument after its flag; none uses the Overseer Buy tab as saved
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:BuyMissions[-season,2,-amount,5]

ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:BuyMissionsStatus
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer
  what: Prints whether the Overseer mission buy run is idle or, if running, the phase it is in.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:BuyMissionsStatus

ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:BuyMissionsStop
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer
  what: Aborts the Overseer mission buy run in progress and prints the reason. Prints "nothing running." when idle; same as `ogre end buyoverseermissions`.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:BuyMissionsStop

ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:Run
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer
  what: Starts a manual Overseer run on this session now, skipping the 60-minute throttle; it uses OgreBot's Overseer tab when OgreBot is open, and the defaults (complete finished quests, add bag missions, start mishaps and new quests, take rewards) when it is not. Refused with a console line when any argument is passed, a run is already going, a bag-mission add is busy, or 'Do not touch overseer at all no matter what' is ticked - the same run as OgreBotAPI.Overseer:CheckQuests and `ogre overseer`.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:Run

ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:Status
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer
  what: Prints the Overseer run's current phase, whether it is running, and how many quests it has started and completed. When idle after a run it also prints roughly how many seconds until the next automatic run is allowed.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:Status

ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:Stop
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer
  what: Ends the Overseer run in progress on this session and prints "run aborted", or prints "nothing to stop" when idle. Same as `ogre end overseer`.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Overseer:Stop


== ISXOgreEQ2.PackPony ==

ISXOgreEQ2.PackPony:Start[word,word]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.PackPony
  what: Sends the pack pony out and unloads it, once. An unknown word refuses the whole line and nothing starts; a run that cannot start says why.
  arg word (string): nodismiss leaves the pony summoned afterwards. Optional.
  arg word (string): nopause does not pause OgreBot for the run. Optional.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.PackPony:Start[nodismiss]

ISXOgreEQ2.PackPony:Status
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.PackPony

  example: ISXOgreEQ2.PackPony:Status

ISXOgreEQ2.PackPony:Stop
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.PackPony
  what: Abandons a run in progress and cleans up after it. With no run it says so.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.PackPony:Stop


== ISXOgreEQ2.Paths ==

ISXOgreEQ2.Paths:End
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Paths
  what: Closes the Points of Interest and Paths window, which is what `ogre end paths` and the window's X do. A path being walked goes on.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Paths:End

ISXOgreEQ2.Paths:Open[path]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Paths
  what: Opens the Points of Interest and Paths window (the same as `ogre paths`), on a saved path of the zone you are in when you name one: this is the one way to open it, from a panel, a button or a script. A window already open comes to the front on that path, a path this zone does not have prints one line and the window opens with nothing picked, and without the Ogre UI desktop it prints a warning.
  arg path (string, default: none (nothing picked)): The path to open on, in any case. A name with spaces may be quoted or written as several words. Leave it out to open the window with nothing picked.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Paths:Open["North Loop"]


== ISXOgreEQ2.Perf ==

ISXOgreEQ2.Perf:Measure[seconds,nothreads]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Perf
  what: Measures the frame rate and what uses each frame for a number of seconds, then prints a report to the console and the log file - the same as ogre perf. The capture starts on the next frame; if one is already running, or a word other than a number or nothreads is given, it prints a line and measures nothing.
  arg seconds (int, default: 10): how long to measure, 3 to 120 (values outside are clamped)
  arg nothreads (string, default: ""): the word nothreads turns off the per-thread breakdown; it may come before or after the seconds
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Perf:Measure[30]

ISXOgreEQ2.Perf:Status
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Perf
  what: Prints one console line saying whether a measurement is idle, about to start, or running with the seconds done and left - the same as ogre perf status.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Perf:Status

ISXOgreEQ2.Perf:Stop
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Perf
  what: Ends a running measurement early and prints the report for what was measured, or cancels one that has not started yet - the same as ogre perf stop. With nothing running it prints that nothing is being measured.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Perf:Stop

ISXOgreEQ2.Persona:Open

== ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb ==

ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:End
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb
  what: Stops the Potency / Crit Bonus / Fervor sampler if it runs and always closes its panel, keeping the history. This is what `ogre end potcb` and the panel's X do.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:End

ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Help
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb
  what: Prints the `ogre potcb` usage to the console: open, on / off, status, reset and interval.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Help

ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Interval[ms]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb
  what: Sets how often the sampler reads Potency, Crit Bonus and Fervor, held between 50 and 10000 ms (a negative is 50), and prints the new value. With no value it prints the current interval; a value that is not a number keeps the interval in force and says so.
  arg ms (int): Sampling interval in milliseconds, 50 to 10000 (the sampler starts at 200). Optional: leave it out to print the current interval.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Interval[500]

ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Off
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb
  what: Stops the Potency / Crit Bonus / Fervor sampler and closes its panel, keeping the recorded history. If it was not sampling it prints "potcb: not running." and leaves the panel open.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Off

ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:On
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb
  what: Starts the Potency / Crit Bonus / Fervor sampler, which reads the three stats every interval (default 200 ms) while you are in world, and prints one line saying so. Does nothing if it is already sampling, and does not open the panel.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:On

ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Open
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb
  what: Opens the Potency / Crit Bonus / Fervor tracker panel, starting the sampler first if it was stopped (the same as bare `ogre potcb`). If the panel is already up it stays as it is, and without the Ogre UI desktop it prints a warning while sampling still starts.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Open

ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Reset
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb
  what: Clears every recorded Potency / Crit Bonus / Fervor figure and the sampled time, then prints "potcb: history cleared". The sampler stays on or off as it was.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Reset

ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Status
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb
  what: Prints every Potency / Crit Bonus / Fervor figure to the console: running or stopped and time sampled, then per stat the current value and peak, the in-combat min / avg / max, time at cap, time at peak and combat time by tenth of the peak, and the overall min / avg / max. It also warns when readings were skipped because a stat showed no number.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.PotCb:Status


== ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget ==

ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Ceiling[us]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget
  what: Sets the shared frame ceiling and saves it; below 0 reads as 0. With no value it prints one warning and changes nothing.
  arg us (float): The ceiling in microseconds; 0 means none.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Ceiling[4000]

ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Close
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget
  what: Closes the Pulse Budget window, the same as `ogre end pulse`. The budget keeps running.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Close

ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:JobTest[state]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget
  what: A test mode for this session only: every pulse job pauses at every checkpoint, so state that does not survive a frame shows up at once. It is never saved.
  arg state (string): on or 1 turns it on; any other word turns it off. Required.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:JobTest[on]

ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Off
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget
  what: Turns the shared frame ceiling off and saves it. Each section still keeps its own slice.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Off

ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:On
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget
  what: Turns the shared frame ceiling on, resets the counters and saves it.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:On

ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Open
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget
  what: Opens the Pulse Budget window, the same as bare `ogre pulse`.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Open

ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Report
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget
  what: Prints the per-section table to the console.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Report

ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Reset
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget
  what: Resets the counters.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Reset

ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Slice[section,us]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget
  what: Sets how long a resumable section may run per frame and saves it; a slice paces the work and never skips any of it. A missing section or value prints one warning, and a section nothing matches prints another.
  arg section (string): The section's name, or its number from :Report.
  arg us (float): Microseconds per frame; 0 lets it run to completion.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.PulseBudget:Slice[3,200]
