== ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper ==

ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:Help
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper
  what: Prints the `ogre quest` usage lines (start, stop, status, list, reload) to the console.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:Help

ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:List
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper
  what: Prints what the loaded reply table holds: the total rule count, the rules that apply in every zone, the rules in each zone's own list, and the counts of ignored objects and chat captures. A zone that has its own list does not also use the every-zone rules.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:List

ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:Off
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper
  what: Stops the quest helper and prints its hail, object-click and reply counts, which add up across every run this session. When it is not running it prints 'questhelper: not running.' instead.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:Off

ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:On[option1]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper
  what: Starts the quest helper (`ogre quest`), which runs until QuestHelper:Off and about every half second answers an open NPC conversation from its reply table (or takes the only reply), otherwise hails a non-attackable NPC within 10 units that has a quest to give, update or complete, otherwise double-clicks an interactable object within 5 units that is not on its ignore list and is not a way out of the zone (a name with the word zone, teleporter or exit), logging every hail and click with its zone. It does nothing while you are moving, out of the world or in a guild hall, the hail goes through the bot's queued Hail action, and it prints one line when it starts (or says it is already running).
  arg option1 (int, default: none): Optional. 1 = always click reply 1 and ignore the reply table; leave it out to use the table. Any other value is refused with one line and nothing starts. Calling On again while it runs switches this mode.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:On[1]

ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:Reload
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper
  what: Re-reads the reply table from the shipped files (Scripts/Ogre/EQ2/QuestHelper/default) and your own (Scripts/OgreSave/EQ2/QuestHelper/custom), warns about each file that fails to load, and prints the rule count. If no file loads at all, the table already in use is kept and the line says so instead of a loaded count.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:Reload

ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:Status
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper
  what: Prints the quest helper's state to the console: running or stopped, whether it always takes reply 1, your zone, what it last did, how long since it last acted, its hail, object-click and reply counts for this run (they start from 0 at each start), and how many reply rules are loaded.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.QuestHelper:Status


== ISXOgreEQ2.Queue ==

${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.Blocking}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Queue
  what: Why the most urgent waiting entry cannot start yet, as a line like seq=5 CastAbility prio=100 age=900ms: resource busy: CastBar, or starved by a higher-priority haltQueue entry. Empty when nothing is waiting or the next entry is free to start.
  returns: string: the reason line; empty when nothing is held up
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.Blocking}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.Count}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Queue
  what: Number of entries in the action queue, running plus waiting.
  returns: int: entries running plus waiting; 0 when the queue is empty
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.Count}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.Enqueue[priority,kind,arg0,arg1,ttlstart,ttlmax]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Queue
  what: Adds an entry exactly like ISXOgreEQ2.Queue:Add and returns its seq, the id you pass to Status, IsDone and Remove. Reading the member is what adds the entry, so every read queues another one, and an unknown kind (ApplyVerbCastBar and DialogChoices included) or a flow name that is not registered adds nothing and returns 0.
  arg priority (int, default: 100): Higher runs first; 0 means the default 100
  arg kind (string): What to do, any case: CastAbility, CastItem, ClickCastBar, RawCommand, Movement or Flow. ApplyVerbCastBar and DialogChoices are not kinds here; OgreBotAPI.Actors:ApplyVerbIDQueued queues an apply-verb
  arg arg0 (string): Depends on kind: RawCommand the console command, CastAbility the ability id or name, CastItem the item name, ClickCastBar the actor id, Movement x,y,z with an optional precision, Flow the flow name
  arg arg1 (string): Depends on kind: CastAbility the target name (empty = current target), CastItem the equip slot (empty = the bag item by name), ClickCastBar the wait in tenths of a second (empty = 4 seconds), Flow its arguments
  arg ttlstart (int, default: 0): Milliseconds the entry may wait to start before it is dropped with status Expired; 0 = no limit
  arg ttlmax (int, default: 0): Milliseconds the entry may run before it is stopped with status Aborted; 0 = no limit
  returns: int64: the new entry's seq (1 and up); 0 when the kind is unknown
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.Enqueue[100,RawCommand,"echo queued"]}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.Entry[index]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Queue
  what: One queue entry as a readable line, such as seq=12 prio=100 RawCommand waiting age=40ms arg0=echo hi, where seq is the entry's id. The index counts from 1, running entries first and then waiting ones, each sorted by priority then by the order they were added.
  arg index (int): Position in the queue counting from 1: running entries first, then waiting ones, highest priority first
  returns: string: the entry line; empty when the index is 0, past the end or missing
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.Entry[1]}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.EntryJSON[index]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Queue
  what: One queue entry as a JSON object with seq, priority, kind, status (running or waiting), holds, haltQueue, haltCastStack, ageMs, blocked, arg0, arg1 and label. Same index as Entry, counting from 1, so a loop from 1 to Count reads the whole queue.
  arg index (int): Position in the queue counting from 1: running entries first, then waiting ones, highest priority first
  returns: string: the entry as a JSON object; {} when the index is 0, past the end or missing
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.EntryJSON[1]}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.InFlight}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Queue
  what: Whether any queue entry is running right now.
  returns: bool: TRUE when at least one entry is running; FALSE when none is
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.InFlight}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.IsDone[seq]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Queue
  what: Whether the queue entry with that seq has finished in any way (Done, Failed, Expired, Aborted or Removed), so a wait loop never hangs on a failed entry; read Status for how it ended. A seq that finished and has since been forgotten also reads TRUE, while a seq never issued reads FALSE.
  arg seq (int64): The entry's id, from Enqueue or the seq= field of Entry and Spew
  returns: bool: TRUE when the entry has finished, however it ended; FALSE while it is waiting or running, or when the seq was never issued
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.IsDone[1]}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.Status[seq]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Queue
  what: The state of the queue entry with that seq. Unknown means the seq was never issued or finished too long ago to remember (only the most recent 256 are kept).
  arg seq (int64): The entry's id, from Enqueue or the seq= field of Entry and Spew
  returns: string: Pending, InFlight, Done, Failed, Expired, Aborted, Removed or Unknown
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Queue.Status[1]}

ISXOgreEQ2.Queue:Add[priority,kind,arg0,arg1,ttlstart,ttlmax]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Queue
  what: Adds an action to the priority queue, which runs it on its turn once the cast bar or movement it needs is free (highest priority first, even while OgreBot is paused), and prints an Add seq=N line to the console. Waiting and running entries are dropped on a zone change or when OgreBot ends, a Flow lives as its registered flow does, with that flow's holds and halts, and a flow name that is not registered gets one line; use the Enqueue member instead when you need the seq back.
  arg priority (int, default: 100): Higher runs first; 0 means the default 100
  arg kind (string): What to do, any case: CastAbility, CastItem, ClickCastBar, RawCommand, Movement or Flow. ApplyVerbCastBar and DialogChoices are not kinds here; OgreBotAPI.Actors:ApplyVerbIDQueued queues an apply-verb
  arg arg0 (string): Depends on kind: RawCommand the console command, CastAbility the ability id or name, CastItem the item name, ClickCastBar the actor id, Movement x,y,z with an optional precision, Flow the flow name
  arg arg1 (string): Depends on kind: CastAbility the target name (empty = current target), CastItem the equip slot (empty = the bag item by name), ClickCastBar the wait in tenths of a second (empty = 4 seconds), Flow its arguments
  arg ttlstart (int, default: 0): Milliseconds the entry may wait to start before it is dropped with status Expired; 0 = no limit
  arg ttlmax (int, default: 0): Milliseconds the entry may run before it is stopped with status Aborted; 0 = no limit. For a Flow it can only shorten the flow's own limit
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Queue:Add[100,RawCommand,"echo queued"]

ISXOgreEQ2.Queue:Remove[seq]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Queue
  what: Removes the waiting queue entry with that seq (its Status becomes Removed) and prints the result to the console. A running entry is not removed, and an unknown or missing seq only prints that there is no such entry.
  arg seq (int64): The entry's id, from Enqueue or the seq= field of Entry and Spew
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Queue:Remove[1]

ISXOgreEQ2.Queue:Spew
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Queue
  what: Prints every queue entry to the console, running entries then waiting ones, one line each starting with its seq, then a line on how to remove one. Prints empty - 0 entries when the queue is empty.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Queue:Spew


== ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver ==

${ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver.Running}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver
  what: TRUE while a quiver refill is moving ammo out of your bags, or while the ammo depot pull it started is still running. A depot errand started by something else does not count.
  returns: bool: TRUE while either half of a quiver refill runs; FALSE when idle.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver.Running}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver.Status}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver
  what: Progress of a quiver refill: the bag half with its count, then the ammo depot pull while that runs.
  returns: string: "idle", "filling from bags (done/total)", "arming the depot pull" or "pulling ammo from the depot".
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver.Status}

ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver:Refill
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver
  what: The engine behind `ogre quiver` and the quiver step of the Inventory Manager chain: moves matching ammo from your bags into the equipped quiver or pouch (1 s apart, 2 s in combat), then, in a guild hall, tops it up from the ammo depot, warning and stopping when no ammo container is equipped or the ammo kind cannot be told. To tell arrows, bolts or thrown ammo it makes ONE SERVER CALL (the equipped ranged weapon's `.ToItemInfo.SubType`, only when that item's info is already available), then falls back to what is in the container, then to the container's name.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver:Refill

ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver:Stop
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver
  what: Stops both halves of a quiver refill, the bag moves and the ammo depot pull it started, and prints "quiver: stopped.". Prints nothing when neither half is running; it is the same stop `ogre end quiver` uses.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Quiver:Stop


== ISXOgreEQ2.Radar ==

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Budget[n,ms]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: The read budget: how many actors a pulse may read their slow fields, and how old a slow field may get. With no argument it prints both; an age out of range is refused, but the actor count is still written.
  arg n (int): Actors per pulse, 0-5000. Optional.
  arg ms (int): The oldest a slow field may get, 0-600000 ms. Optional.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Budget[60,3000]

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Cap[n]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Draws only the nearest n blips, where 0 means no cap; it bounds what is drawn, not what is read. With no argument it prints the cap, and out of range is refused.
  arg n (int): The cap, 0-5000. Optional.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Cap[200]

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:CfgPath
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Prints the path of the radar's settings file.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:CfgPath

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:CfgSave
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Writes the settings the panel left in the host store to the radar's settings file, and says whether it worked. The Save button sends this.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:CfgSave

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Chunk[n]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Spreads a refresh over frames: n actors a frame, 0 to 500, where 0 means the whole refresh on one frame. With no argument it prints it.
  arg n (int): Actors per frame, 0-500. Optional.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Chunk[50]

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Click[word]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: on lets the mouse pass through the panel to the game; off captures it again. A click-through panel can never be clicked back, so this is the way out.
  arg word (string): on or off (any yes or no word). With neither it prints the usage.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Click[off]

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Dump[n]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Prints the first n blips of the last snapshot to the console.
  arg n (int): How many. 10 when absent.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Dump[25]

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Fields[word]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: full reads level, health and con on the slow budget; lean stops reading them, so they stop updating. It is not saved, and any other word prints the usage.
  arg word (string): lean or full.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Fields[lean]

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Help
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Prints every radar word to the console, the same as `ogre radar help`.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Help

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:LoadTest[range,labels,glide]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Panel only: widens the zoom so that many blips are really drawn, for measuring a loaded panel.
  arg range (int): The range to draw. 400 when absent.
  arg labels (string): on to draw labels. Optional.
  arg glide (string): on to glide. Optional.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:LoadTest[800,on,on]

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:MaxRate[n]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Never refreshes faster than n a second, where 0 means no ceiling and a number outside 0-240 is clamped. Without the number it prints the usage.
  arg n (int): The ceiling. Required.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:MaxRate[30]

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Off
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Stops scanning and closes the panel, the same as `ogre end radar` and the panel's X.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Off

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:On
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Starts scanning and opens the panel, the same as bare `ogre radar`. On a radar already on and open it says nothing.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:On

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Panel[word]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: The panel only, scanning left as it is: on opens it, off closes it, reload reads radar.html and radar.js from disk again. Any other word prints the usage.
  arg word (string): on, off or reload.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Panel[reload]

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Parity
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Prints every field of every blip in the last snapshot, one line each sorted by id, so two captures compare as a line diff. It reads the snapshot only.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Parity

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Perf[word]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Prints the radar's cost report to the console. With reset it clears the counters, so the next report covers from now.
  arg word (string): reset. Optional.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Perf

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Push[word]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: off stops handing snapshots to the panel while refreshes still run, so Perf shows the data cost alone; on hands them over again.
  arg word (string): on or off (any yes or no word). With neither it prints the usage.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Push[off]

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Quest[word]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: on makes the radar read UpdatesMyQuest for the panel's quest-only filter and off stops it, so it costs nothing unless it is used. With no argument it prints the setting.
  arg word (string): on or off. Optional.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Quest[on]

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:QuestNpc[word]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: on makes the radar find quest NPCs for the panel's quest NPC filter and off stops it. With no argument it prints the setting.
  arg word (string): on or off. Optional.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:QuestNpc[on]

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Radius[n]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Sets the display radius in game units; the panel applies it, so no game read is saved. With no argument it prints the radius, and out of range is refused.
  arg n (int): The radius, 5-500. Optional.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Radius[150]

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Rate[hz]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Sets refreshes per second, where 0 means every pulse. With no argument it prints the rate, and out of range is refused.
  arg hz (int): The rate, 0-60. Optional.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Rate[20]

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Reload
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Reads radar.html and radar.js from disk again and redraws the panel, with no rebuild and no client restart.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Reload

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Scan
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Forces one refresh on the next pulse, ignoring the rate.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Scan

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Settings
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Opens the panel's settings drawer and forces mouse capture on while it is open, so it works on a click-through or borderless panel.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Settings

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Shake[word,rotate]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Panel only: synthetic blip motion every tick, no running required. on starts it, anything else stops it; a second argument of on rotates as well.
  arg word (string): on or off (any yes or no word). With neither it prints the usage.
  arg rotate (string): on to rotate too. Optional.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Shake[on,on]

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Status
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Prints the radar's state to the console: scanning, panel, push, radius, rate, fields, chunk and cap, what the rate really works out to, where the actors come from, the last snapshot and the settings file.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Status

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Target[id]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Targets an actor through the targeting arbiter on the radar's next pulse: what a blip click sends. No id prints the usage; an id that reads as 0 is refused.
  arg id (string): The actor id. Required.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Target[12345]

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:TestPattern[word]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: A pink dot orbits the scope on the panel's own clock, with no game data, so the eye can judge the panel's smoothness alone.
  arg word (string): on or off (any yes or no word). With neither it prints the usage.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:TestPattern[on]

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Toggle
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Turns the radar on with its panel if it is off, and off if it is on.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Toggle

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:TypeLive[word]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: on reads Type every pass, so a corpse draws as a corpse on the next refresh; off puts Type on the slow budget. With no argument it prints the setting.
  arg word (string): on or off. Optional.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:TypeLive[on]

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:UiDump[word]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Prints what the panel itself reports: draw rate, render cost and JS errors, or says it has published nothing. With reset it clears the panel's held peaks.
  arg word (string): reset. Optional.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:UiDump

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:UiEcho[words]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Prints its words to the console: the panel's way of putting a value where a redirect can capture it.
  arg words (string): What to print, joined with spaces.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:UiEcho[hello]

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:UiReset
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Puts the panel's look back to its defaults, for a look that left nothing on screen to click. It is not saved until you press Save in the drawer.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:UiReset

ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Verify
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Radar
  what: Compares the held actor index against a fresh scan and names any drift on the console; on drift it rebuilds the index and clears the radar's field cache. The Verify button sends this.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Radar:Verify


== ISXOgreEQ2.Refine ==

ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Bags[bags...]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Refine
  what: Sets which carried bags (1 to 6) a refine run scans - bags 1 and 2 by default - and echoes the new list. A missing list is refused with a console line, anything that is not bag numbers, all or none prints the usage line and changes nothing, and the setting is not saved.
  arg bags... (string): bag numbers 1 to 6, as separate arguments or one list such as 1,2,5; each digit is one bag, so 12 means bags 1 and 2; or all / none
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Bags[1,2,3]

ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Plan
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Refine
  what: A dry run: scans the selected bags with the current settings and prints each item a run would refine (bag, slot, quantity, name) and why the others were skipped. Nothing is refined, and out of the world it only prints a warning.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Plan

ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Rare[value]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Refine
  what: Turns refining of Rare resources on or off (off by default) and echoes the new setting. A missing value is refused with a console line, a value that is not on or off prints the usage line, and the setting is not saved.
  arg value (string): on or off (1 / 0 and true / false also work)
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Rare[off]

ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Raw[value]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Refine
  what: Turns refining of Raw resources on or off (on by default) and echoes the new setting. A missing value is refused with a console line, a value that is not on or off prints the usage line, and the setting is not saved.
  arg value (string): on or off (1 / 0 and true / false also work)
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Raw[on]

ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Reload
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Refine
  what: Re-reads the refiner's resource list now: the shipped files under Ogre/EQ2/Refine/default plus your own under OgreSave/EQ2/Refine/custom. It echoes how many resources loaded, and a warning for any file it could not read or when no files were found.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Reload

ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Rewards[value]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Refine
  what: When on, every reward window that appears while a refine run is in progress is accepted automatically - including ones unrelated to refining, such as a quest reward. Off by default; a missing value is refused with a console line, and the setting is not saved.
  arg value (string): on or off (1 / 0 and true / false also work)
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Rewards[off]

ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Start
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Refine
  what: Starts one background pass over the selected carried bags: for each Raw or Rare resource on the refiner's list (provisioner resources skipped) it uses your Refine ability, refines the item until the stack is gone or a try limit is reached, and answers the refine confirm window itself while the run lasts. It refuses with a console line when a run is already going, you are not in the world, the resource list is empty, you lack the Refine ability, or Raw and Rare are both off.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Start

ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Status
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Refine
  what: Prints the refiner's state to the console: how many resources its list holds, whether Raw and Rare are on, which bags it scans, whether reward windows are auto-accepted, and the progress of a run in flight, then the usage line. The same as `ogre refine` or `ogre refine status`.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Status

ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Stop
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Refine
  what: Stops a refine run in progress, the same as `ogre end refine`. When nothing is running it prints "refine: not running." to the console.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Refine:Stop


== ISXOgreEQ2.ReplenishNames ==

ISXOgreEQ2.ReplenishNames:Reload
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.ReplenishNames
  what: Re-reads both replenish name files now, warning in the console about any problem it finds, then prints the same report as ReplenishNames:Show. A changed file is picked up on its next use anyway, so this is only needed to see the result straight away.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.ReplenishNames:Reload

ISXOgreEQ2.ReplenishNames:Show
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.ReplenishNames
  what: Prints the fallback potion, food and drink names the replenish options use when nothing better is set, plus where the shipped file and your own file (OgreSave/EQ2/Replenish/custom/replenish-names.json) live. The files are re-read first when either has changed since the last read.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.ReplenishNames:Show


== ISXOgreEQ2.SafeFall ==

ISXOgreEQ2.SafeFall:End
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.SafeFall
  what: Stops the trainer and closes the window, the same as `ogre end safefall` and the window's X. It takes no arguments.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.SafeFall:End

ISXOgreEQ2.SafeFall:Help
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.SafeFall
  what: Prints the `ogre safefall` usage to the console.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.SafeFall:Help

ISXOgreEQ2.SafeFall:Off
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.SafeFall
  what: Stops the trainer on the next tick and leaves the window up. It takes no arguments.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.SafeFall:Off

ISXOgreEQ2.SafeFall:On[ticks]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.SafeFall
  what: Arms the trainer: on the next tick it flies up, falls and repeats, gaining flight time as it goes. Already running, it restarts; a bad value prints why and the usage.
  arg ticks (int): Flight time in tenths of a second, 5 to 600. Optional: 30 when left out.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.SafeFall:On[45]

ISXOgreEQ2.SafeFall:Open
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.SafeFall
  what: Opens the Safe Fall Trainer window. It takes no arguments.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.SafeFall:Open

ISXOgreEQ2.SafeFall:Status
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.SafeFall
  what: Prints the trainer's state and usage to the console, the same as bare `ogre safefall`. It takes no arguments.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.SafeFall:Status


== ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler ==

${ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler.Active[key]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler
  what: Whether a timer with this key still has a fire pending. Keys ignore case; a one-shot timer reads FALSE once it has fired.
  arg key (string): the timer's key (its event name unless it was armed with -key)
  returns: bool: TRUE when a fire is still pending for this key; FALSE when there is no such timer.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler.Active[MyTimerEvent]}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler.Count}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler
  what: How many keyed timers are pending in the scheduler. The encounter engine's timers live in the same table, so they count too.
  returns: int: number of pending keyed timers.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler.Count}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler.Remaining[key]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler
  what: Milliseconds until the next fire of the timer with this key. Reads 0 when there is no such timer or it is due now.
  arg key (string): the timer's key (its event name unless it was armed with -key)
  returns: int64: milliseconds to the next fire; 0 when there is no such timer or it is due.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler.Remaining[MyTimerEvent]}

ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler:Cancel[key]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler
  what: Stops the timer with this key before it fires again. Keys ignore case, and a key with no timer does nothing.
  arg key (string): the timer's key (its event name unless it was armed with -key)
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler:Cancel[MyTimerEvent]

ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler:ClearNonPersistent
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler
  what: Cancels every script and encounter timer that was not armed with -persistent, and leaves the bot's own pending delayed casts and actions. Finishing a zone clears every non-persistent timer, the bot's included.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler:ClearNonPersistent

ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler:FireEvent[delay,eventName,payload,-persistent,-key]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler
  what: Fires the LavishScript event eventName once after the delay, always with exactly one argument (the payload, or an empty string). Arming a key that is already pending replaces that timer, and unless -persistent is given the timer is dropped when you finish zoning; a bad delay such as 30x fires nothing and warns on the console.
  arg delay (string): how long to wait: a whole number of milliseconds, or a number with ms, s, m or h (30s, 1.5s, 2m)
  arg eventName (string): the LavishScript event to fire
  arg payload (string, default: ""): the one argument passed to the event; the first extra word not starting with a dash
  arg -persistent (switch, default: off): keep the timer across zoning
  arg -key (switch, default: the event name): -key <k>: the timer's key, case-insensitive
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler:FireEvent[5s,MyTimerEvent,hello]

ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler:FireEventEvery[interval,eventName,repeats,payload,-persistent,-key]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler
  what: Fires the LavishScript event eventName every interval, repeats times, always with exactly one argument (the payload, or an empty string); a missing, 0 or negative repeats means forever. Re-arming a pending key replaces it, and unless -persistent is given the timer is dropped when you finish zoning; a bad interval fires nothing and warns on the console.
  arg interval (string): time between fires: a whole number of milliseconds, or a number with ms, s, m or h; the first fire comes one interval after the call
  arg eventName (string): the LavishScript event to fire
  arg repeats (int, default: forever): how many times to fire; 0 or less fires until cancelled
  arg payload (string, default: ""): the one argument passed to the event; the first extra word not starting with a dash
  arg -persistent (switch, default: off): keep the timer across zoning
  arg -key (switch, default: the event name): -key <k>: the timer's key, case-insensitive
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler:FireEventEvery[10s,MyTimerEvent,6,tick]

ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler:Spew
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler
  what: Prints every pending keyed timer to the console, the encounter engine's included: a count line, then one line per timer with its key, event, milliseconds to the next fire, how many times it has fired, and whether it is persistent.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Scheduler:Spew


== ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn ==

${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.ChestId}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn
  what: The actor ID of the Exquisite Chest that spawned in this zone, taken from the spawn feed. It goes back to 0 when that chest despawns or you zone.
  returns: int64: the chest's actor ID; 0 when there is none.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.ChestId}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.DespawnsDispatched}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn
  what: The number of despawn events handed on to the bot's internal listeners since the extension loaded.
  returns: int64: despawn events dispatched.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.DespawnsDispatched}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.Dispatched}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn
  what: The total number of spawn and despawn events handed on to the bot's internal listeners since the extension loaded. It is SpawnsDispatched plus DespawnsDispatched.
  returns: int64: spawn plus despawn events dispatched.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.Dispatched}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.HasChest}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn
  what: Whether an Exquisite Chest is up in this zone, the same test as ChestId being non-zero.
  returns: bool: TRUE when ChestId is not 0; FALSE otherwise.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.HasChest}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.IsLive[id]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn
  what: Whether the actor ID is in the live set: seen spawning (or present when the zone settled) and not yet despawned. The set is wiped when you zone and filled again once the new zone settles, so it can read FALSE for a moment after zoning.
  arg <id> (int64): The actor ID to test.
  returns: bool: TRUE when that actor is live; FALSE when it is not, or when no ID is given.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.IsLive[${Target.ID}]}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.LiveCount}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn
  what: How many actor IDs are in the live set for this zone. It drops to 0 while zoning and refills once the new zone settles.
  returns: int: the number of live actors tracked.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.LiveCount}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.OnSpawnDelay}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn
  what: How long after an actor spawns the delayed spawn event EQ2_ActorSpawned_Delayed fires for it (only if it is still live). The default is 1000 ms and the most is 60000; SetOnSpawnDelay changes it for this session only.
  returns: int: the delay in milliseconds.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.OnSpawnDelay}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.Received}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn
  what: The total number of actor spawn and despawn events received from the game since the extension loaded. It is a diagnostic counter and is not reset by zoning.
  returns: int64: spawn plus despawn events received.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.Received}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.SpawnsDispatched}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn
  what: The number of spawn events handed on to the bot's internal listeners since the extension loaded.
  returns: int64: spawn events dispatched.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.SpawnsDispatched}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.Subscribers}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn
  what: How many internal listeners are attached to the spawn feed. It counts spawn, despawn and delayed-spawn listeners together.
  returns: int: the number of attached listeners.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn.Subscribers}

ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn:DelayStatus
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn
  what: Prints the delayed spawn event's state to the console: the delay, the per-drain cap, what is waiting and ready, and the counters since the last zone-in.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn:DelayStatus

ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn:ResetOnSpawnDelay
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn
  what: Puts the delay before EQ2_ActorSpawned_Delayed back to the default of 1000 ms and prints the value to the console.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn:ResetOnSpawnDelay

ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn:SetOnSpawnCap
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn
  what: Sets how many due spawns one drain may emit, for this session only, held between 1 and 5000 (0 or a negative is 1), and prints the value in force to the console. A value that is not a number keeps the cap and says so; with no value it prints one warning and changes nothing.
  arg <k> (int): The per-drain cap, 1 to 5000.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn:SetOnSpawnCap[25]

ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn:SetOnSpawnDelay[<ms>]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn
  what: Sets the delay before EQ2_ActorSpawned_Delayed fires, for this session only (it is not saved), and prints the value in force to the console. More than 60000 ms is held at 60000; a value that is not a whole number of 0 or more is refused with a warning and the delay is unchanged.
  arg <ms> (int): The delay in milliseconds, 0 to 60000.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn:SetOnSpawnDelay[1500]

ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn:Status
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn
  what: Prints the spawn consumer's counters to the console: spawns and despawns seen, duplicate and unknown ids, the live actor count, the chest id and the router's subscribers and throughput.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Spawn:Status


== ISXOgreEQ2.TagTimers ==

ISXOgreEQ2.TagTimers:Close
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TagTimers
  what: Closes the Tag Timers window, the same as `ogre end tags` or its X, and does nothing while it is closed. A ticked Show Tag Timers window box stays ticked and opens it again on the next profile load.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TagTimers:Close

ISXOgreEQ2.TagTimers:Open
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TagTimers
  what: Opens the Tag Timers window, the same as `ogre tags`, and does nothing while it is already up. The Show Tag Timers window box on the Tags tab opens it with the profile.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TagTimers:Open


== ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting ==

${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.ActiveList}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting
  what: The name of the saved auto-target list last loaded or saved into the working list, like OgreBotAPI.AutoTarget.ListName. Reading it also refreshes the saved-list catalogue for the current zone.
  returns: string: the saved-list name; "" when none is loaded or when not in the world.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.ActiveList}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.AssistId}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting
  what: The assist decision as one number, read fresh on each call - the same call as OgreBotAPI.Assist.TargetID. It answers even when the Auto Assist box is off.
  returns: int64: greater than 0 is the ID this character would target; 0 when it picks its own target; -1 when its current target should be left alone; NULL when not in the world.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.AssistId}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.Enabled}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting
  what: Whether either targeting engine is switched on: the Auto Assist box or the auto-target box. This is not OgreBotAPI.AutoTarget.Enabled, which reads only the auto-target box.
  returns: bool: TRUE when the Auto Assist box or the auto-target box is ticked; FALSE when both are off.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.Enabled}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.InControl}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting
  what: Whether this character picks its own target instead of following someone else's - the same call as OgreBotAPI.Assist.InControl. With the Auto Assist box off it reads TRUE.
  returns: bool: TRUE when this character picks its own target; FALSE when it follows another player, and FALSE when not in the world.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.InControl}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.SavedList[index]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting
  what: The name of one saved auto-target list for the current zone, counting from 1 in file order, the same as OgreBotAPI.AutoTarget.SavedName.
  arg index (int): Which saved list, counting from 1. 0, or text that is not a number, reads empty.
  returns: string: the saved list's name; "" when index is 0 or past the count, when no index is given, or when not in the world.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.SavedList[1]}

${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.SavedListCount}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting
  what: The number of saved auto-target lists for the current zone, like OgreBotAPI.AutoTarget.SavedCount. Unlike that member it reloads the zone's catalogue first when the zone has changed, so it never shows the previous zone.
  returns: int: the number of saved lists; 0 when the zone has none or when not in the world.
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting.SavedListCount}

ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting:ClearList
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting
  what: Empties the working auto-target list and blanks ActiveList - OgreBotAPI.AutoTarget:Clear without the for-who. Auto-target then falls back to the profile's own AutoTarget entries (nothing to pick if it has none) until a list is loaded or entries are added, and saved lists on disk are not touched.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting:ClearList

ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting:LoadList[<name>]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting
  what: Replaces the working auto-target list with the saved list of that name for the current zone (the name is matched ignoring case) - OgreBotAPI.AutoTarget:LoadSaved without the for-who. If the zone has no list by that name, or you are not in the world, nothing changes and nothing is printed.
  arg <name> (string): The saved list's name.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting:LoadList[Trash]

ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting:Status
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting
  what: Prints the assist state to this character's console, the same as `ogre assist`: the Auto Assist, auto-target and direct targeting boxes, the decision and why, the assist anchor, each assist-list entry with their target, and your own target. Prints nothing when not in the world.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting:Status

ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting:Target[id]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting
  what: Queues a one-time retarget to the actor ID, issued on the next pulse even while OgreBot is paused; it beats auto-target and assist but yields to a target lock or a manual target. It is skipped when that is already your target or is you, and does nothing without an ID.
  arg id (int64): The actor ID to target.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting:Target[${Target.ID}]

ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting:Tick
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting
  what: Runs the assist and auto-target decision now and queues any retarget for the next pulse; it never targets during the call. The bot already does this on its own every 250 ms, and with auto-target on and entries to pick from each call can run a nearby-actor scan, so a script rarely needs it.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Targeting:Tick


== ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner ==

ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Clear[toon,task]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner
  what: Clears error and backoff records and saves them. Last-completed stamps are left alone.
  arg toon (string): Only this character. Optional: with none, every character.
  arg task (string): Only this task. Optional.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Clear[Bob,packpony]

ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Close
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner
  what: Closes the Lists window and leaves a run going. :End stops it too.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Close

ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:End
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner
  what: Stops a run and closes the Lists window, the same as `ogre end taskrunner` and the window's X.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:End

ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Lists
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner
  what: Prints the configured lists and their characters to the console.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Lists

ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Now
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner
  what: Scans for due work now rather than at the next interval. Only while the runner is idle.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Now

ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Open
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner
  what: Opens the TaskRunner Lists window, the same as bare `ogre taskrunner`.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Open

ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Plan[list]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner
  what: Prints what is due to the console.
  arg list (string): Only this list. Optional: with none, the list this session runs.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Plan[daily]

ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Reload
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner
  what: Reads the config again. Refused while a batch is in flight; if the list you are on is gone, the run stops.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Reload

ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Run[list,options]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner
  what: Starts this session on one list, the same as `ogre taskrunner run <list>` and `ogre taskrunner -list <list>`. An unknown option, or no list, prints one warning and nothing starts.
  arg list (string): The list's name, after an optional -list or -l; required.
  arg options (string): once or loop, stagger or nostagger, with or without a leading dash, one argument each. Optional.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Run[daily,once]

ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Start
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner
  what: Starts cycling all configured characters. Refused while a batch is in flight, when the config is off, with no characters, or when lists exist and none was named: use :Run then.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Start

ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Status
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner
  what: Prints what the runner is doing to the console.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Status

ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Stop
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner
  what: Stops a run and leaves the window up.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TaskRunner:Stop


== ISXOgreEQ2.Tour ==

ISXOgreEQ2.Tour:Close
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Tour
  what: Closes the New User Tour window, and its intro if that is still playing. The tour is not marked as seen, so it opens by itself again on the next load.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Tour:Close

ISXOgreEQ2.Tour:Done
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Tour
  what: Marks the New User Tour finished: prints 'tour: completed', saves it as seen so it no longer opens on load, and closes the window, then starts the Migration Assistant's automatic run, which copies any OldBot settings files that have no new copy yet and shows a progress window only when something is copied. A call when the tour is not open does nothing.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Tour:Done

ISXOgreEQ2.Tour:Open
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Tour
  what: Opens the New User Tour, the same as `ogre tour`: a short walkthrough of three window controls (drag to resize, right-click the title bar, Save Position), which also opens by itself on first load until it has been finished or skipped. It hides the InnerSpace console if that is showing and prints 'tour opened', and it does nothing while the tour is already up.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Tour:Open

ISXOgreEQ2.Tour:Skip
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Tour
  what: Skips the New User Tour: prints 'tour: skipped', saves it as seen so it no longer opens on load, closes the window and, like Tour:Done, starts the Migration Assistant's automatic run of any OldBot settings not yet copied. A call when the tour is not open does nothing.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Tour:Skip

ISXOgreEQ2.Tour:Step[step]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Tour
  what: Called by the tour window when it moves to a new step, and all it does is print 'tour: advanced to step N' to the console. Nothing is saved and the tour window does not change, so a script has no reason to call it.
  arg step (int, default: 0): the step number to print (the tour has steps 1 to 3); text that is not a number prints 0
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Tour:Step[2]


== ISXOgreEQ2.Travel ==

ISXOgreEQ2.Travel:End
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Travel
  what: Stops a list it is opening and reading and closes the window, the same as `ogre end travel` and the window's X. A pick already sent is the group's travel and goes on.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Travel:End

ISXOgreEQ2.Travel:Help
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Travel
  what: Prints the `ogre travel` usage to the console.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Travel:Help

ISXOgreEQ2.Travel:Open[method]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Travel
  what: Opens the Travel Helper window, and with a method also lists that map's destinations. An unknown method prints a warning and still opens the window.
  arg method (string): fast, spire, druid, bell or map. Optional: leave it out to only open the window.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Travel:Open[spire]


== ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh ==

${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMActive}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: TRUE while a travel route is running on this character. It reads FALSE while idle, after arriving or giving up, and while a Go is still waiting for a zone to finish loading.
  returns: bool: TRUE when a route is running; FALSE otherwise
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMActive}

${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMBias[kind]}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: The cost multiplier the planner uses for one kind of hop (door, bell, spire, druid, map, amenity or item): 1 is neutral, below 1 prefers it, above 1 avoids it, 0 or less forbids it. Every kind starts at 1.
  arg kind (string): the hop kind: door, bell, spire, druid, map, amenity or item
  returns: float: the multiplier for that kind; -1 when the kind is unknown or missing
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMBias[bell]}

${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMCurrentHop}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: A one-line description of the hop in progress: the kind (door, bell, spire, druid, map, amenity or item), the from and to zone short names, and the travel action and destination label when there is one. Empty when no hop is in progress, including after arrival.
  returns: string: the current hop's description; empty when there is none
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMCurrentHop}

${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMDataErrors}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: How many travel data files had a problem at the last load, counting files that were skipped and files that loaded with a warning. It reads 0 until the travel data has loaded.
  returns: int: the number of problem files; 0 when the data loaded cleanly
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMDataErrors}

${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMDataErrorText}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: The problem report from the last load, one line per file: its path, which layer it came from (default or custom) and the message. Empty when every file loaded cleanly, or until the travel data has loaded.
  returns: string: the problem report, one file per line; empty when clean
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMDataErrorText}

${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMEdges}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: How many zone-to-zone connections (doors, zone lines, guild hall amenities, travel items and so on) the loaded travel data holds. It reads 0 until the travel data has loaded.
  returns: int: the number of connections in the travel data
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMEdges}

${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMFeatures}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: One line per account feature the travel data can require (the expansion Friends and Family features), with this character's answer: YES or no, and whether it was scanned or set by you, or unanswered. A no from a scan is checked again after a week, a YES or your own answer is kept, and the lines are read by the travel engine about once a second while you are in the world.
  returns: string: one line per account feature
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMFeatures}

${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMGoal}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: The short zone name of the destination of the current or last route, such as antonica. Empty before any route has started.
  returns: string: the destination zone short name; empty before the first route
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMGoal}

${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMHop}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: The number of the hop the route is on, counting from 1. It reads 1 before any route has run and one more than TMHops once the route has arrived.
  returns: int: the current hop number, 1-based
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMHop}

${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMHops}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: How many hops the current plan has. After a re-plan this is the hop count of the new plan for the rest of the trip, not the original total.
  returns: int: the hop count of the current plan; 0 before any route
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMHops}

${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMParty}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: For the current or last route: the route id, how many group members it counted, and either "everyone is here" or the names of members not yet in this zone and settled. It is empty before any route has started, and read by the travel engine about once a second while you are in the world.
  returns: string: the group status line; empty before the first route
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMParty}

${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMReason}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: Why the last route stopped, or what its last step reported, such as "stopped by request" or "replaced by a new route". Empty while a route runs normally.
  returns: string: the stop reason or last step message; empty when there is none
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMReason}

${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMReplans}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: How many times the current route has re-planned around a hop that failed. A route gives up after 3 re-plans.
  returns: int: the re-plan count for the current or last route
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMReplans}

${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMRoute}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: The whole current plan as text, one numbered hop per line in the same form as TMCurrentHop. It still holds the last plan after the route ends.
  returns: string: the plan, one hop per line; empty before any route
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMRoute}

${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMStagger}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: The start delay in milliseconds per group member for group travel, so members do not all set off at once. The default is 10000, and 0 means everybody starts at once.
  returns: int: milliseconds of start delay per group member
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMStagger}

${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMState}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: The step the route is on: idle, hop-start, walk, wait-for-group, ride, act, verify, done or failed. It keeps done or failed after a route ends until the next route starts.
  returns: string: the current route step name
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMState}

${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMValidate}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: A health check of the loaded travel data, one issue per line. Empty when no issues are found, or until the travel data has loaded.
  returns: string: the issues, one per line; empty when there are none
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMValidate}

${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMZones}
  kind: member of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: How many zones the loaded travel data knows. It reads 0 until the travel data has loaded.
  returns: int: the number of zones in the travel data
  example: echo ${ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh.TMZones}

ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:Go[destination,poi]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: Starts a route like OgreBotAPI.Travel:Mesh, from your current zone to the destination, walking and using doors, zone lines, bells, spires, druid rings, the fast-travel map, guild hall amenities and travel items in your bags as needed; it replaces a running route, whoever started it, only when the new one can be planned. Problems (no destination, unknown destination with suggestions, current zone not in the travel data, no route) are echoed to the console, a Go made while zoning waits for the zone to settle, and the route moves with OgreBot closed too - TravelMesh:Stop ends it.
  arg destination (string): the zone to travel to - its display name, an alias or its short name, any case
  arg poi (string, default: none): optional point of interest in the destination zone to finish at; one the zone data does not list is reported and the trip still goes to the zone
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:Go[Antonica,"Druid Rings"]

ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:GoGroup[destination,poi]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: Like OgreBotAPI.Travel:MeshGroup: starts your own route as Go does, then sends -TravelMesh for the same destination to the rest of your group through OgreConsole, so each member plans its own route from where it stands, with starts staggered by TMStagger. If your own route cannot be planned the error is echoed and nothing is sent; the other members' copies run as OgreBot routes, so they are stopped with -TravelMeshStop.
  arg destination (string): the zone to travel to - its display name, an alias or its short name, any case
  arg poi (string, default: none): optional point of interest in the destination zone to finish at; one the zone data does not list is reported and the trip still goes to the zone
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:GoGroup[Antonica]

ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:Preview[destination]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: Plans a route from your current zone to the destination and prints it to the console without moving: a summary line with the hop count and rough time in seconds, then one numbered hop per line. An unknown destination prints an "unknown destination" line with suggestions, and no destination prints an error.
  arg destination (string): the zone to plan to - its display name, an alias or its short name, any case
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:Preview[Antonica]

ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:Reload
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: Re-reads the travel data from Ogre/EQ2/Travel/default and your own OgreSave/EQ2/Travel/custom files and echoes a summary of zones, connections, files and errors. Any running route is stopped first, whoever started it; if the first load has not finished within 5 seconds it says so and changes nothing.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:Reload

ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:ScanFeatures
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: Runs the game's show_account_features command to answer this character's unanswered or expired account features, and echoes a status line. Each feature is scanned at most once per session, a scan also starts by itself when a route is planned, and when nothing is scanned (out of the world included) the line says every feature is already answered.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:ScanFeatures

ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:SetBias[kind,multiplier]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: Sets how much the planner likes one kind of hop: 1 is neutral, below 1 prefers it, above 1 avoids it, 0 or less forbids it, and the new value is echoed. It applies to the next plan and is not saved; a multiplier that is not a number sets the normal bias of 1 and says so.
  arg kind (string): the hop kind: door, bell, spire, druid, map, amenity or item; anything else is refused with a console error
  arg multiplier (float): the cost multiplier: 1 neutral, below 1 prefer, above 1 avoid, 0 or less forbid; a word is 1
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:SetBias[druid,0.5]

ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:SetFeature[flag,value]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: Saves your own answer for one account feature for this character in OgreSave/EQ2/Travel/account-features.json; it is permanent and never scanned over, and the answer is echoed. A feature name the travel data does not use is refused with a line naming the ones it does, a blank value prints an error, and a word that is not yes or no leaves the feature as it is and says so.
  arg flag (string): the account feature name as TMFeatures shows it, such as roc_friends_and_family, in any case
  arg value (bool): TRUE, 1, yes or on means this character has the feature; FALSE, 0, no or off means it does not
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:SetFeature[roc_friends_and_family,TRUE]

ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:SetStagger[ms]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: Sets the start delay in milliseconds per group member for group travel (0 = everybody at once) and echoes it. A negative number is stored as 0, a value that is not a number counts as 0, and the setting is not saved.
  arg ms (int): milliseconds of start delay per group member; 0 starts everybody at once
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:SetStagger[5000]

ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:Stop[-force]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh
  what: Cancels a route started with this object's Go or GoGroup, including one still waiting for a zone to settle. A route someone else started is refused with one line naming the owner and how to stop it, and -force stops it anyway.
  arg -force (switch): stop the route whoever started it
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.TravelMesh:Stop


== ISXOgreEQ2.Watcher ==

ISXOgreEQ2.Watcher:End
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Watcher
  what: Turns off both the name watch (Find) and the shiny watch (TrackShiny), closes the Watcher window and prints which of them were on; the off state is saved, so they stay off on the next load. This is what `ogre end watcher` and the window's close button do.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Watcher:End

ISXOgreEQ2.Watcher:Find[word...]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Watcher
  what: Watches for actors by exact name, case not mattering (`ogre find`): given names it replaces the watch list, arms and checks the zone once, then each time a watched name spawns it prints where, broadcasts '<you>: APPEARED: <name>' to your bot sessions and sets an in-game waypoint on it, and it prints when one despawns (these alerts are skipped in a guild hall). A first word that is an option does that instead (-add or -remove <name>, -clear, -list, -on, -off, -scan, -status, -panel opens the Watcher window, -rorr adds the four Renewal of Ro researchers to the names), no words prints the usage, and the list and armed state are saved and restored on the next load.
  arg word... (string, default: none (prints the usage)): the names to watch (quote a name that has spaces), or one option first followed by its value
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Watcher:Find[${Target.Name}]

ISXOgreEQ2.Watcher:TrackShiny[word...]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.Watcher
  what: Watches for shiny harvest nodes of one colour within 100 units, every 500 ms by default (`ogre trackshiny`): when it finds one it did not just announce, it prints '<colour> shiny!', broadcasts it to your bot sessions and sets an in-game waypoint on it. No word arms it on Purple, a colour name (White, Green, Purple, Red, BlueShimmer, Blue) arms that colour and an unknown one is refused with the list, the options are -off, -status, -colours (or -colors), -interval <ms> (held to 250..30000) and -panel, and the settings are saved and restored on the next load.
  arg word... (string, default: Purple): a colour to watch for, or one option first followed by its value
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.Watcher:TrackShiny[Red]


== ISXOgreEQ2.WindowReactions ==

ISXOgreEQ2.WindowReactions:Status
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.WindowReactions
  what: Prints the window reaction counters to the console: loot, choice and quest-offer windows seen, acted on and deferred, then how each loot window is being read. It makes no game read.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.WindowReactions:Status


== ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset ==

ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Add[zone]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset
  what: Adds one zone to the reset queue and prints how many it holds.
  arg zone (string): The zone's name; several words are joined into one name; required.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Add["The Feerrott"]

ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:AddFilter[filter]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset
  what: Adds every zone the filter picks from the last read to the reset queue and prints how many.
  arg filter (string): resettable, noraid or notlocked. Optional: anything else reads as resettable.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:AddFilter[resettable]

ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Clear
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset
  what: Empties the reset queue.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Clear

ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Dump
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset
  what: Prints the zone table from the last read to the console.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Dump

ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:End
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset
  what: Stops what this tool asked for, drops what it had queued to run, and closes the window, the same as `ogre end zone` and the window's X. A reset that an Instance Controller run or a script asked for carries on.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:End

ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Flags[flags]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset
  what: The flag form, the same as `ogre zone -zone ...`; -all with -force is refused. -h prints the usage.
  arg flags (string): -zone names one zone and takes every word up to the next flag, -force force resets it and spends a charge, -all resets every resettable zone, -allowRaid includes raid zones, -fleet goes to the For Who selection; one argument each; required.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Flags[-zone,"The Feerrott"]

ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Force[zone]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset
  what: Force resets one zone, which SPENDS one of your limited reset charges and cannot be undone. With no zone it prints one warning and does nothing, and it is refused while a flow runs.
  arg zone (string): The zone's name; several words are joined into one name; required.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Force["The Feerrott"]

ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Help
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset
  what: Prints the `ogre zone` words and flags to the console.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Help

ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:List
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset
  what: Reads the Zone Reuse window again; it opens and closes. Refused while a flow runs.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:List

ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Open
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset
  what: Opens the Zone Resetter window, which reads the Zone Reuse window, the same as bare `ogre zone`.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Open

ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Queue
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset
  what: Prints the reset queue to the console.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Queue

ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Reset[word]
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset
  what: Resets the timer of every zone in the queue. Refused while a flow runs.
  arg word (string): fleet also sends it to the For Who window's selection. Optional.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Reset[fleet]

ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Status
  kind: method of ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset
  what: Prints the flow state, zone and queue counts and counters to the console.
  example: ISXOgreEQ2.ZoneReset:Status

== ogre commands ==

What a user types in the game's chat box (or a script runs): ogre <word> ...

ogre abilitydetails [name or id]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  what: Show every field your ability export holds for an ability, with a search
  arg <name or id> (text, default: the window opens with nothing picked): An ability's name or ID: a base name picks the rank the bot uses, a rank's full name or an ID picks exactly that rank, and the search box is filled in with it.
  example: ogre abilitydetails Kick

ogre account
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  what: Show this session's account and access level
  example: ogre account

ogre ae [-nogui] [-targets <n>] [-list]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  also: ogre abilityefficiency
  what: Your abilities' damage / (cast + recovery), at 1 to n targets: a window, or -nogui for the report file
  example: ogre ae

ogre afk [0|on|off]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  also: ogre antiafk
  what: Keep the session alive (bare = silent; 0 = noisy; off = stop)
  arg 0 (word, default: bare `ogre afk` turns it on silent): Turn the keepalive on in noisy mode: it prints a line each time it sends its /who all (every 10 to 15 minutes).
  arg on (word): Turn the keepalive on and keep the silent or noisy choice it already has.
  arg off (word): Stop the keepalive (the same as `ogre end afk`); invite accepting is not changed.
  arg invites (word, default: off at load): `invites on` or `invites off`: auto-accept group invites from names on your characters list; separate from the keepalive.
  example: ogre afk off

ogre analysis [scan|monitor|taps|export|import|end]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  also: ogre anal
  what: Watch actors, record what changes and when, and diff two of them
  arg scan (word, default: bare `ogre analysis` opens the window): Scan the zone's actors; add `<member>=<value>` terms (`<member><<value>` and `<member>><value>` too) to keep only matching ones, none reuses the window's terms or scans everything.
  arg monitor (word): `monitor on|off|clear|list`, or `monitor add <id|target|cursor>` / `monitor remove <id>`: pick the actors to watch and record their changes.
  arg taps (word): `taps on` or `taps off`: log the choice and reward windows that appear (any word but off turns them on).
  arg export (word): `export [<name>]`: save what was recorded to a file.
  arg import (word): `import <name|path>`: load a saved session back in.
  arg end (word): Stop sampling, the taps and any scan, then close the window (the same as `ogre end analysis`).
  arg panel (word): Open the window.
  arg close (word): Close the window only; recording goes on.
  arg status (word): Print what is monitored, the sample count, the scan and the taps.
  arg rate (word): `rate <ms>`: how often monitored actors are sampled, 100 to 10000 ms.
  arg sessions (word): List the saved sessions you can import.
  example: ogre analysis monitor add target

ogre assist
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  what: Show who this toon is assisting right now, and why
  example: ogre assist

ogre atb
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  also: ogre autotargetbalance
  what: Open OgreBot at the AutoTarget tab (Balance generator)
  example: ogre atb

ogre autologin
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  what: Open the auto-login config panel
  example: ogre autologin

ogre bgrender [on|off|draw <ms>|hz <n>|force on|off|hold <name>|release <name>|clear]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  what: Skip drawing while this client is in the background (once a second; full drawing when active)
  arg on (word, default: off at load; bare `ogre bgrender` prints the status): Turn background render skipping on.
  arg off (word): Turn it off - full drawing again (the same as `ogre end bgrender`).
  arg draw (word): Set how often a background client still draws a frame, the `<ms>` after it.
  arg <ms> (number, default: 1000): The background draw interval in milliseconds; 0 means never draw in the background.
  arg hz (word): Set the background loop cap, the `<n>` after it.
  arg <n> (number, default: 100): Loops per second while in the background; 0 means no cap.
  arg hold (word): `hold <name>`: keep every frame drawn until that name is released (for scripts that need the screen drawn).
  arg release (word): `release <name>`: drop that hold.
  arg clear (word): Drop every hold.
  example: ogre bgrender on

ogre bot [<toon>] [-s <server>] [-c <class>]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  what: Load OgreBot (logs <toon> in first if given, on that server and as that class if given)
  arg <toon> (name, default: OgreBot loads on the character you are on now): Log this character in first, then load OgreBot.
  arg -s (flag): Log in on the server named next (`-server` works too); needed when the character is on more than one server and none is the default.
  arg <server> (name, default: the character's default server): The server for `-s`; `ogre login -?` lists the short forms.
  arg -c (flag): Log in as the class named next (`-class` works too).
  arg <class> (name, default: whatever class it was): The class for `-c`.
  example: ogre bot Mytoon

ogre buycrate [-r|-h|-all]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  what: Buy this zone's heroic/raid crates (-r raid, -h heroic, -all)
  arg -r (flag, default: with no flag both crates are bought): Buy only the raid crate (`-raid` works too).
  arg -h (flag): Buy only the heroic crate (`-heroic` works too).
  arg -all (flag, default: on): Buy both the heroic and the raid crate.
  example: ogre buycrate -r

ogre buyfuel [amount]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  what: Buy the EXAMINED fuel up to <amount> in the guild fuel depot
  arg <amount> (number, default: 90000): Buy the examined fuel until the guild Fuel Depot holds this many.
  example: ogre buyfuel 50000

ogre buyoverseermissions [flags] | stop | status
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  also: ogre bom
  what: Buy Overseer missions from the Administrator agent
  arg -season (flag, default: bare = the options on this character's Overseer Buy tab): `-season <n>`: only missions of season 1 to 7 (`-s` works too).
  arg -colour (flag, default: any colour): `-colour <name>`: only Blue, Yellow, Purple or Green missions (`-c` / `-color` work too).
  arg -num (flag, default: 10): `-num <n>`: how many different missions to buy (`-n` works too).
  arg -amount (flag, default: 10): `-amount <n>`: how many of each to buy, at most 20 (`-a` works too).
  arg -replenishonly (flag, default: off): Only top up missions you already have (`-r` / `-ro` work too).
  arg -noscribe (flag, default: scribe is on): Do not scribe the bought missions (`-scribe` turns it back on).
  arg -destroy (flag, default: off): Destroy the copies left over after scribing (`-nodestroy` turns it off).
  arg -gettogh (flag, default: off): Go to the guild hall when the run finishes (`-gh`; `-nogettogh` / `-nogh` turn it off).
  arg stop (word): Stop a running buy (`abort` works too).
  arg status (word): Print how the buy run is going.
  example: ogre buyoverseermissions -num 5 -amount 2

ogre camp [charselect]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  what: Camp out to login+exit ('charselect' stays at char select)
  arg charselect (word, default: camps to the login screen, then exits the game): Camp to character select and stay there (`cs` / `select` work too).
  example: ogre camp charselect

ogre chatcmd [off|status|debug [on|off]|reloadauth|test <chattype> <speaker> [message]]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  what: Run the commands your own characters send you in chat
  arg off (word, default: bare `ogre chatcmd` turns it on): Stop running commands sent to you in chat (the same as `ogre end chatcmd`).
  arg status (word): Print whether it is on, how many names it trusts, and how many lines it ran or rejected.
  arg reloadauth (word): Re-read the names of your own characters whose chat lines it will obey.
  example: ogre chatcmd status

ogre cm [-small|-large]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  also: ogre collection, ogre collections
  what: Add collectibles from your collectible depot to your collections
  arg -small (flag, default: the nearest Collectible Depot, else your Personal Collectible Stash): Use the Collectible Depot (the small one) only.
  arg -large (flag): Use the Collectible Depot (Large) only.
  arg -inventory (flag, default: off): Add the collectibles in your bags instead of a depot (`1` / `-1` work too).
  example: ogre cm -large

ogre codexinspect <Name[,Name...]|reset>
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  what: Inspect group/raid members and upload their gear to eq2codex.com
  arg <Name[,Name...]> (text, default: bare prints the status and the usage): Inspect these group or raid members (names split by commas) and upload their gear to eq2codex.com.
  arg reset (word): Reset your active raid on eq2codex.com.
  arg status (word): Print how the upload pass is going (`?` works too).
  example: ogre codexinspect Alpha,Bravo

ogre codextoon [status]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  what: Upload your own gear/stat snapshot to eq2codex.com
  arg status (word, default: bare uploads your own gear and stats now): Print the upload status instead of uploading (`?` works too).
  example: ogre codextoon
