ogre craft [status|start|writs|tinker|lll|stop|end|minimize|scan|add|set|shop|?]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  also: ogre craft2
  what: Open the crafting panel
  arg status (word, default: bare `ogre craft` opens the panel and turns on craft reactions): Print what crafting is doing, how many are crafted and the last error.
  arg start (word): Craft what is in the queue.
  arg writs (word): Run the writ flow.
  arg tinker (word): Run auto tinkering.
  arg lll (word): Run low level leveling.
  arg stop (word): Stop the run; the panel stays open.
  arg end (word): Stop everything and close the window (the same as `ogre end craft`).
  arg minimize (word): Roll the window up to its title bar; crafting goes on, bare `ogre craft` brings it back.
  arg scan (word): Re-read your recipe book.
  arg add (word): `add <recipe name|id|lastknownrecipe> [<quantity>]`: put a recipe in the queue; a trailing whole number is the quantity (default 1), lastknownrecipe is the last one you scribed.
  arg set (word): `set <key> <value>`: change one craft setting (saved a second later).
  arg shop (word): `shop books`, `shop sell <name>...` or `shop destroy <name>...`: run one merchant errand by hand (not while a craft runs).
  arg ? (word): Print the word list (`help` works too).
  arg pause (word): `pause` or `pause on` pauses the run; `pause off` resumes it.
  arg clear (word): Empty the queue.
  arg queue (word): List what is in the queue.
  arg quest (word): Craft the recipe steps of your current quest until none is left.
  arg save (word): Save the craft settings now.
  arg reload (word): Re-read the craft settings and the data files.
  example: ogre craft writs

ogre craftgm [<range>] | scan [<range>] | start [<range>] | queue [<range>] | status | stop | end | close  [depot|nodepot]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  what: Open the Grandmaster crafting panel ((Master) scrolls -> (Grandmaster) crafts)
  arg <range> (text, default: bare opens the panel and does nothing else): A level (`131`), a range (`131-135` or `131 135`), or `all`; on its own it opens the panel with the range filled in and scans nothing.
  arg scan (word): `scan [<range>]`: open the panel and find the (Master) scrolls to craft, crafting nothing.
  arg start (word): `start [<range>]`: open the panel and scan, queue and craft the (Grandmaster) recipes.
  arg queue (word): `queue [<range>]`: scan and replace the Craft queue with the (Grandmaster) recipes, then stop; never uses the Scroll Depot.
  arg status (word): Print the state; does not touch the panel.
  arg stop (word): Stop a run; the panel stays as it is.
  arg end (word): Stop a run and close the panel (the same as `ogre end craftgm`).
  arg close (word): The same as end.
  arg depot (word, default: as last set (off to start)): Also pull scrolls from the Scroll Depot; sticks, and works with any word that takes a range.
  arg nodepot (word): Use your bags only (`bagsonly` works too); sticks.
  example: ogre craftgm start 131-135 depot

ogre craftingmats [-<expansion> -<category> ...] | ogre craftingmats plan|help|end
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  also: ogre cmats
  what: Edit the crafting-mats lists; with flags, pull a craft's mats from the harvest depot
  arg -<expansion> (flag, default: with only a category, Visions of Vetrovia): Which list to pull from: -vov, -cd, -mm, -pop or -ka (any list file's key); several may be given.
  arg -<category> (flag, default: the list's own line (signature; for -ka daily and weekly)): -sig (or -s), -daily (or -d) or -weekly (or -w).
  arg plan (word): `plan [-<expansion> -<category> ...]`: print the shopping list and stop, without the depot (`preview` and `-plan` work too).
  arg help (word): Print the usage (`?` works too).
  arg end (word): Stop a pull and close the editor (the same as `ogre end craftingmats`).
  arg panel (word, default: bare `ogre craftingmats` opens the editor): Open the list editor (`config` / `edit` work too).
  example: ogre craftingmats -vov -sig

ogre effecttracker [on|off|npc on|merge|status|end]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  also: ogre oet
  what: Capture what every detrimental and NPC effect says it does, into the shared zone dataset
  arg on (word, default: bare opens the window): Start capturing your detrimental effects.
  arg off (word): Stop both captures (players and NPCs); the window stays open.
  arg npc (word): `npc on` or `npc off`: also capture NPC effects.
  arg merge (word): Merge every character's captures for the zone you are in into the zone's one dataset file.
  arg status (word): Print what is armed and how much was captured.
  arg end (word): Stop both captures and close the window (the same as `ogre end effecttracker`).
  arg panel (word): Open the window.
  arg close (word): Close the window only.
  arg reload (word): Re-read the capture files from disk; anything not yet saved is dropped.
  arg describe (word, default: on): `describe on` or `describe off`: read each new effect's info once from the server (off loses only the Description).
  arg closewindow (word): `closewindow [all]`: close one leftover examine window, or all of them.
  example: ogre effecttracker on

ogre encounter [reload|debug comms|steps on|off|sequences]

  arg reload (word, default: bare prints the word list): Re-read the encounter json from disk and swap it in; a line follows with the loaded, scanned and error counts.
  arg debug (word): `debug comms on|off` or `debug steps on|off`: console echo for comms or step changes; `debug` alone prints the current switches.
  arg sequences (word): List every live sequence: its step, how long it has been there and what holds it (`seq` works too).
  example: ogre encounter reload

ogre er [on | off | end | status | start | stop | mark <text> | pets | npceffects | everydet | trash | onforwho | offforwho | pages [zone] [rebuild] | upload [on|off|now] | raid <slug> | raids]

ogre examine [on|off|reset]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  what: Examine each NEW detrimental signature once and report it
  arg on (word, default: bare turns it on): Examine each new detrimental once and report its Name and Description (`start` works too).
  arg off (word): Stop examining (`stop` works too; the same as `ogre end examine`).
  arg reset (word): Forget the ones already seen, so each is examined again (`clear` works too).

ogre experiment [-<stat> <n>]... | items | run <row> ...
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  also: ogre experimentui
  what: Boost item stats on the tradeskill Experiment tab
  arg -<stat> (flag, default: bare prints the status and the usage): A stat to boost on the item already selected on the Experiment tab: -potency (or -p), -critbonus (or -cb), or any other option's label.
  arg <n> (number): How many times to boost the stat before it; a count of 0 or less adds nothing.
  arg items (word): List the item rows on the Experiment tab.
  arg run (word): `run <row> -<stat> <n> ...`: the same boost on item row `<row>` from `items`.
  arg stop (word): Stop and put the window size back (`off` works too; the same as `ogre end experiment`).
  arg status (word): Print the state and the usage.
  example: ogre experiment -potency 3

ogre ghtohouse [flags]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  what: Move the guild-hall depots into your house ones (-all, -scroll, ...)
  arg -all (flag, default: no depot = refused): Move all eight shared depots (harvest, ammo, adorn, food, lore, potion, collectible, fuel); not scroll.

  arg -ammo (flag): Move the ammo depot.
  arg -adorn (flag): Move the adornment depot.
  arg -food (flag): Move the food and drink depot.
  arg -lore (flag): Move the lore and legend depot.

ogre hl [off|status|interval <ms>]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  also: ogre harvestlite
  what: Collect resource nodes already in reach (no walking)
  arg off (word, default: bare turns it on): Stop collecting (the same as `ogre end hl`).
  arg status (word): Print whether it is on and what it has done.
  arg interval (word): Set how often it looks for nodes in reach, the `<ms>` after it.
  arg <ms> (number, default: 500): The pass interval in milliseconds, 250 to 10000.
  example: ogre hl interval 1000

ogre housetogh [flags]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  what: Move your house depots into the guild-hall ones (-all, -harvest, ...)
  arg -all (flag, default: no depot = refused): Move all eight depots (harvest, ammo, adorn, food, lore, potion, collectible, fuel).
  arg -harvest (flag): Move the harvest depot (`-h` works too).
  arg -ammo (flag): Move the ammo depot.
  arg -adorn (flag): Move the adornment depot.
  arg -food (flag): Move the food and drink depot.
  arg -lore (flag): Move the lore and legend depot.
  arg -potion (flag): Move the poison, potion and totem depot.
  arg -collectible (flag): Move the collectible depot (`-collect` / `-c` work too).
  arg -fuel (flag): Move the fuel depot.
  arg -no<depot> (flag): Turn one depot back off, e.g. `-nofuel` after `-all` (also `-nh`, `-nc`).
  arg <owner> (name, default: your own house): Whose house to take from.
  example: ogre housetogh -all -nofuel

ogre ic [status|list|run|check|pause|end|options] | ogre ic -<option>[=off] ...
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  also: ogre icx, ogre instancecontroller
  what: Open the instance controller - run zones from a queue (doc 28)
  arg status (word, default: bare opens the window): Print the run's state as text.
  arg list (word): `list [<filter>]`: every loaded zone file, or those whose zone or path holds the filter.
  arg run (word): `run <tier> <relative/path.json>`: run that one zone file (not the list); tier is default, test or custom.
  arg check (word): `check [<zone>]`: which files claim the zone (no zone = the one you are in) and whether it is available.
  arg pause (word): Pause the run.
  arg end (word): Close the instance controller out (the same as `ogre end ic` and the window's X).
  arg options (word): `options` lists every option; `options -<option>[=on|off] ...` sets them.
  arg -<option> (flag, default: a bare -option means on): Set any option of the window, e.g. `-loop`, `-haltAtEnd=off`, `-maxwait=30`; several at once.
  arg resume (word): Resume a paused run.
  arg stop (word): End the run (the window's End button).
  arg runlist (word): `runlist [<row>]`: run the queue from the top, or from row `<row>`.
  arg queue (word): `queue` lists it; `queue add <zone name>`, `queue add <tier> <path.json>`, `queue startat <row> <N>` (start that row at step N) or `queue clear`.
  arg wipe (word): Declare a wipe now and start recovering.
  arg reload (word): Re-read the zone files (the window's Reload).
  arg refresh (word): Refresh the zone lock table.
  arg panel (word): Open the window.
  example: ogre ic -loop -haltAtEnd=off

ogre im [-depot -sell -destroy -tse -end] | depot|sell|destroy|tse|restock|trade <args> | chain | status | stop | close
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  also: ogre inventorymanager
  what: Inventory manager - the window is the session; runs depot/sell/destroy/tse/restock/trade
  arg -depot (flag, default: bare opens the window): In a chain: deposit to depots. Chain flags run in order: -depot, -sell, -destroy, -tse, -restock, -trade.
  arg -sell (flag): In a chain: sell to the merchant.
  arg -destroy (flag): In a chain: destroy the listed items.
  arg -tse (flag): In a chain: consume items for tradeskill experience.
  arg -end (flag): Close the window once the chain is done.
  arg depot (word): `depot <depot flags>`: deposit into house or guild-hall depots; `ogre im help` lists the flags.
  arg sell (word): Sell; `sell preview|list|add|remove|status|stop|reload` too.
  arg destroy (word): Destroy the list, or `destroy <name>` for one item; `destroy preview|list|add|remove|status|stop` too.
  arg tse (word): Consume items for tradeskill experience; `tse -stopafter <n>` stops after that many.
  arg restock (word): `restock [<profile>]` buys up to a profile; `restock list|show <profile>|preview|stop` too.
  arg trade (word): Run the trade queue; `trade add <player> <qty|all> <item>`, `trade list|remove <n>|clear|preview`.
  arg chain (word): Show what each chain flag does.
  arg status (word): Print what the window and each mode is doing.
  arg stop (word): Stop whatever mode or chain is running.
  arg close (word): Close the window only.
  arg end (word): Stop and close the window (the same as `ogre end im`).
  arg queue (word): `queue <mode>`: run that mode when the current one finishes; `queue` alone shows what waits.
  arg console (word): `console [always|running|never|clear]`: the activity log strip.
  arg settings (word): Print the saved options; `settings bag ...` and `settings tse <option> <value>` change them.
  arg transmute (word): `transmute <name>`: transmute that item.
  arg reload (word): Re-read the data files.
  arg help (word): Print the full usage (`?` works too).
  example: ogre im -depot -sell -end

ogre lag [report [s]|dump [s]|on|off|overhead|budget <ms> <ms>|minutes <1-60>|clear|close]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  what: Every frame of the last few minutes - what it cost and what ran in it; find and open the FPS dips
  arg report (word, default: bare opens the window): Print a report of the last `<s>` seconds: the FPS dips and what caused them.
  arg <s> (number, default: 60 for report; everything recorded for dump): How many seconds back report or dump looks.
  arg dump (word): Save the last `<s>` seconds of frames to a file (the save itself costs one frame).
  arg on (word, default: on): Record every frame (saved).
  arg off (word): Stop recording; frames already recorded are kept.
  arg overhead (word): Measure and print what the recorder itself costs.
  arg budget (word, default: 25 and 33.3 ms): `budget <ms> <ms>`: the two frame budgets the report counts against; the second must be above the first.
  arg minutes (word, default: 5): `minutes <1-60>`: how many minutes of frames are kept; it starts again empty.
  arg clear (word): Throw away the recorded frames.
  arg close (word): Close the window (the same as `ogre end lag`).
  example: ogre lag report 30

ogre leveltransmuting [on|off|status|end]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  also: ogre lt
  what: Buy transmuter's stones from Barnaby, then transmute them, for transmuting skill-ups
  arg on (word, default: bare opens the panel): Start: buy transmuter's stones from Barnaby (travelling there if needed), transmute them, and repeat.
  arg <count> (number, default: 60): For `on`: stones to hold per merchant visit, 1 to 800.
  arg <rounds> (number, default: 20): For `on`: stop after this many rounds, 1 to 500; there is no unlimited mode.
  arg off (word): Stop the run.
  arg status (word): Print the run's phase and round count.
  arg end (word): Stop and close the panel (the same as `ogre end leveltransmuting`).
  arg panel (word): Open the panel (`gui` / `ui` work too).
  example: ogre leveltransmuting on 60 20

ogre login <toon> [-s <server>] [-c <class>]

  what: Log a character in (does not load OgreBot). 'ogre login -?' lists the server short forms
  arg <toon> (name): The character to log in; nothing happens without it.
  arg -s (flag, default: the character's default row): Log in on this server, a full name or a short form such as `ab`; it matters only for a name on more than one server.
  arg -c (flag, default: logs in whatever class it was): Log in as this class; a character already in the world as another class camps and comes back as it.
  arg -? (flag): List the server short forms instead of logging in.

ogre nav -loc \"x,y,z\" [flags]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  also: ogre navigate
  what: Walk somewhere over the baked navmesh (`ogre nav -help` for the flags)
  arg -loc (flag): Walk to these coordinates: x,y,z as one quoted word or three words (Y is up).
  arg -precision (flag): Stop within this many units of the spot; it stays set for the session.
  arg -fly (flag, default: auto: flies only on a long detour): Fly this trip.
  arg -nofly (flag, default: auto: flies only on a long detour): Never fly this trip.
  arg -nodoors (flag, default: doors are opened): Do not open doors on the way.
  arg -doors (flag): Open doors on the way again.
  arg -on (flag): Let nav move this character.
  arg -off (flag): Stop nav from moving this character at all.
  arg -set (flag): Change one nav setting: `-set <key> <value>` (arrive, lookmax, avoid, doortries and more). `-set` alone lists the keys.
  arg -reset (flag): Put every nav setting back to its default, or only `<key>` when you name one.
  arg -panel (flag): Open the nav window now and on every trip.
  arg -nopanel (flag): Close the nav window and stop it opening on each trip.
  arg stop (word): Stop the trip; the nav window stays open.
  arg end (word): Stop the trip and close the nav window (the same as `ogre end nav`).
  arg status (word): Say what nav is doing, which mesh is loaded and any setting you changed.
  arg panel (word): Open the nav window.
  arg help (word, default: this is what no word does): Show the flags.
  example: ogre nav -loc "100,20,-300" -precision 3

ogre npccast [monitor [target|named|all|off|copy]|status|zone|capture|reload|import|end]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  also: ogre npccastmonitoring
  what: Log what mobs cast (spell name + ability id) to copy or send; watch named mobs' casts - interrupt them or run your own commands
  arg monitor (word): Start the cast monitor: each cast is logged with mob, spell name, ability id and cast time, ready to copy.
  arg target (word, default: the monitor's default): After `monitor`: watch your target and its target (these casts come with the spell name).
  arg named (word): After `monitor`: also watch every named mob nearby.
  arg all (word): After `monitor`: also watch every NPC nearby.
  arg off (word): After `monitor`: stop the monitor (it saves its list).
  arg copy (word): After `monitor`: put the logged casts on the clipboard.
  arg watch (word): Add a mob to the watch list: `watch <mob name>`, every word after it is the name.
  arg unwatch (word): Take a mob off the watch list: `unwatch <mob name>`.
  arg clear (word): Clear the watches you added; the zone's and the fights' own stay.
  arg radius (word): Set the scan radius for this zone: `radius <n>`.
  arg status (word): Show the scan counters, the watch list and what is being cast now.
  arg zone (word): Show the cast data loaded for this zone.
  arg capture (word): Add the spell your target is casting right now to your own copy of this zone's file.
  arg reload (word): Re-read this zone's cast files.
  arg import (word): Copy the shipped OgreBot Classic custom cast files into your own folder, never over a file you already have.
  arg end (word): Stop the monitor and close the window (the same as `ogre end npccast`); the watch list keeps running.
  example: ogre npccast monitor named

ogre pulse [report|on|off|reset|ceiling <us>|slice <section> <us>|jobtest on|off]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  also: ogre pulsebudget
  what: Tune the per-frame time slice each resumable section gets
  arg report (word): Print the budget report: every resumable section, its number and its slice.
  arg on (word): Turn the shared frame ceiling on and reset the counters.
  arg off (word): Turn the shared frame ceiling off; each section keeps its own slice.
  arg reset (word): Reset the counters.

  arg close (word): Close the Pulse Budget window; the budget keeps running.

  example: ogre replenishnames reload

ogre safefall [on|off|panel|end]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  also: ogre levelsafefall
  what: Level Safe Fall: fly up, drop, remount, repeat
  arg status (word, default: this is what no word does): Show the trainer's state and the usage.
  arg on (word): Start: mount, climb, dismount, fall, repeat.
  arg <ticks> (number, default: 30): After `on`: the flight time in tenths of a second (5-600); it grows by 5 every 100 rounds.
  arg off (word): Stop the trainer.

  arg end (word): Stop and close the window (the same as `ogre end safefall`).
  arg help (word): Show the usage.

ogre taskrunner [-list <list>|run <list>|start|stop|end|status|panel|lists]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  also: ogre tr, ogre packpony, ogre pony
  what: Cycle characters through their scheduled chores
  arg -list (flag): Start this session on a list: `-list <list>` (the classic spelling of `run`).
  arg run (word): Start this session on a list: `run <list>`.
  arg <list> (name): After `-list`, `run` or `plan`: the list's name.
  arg once (word, default: the list's own setting): After the list: go through it once.
  arg loop (word, default: the list's own setting): After the list: keep going round it.
  arg stagger (word, default: the stagger setting): After the list: turn stagger on for this run.
  arg nostagger (word, default: the stagger setting): After the list: turn stagger off for this run.
  arg start (word): Cycle every configured character; only when no lists are set up.
  arg stop (word): Stop the run; the window stays open.
  arg end (word): Stop the run and close the window (the same as `ogre end taskrunner`).
  arg status (word): Print the run's state.
  arg close (word): Close the Lists window.
  arg lists (word): Show the lists and their characters.
  arg reload (word): Re-read the task files (refused while a character is mid-batch).
  arg plan (word, default: this session's list): Show what is due, character by character; nothing runs.
  arg now (word): Check what is due right away instead of waiting.
  arg clear (word, default: every character): Clear error and back-off records: all, one `<toon>`, or one `<task>` of that character.
  arg <toon> (name): After `clear`: the character.
  arg <task> (name): After `clear <toon>`: the task.
  example: ogre taskrunner run mylist loop

ogre zone [force <name>|end]
  kind: ogre command (typed in the game's chat box or a script)
  also: ogre reset, ogre zonereset
  what: Open the zone-reuse resetter (OldBot's `zone` / `reset`)
  arg list (word): Refresh and print the zone table (the Zone Reuse window opens and closes).
  arg force (word): Force-reset one zone, `force <zone name>`; this spends one of your reset charges.
  arg add (word): Add one zone to the reset queue: `add <zone name>`.
  arg addfilter (word): Add many zones to the queue at once: `resettable` (the default), `noraid` or `notlocked`.
  arg queue (word): Show the reset queue.
  arg clear (word): Empty the reset queue.
  arg reset (word): Reset the timers of every zone in the queue.
  arg fleet (word): After `reset`: do it for the characters picked in the For Who window too.
  arg status (word): Show the counters and what it is doing.
  arg end (word): Stop what it was asked to do and close the window (the same as `ogre end zone`).
  arg help (word): Show the usage.

  arg -force (flag): With `-zone`: force-reset it, which spends a charge.
  arg -all (flag): Reset every resettable zone; raid zones are skipped.
  arg -allowraid (flag): With `-all`: include raid zones.
  arg -fleet (flag): Do it for the characters picked in the For Who window too.
  example: ogre zone add Kralet Penumbra: The Hive Mind


== ISXOgreX console commands ==

Sent as `oc !c <command> <who> ...` to the sessions on this PC, this one included; the for-who in <who> picks which act. `oc !ci` does the same without showing the line.

oc !c -auth <nick>
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  what: IRC only: authorizes an IRC nick to send this hub commands.
  arg nick (string): The IRC nick to authorize
  example: irc !c -auth SomeNick

oc !c -authlist
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  what: IRC only: says which IRC nicks are authorized.
  example: irc !c -authlist

oc !c -KillSession <target>
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  what: IRC only, authorized senders only: ends one InnerSpace session on this PC, or all of them.
  arg target (string): The session name (is1, is2, ...) or all
  example: irc !c -KillSession is3

oc !c -LaunchAutoLogin <profile>
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  what: From IRC, authorised senders only: runs an auto-login profile.
  arg profile (one): The auto-login profile to run.
  example: irc !c -LaunchAutoLogin MyProfile

oc !c -List_AutoLoginProfiles
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  what: From IRC, authorised senders only: lists the auto-login profiles. -details adds each row, -profile <name> shows one.
  example: irc !c -List_AutoLoginProfiles

oc !c -List_Sessions
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  what: IRC only, authorized senders only: lists this PC's InnerSpace sessions.
  example: irc !c -List_Sessions

oc !c -LoadCharacter <toon>
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  what: From IRC, authorised senders only: logs one toon in, using the first auto-login profile that holds it.
  arg toon (one): The toon, or toon:isN to name the session.
  example: irc !c -LoadCharacter MyToon

oc !c -unauth <nick>
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  what: IRC only: removes an IRC nick from the authorized list.
  arg nick (string): The IRC nick to remove
  example: irc !c -unauth SomeNick

oc !c -unauthall
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  what: IRC only: clears the authorized list.
  example: irc !c -unauthall


== ISXOgreEQ2 console commands (-AbilityEmbargo to -LoadProfile) ==

Sent as `oc !c <command> <who> ...` to the sessions on this PC, this one included; the for-who in <who> picks which act. `oc !ci` does the same without showing the line.

oc !c -AbilityEmbargo <who> <abilityid> <duration> <args>
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  also: -AbilityRotate
  what: Embargo an ability (its name or id) for N seconds on the toons the for-who names (an ability rotation: the caster tells the others not to cast it).
  arg who (forwho, default: auto): Who embargoes - leave blank to use the For Who window; `all` = every session that hears it.
  arg abilityid (string)
  arg duration (string)
  arg args (rest)
  runs: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:AddEmbargo
  example: oc !c -AbilityEmbargo all 1234567890 15

oc !c -AbilityEmbargo_ResetAbilityEmbargo <who> <value>
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  what: Clears the embargo on one ability, given by name or id, on the matching characters. A name that cannot be found (including the default Unknown) does nothing.
  arg who (forwho, default: auto): Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window.
  arg value (string, default: Unknown)
  runs: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:ClearEmbargo
  example: oc !c -AbilityEmbargo_ResetAbilityEmbargo all 1234567890

oc !c -AbilityEmbargo_ResetAllAbilityEmbargos <who>
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  what: Clears every ability embargo on the matching characters, so their cast stacks may cast those abilities again. Item embargos are not touched.
  arg who (forwho, default: auto): Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window.
  runs: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:ClearAllEmbargos
  example: oc !c -AbilityEmbargo_ResetAllAbilityEmbargos all

oc !c -AbilityTag_ResetAbilityTagAllow <who> <value>
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  what: Clears one held allow tag, by name, on the matching characters. A blank tag does nothing.
  arg who (forwho, default: auto): Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window.
  arg value (string, default: Unknown)
  runs: OgreBotAPI.CastStack:ClearAllow
  example: oc !c -AbilityTag_ResetAbilityTagAllow all Stifle

oc !c -AbilityTag_ResetAbilityTagEmbargo <who> <value>
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  also: -AbilityEmbargo_ResetAbilityTagEmbargo
  what: Clears one held embargo tag, by name, on the matching characters. A blank tag does nothing.
  arg who (forwho, default: auto): Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window.
  arg value (string, default: Unknown)
  runs: OgreBotAPI.CastStack:ClearEmbargo
  example: oc !c -AbilityTag_ResetAbilityTagEmbargo all Stifle

oc !c -AbilityTag_ResetAllAbilityTagAllows <who>

  arg who (forwho, default: auto): Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window.
  runs: OgreBotAPI.CastStack:ClearAllAllows
  example: oc !c -AbilityTag_ResetAllAbilityTagAllows all

oc !c -AbilityTag_ResetAllAbilityTagEmbargos <who>
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  what: Clears every held embargo tag on the matching characters, so entries those tags were blocking may cast again.
  arg who (forwho, default: auto): Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window.
  runs: OgreBotAPI.CastStack:ClearAllEmbargos
  example: oc !c -AbilityTag_ResetAllAbilityTagEmbargos all

oc !c -AbilityTagEmbargo <who> <tagname> <duration> <type> <args>
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  also: -AbilityTagRotate, -AbilityTag
  what: Holds a cast stack tag on the matching characters for duration seconds: type Embargo (the default) stops entries carrying that embargo tag from casting, and type Allow lets entries that need that allow tag cast. It only takes effect while the Settings tab's Enable Tag Embargo or Enable Tag Allow box is ticked; -m <buff> in the extra arguments ties the tag to a maintained buff, and a missing or 0 duration ends it at once.
  arg who (forwho, default: auto): Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window.
  arg tagname (string)
  arg duration (string)
  arg type (string, default: Embargo)
  arg args (rest)
  runs: OgreBotAPI.CastStack:HoldTag
  example: oc !c -AbilityTagEmbargo all Stifle 20 Embargo

oc !c -AbilityTracker_Add <who> <abilityname>
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  what: Adds the named ability to the Ability Tracker watch list (an id is stored as the ability's name) and echoes the result. The name is not checked against the export, one already on the list is not added again, and the change is lost unless you save the profile.
  arg who (forwho, default: auto): Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window.
  arg abilityname (string)
  runs: OgreBotAPI.Abilities:TrackerAdd
  example: oc !c -AbilityTracker_Add ${Me.Name} "Bulwark of Order"

  what: Uses your Champion's Zone Lockout Reset item to reset the lockout of the named zone, picking it from the item's select window, and skips when the reset is on cooldown. Runs in the action queue, and prints a console line and stops when the item is not in your bags.
  arg who (forwho, default: auto): Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window.
  arg zonename (string, default: DoesNotExist)
  runs: OgreBotAPI.Zone:ChampionsResetter
  example: oc !c -Champions_Zone_Resetter ${Me.Name} "${Zone.Name}"

oc !c -ChangeBeltAdorn <who> <value> <unequip>
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  what: Changes your belt adorn. Valid options are stun stifle mez fear medic.
  arg who (forwho, default: auto): Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window.
  arg value (string, default: ?): Which adornment to put on the belt: Stun, Stifle, Mez, Fear or Medic.
  arg unequip (string, default: TRUE): Unequip belt
  runs: OgreBotAPI.Inventory:ChangeBeltAdorn
  example: oc !c -ChangeBeltAdorn igw:${Me.Name} Stun TRUE

== ISXOgreEQ2 console commands (-LogToonIn to -ZoneResetAll) ==

oc !c -LogToonIn <who> <name> <server> <class>
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  what: Logs a character in on one box: from the login screen, from character select, or from the world on another character (it camps first). Name the box by its InnerSpace session or its character, and at character select or the login screen by the character it last played: oc !c -LogToonIn MyToon MyToon logs MyToon back in after a zone dropped it to character select.
  arg who (string): The box: its InnerSpace session name or its character's name (at character select, the character it last played). all and groups pick no box.
  arg name (string): The character to log in. It needs a saved login on this PC.
  arg server (string): The server, for a character saved on more than one. Blank uses its default. A short form works: ior, md.
  arg class (string): The class to log in as, like ranger. Blank logs in whatever class it was.
  runs: OgreBotAPI.Session:LogToonIn
  example: oc !c -LogToonIn ${Me.Name} ${Group[1].Name}

oc !c -Move2Area <who> <x> <y> <z> <precision>
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  also: -MoveToArea
  what: Tells [Bots] to move to a specific area.
  arg who (forwho, default: auto): Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window.
  arg x (string, default: ${Me.X}): X coordinate (paste ${Me.X}), or the name of a point of interest in this zone
  arg y (float, default: ${Me.Y}): Y/height - IGNORED (2D ground move); pass ${Me.Y} for game-order convenience
  arg z (float, default: ${Me.Z}): Z coordinate (paste ${Me.Z})
  arg precision (float, default: 3): Arrival precision
  runs: OgreBotAPI.Movement:Move2Area
  example: oc !c -Move2Area igw:${Me.Name} ${Me.X} ${Me.Y} ${Me.Z} 3

  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  also: -Move2AreaNoTarget
  what: Walks to the given X and Z (Y is ignored) and stops within the precision distance, whether or not the toon has a target. A toon on a campspot stays there until -joustout or -letsgo; nothing moves if X or Z is missing or OgreBot is not open.
  arg who (forwho, default: auto): Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window.
  arg x (string, default: ${Me.X}): X coordinate (paste ${Me.X}), or the name of a point of interest in this zone
  arg y (float, default: ${Me.Y}): Y/height - IGNORED (2D ground move)
  arg z (float, default: ${Me.Z}): Z coordinate (paste ${Me.Z})
  arg precision (float, default: 3): Arrival precision
  runs: OgreBotAPI.Movement:Move2AreaNoTarget
  example: oc !c -MoveToAreaNoTarget igw:${Me.Name} ${Me.X} ${Me.Y} ${Me.Z} 3

  also: -nav-to, -nav_to
  what: Nav (the mesh router) to an x y z, or to a point of interest in this zone. Left blank, x y z are where the box that sends the line stands, so everyone comes to you. It waits while OgreBot is paused and stops when OgreBot closes. It leaves an encounter's trip alone.
  arg who (forwho, default: auto): Who navs - leave blank to use the For Who window.

  what: Craft the current quest’s recipe steps - one of each per pass, re-reading the quest, until none is pending.
  arg who (forwho, default: auto): Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window.
  runs: OgreBotAPI.Craft:StartQuest
  example: oc !c -OgreCraft_StartQuest ${Me.Name}

oc !c -ogrefollow <who> <whotofollow> <mindistance> <maxdistance> <breakonfollow> <backoffdistance>
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  also: -ofollow, -ofol
  what: Ogre Follow Default.
  arg who (forwho, default: auto): Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window.
  arg whotofollow (string, default: ${Me.Name}): Who to follow
  arg mindistance (float, default: 8): Min Distance
  arg maxdistance (float, default: 200): Max Distance
  arg breakonfollow (bool, default: FALSE): Break on follow
  arg backoffdistance (float, default: 0): Back off distance - back up while closer than this to the one you follow (0 = off)
  runs: OgreBotAPI.Movement:Follow
  example: oc !c -ogrefollow igw:${Me.Name} ${Me.Name} 8 200 FALSE 0

oc !c -OpenAndBuyFromMerchant <who> <merchantname> <itemname> <value>
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  what: Opens the nearest merchant whose name contains the merchant name (when no merchant window is open), then buys the quantity of the item and accepts the purchase confirmation. Runs in the action queue, and prints a console line when the window never opens or the merchant does not sell the item.
  arg who (forwho, default: auto): Who to target - leave blank to use the For Who window.
  arg merchantname (string)
  arg itemname (string)
  arg value (string, default: 1)
  runs: OgreBotAPI.Merchant:OpenAndBuy
  example: oc !c -OpenAndBuyFromMerchant ${Me.Name} ${Target.Name} "Bundle of Arrows" 1

  arg name (string): The path's name, in any case. IE: autohuntpath1

oc !c -POI_Add <name> <x> <y> <z> <sender>
  kind: console command (oc !c / oc !ci - a line, an MCP button or a script)
  what: Saves a named point of interest in the zone you are in, where you stand or at x y z. The name then works with -TravelMesh and wherever a location does. Only the box that sends the line saves it, and every box on this PC can use it.
  arg name (string): The name. It cannot be empty, hold a comma or read as a number. IE: "Quest giver"
  arg x (string): X, or leave blank for where you stand
  arg y (string): Y
  arg z (string): Z
  arg sender (string, default: ${Me.Name}): The box that saves it. Leave this out: it is the box that sent the line.
  runs: OgreBotAPI.POI:Add
  example: oc !c -POI_Add "Quest giver"

  arg name (string, default: Prowess): Scroll Name. Shortform of Prowess or Pain or Power or PowerLink is acceptable
  arg value (int64, default: 0): If duration less than this cancel it first. Leave blank or 0 to disable
  arg usebest (string, default: FALSE)
  runs: OgreBotAPI.Consumables:ScrollOf
  example: oc !c -ScrollOf ${Me.Name} Prowess 0 TRUE

== ISXOgreX events ==

OgreUI_Closed
  kind: event
  what: Fires when a window on the Ogre HTML desktop goes away, passing two arguments: the window name, then the reason - "closed" (title-bar X or ISXOgreX.UI:Close) or "reload" (the desktop was reloaded and took the window with it). On a reload every open window fires it, so a script that wants its window back re-opens it from this event.
  example: Event[OgreUI_Closed]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreUI_Hidden
  kind: event
  what: Fires when an open window on the Ogre HTML desktop changes from visible to hidden, passing one argument, the window name. It fires only on a change, and not when the window is closed (that is OgreUI_Closed).
  example: Event[OgreUI_Hidden]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreUI_Opened
  kind: event
  what: Fires when a window is created on the Ogre HTML desktop - any window, a script's own (ISXOgreX.UI:Open), OgreBot's or a help window. It passes one argument, the window name.
  example: Event[OgreUI_Opened]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreUI_Shown
  kind: event
  what: Fires when an open window on the Ogre HTML desktop changes from hidden to visible, passing one argument, the window name. It fires only on a change and not for a window that opens already visible (that is OgreUI_Opened), but a window opened hidden fires it the first time it is shown.
  example: Event[OgreUI_Shown]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]


== ISXOgreEQ2 events ==

BalancedSynergy_QueueCasting
  kind: event
  what: Fires on every box of the group that runs on this PC (the asking box included) when a box's cast stack reaches its Balanced Synergy entry: instead of casting it, that box sends this event to its group with one argument, the delay in seconds (always 10). On each box that receives it the bot itself casts Balanced Synergy after that delay unless "Ignore Balanced Synergy" is ticked or DoHO is running on that box when the delay ends, and a script atom attached here sees the same delay argument.
  example: Event[BalancedSynergy_QueueCasting]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

CampSpotJump_Completed
  kind: event
  what: Fires on this session when a jump route (OgreBotAPI.Movement:JumpRoute, or one an encounter starts) reaches its end, with two arguments: the result ("succeeded" or "failed") and why ("arrived", "already there", "timed out", "dead", "zoning", "cancelled" or "not above the check height"). A stopped route fires it as failed / cancelled, and a route that is refused at start never fires it.
  example: Event[CampSpotJump_Completed]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreCraft_CraftingStatusUpdate
  kind: event
  what: Fires on this session as the craft engine starts and ends its work, with one argument: a JSON object holding EventName, CharacterName, Time (unix seconds), Status, the flow flags (Writs / AutoTinkering / LLL / Quest), noMassProduction, craftingType, CraftedCount and CraftCount, plus Index, Error and the active recipe's _recipeName / _recipeID / _quantityToCraft / _quantityCrafted when they apply. Status is one of CraftQueue_Start, CraftQueue_CraftRecipe_Start, CraftQueue_CraftRecipe_End, CraftQueue_Finished, CraftQueue_End (bags full), Writs_Start, Writ_Start (with Writ and TotalWritsToDo), Writ_End, Writs_End, Quest_Start, Quest_End, AutoTinkering_Start, AutoTinkering_End, LLL_Start or LLL_End.
  example: Event[OgreCraft_CraftingStatusUpdate]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreCraft_NavigationRequired
  kind: event
  what: Fires on this session only when the craft option to manage movement with events (checkbox_craft_useevents) is ticked and craft needs to walk to an out-of-range station, merchant or other craft target, or cannot find it at all; it passes one JSON argument with requestID, action ("move"), category, key, displayName, customNamedPoint, precision, zone, characterName and targetFound, plus targetID, targetName, targetX/Y/Z and targetDistance when the target was found. Craft then waits with no time limit until your script calls ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:CompleteNavigation (you moved it) or ISXOgreEQ2.Craft:DeferNavigation (craft walks itself), and the same JSON stays readable as ${ISXOgreEQ2.Craft.NavigationDetails}.
  example: Event[OgreCraft_NavigationRequired]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreCraft_RecipeQueueUpdated
  kind: event
  what: Fires on this session when a recipe is added to the craft setup queue, its quantity changes, or it is removed, with one JSON argument holding EventName, CharacterName, Time (unix seconds), changeInRecipeQuantity, _recipeName, _recipeID, _quantityToCraft and _quantityCrafted. A removal (including a quantity change that reaches zero) also carries RemoveRecipe with the text "TRUE".
  example: Event[OgreCraft_RecipeQueueUpdated]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreEvent_CastMonitoring_CastingEnded
  kind: event
  what: Fires on this session when a watched NPC that was casting stops casting that ability, switches to another ability, or leaves the scan, with two arguments: the actor ID and the ability ID that ended. It is part of NPC cast monitoring (watched mobs come from zone data or `ogre npccast watch`, checked every 250 ms within 50 m by default while "NPC Cast Monitoring" is ticked and you are alive), and a cast cut off by zoning or by unticking the box ends silently with no event.
  example: Event[OgreEvent_CastMonitoring_CastingEnded]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreEvent_CastMonitoring_CastingStarted
  kind: event
  what: Fires on this session when a watched NPC begins casting, with three arguments: the actor ID, the ability ID it is casting, and the cast time the game reports for it (AbilityCastingTime, as a decimal). Only mobs on the NPC cast monitoring watch list (zone data or `ogre npccast watch`) are checked, every 250 ms within 50 m by default, and only while "NPC Cast Monitoring" is ticked, you are alive and not zoning.
  example: Event[OgreEvent_CastMonitoring_CastingStarted]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreEvent_DoHODisabled
  kind: event
  what: Fires on this session, with no arguments, every time DoHO is turned off here: OgreBotAPI.HOs:DoSetEnabled with FALSE, the target number of completed HOs reached, the DoHO timeout running out, or the DoHO target dying or going away. Turning off a DoHO that is already off does nothing and fires nothing unless -Force is passed.
  example: Event[OgreEvent_DoHODisabled]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreEvent_DoHOEnabled
  kind: event
  what: Fires on this session, with no arguments, when OgreBotAPI.HOs:DoSetup or :DoSetEnabled with TRUE primes this box as the HO starter for the first time and it takes over the group's HO options. A re-enable of a box that is already primed, an enable that is already on, or a setup with -NoModifyOptions does not fire it.
  example: Event[OgreEvent_DoHOEnabled]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreEvent_GearConditionReport
  kind: event
  what: Fires on this session after every gear check, with two arguments: the character's name and the condition of the item in the primary slot as a whole percent. A gear check runs from OgreBotAPI.Inventory:CheckGear and automatically once each time the character dies while OgreBot is loaded; if the item details are not available within 5 seconds the check fails and nothing fires.
  example: Event[OgreEvent_GearConditionReport]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreEvent_GroupQueryDone
  kind: event
  what: Fires on the session that started a group query (${OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery[...]} or OgreBotAPI.Comms:GroupQuery) when that query finishes or fails, with two arguments: the query id ("gq:<session>:<n>") and the result as JSON. The same result stays readable with ${OgreBotAPI.Comms.GroupQuery.Result[id]} for 60 seconds after it finishes.
  example: Event[OgreEvent_GroupQueryDone]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreEvent_InGameTell
  kind: event
  what: Fires on this session each time this character receives an in-game tell, with three arguments in this order: the speaker, the chat target (this character) and the message. It fires only on the receiving session and is not sent to other sessions.
  example: Event[OgreEvent_InGameTell]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreEvent_InGameTellSent
  kind: event
  what: Fires on this session each time this character sends an in-game tell, with three arguments in this order: the speaker (this character), the chat target (who the tell went to) and the message. It fires only on the sending session and is not sent to other sessions.
  example: Event[OgreEvent_InGameTellSent]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreEvent_KronoRedemption
  kind: event
  what: Fires on this session when a Krono redemption started by OgreBotAPI.Inventory:RedeemKrono reports its result, with two arguments: the character's name and TRUE (redeemed) or FALSE (the game said it failed). Nothing fires when there is no Krono to redeem, when no result shows up after 100 checks about a second apart, or when the character dies or leaves the world first.
  example: Event[OgreEvent_KronoRedemption]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreEvent_OnAbilityCast
  kind: event
  what: Fires on this session the moment the bot sends an ability cast (not when the cast lands), with five arguments: the caster (this character), the ability ID, the ability name, the target's actor ID (0 for none) and the target's name (empty for none); the other sessions in this session's relay group get the same arguments as OgreEvent_OthersOnAbilityCast. A handler that casts from inside this event can nest it at most 8 deep, after which the fire is skipped with a console line.
  example: Event[OgreEvent_OnAbilityCast]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreEvent_OnAbilityCastCompleted
  kind: event
  what: Fires on this session when an ability the cast stack cast finishes, meaning its cast bar ended or an instant ability went on cooldown, with three arguments: the character's name, the ability ID and the ability name; the other sessions in this session's relay group get the same arguments as OgreEvent_OthersOnAbilityCastCompleted. Items never fire it, and neither does a cast the bot cancelled or saw fail to start, but a cast bar that drops for any other reason (an interrupt, say) counts as finished.
  example: Event[OgreEvent_OnAbilityCastCompleted]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreEvent_OnAbilityReadyTimersUpdate
  kind: event
  what: Fires on this session about every 500 ms for each enabled ability on the OgreBot Ability Tracker list, whether or not anything changed, with four arguments: the character's name, the ability ID, the ability's short name and its time until ready in seconds (as a decimal). It fires only while the Ability Tracker option is ticked, the list has entries, and the character is in the world; an entry that does not match one of your abilities is skipped.
  example: Event[OgreEvent_OnAbilityReadyTimersUpdate]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreEvent_OnDetrimentalAdded
  kind: event
  what: Fires on this session when a detrimental with a new icon pair appears on this character, with six arguments: the effect ID, BackDropIconID, MainIconID, CurrentIncrements, Duration and MaxDuration. Your detrimentals are checked about every 500 ms while you are in the world and alive, and a detrimental whose icon changes shows up as a Removed for the old pair and an Added for the new one.
  example: Event[OgreEvent_OnDetrimentalAdded]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreEvent_OnDetrimentalRemoved
  kind: event
  what: Fires on this session when a detrimental's icon pair is no longer on this character, with six arguments describing it as last seen: the effect ID, BackDropIconID, MainIconID, CurrentIncrements, Duration and MaxDuration. Checks run about every 500 ms and pause while you are dead, so detrimentals that dropped at death are reported once you are alive again.
  example: Event[OgreEvent_OnDetrimentalRemoved]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreEvent_OnDetrimentalUpdated
  kind: event
  what: Fires on this session when a detrimental that is still on this character (same icon pair) changes its increments, Duration or MaxDuration, with six arguments: the effect ID, BackDropIconID, MainIconID, CurrentIncrements, Duration and MaxDuration. Because Duration counts down, expect it for every timed detrimental on about every 500 ms check.
  example: Event[OgreEvent_OnDetrimentalUpdated]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreEvent_OnItemUse
  kind: event
  what: Fires on this session the moment the bot uses an item (not when the use lands), with four arguments: the user (this character), the item name, the target's actor ID and the target's name; food, drink, potions and other self-used items pass 0 and an empty name for the target. The other sessions in this session's relay group get the same arguments as OgreEvent_OthersOnItemUse.
  example: Event[OgreEvent_OnItemUse]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreEvent_SmartLootAssigned
  kind: event
  what: Fires on the looting session when SmartLoot decides to assign an item to a character, with three arguments: the character's name, the item it counted (the adornment's name when the assign was for an adornment) and that character's new count for it. It fires at decision time, so it still fires if the assign later fails in the loot window.
  example: Event[OgreEvent_SmartLootAssigned]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]

OgreEvent_SpewStats
  kind: event
  what: Fires when OgreBotAPI.Debug:BroadcastStat (or OgreBotAPI.Roster:SpewMarked) resolves a value, on the asking session and on the other sessions in its relay group, with one JSON argument holding Character, Command, Label and Value (a faction result also has FactionStanding). Command is the request as typed, such as "-item a frog leg", except the faction, currency and recipe lookups send "Faction", "Currency" or "Recipe", and a bad request prints an error and fires nothing.
  example: Event[OgreEvent_SpewStats]:AttachAtom[MyHandler]
